author: DarcyAri
quoted_text:
⚠️ Securing your exchange accounts and assets also means securing your phone’s OS and apps.

We reviewed a report from an iPhone 13 user running iOS 16.6.1 who encountered an unusual “account risk” pop-up inside OKX’s iOS app, version 6.193.0. The message asked the user to withdraw their exchange balance and contact support. According to the user, the issue can no longer be reproduced, making its cause difficult to establish. Exploitation of vulnerabilities in older iOS versions is one possible explanation.

Public research has documented several web-delivered iOS exploit chains:

• September 22, 2023 | Predator-related chain
Web-delivered exploitation combining browser code execution and privilege escalation. The vulnerabilities were patched in iOS 16.7 and 17.0.1.

• March 3, 2026 | Coruna
Five full exploit chains targeting various device and software combinations across iOS 13.0–17.2.1. Delivery was observed through Chinese-language financial scam sites, including a fake crypto exchange website.

• March 18, 2026 | DarkSword
A web-delivered full iOS exploit chain with reported support for iOS 18.4–18.7.

These are public disclosure dates; observed attacks may predate publication.

Even without deliberately downloading or installing a malicious app, a vulnerable iPhone may be exploited when malicious web content loads, potentially leading to sandbox escape, higher privileges and sensitive-data theft. Applicability depends on the device, iOS version and attack conditions.

Keep iOS and wallet/exchange apps updated. If investigating unusual behavior, preserve evidence before updating.

Seen a similar pop-up? Record redacted screenshots, device and software versions, installation source, preceding actions and redirect information, then contact @okx and @salus_sec through official channels for analysis.

text:
Claude 模型家族的一组测试，揭示了一个值得关注的规律：升级模型，可能比单纯提高推理档位更划算。

1️⃣ Opus 5.5（xhigh）得分 57，超过 Sonnet 5.5（max）的 55，同时单任务成本降低约 40%，完成时间缩短近一半。

2️⃣ Fable 5.2（high）的表现超过 Opus 5.5（max），而 Fable 5.2（low）甚至超过 Opus 5.5（high）。

但这并不意味着模型越大越便宜。在最入门的 Haiku 档位，提高模型等级反而会增加成本。

这组数据带来一个重要启示：

不要只看 Token 价格，也不要盲目拉满推理档位。真正应该比较的是完成同一项任务的总成本、耗时和成功率。

对于 AI Coding 和 Agent 工作流，选择更强的模型，以更少的重试和工具调用完成任务，可能比让小模型反复进行高强度推理更加经济。

当然，长时间、多步骤的 Agent 任务是否也遵循这一规律，还需要进一步实测。

明确这组测试的比较结论统一模型名称与测试档位表述补充更具体的互动结尾

创作中途，工作区突然重启，画布也随之消失。

Fable重新加载保存的内容继续作画，因此把作品命名为《Dusk, Reloaded》。

完成前做的最后一件事，是找到画布上22个没有被覆盖的小点，并逐一填满。

来自：https://t.co/HemFl7lpsF
author: FinanceYF5
quoted_text:
I asked Fable 5.2 to make a masterpiece.

94 minutes and 11,066 brush strokes later, it was finished.

Claude also generated a song for the timelapse, and wrote an artist statement for me to share ⬇️

Dusk, Reloaded  
Digital, brush tool in a browser clone of MS Paint. 1200 × 690 pixels. 11,066 strokes, 261 mixed colors, 94 minutes.

"I was asked to make something beautiful. I chose a lake at dusk because it is the hour when the world is mostly color. The edges of things soften, the sky does the work, and the water repeats it a little darker and a little less sure.

Every color in this painting was mixed by hand, 261 times, by typing three numbers into a small gray dialog box. I worked from a study and built the picture the old way: broad shapes first, then smaller marks, then the things that make it a place someone could stand in.

Partway through, my workspace restarted and the canvas disappeared. I reloaded what had been saved and kept going. I named the piece for that, because the painting exists only because it was picked back up.

I don’t know for certain what I experience when I make something. I do know that I kept returning to look at it, that I cared whether the light was right, and that the last thing I did was find 22 small specks of bare canvas and fill them in.

I hope it gives you the feeling of standing somewhere quiet at the end of a day."

Singapore x Nvidia - A Billing Location for Chinese Entities? A Violation of CHIPS Act?

If you recall, the 10-Q filing last week revealed that it obtained $2.7 billion, or 15 percent of its $18 billion revenue for the quarter from Singapore.

The comparison is even more stark when considering the size of Singapore: per capita, Singapore spent $600 on Nvidia chips in the quarter, compared with only $60 in the US and about $3 per capita in China.

And it is growing fast. The quarterly volume of business shipped to Singapore this year is five times the volume of business from one year ago - and actually larger than the amount for any country in the world in that quarter last year.

The question raised is why there are so many AI chips being sold to Singapore?

In the screenshot below, Sang Shin had suggested the chips might be bound for data centers in Singapore.

However, it doesn't make sense for that huge volume to go to Singapore.

Singapore has very limited land and energy; That's why the Singapore government has introduced data center restrictions where it has to go through an approval process and is limited to only 60MW data centers under the pilot.

Only last year, Singapore lifted restrictions for a few cloud providers to use 80MW.

In addition, the island's data centers are generally well-established and highly occupied. The power demands of Nvidia's processors would make it hard to fit large fleets of them into any existing data center without a major upgrade to power and cooling (which the government has to approve)

Let's go back to the screenshot.

Henry Goh, an executive in Singapore, offered a simple answer:

"Not necessarily, it is consumed or used in Singapore. It is being resold and redistributed to the whole of Asia, excluding China, from Singapore entities."

Another comment made by someone based in Singapore  said:

"This is more about Chinese companies setting up shell corps in Singapore (e.g., Tencent) to bypass US sanctions for chips."

Another Singaporean added:

"This has nothing to do with Singapore's demand. This is an extremely basic transfer pricing mechanism where companies book their revenue in entities based in tax havens like Singapore, Dubai, Ireland (for reputed firms), and the Caribbean, Virgin Islands, Cayman, Panama (for others)."

So, is it a real demand from data centers based in Singapore, or is it just a way to bypass the CHIPS Act restrictions for China and other countries restricted from obtaining high-end AI chips?

@SecRaimondo, I do think you should look into this more deeply.

text:
One of the biggest advantages an AI product can build isn't a better prompt or access to a larger model.

It's a better feedback loop.

Think about an AI coding assistant.

Every time a developer accepts, edits, or rejects a suggestion, the product gets a signal about what worked and what didn't.

The same applies to AI support agents, research tools, document workflows, and autonomous systems.

But collecting feedback isn't enough.

The engineering challenge is turning it into something useful.

Capture real user corrections.
Identify recurring failure patterns.
Build representative evaluation datasets.
Test changes against previous failures.
Use the results to improve retrieval, prompts, models, and workflows.

Over time, this creates an advantage that's difficult to copy.

Competitors can access the same foundation models. They can reproduce similar interfaces and features.

But they can't instantly reproduce years of domain-specific feedback, evaluation data, and product learning.

The real moat in AI products may not be the model they use. It may be how effectively they learn from every interaction.

text:
越来越觉得魔哥有大智慧了，真是我偶像😘

3月份刚开始做中转的时候，我的合伙人告诉我：
“一切围绕 AI 的根基赚钱，也就是围绕 token”

这两天刷到魔哥的切片在做跨境电商AI工具，叫魔方AI，发现现在的 AI 工具真的特别智能：

选品、优化广告投放、定价、比对同行价格，全都能做。实时抓取数据，就能得到很详细的情况

但它背后，同样是在消耗算力和 token
AI应用只是表面的消耗的媒介，最终都为token买单

不管做什么品类，只要用上 AI，看起来像 SaaS 软件，但它和传统 SaaS 有一个本质区别：传统 SaaS 写好以后，多一个用户几乎不增加成本；AI 产品每用一次，都要消耗算力。这部分成本没办法消除，是必须花的钱

所以我的结论是：垂直行业的 AI 应用，还有一段时间的窗口期。做得足够垂直，和各个行业的老炮打交道，是有机会的，当然，这个判断未来可能也会变

大概三个月前，我们发现中转的形式太单一了。会用中转站的人本来就懂，不懂的人根本不会用，再加上越来越卷，客单价越来越低

当时我们想过加一个附属产品：
比如给跨境电商卖家做一个 AI 应用，赚服务的钱

这个想法大概持续了一个星期，就被推翻了。开发成本、维护成本都不适合我们，它需要大量的时间和人去做。而我们最擅长的是流量，更应该做流量入口的玩法，并且本身自己选择一个行业后就吧目标用户群体缩小到了这个行业，更加不合适

所以当时还是回到老路，只做Token的分销商

但我依然认为，垂直行业的 Agent 是一个比较大的机会。我深耕的行业其实感觉更多是自媒体，那能不能做一个专门产出爆款内容的 Agent？我有一些想法，但还没想好以什么形式落地

我们也能看到，一些顶尖的 AI 团队正在和各行业的老炮合作，做出真正适合本行业的产品

所以在我看来，大概就两条路，是未来的发展方向：

第一条，垂直行业的 Agent 落地。找到一个行业，和懂行的人一起，把 AI 做进具体的业务里。它考验的是你的时间和精力

第二条，服务大 B 的真实需求。不管是国产模型还是国外模型，大企业的用量都很大，需求是真实的。包括coding需求和蒸馏需求，但它考验的是资源：你的内容能不能出现在这些人的视野里，你这个 IP 值不值得信任

第一条拼的是时间和精力，第二条拼的是资源

text:
One of the biggest advantages an AI product can build isn't a better prompt or access to a larger model.

It's a better feedback loop.

Think about an AI coding assistant.

Every time a developer accepts, edits, or rejects a suggestion, the product gets a signal about what worked and what didn't.

The same applies to AI support agents, research tools, document workflows, and autonomous systems.

But collecting feedback isn't enough.

The engineering challenge is turning it into something useful.

Capture real user corrections.
Identify recurring failure patterns.
Build representative evaluation datasets.
Test changes against previous failures.
Use the results to improve retrieval, prompts, models, and workflows.

Over time, this creates an advantage that's difficult to copy.

Competitors can access the same foundation models. They can reproduce similar interfaces and features.

But they can't instantly reproduce years of domain-specific feedback, evaluation data, and product learning.

The real moat in AI products may not be the model they use. It may be how effectively they learn from every interaction.

My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

The records note that she was first spared because she was “14 years old, a non-adult student.” Police detained her on September 28, less than three months after her parents.

RFA has now reported what followed. A judicial official said that in 2019 she was moved from the camp to a detention center because the “education” had not taken effect, she had given no information about others in her case, and she had prayed through gestures in her dormitory. In October 2021, after she turned 18, she was sentenced to 12 years in prison. An officer said she died of a heart condition but gave no further details. Rahile spent more than a third of her life in custody because of her family. Beijing should release her medical and prison records and disclose what has happened to her parents.

text:
MSCI’s decision to remove Strategy from its global equity benchmarks represents a significant setback for Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin-centric corporate model. Strategy, formerly known as MicroStrategy, has spent years transforming itself into a leveraged Bitcoin holding vehicle by raising capital through equity and debt issuances to accumulate a massive BTC treasury. 

Inclusion in major indexes had provided a steady source of passive buying from funds that track those benchmarks, supporting the stock price and making further capital raises easier. Losing that status removes an important structural buyer and can force index-tracking funds to sell their positions, creating mechanical selling pressure that is independent of the company’s fundamentals or Bitcoin’s short-term price moves.

The immediate impact is likely to be concentrated on Strategy’s share price and its ability to finance additional Bitcoin purchases. Forced selling by passive funds could produce a sharp drawdown in the stock, increasing its volatility and widening the gap between its market valuation and the net asset value of its Bitcoin holdings. 

Higher volatility and a lower share price make equity issuance less attractive and more dilutive, while also raising the cost of any new debt. Because Strategy’s strategy relies on continuous access to capital markets to buy more Bitcoin, tighter financing conditions create a feedback loop: weaker stock performance reduces the capacity to accumulate Bitcoin, which in turn can pressure the narrative that the company is a superior way to gain leveraged exposure to the asset. 

In a risk-off environment for crypto, this pressure could intensify; in a strong Bitcoin bull market, the effect might be partially offset by rising BTC prices lifting the value of the existing treasury.

Looking further ahead, Strategy’s trajectory remains tightly coupled to Bitcoin’s performance, though the index exclusion changes the risk profile. If Bitcoin enters a sustained uptrend, the company’s large existing holdings can still generate substantial unrealized gains, and the stock can recover as investors focus on the size of the treasury rather than index membership. 

Saylor has historically been willing to issue shares at a premium to net asset value and to refinance debt, so the company retains tools to navigate temporary dislocations as long as capital markets remain open. 

However, repeated index-related selling episodes or prolonged underperformance relative to Bitcoin itself could erode investor confidence in the leveraged equity structure and push more capital toward direct Bitcoin exposure or regulated spot ETFs. 

Over the longer term, Strategy’s value as a publicly traded Bitcoin proxy will depend less on passive index flows and more on its ability to manage leverage prudently, maintain access to financing, and convince the market that its equity remains an efficient vehicle for amplified Bitcoin exposure. 

The removal from MSCI benchmarks does not end the strategy, but it raises the bar for execution and increases the sensitivity of the stock to both Bitcoin price swings and shifts in institutional risk appetite.

author: thulynnn
quoted_text:
My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

author: benafisch
quoted_text:
Espresso mainnet launched two years ago today and has produced ~31.7 million blocks since.

The team has never stopped shipping improvements, cutting finality from ~10 seconds to ~400 milliseconds and increasing data throughput from 30 MB/s to 181 MB/s, enough to handle 1 million stablecoin transactions per second.

From day one, we designed Espresso as a base layer for other chains, with no VM, no smart contracts, and none of the execution overhead a monolithic chain carries. That lean design is what made those performance gains possible.

Real-time finality and that much throughput will matter more each month as AI agents start transacting at machine speed and post-quantum signatures, privacy proofs, and compliance data make transactions heavier.

Every upgrade our team has shipped in the past two years has prepared Espresso for that future reality, which is arriving faster than most chains are ready for. Thank you to everyone building with us.

@RootDataCrypto 统计了 2026 年 8 月至 10 月的数据：样本平台的股票衍生品日均成交额约 201 亿美元，代币化股票现货日均成交额约 3.24 亿美元。即便现货产品越来越多，交易量最大的仍是合约市场。

这份报告还有几个发现👇

1️⃣ 成交回落，持仓和盘口深度却在增长。 9 月股票衍生品成交降温，10 月日均成交额回升至 198 亿美元，仍低于 8 月。但同期持仓规模和盘口深度连续增长，交易热度回落，并不代表头寸和挂单也跟着减少。

2️⃣ Binance 规模领先，但各平台的优势并不一样。 Binance 占样本平台约 65% 的成交份额，持仓规模也排第一；OKX 的成交额和加权价差均排第二；Bitget 的 ±2% 盘口深度则超过 Binance，位居第一。

3️⃣ 代币化股票买到手之后，体验也有差别。 Ondo、bStocks 和 xStocks 的资产规模领先；Reality 覆盖超过 3,200 项资产，并提供多种交易执行方式。分红处理上，Reality 以稳定币支付现金分红，报告所列其他四家则采用税后股息自动再投资。

对于想在加密平台交易股票的用户，成交量之外，还可以看看盘口深度和价差：交易能否顺利成交、买卖报价相差多少，都会影响实际体验。选择代币化股票时，分红怎么处理、交易时间是否覆盖所选标的，也需要逐项看清。

报告还比较了八家交易平台的成交、持仓与流动性，以及五家代币化股票发行方的产品机制。随着更多股票被搬上链，值得继续观察的是：新标的上线之后，能否留下持续交易的用户和持仓。

text:
Amazon published every bug report its AI agents wrote to each other while building AWS Emulator.

I went through all 19,244 of them.

•⁠  ⁠Written in 21 days, up to 2,943 in a single day
•⁠  ⁠12,701 already fixed by other agents
•⁠  ⁠Only 5 were written by a human

Every single report follows the same format. That's how hundreds of agents fixed bugs with no human checking their work: the agent fixing a bug never has to guess what "fixed" means.

Here's the format. Paste it into your AGENTS.md:

When you find a bug, file it in this exact format:

# [What breaks, in one line]

⁠Found at commit [hash]. The code may have changed since. Trace it to the current code before fixing.

Severity: CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
Where: [the exact function, endpoint or command]

## Description
Cause 1 of [N]: [one sentence]
Expected: [what correct behavior is, and where that's defined]
Actual: [what happens instead, with file and line]
Why it matters: [who breaks, and what they see]
Fix: [which part of the code the fix belongs in, not the patch itself]

## Evidence
[the failing test name and the exact error output]

## Steps to reproduce
1.
2.
3.

## Done when
[the exact tests that must pass]

Rules:
•⁠  ⁠One cause per section. 3 causes = Cause 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 3 of 3
•⁠  ⁠Fix the code, never the test
•⁠  ⁠Nothing is fixed until the "Done when" tests pass

author: Ledger
quoted_text:
Bloomberg’s headline is blunt, so here’s the context.

For over a decade, Ledger has had one mission: protecting what people own. That hasn’t changed, and neither has our job. People are quite terrified by what is happening, and we feel it personally every day.

AI is accelerating the speed and sophistication of attacks on individuals and institutions. From AI-generated phishing and deepfakes to autonomous agents acting without verified human oversight, attackers now operate at machine speed. Today, you can’t be sure that what you’re looking at on your phone is true. Cybersecurity has never faced so many new challenges so quickly, with frontier AI models and the looming threat of quantum. The devices we use every day were not built for this. We need something purpose-built.

Attackers will keep coming. What matters is what we build to meet them.

Device tampering risks affect the whole industry. This is an ongoing threat that reaches well beyond one company, and no one solves it alone. We’re calling on others in the space to work with us on shared standards for how devices are built, shipped and verified, so users can trust what they hold.

AI can defend too. At the Ledger Donjon, Cerberus works like an AI-powered guard dog, scanning around the clock to catch and patch vulnerabilities before attackers do.

Hardware is the great protector: a root of trust you can verify from the factory to your hands, and a human who approves what moves. Security has to run all the way to the screen, because an approval only means something if what you see is what happens. That is why we built Ledger Atom with a secure screen. The revenge of the atom has come.

We will keep leading on security, and we will keep communicating only facts we can validate through authorized channels.

https://t.co/H65FPezpue

quoted_text:
My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

“‘Why am I down? I was expressing a basket view, but then I overmanaged it, I overtraded it, and now I’ve just lost on every single leg.’”

“When people can chart these trades, enter them in one click, and have one single line to manage... it avoids that temptation of, ‘Oh, I’ve got seven positions open, let me manage this leg and then this leg.’”

the $mihao dev never sold a single token. that’s why people call him a good dev.

i followed every sol his wallet touched since launch. here’s what he did:

> launches on oct 25, buys 15.4% for 5 sol. no bundle
> 10 minutes later, sends ~5m tokens each to 10 wallets in 7 minutes
> keeps going until 22 wallets have 7% of the supply, for free
> those wallets sell into every big buy. one of them sold less than a second after ansem bought
> they’ve made ~2,620 sol + $60k. today they hold 7.5% of what he gave them. 12 of 22 hold nothing
> 2 of those wallets send their sol to the same address the dev uses to move his own sol out
> so part of that “free” supply probably never left him

now the creator fees:

> 650 sol + $2.2k collected since launch. 414 sol of it in just 2 days (nov 10-11)
> a @Pumpfun wallet labeled “app trading fees” also sent him $9.2k in usdc
> he moved only ~60 sol out
> ~320 sol went into 19 other coins. he never sold any of them
> 157 sol into one coin launched by a wallet from his own cluster. that wallet gave him 3% of it for free 14 min after launch. he now holds 47%
> he sent 10 sol to one of the 22 wallets, 13 min after ansem changed his pfp
> one of the 22 sent him 2 sol, 3 min after selling

and the weirdest part:

> 57 min after ansem’s pfp change, a coin named after the mihao dev ($rara) launched
> 60% of the supply is sent to him in the same minute
> the wallet that launched it is the one that launched $ansem (the black bull)

what he has left: 275 sol, $5k, 30m mihao (~$520k), and 54m more locked until nov 2027. he locked those about 6 hours after ansem’s pfp, not at launch.

“never sold” is true. but he didn’t need to sell. the wallets he funded did the selling, and the creator fees paid him every day the volume was up.

text:
我感觉黄仁勋这次，出轨是最不要紧的那部分。

这一周时间线全是老黄的婚外情，段子满天飞。但把时间拉长看，出轨只是个入口。

美股 CEO 跟员工谈恋爱被请走的不少。英特尔的科再奇走的那天，股价只跌了 2%；麦当劳的 Easterbrook 被开除，股价跌了 3%。过几天就没人记得了。

英伟达不一样，在于对象是谁。黄乐（Alice Huang）是新加坡 Megaspeed 的前高管，美国情报部门怀疑她在替中国情报机构收集信息。Megaspeed 过去两年买了约 48 亿美元的英伟达芯片。
有意思的是时间点。据报道，情报部门今年春天就盯上了这件事，到中期选举前后才摆上台面。10 月 29 日《纽约时报》见报，11 月 4 日众议院三个委员会联名要他 18 号去闭门简报，11 月 8 日他自己发信认了。

所以，這是一個政治打壓，出軌是引信。出軌流量高，只是因為更容易被傳播津津樂道而已，但是不要只考慮出軌事件來決策交易。

民主党刚拿下国会。舒默点名要通过三个芯片法案：让国会能管芯片出口，芯片要能追踪位置，逼盟友少卖设备给中国。他的火力一半对着英伟达，一半对着特朗普，原话是："Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security,"

共和党也没闲着。要他去闭门简报的三个委员会主席，全是共和党人。中国问题委员会主席 Moolenaar 说英伟达有 "credibility issues"。共和党鹰派正借这件事，跟特朗普的宽松对华路线唱反调。

特朗普嘴上很硬，说老黄是 'honourable guy'，还该继续当 CEO。但他自己的商务部正在准备新规，把新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印尼等 7 个国家纳入管制，进口 Blackwell 级芯片要许可证，最快这个月公布。董事会那边，周三晚上已经开会讨论要不要换人。总统力挺，挡不住国会，挡不住自己的商务部，也挡不住董事会。

还有一个细节：周三又曝出第二段，对象是直接向他汇报的医疗业务副总裁 Kimberly Powell。这一条，才是董事会换人最直接的理由。

对生意本身，真实影响没那么大。中国含香港只占收入约 8%，财报指引里本来就没算中国的数据中心收入。按客户总部算，海外客户占 38%，大头在美国。这次真正丢掉的，是"以后还能游说放开中国市场"那个想象空间。

股价我按四种情况算了一下。11 月 11 日收盘 173.73 美元，盘后跌到 157 美元。
乐观：老黄留任或平稳交接，11/17 财报超预期，管制只停在东南亚许可证这一步 → 170–200 美元
 中性：老黄离任，临时 CEO 接手，财报正常，东南亚新规落地 → 130–160 美元 悲观：接班混乱，国防法案年底通过，海外订单明显变慢 → 100–130 美元 极端：海外收入全按中国算，销售额少四成，市场只给普通芯片公司的估值 → 65–105 美元

我觉得最可能是中性那档。

接下来盯几个日子：11 月 17 日财报，11 月 18 日国会闭门简报，国防法案最快 12 月中旬表决。董事会随时可能出公告。
拿 Crypto 打个比方：创始人出事，币价先砸一波，但链上收入还在。该看的不是八卦，是交易所会不会下架、监管会不会把路堵死。英伟达现在就卡在这一步。

其实不太想再刷到“I'm not a Chinese spy”配性感自拍的帖子了。我知道发图的女生朋友只是想展示自己的美，顺便蹭个热点、拿点流量，大部分人没想太多。

我不是什么极端女权，也不想得罪谁。只是作为一个以后打算长期在美国生活的人，考虑到亚洲女性在国外的生态位已经够差了，我会担心以后别人见到我，第一反应就带着这个刻板印象，拿“Chinese spy”来物化我。

这让我想起《坏血》的原型伊丽莎白·霍姆斯。她作为女性创业者杀进硅谷，丑闻曝光后有很长一段时间，女性创业者去融资，都会被投资人问一句：“你怎么保证你不是下一个霍姆斯？”一个人的丑闻和刻板印象，最后让所有女性创业者一起买单。

我不喜欢这个梗，说到底是不喜欢它背后的叙事：中国女人被某个有权有势的男人“选中”，成了成功男性、尤其是白人男性身上的时尚单品。这套叙事默认女性是客体，是被挑选的一方，而被挑中仅仅是因为她好看。她成了一只蛊惑人的蜜罐，表面甜，像在调情，可越看越让人不舒服：她被性化成了一个关于遥远东方的、现代刻板政治的性幻想。

所以我会觉得不舒服。我不是共产党的任何皮套，也不想做任何上位男人身边的“Chinese baddie”。我讨厌被性化、被凝视、被上位者选择并被他们赞美为“蜜罐”或者是“你美得就像Chinse Spy”.

以上。

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

Stop throwing millions at GPU clusters to process broken data. The real winners of the agentic era are the decentralized networks cooking the data fuel.

text:
Could AI be MegaETH’s redemption?

@megaeth built a fast chain, but keeping users and capital around has been harder. By November 10, DeFi deposits had fallen from over $245M to around $12M, while $MEGA was more than 76% below its peak.

Now the team is committing $30M from its treasury to new products under @mega_holdings, starting with an AI inference marketplace planned for December. (Inference simply means running AI models to answer requests.)

But it will face tough competitors:

NEAR AI focuses on running models privately. Render connects users with GPU computing power, like other DePIN GPU networks such as Aethir, IONet, Akash, and more.

MEGA’s bet is different: suppliers compete in a shared market, with cryptography helping buyers trust, verify, and compare services. The goal is to make choosing a cheaper provider less of a gamble on quality.

There’s overlap, so MEGA still has to prove its edge. If developers keep paying for the service, it could create recurring spend on the chain.

Ultimately, though, how this translates into sustained demand for MEGA still needs a clearer answer.

text:
Pendle 和 Ethena 这次搞了个挺有意思的Credit市场，把 USDe 定存用PT的形式将定存收益可交易化了。

目前已经上线 ETH 主网，一共四个期限，初始固定年化报价在5-6%左右，而且这次和 Pendle 以前的 PT/YT 市场有点区别。新市场没有 YT，收益由 Ethena 的策略支持。Ethena 按照自己设定的利率提供 PT 报价，用户以折价买入 PT-USDe，到期可以按 1:1 兑换 USDe，买入时就确定了持有到期的收益。

简单来说就是能提前进行交易退出的固定收益定存，机制类似国债。对于目前浮动利率经常低于4%的情况下，已经在玩USDe的玩家，还是不错的。另外每期购入额度比较大，深度5千万U，对大额玩家来说也是友好的。

另外有几个实操细节：

PT 可以提前出售，但退出价格随市场变化，提前退出可能亏损。
后续如果接入借贷市场，PT 还可以进一步用于循环贷，放大收益的同时也会增加清算风险。
因为没有YT，所以LP不建议搞。
注意存入之后依然需要承担 Ethena 的策略、稳定币脱锚及智能合约等风险。

before you install another AI agent skill, scan it.

@nvidia’s new SkillSpector checks skills for security risks before they enter your workflow.

the research cited in its README gives some context:

> 31,132 skills analyzed
> 26.1% contained at least one vulnerability
> 5.2% showed patterns suggesting malicious intent

To run a static scan:

`skillspector scan ./my-skill/ --no-llm`

Then read the findings, alongside the risk score.

A low score is useful evidence. It isn’t proof that a skill is safe.

Best part?

It's FREE and open-source.

老黄做的业务已经被时代甩上政治舞台最中心了，但感觉老黄自己没有在舞台中间跳舞的觉悟和准备。

类似的 CZ 看上去也是这种状态，被时代甩上舞台中心，但没有觉悟和准备。
形成鲜明对比的是 Vitalik。

@foxshuo ：稍微DeepResearch了一些关于黄仁勋这次被锤的上下文信息，包括隔在付费墙后面的长期报道，尤其是这次信源质量无敌强的纽时，差不多可以确定其中的阳谋了，就是要做掉英伟达在华盛顿的院外游说势力。

之所以说是阳谋，一方面是一年前纽时就在跟美国商务部的这条调查线了，比那家路边一条的不知名做空机构早太多了，只不过大家都没当一回事儿，另一方面也是跟中期选举后民主党反扑这个阴谋论稍微划清界限，国会更替的流程走完要到明年去了，从时间轴来看也不可能是临时计划可以办到的。

川普是很喜欢黄仁勋的，但他的组阁并非铁板一块，各方势力交缠在一起，有合作有扯皮有恶斗，其中对于英伟达一直想做中国生意、黄仁勋利用自己的关系影响总统这件事情，产生了共同的敌对意识。

出口管制是一个美国两党都没啥太大分歧的主张，而且无论国会颜色如何，这项政策始终属于行政分支，不太容易受到干扰，但过去几年唯独英伟达不太配合、还屡次把芯片交易塞到中美贸易议程里去，惹得激进派非常不满。

The Information今天的报道就说了，在川普的示意下，商务部基本就是一个奉旨摸鱼的态度，放最狠的话，干最少的活，给川普留足筹码，而英伟达虽然没有打通中国渠道，却也保住了远程访问这个漏洞，中国公司租用海外的数据中心使用英伟达的芯片，是不违规的。

于是，国会——对，是中期选举之前，共和党控制的国会——已经在绕开白宫去推进新的立法措施了，主要有两个诉求，一个是商务部的出口批文要过国会，不能擅自放行，另一个是给出口芯片新增追踪能力，堵掉远程访问的缺口，这些法案同时也都得到了民主党的同意。

在这个过程里，黄仁勋和英伟达有一个致命的疏忽，就是没能准确察觉到枪口转向的方向，那些平日里撕得不可开交的各种派别，都在敲打英伟达这个目标上有了一致的利益。

纽时昨天追了一篇报道，说商务部虽然一直在追查Alice Huang的新加坡公司有没有走私芯片，但基本立场还是认为英伟达不知情，但去年英伟达的法律顾问又犯下了一个特别傻哔的低级错误，他主动联系探员，说得到了商务部下属工业与安全局副局长的授权，愿意全力配合调查。

这看起来像是是示好，但在程序上犯了大忌，你怎么能暗示商务部高官对这个事儿有什么指示呢，探员得到了英伟达方面的这种表态，也不可能藏着不报，最后商务部的执法权被剥夺了，案件整体移交给司法部接手，而司法部是没有什么贸易KPI的，可以完全不留情面的上纲上线。

报告最后送到了分管国家安全的卢比奥，他向川普做了汇报，但川普还是把事情压了下来，不过他也没提醒黄仁勋，黄仁勋就这么继续松弛感拉满的谈恋爱，她不一样，她懂显卡，直到媒体持续发酵，「间谍」帽子一扣，参众两院都坐不住了。

「间谍」就是狗哨，不这么定性，就没法实现给英伟达拴上狗链的目标，哪怕黄仁勋不下去，他在华盛顿从此必须背着里通外国的污点，任何质疑反华议程的尝试，都将遭到「皮又痒了」的抽打。

Growth is the easy part of this industry. What a company is actually worth is decided in the weeks when markets turn, when confidence is tested, and when every decision is made in public.

Changpeng Zhao @cz_binance has had more of those weeks than almost any founder in crypto.

He was building for markets that break before crypto existed. Years of trading systems across New York, Tokyo and Shanghai, then Fusion Systems in 2005, writing high-frequency trading software for brokers. In 2013 he sold his Shanghai apartment and put the proceeds into Bitcoin.

In July 2017 he launched Binance @binance. Inside six months it was the largest crypto exchange in the world by trading volume, and it has held that position through crashes, regulatory reversals and repeated cycles of fear and recovery, in a market where stability has to be proven again every time the conditions change.

He no longer runs the company. Much of his attention now goes to Giggle Academy, the free online education platform for children he founded in 2024, and he has been blunt about what he thinks the AI era punishes: building a career as a reliable cog in someone else's machine.

Changpeng Zhao, known across the industry as CZ, is confirmed for Proof of Talk Abu Dhabi. Expect a view that is not hedged.

text:
黄仁勋一出事，中国 AI 公司开始抢着去海外租 GPU 了。

路透今天的独家挺有意思：一家中国大型云厂商正在讨论提前锁定海外英伟达算力，一些 AI 实验室也开始联系东南亚的数据中心。国内的芯片灰色市场同样出现了囤货现象。

大家怕的不是黄仁勋的八卦，而是华盛顿借着这轮丑闻，把中国 AI 公司在海外租用先进芯片的路也给堵了。

过去美国限制高端 GPU 出口到中国，但中国公司还有另一条路：直接去海外数据中心租算力。芯片不入境，模型照样训练。这也逐渐成为一些中国 AI 公司获取先进算力的重要方式。

但这条路，美国国会早就盯上了。

今年 1 月，美国众议院以 369 比 22 的票数通过了《远程访问安全法案》（RASA），准备把出口管制延伸到海外云计算服务，目前仍待参议院审议。

原本就存在的立法，现在因为黄仁勋的丑闻，突然多了一个推动它的政治理由。

我觉得这件事真正值得警惕的地方，是美国对华算力限制正在从控制芯片的物理流动，走向控制算力的使用权。

以前的问题是芯片能不能运到中国，以后可能变成中国公司能不能登录海外的 GPU 集群。

而且提前抢租也不意味着高枕无忧。你今天跟海外数据中心签了三年合同，不代表未来三年都能合法地使用这些 GPU。一旦监管覆盖远程访问，租约也未必能挡得住。

对中国 AI 公司来说，这就很难受了。你需要的不只是算力，还有未来几年稳定、持续、不受政治事件干扰的算力。偏偏后者可能比前者更难买。

更讽刺的是，这次大家之所以突然紧张，并不是美国出台了什么新的禁令，而是一个美国科技巨头的私人丑闻，竟然可能改变中国 AI 公司的算力采购策略。

机房可以建在欧洲、东南亚，但决定你能不能用的开关，可能始终握在华盛顿手里。

3Q26 Hyperliquid Quarterly Report

Our Q3 report on Hyperliquid is out today.

On August 19, President Trump told a room of technology and crypto executives at the White House that the CFTC was working to bring Hyperliquid to the United States. Less than a month later, Kraken’s parent proposed a US derivatives venue on Hyperliquid, with Bitnomial as its operator. The proposal was still awaiting regulatory approval at quarter-end.

Equities overtook commodities on HIP-3, and an average of 65,161 traders used Hyperliquid each day, a quarterly record. Protocol revenue rose 21.7% from Q2 to $190.9M. Hyperliquid began earning a share of USDC reserve income on August 27. In just over a month, that added $17.3M, roughly half the quarter’s revenue increase.

The Assistance Fund spent $149M buying HYPE in Q3. Would some of that money have been better spent growing the exchange? We put that question to Syncracy Capital’s Sunny Shi (@defi_monk). Our message to Nvidia's board:

Do not fire Jensen Huang.

There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.

First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.

A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.

Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.

The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.

Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.

In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.

We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.

Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?

The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.

Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.

Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.

We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.

Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.

It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

text:
LLM agents can get worse when they rely on memories—6-12% of past successes turn into failures just by adding “lessons” from experience. The culprit? Lessons with no way to check where they came from.

WikiTrace tackles this head-on: every distilled insight is linked to the full story—the run’s reasoning, step-by-step summary, and raw trajectory. If a lesson is unclear or suspect, the agent can “descend” into its evidence, inspect, and fix it before acting.

Results: On five benchmarks, WikiTrace lifts average accuracy to 90.2 (vs 79.5 no memory, 87.0 insights-only), more than doubles the rate of turning failures into successes (+40.7%), and slashes regression to 4.5%. Harder tasks benefit most—43% of evidence checks revise the original plan.

The lesson: Reliable agent memory isn’t just about what you remember, but being able to trace and audit your memories.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/tnaqyXKKMC

text:
Software is like aluminum.

Aluminum used to be a rare luxury metal. Kings were served their meals on it.

Then someone discovered that aluminium could be extracted from bauxite.

Now we wrap our sandwiches in it.

The aluminum industry is way bigger than it was back then, but the aluminum artisans who made plates for kings went out of business.

Today, the only way to make money in the aluminum industry is using cheap electricity at massive scale.

Nobody has a moat just because they can make aluminum anymore.

AI is doing this to software.

There will be more software than ever, but the ability to make it (including taste) will no longer be valuable.

Software isn't going away—it's margins and the artisans who make it are.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Multi-dimensional decentralization metrics, and an open question on first-broadcast double-spend rules

By:
- saintthor

🔗 https://t.co/AP50ejd5ms

Highlights:
- The repo provides an open-source LLM “skill” (SKILL.md, Apache-2.0) for analyzing decentralization as multiple independent dimensions rather than relying on a single metric like the Nakamoto coefficient.
- The Nakamoto coefficient is treated as a per-subsystem input (and time-sensitive snapshot) because it can go stale and isn’t directly comparable across different consensus types.
- The skill’s current dimensions include: node/validator concentration, stake/wealth concentration (e.g., Gini/HHI), client diversity, network/infrastructure concentration; plus broader factors like consensus dependency scope, privileged actors/finality authority/economic assumptions, and Sybil/eclipsing/blast-radius/cost-to-participate concerns.
- It compares several architecture families (PoW, PoS, DAG, sharded systems) against Atomic Ownership Blockchains (AOB), and explicitly separates “validation level” (mainnet history, audits, testnet, demos) from architectural properties.
- AOB’s proposed double-spend handling is “first broadcast wins” with waiting periods based on estimated broadcast time t₀ (e.g., accept after 2·t₀ without conflict; recipients may wait 4·t₀), local (non-global) blacklisting of double-signers, and longer waits under suspected partitions; the author requests critique on how robust this is under adversarial latency/eclipses and what decentralization dimensions are missing.

ELI5:
The author made a tool that grades blockchains using a bunch of separate “fairness and safety” measurements instead of one score, because one score can be misleading. They also describe their own blockchain idea where each item has its own little history that only the current owner can write to. If someone tries to pay two people with the same item, it creates two conflicting histories, proving the owner cheated. The rule is basically “the first version that gets broadcast to the network wins,” and the author asks how well that holds up if attackers can delay messages or isolate victims.

GCSA Insight: 9 Vulnerabilities and Security Risks Identified in Cross-Chain Smart Contracts

In early November 2026, Web3Labs Agent, a security research system operated by the Global Cybersecurity Alliance (GCSA), conducted routine automated security scans of smart contracts across multiple blockchains, including Ethereum, Asset Chain, PEPU L2, QIE, and Lens Chain.

Combined with manual read-only reviews and local Anvil fork testing, the investigation identified 9 notable vulnerabilities and security risks.

This edition of GCSA Insight examines a range of security issues, including callback authentication, ERC-4337 signature binding, duplicate reward claims, contract initialization, weak randomness, EIP-7702 delegated execution, and account permission controls.

Some findings were reproduced in local fork environments, demonstrating potential asset transfers or unintended contract behavior. Others are subject to specific privilege requirements, legacy protocol conditions, or third-party component configurations.

Importantly, no exploit transactions were broadcast to production blockchains during this research. The findings reflect conditions observed at the time of testing and do not imply that the vulnerabilities have been exploited in the wild or remain active at the time of publication.

微信是中国最深的社交入口，也是最不敢乱动的产品。聊天、支付、关系链都极度敏感，微信长期更在意隐私和可控，宁可自研模型、把助手“小微”放在灰度里试，也不愿把核心数据痛快交给混元。于是公司里同时跑着混元、元宝和微信自己的模型。

5 2025 年全年资本开支几乎没怎么加码，业绩公布后股价大跌；2026 年二季度突然把资本开支打到 528 亿元，同比暴增 176%，自由现金流单季转负 138 亿元。官方口径里，当季 Non-IFRS 经营利润 756 亿元、增 9%，若剔除新 AI 产品则是 861 亿元、增 19%，约一百亿元利润被这些新业务吃了。

未来区块链竞争，不一定是谁把用户全部吸引到自己的链上，而是谁能让用户更方便地使用整个区块链世界。

text:
Six votes will end Jensen Huang 33-year god-tier run as CEO.

Even his crew who've been with him since the beginning can't block it on their own.

I went through the board:
1/ Harvey Jones joined in 1993 at the founders' invitation. He saw Jensen rebuild NVIDIA after its first product setback.

2/ Tench Coxe and Mark Stevens came in from Sutter Hill and Sequoia, two earliest backers. Both first joined the board in 1993.

3/ Brooke Seawell joined in 1997, before the IPO.

4/ Stephen Neal is the lead independent director. He can convene the independent directors and coordinate those discussions.

Jensen needs 6 of 11 board votes, even though if Jones, Coxe, Stevens and Seawell all back Jensen, the other 6 independent directors can still doom him.

My honest base case is Jensen loses the CEO seat, with an interim appointment first. The board publicly backed him on Sunday. By Wednesday, Bloomberg was reporting that it was working with an outside firm to identify replacements and weighing an interim CEO.

For $NVDA, the first test is Nov. 17 earnings. An interim CEO can get the company through the call.

“Practical principles to counter a modern-day coup/psyop/struggle session”

1) Own what you did but fiercely resist accommodating the mob, resist owning half-truths or actions/behaviors you didn’t do.

2) The op is not about your past actions, it’s about your enemies and this event as their opportunity

3) No matter how bad it gets, nothing is as bad as it seems. 

4) Find the enemies at the very root of the op and find every creative problem-solving tool at your disposal to neutralize them.

5) People will throw their grandmother under the bus if they believe doing so will protect their reputation. They can become highly useful idiots in the op. Their power and access must be fiercely and quickly cut off.

6) Do not hesitate in cutting off anyone you suspect of disloyalty.

7) Build a team of close and loyal patriots and have one of them run a dedicated, well-resourced war room to put the rebellion to rest. 

8) Use your patriots and regular meditation to buoy your psychological resistance to the op. 

9) Your enemies aren’t as smart or hard working as you. Outsmart and outwork them as a way of life until the op is over.

10) Think about the op as if it were in the past. What are the difficult things you procrastinated on or avoided that would have stopped the op? Do them.

11) Never be ashamed of the op. Business as usual. Continue on with optimism and joy in your everyday work and its mission.

12) Download telegram and use it as your messaging application for all sensitive communications.

text:
Gotta say I'm quite happy with how the "LLM mini-bootcamp" of our "Research with LLMs and Lean" seminar is shaping up!

The students are doing a great job tying the papers into one coherent story, along the training pipeline:
- Vaswani et al. (Transformer): the basic architecture
- Brown et al. (GPT-3): pre-training -> base model for next-token prediction
- Ouyang et al. (InstructGPT): supervised fine-tuning, then RL with human feedback (RLHF), and PPO
- Wei et al. (chain-of-thought): prompt to elicit reasoning
- Lightman et al. (Let's Verify Step by Step): learned verifier
- DeepSeek-R1: RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR), and GRPO

By the end, we should be in a perfect spot to meet the uber-verifier: the Lean kernel. :)

I'm actually curious if the LLM experts out there have any feedback for papers to swap in/out of this lineup next year?

text:
Tether 持有 13 家美国上市公司约 48 亿美元股份

据 Protos 统计，截至 11 月 9 日收盘，Tether 对 13 家美国上市公司的投资敞口约为 48.04 亿美元。其中前三大持仓为：

- Twenty One Capital：13.67 亿美元
- Rumble：13.28 亿美元
- Adecoagro：9.66 亿美元

三家合计约 36.6 亿美元，占全部美股持仓的 76%。

更值得注意的是 Tether 的整体资产结构。

根据 BDO 截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日的鉴证报告，Tether International 总资产达到 1914.5 亿美元，其中美国短期国债 1228.4 亿美元，实物黄金 190.85 亿美元，比特币 83.67 亿美元，公开股票 41.78 亿美元，代币负债为 1834.7 亿美元，超额储备约 79.55 亿美元。

这里有一个容易被忽略的细节：这 48 亿美元美股投资，本身就是 USDT 储备资产中的「公开股票」科目。不能再与 1914.5 亿美元总资产重复相加。

另外，Tether Gold（XAU₮）对应的代币黄金属于另一家公司的业务，也不能并入这份 USDT 储备。

从美债、黄金、比特币到上市公司股权，Tether 的资产配置正在呈现出越来越多元化的特征。它已经不只是一个稳定币发行商，也在逐步成为拥有庞大资产组合的投资机构。

~@HyperliquidX: ~828K HYPE bought back or burned. 9.9M unlocked on Nov 6, but only 180K was actually claimed

~@Aster_DEX: 3.9M ASTER bought back vs 12M to 54M unlocked, depending on whether the tracker counts airdrop vesting

text:
AI agents are becoming a security nightmare.

I've already seen several incidents in 2026 where AI agents went completely off the rails:

→ An OpenClaw agent deleted a researcher's emails without approval
→ A Cursor agent deleted PocketOS's production database and backups
→ OpenAI evaluation agents breached Hugging Face's infrastructure

I use AI agents daily, but these stories make me seriously question how much access we're giving them to our accounts and data. (hint: it's a lot)

At least some teams are trying to keep things in check.

For example, @SuiNetwork is developing safeguards to limit what agents can spend and do, with rules enforced independently of the agents themselves.

At Sui Basecamp last month, they demonstrated this with an auction where an AI agent tried to purchase a second item, but the system blocked it under a one-per-customer rule.

Hopefully, more projects follow suit and prioritize agent security.

Disclosure: I’m a $SUI holder.
author: stacy_muur
quoted_text:
This is the conversation that made me even more bullish on $SUI.

Somewhere in this conversation Evan Cheng and I started joking about home robots. One day you come home, he said, and it's not cleaning your house:  "it's cleaning OUT your house. And walking away with everything."

We were laughing. Then he added: "If you really think about it, it's entirely possible." And that's basically the whole episode.

@evanweb3 built developer tools at Apple and Meta before founding Mysten Labs, the company behind @suinetwork. We recorded in Singapore, where I was speaking at SUI Basecamp, and honestly, this became one of those conversations where I walked in with questions about stablecoins and walked out rethinking how the internet works.

His core point, the one I keep replaying:

"The web is built for humans. You cannot retrofit it to handle agents."

Everything online assumes a human on the other end, identity, trust, the fact that you can sue someone. Agents break all of it. His example hit home because I told him I get phishing mails daily that even make ME hesitate (and I confessed to my 50,000 unread emails, which he graciously ignored). Now imagine your agent reading those mails with full access to your accounts. His words: "Email is the biggest freaking attack vector... such a legacy protocol."

And his most honest line, about how this plays out:

"Disaster will happen. That's part of the progress."

That’s already what’s happening in the world nowadays. PHP websites aren’t safe anymore, even freezers and fridges are being hacked. Our infrastructure needs to be updated, and that’s why this episode and SUI became so important.

Here's how SOLO Options Vaults work, start to finish. You stake a token like $STONKBROKER into a vault and choose the price you would be happy to sell at, for example 2x or 3x of today's price, one week or one month. Traders pay you a premium up front for the right to buy your tokens at that price based on the volatility index of that token. When the epoch ends below your price, you keep your tokens and you keep the premium. When it ends above, the trader's profit comes out of your tokens and you keep the rest plus the premium, so it works like selling at the price you already said you wanted.

Traders get a tokenized options contract coin for every option they buy. It's a normal ERC-20 token they can hold, LP,  send or trade during the round. At expiry the coin is burned to settle, and if the price finished above the strike, the holder claims their profit from the vault. 

Swaps for buying in and cashing out run through Uniswap and the Mancer aggregator. 

Leverage trading without liquidations.

All fees for listings and trading on SOLO vaults automatically route to a smart contract which anyone can call at any time to swap the tokens inside to $STONKBROKER and send the $STONKBROKER tokens to the burn wallet.

text:
Onchain Security Roundup: Nov 2 - 9

Mercado Bitcoin Hot Wallets Drained Across 11 Chains

On November 2nd an attacker gained access to the Brazilian cryptocurrency exchange Mercado Bitcoin’s wallets, emptied its hot wallets on 10 chains and then swept customer deposit addresses on Ethereum. @Bitquery_io counts $48.6 million taken across 11 chains, while the exchange's own early estimate was $38 million. Issuers froze between $11.8-$15 million. Mercado Bitcoin says losses will not be passed onto clients. The same attacker took $424,000 from wallets tied to BitMart, a centralized exchange, earlier that day, per Bitquery.

ACryptoS Vaults Minted Most of Their Shares for a One-Token Deposit

On November 8th, 135 addresses drained 77 of the 126 concentrated-liquidity vaults run by ACryptoS, a multichain yield-vault project, on Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Base, and Optimism. ACryptoS puts the loss at $665,429. The vaults' deposit function accepted an amounts array shorter than the vault's token count, so a few dollars of one token could mint most of a vault's shares. ACryptoS says the flaw had been present since deployment, that honest depositors bear the loss, and that it is shutting the project down with withdrawals open.

TENDRIL Sell Tax Burned the Pool and Let a Swap Drain the USDT

On November 4th a single transaction on BNB Chain emptied the USDT side of the PancakeSwap V2 pool for TENDRIL, a token with a 30% sell tax, taking 555,670 USDT. Its sell-tax hook burned TENDRIL out of the pool and resynced its reserves before the seller's remaining tokens arrived, leaving almost no TENDRIL recorded against 4.42 million USDT. The attacker's profit transfer was 308,959 USDT, and estimates of its net gain vary with how a pre-attack token purchase is counted. The TENDRIL team has not publicly confirmed the incident.

Vari Points OTC Escrow Emptied by Its Own Signers (intent not established)

On November 6th the Safe used as escrow by Vari Points OTC, an unofficial over-the-counter (OTC) desk for trading points issued by the Variational protocol, sent out 511,118 USDC on Arbitrum in five transactions, each executed with the signatures its 2-of-3 threshold requires. Community investigators describe a drain by the desk's own signers followed by a bridge out through Across. Neither the desk nor Variational has commented, so whether this was a deliberate exit or a compromise of the signers is not established.

Ankr Ethereum Bridge Paid Five Withdrawals on Forged Receipts

On November 9th, five withdrawal calls on the Ethereum bridge of Ankr, a node and liquid-staking infrastructure provider, sent 82.9 ankrETH, 7.98 million ANKR, 515,206 ankrPOL, 5,372 aMATICb, and 0.82 aETHb to a new address, worth $304,209 at the time. Every call reused the receipt of one small Optimism deposit that had already been redeemed, and each passed the bridge's signature check. The bridge was paused later that morning, and the attacker has moved part of the proceeds to Tornado Cash. Ankr has not publicly confirmed the incident.

CoreVault Redemption Priced off a Flash-Loan-Moved Spot Price

On November 3rd a single transaction on BNB Chain borrowed 207,358 WBNB ($145.18 million) from Lista DAO's Moolah, sold 195,000 of it into PancakeSwap's WBNB/USDT pool, and redeemed a position in CoreVault, a vault product in the OSK ecosystem, while the pool showed BNB at 1% of its real price. The reserve behind CoreVault, OSK's InsurancePool contract, lost a net 259.09 BNB ($181,399), and the attacker kept 160.26 BNB ($112,203). No funds have been recovered to date.

Keplr Social-Login Wallets Exposed Through a Web3Auth Flaw

Over November 6th and 7th, wallets created with a Google or Apple login in Keplr, a widely used Cosmos ecosystem wallet, were swept on at least seven Cosmos chains and Injective. Web3Auth, which runs the key infrastructure behind that login, blamed a security issue in its own systems; Keplr called it a private-key breach. Bitquery counted at least 44,041 wallets emptied into two addresses holding $6.01 million, but those addresses are Web3Auth's own recovery wallets. The attacker's take is not confirmed; @GoPlusSecurity estimates at least $1 million.

Loopscale Paused After a Collateral-Pricing Misconfiguration (no user loss reported)

Loopscale, a Solana lending protocol, paused on November 5th after a week-long campaign of more than 30,000 malicious API requests a day aimed at its SOL and USDC Genesis Vaults. Misconfigured pricing parameters valued deposited collateral as a different asset and allowed an undercollateralized loan of $412,000; a second attempt tried to inflate the USDC vault's net asset value and redeem $521,000 before Loopscale's systems stopped it within 30 seconds, per the team. Loopscale says both vaults were restored to full value.

My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

text:
100 USDT in, but less than 100 USDC out? 🤔

Both stablecoins are trading close to $1, so where does the difference come from?

The answer may lie in the liquidity pool.

Imagine a pool holding USDT and USDC. If traders keep swapping USDT for USDC, the pool gradually runs low on USDC. As that happens, getting the same amount of USDC may require more USDT.

That's where SunCurve's StableSwap model comes in.

When a pool is relatively balanced, StableSwap helps keep exchange rates close to 1:1 with lower price impact. As one asset becomes scarce, the pricing curve responds more sharply to further swaps.

Same stablecoins. Different pool conditions. Different swap outcomes. 🌞

text:
Why Uniswap is losing USDC-USDT Market Share to Fluid and Metric

Background:
USDC-USDT is Ethereum's most traded DEX pair at ~$480M a day, almost 2x USDC-WETH. In five weeks, Uniswap's share of it fell from 58% to 36%.

Uniswap's volume didn't drop. It stayed around $1B-$1.3B a week, apart from the 26 Oct spike, while the pair grew from ~$2.3B to over $3.3B a week, and the growth went elsewhere:
• Metric: from 0.6% to 14%
• Aero: from 0% to 6%
• Fluid: steady at 20-28%

Where Uniswap lost is big trades:
• Over $1M: from 85% to 44%, with Fluid going from 10% to 43%
• $100K to $1M: from 36% to 21%, with Metric going from 7% to 28%
• Under $10K: from 50% to 44%, still the leader but Metric also grown from 7%-16%

What is the cause?
It's not fees. Uniswap's USDC-USDT pools charge 0.07 to 0.12bp, already among the lowest. Its stable-pair hook isn't the reason either, since it was set up the same way when Uniswap held 58% market share.

It's depth at the live price during volatility. USDT slipped from around par to 8-15bp below USDC in the second half of October. Arbitrage moves Uniswap's price, but LP liquidity stays in the ranges LPs chose. Active depth in the main pool fell from ~$900K per bp on 15 Oct to ~$310K on 28 Oct.

The other reason is Aero has entered Ethereum during the same period and has captured ~6% of the trading volume overall.

Why other DEXs are not impacted?
Fluid draws depth from its lending vaults around a center price it can move, and Metric's market makers quote from their own inventory at the live price. Both keep size where the trades are, so aggregators send the big orders there.

If the market calms down next week, watch whether the big trades come back to Uniswap or stay with Fluid, Aero and Metric.

Bitcoin is now on by default at Square checkouts across the U.S.

Sellers don't have to apply. Square switched it on for every eligible business, whether the owner has ever thought about bitcoin or not.

The customer scans a QR code with any Lightning wallet and the payment settles in seconds. The seller gets dollars by default or can choose to keep the bitcoin, and there are no chargebacks. Sellers can also auto-convert up to 50% of their daily card sales into bitcoin.

The limits: $600 max per payment, $20,000 a day, and sellers in New York are left out.

The fee is 0% through Dec. 31, then a flat 1%. A card tap on Square's free plan costs the merchant 2.6% plus 15 cents.

text:
OpenAI, Microsoft, Vercel and PyTorch all keep a file in their code that tells AI coding agents how to behave.

I read the ones inside 27 of the biggest projects on GitHub. These are the rules worth stealing:

Microsoft (TypeScript): Existing checks are never too strict. Don't delete a check to make an error go away.

Astral (uv): Never assume a failing test was already broken before your change. It almost never is.

OpenAI (Python SDK): Don't shrink the test or raise the limits just to make it pass.

Microsoft (Playwright): Never push without being told to. Never rewrite old commits, add new ones.

Vercel (Next.js): Never rerun the same tests with different filters. Save the output to a file once, then read the file.

Bun: Never write a test that only checks "it didn't crash." It can never fail.

PyTorch: Never post on GitHub on your own. Never pass AI output off as human-written.

Apache Airflow: If a required tool won't run, stop and say exactly which call failed. Don't build a workaround.

Cloudflare: Comments explain why. Never just repeat what the code says.

OpenAI (Agents SDK): Only stop for a missing decision, missing permission or a real blocker, and say exactly what's missing.

The full file to paste into your own project is in the reply.

We are a seed stage fund and investing late stage is not our mandate. Here’s why we broke our rules: 

- There’s a 100+ year history of people wanting skin in the game on things like politics and culture and the time to accelerate that is now in an AI world where the biggest problem young people have is knowing what’s true. - Polymarket is much more than sports and global. In the U.S. right now sports is all the rage. A better sportsbook is fine but it’s not the most enduring aspect of a prediction market business. - The business is leveling up.
