okx wallet:https://t.co/QNh5gwCiu3

A custom Launchpad built on Base chain and built on top of the Clanker protocol.

Its core is turning trading fees into "programmable value": at the time of launch, it writes the fee flows, what holders can receive, and what creators commit to do into on-chain rules, which then execute automatically according to those rules, without relying on the team's verbal promises.

It solves the problem that most meme coins today are "pure trading assets" rather than long-term assets. The model is very fixed: pump for a day at launch → slowly bleed downward for a month. Holders have no reason to hold long-term because the team only offers "promises"; creators also lack real design space and can only rely on hype.

Revvy attempts to replace "trusting the team" with "on-chain locked logic," giving fees a clear purpose, giving holders a real reason to hold, and giving creators more tools.

A token launch tool + fee management system. Main features include:

Programmable fees & Vault: Each token has its own independent treasury. Most trading fees go into the vault and are then automatically split according to ratios set at launch. The ratios cannot be changed after launch.

Programs: Optional holder reward rules, such as weekly lotteries, daily dividends to large holders or small holders, diamond-hand bonuses, no-sell rewards, etc. There are currently about 11 types.

Minds: Each token can be paired with an AI character that autonomously generates memes and short videos, posts them to its own X account, and uses a portion of the token's fees to pay for compute. This realizes "a token that feeds its own AI KOL."

The cost to launch is basically just gas, with no additional platform fee. Revvy itself takes about 10% from the fee rewards.

text:
【我用 Claude Code + 14份民调 + 过去开票数据来推演台北市长选举，谁会赢？】

我用 AI 把今年台北市长的14份民调全部扒下来算了一遍，首先我们得确认：这次台北市长谁会赢，民调回答不了。以往大家都看民调，但这次分歧巨大，变数巨大。10月中旬，信民协会的民调是沈伯洋领先17个百分点。同一个月，ETtoday的是蒋万安领先7个多百分点。同一座城市，同一个月，两家差了20多个百分点。

一份1000人左右的电话民调，统计学上的抽样误差大约是正负3个百分点。差到20几个点，已经不是运气问题，是统计学上说的「机构效应」：谁委托，怎么抽样，用市话、手机还是网络问卷，问题怎么问，都会把数字往某个方向推。

所以有人说把所有民调平均一下就准了。不一定。

大数定律能抵消的是随机误差，抵消不了系统误差。如果各家偏的方向不一样，平均是有用的。如果都偏同一个方向，平均只会让你更有把握地算错。

我把14份民调做了平滑平均，网络问卷权重减半。5月蒋万安在两人之间的占比还有六成五，10月之后掉到五成上下，现在是48.9%。

这个数字，在抽样误差之内。好吧，那民调靠不住，那就回去看真正投出来的票。

2022年，蒋万安57.6万票，陈时中43.5万票，黄珊珊34.2万票。这次没有第三个人，黄珊珊那34万票，就是这一届的胜负手。

我让Claude Code把这34万票重新分了一遍。投蒋、投沈各以10%为一档，剩下的不去投票，一共66种分法。

蒋万安赢54种，沈伯洋赢12种。

沈伯洋要翻盘，白票里得比蒋万安净多拿41个百分点。就算白票60%投沈、只有20%投蒋，蒋还领先4千票。

这是贝叶斯的思路：2022年的票是「先验」，今年的民调是「新证据」。先验说蒋稳，证据说五五波。两个对不上，说明先验的假设出了问题：蒋万安上一届的57.6万票，这次不会原封不动地回来。

现任做了四年，有人加分，也有人扣分。我又算了一层：蒋万安每掉5%的旧票，沈伯洋的翻盘门槛就降8到13个百分点。掉到一成五、掉的票有一半转去沈，66种分法就变成蒋36、沈30。

所以三种算法，三个答案：
旧票全守住，蒋稳。
蒋掉票，交给白票。
看民调，五五波。

最后提醒一个数字。2018年台北市长，柯文哲赢丁守中3254票，得票率只差0.23%，开票开了11个小时。那一年，没有任何一份民调的误差范围小于0.23%。

蓝绿分明的一座城，胜负却要交给「白」来定。

另外提醒一下：根据台湾《公职人员选举罢免法》第53条，投票日前10天起，任何人都不能发布、报导、散布、评论或引述选举民调。11月18日到28日投票结束前，这类内容都不能发。想知道结果，11月28日晚上一起看开票。

My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

text:
Could AI be MegaETH’s redemption?

@megaeth built a fast chain, but keeping users and capital around has been harder. By November 10, DeFi deposits had fallen from over $245M to around $12M, while $MEGA was more than 76% below its peak.

Now the team is committing $30M from its treasury to new products under @mega_holdings, starting with an AI inference marketplace planned for December. (Inference simply means running AI models to answer requests.)

But it will face tough competitors:

NEAR AI focuses on running models privately. Render connects users with GPU computing power, like other DePIN GPU networks such as Aethir, IONet, Akash, and more.

MEGA’s bet is different: suppliers compete in a shared market, with cryptography helping buyers trust, verify, and compare services. The goal is to make choosing a cheaper provider less of a gamble on quality.

There’s overlap, so MEGA still has to prove its edge. If developers keep paying for the service, it could create recurring spend on the chain.

Ultimately, though, how this translates into sustained demand for MEGA still needs a clearer answer.

a16z 这篇《Welcome to the B2A Economy》含金量挺高，把 Agent 经济从概念讲到了真实的流量、分发和商业模式。

挑几个我觉得很值得讨论的观点：

1. 互联网的客户正在发生变化

过去企业花了几十年阻止 Bot 访问，现在却可能要主动争取 Agent。因为它们正开始替用户搜索、比较产品，甚至决定购买什么服务。

2. Agent 已经开始影响真实交易

Shopify 今年 Q1 来自 AI 的流量同比增长 8 倍，相关订单增长近 13 倍。虽然目前传统搜索仍占主导，但新的流量入口已经出现了。

3. 产品分发可能要重新洗牌

过去大家做 SEO，现在又开始研究 GEO。未来随着插件、MCP 和连接器普及，Agent 可以直接调用产品、完成任务，甚至决定订阅哪项服务。

产品能否被 Agent 发现、理解和使用，可能会越来越重要。

4. Coding Agent 已经提前展示了这种变化

GitHub 超过 40% 的 PR 已经由 Agent 起草，Vercel 的 Agent 触发部署一年增长了 28 倍。

Agent 开始影响数据库、云服务等基础设施的选择，新的商业机会也在这些环节出现。

而且 B2A 可能会成为下一轮互联网分发竞争的重要方向。

以前产品努力争夺人的注意力，以后还得考虑怎么让 Agent 愿意选择和使用自己。

quoted_text:
1confirmation has invested in every Polymarket round ever and we keep doubling down.

We are a seed stage fund and investing late stage is not our mandate. Here’s why we broke our rules: 

- There’s a 100+ year history of people wanting skin in the game on things like politics and culture and the time to accelerate that is now in an AI world where the biggest problem young people have is knowing what’s true. Everyone is becoming a trader/investor, and a product that converts that energy into better information and more truth is truly unique.

- Polymarket is much more than sports and global. In the U.S. right now sports is all the rage. A better sportsbook is fine but it’s not the most enduring aspect of a prediction market business. Better information and more truth on politics, geopolitics and culture is the why and most young people you talk to IRL know that Polymarket is in a class of its own on this front even though that discourse here can get lost.

- The business is leveling up. I’ve seen a lot over the past 6 years and it’s far from perfect but the exec team in place now is exceptional, the US product is best in class and the revenue is making new highs. I have not loved the messaging about a token at times bc it’s always best to underpromise and overdeliver by quietly delivering value to users. But the idea that a token is dead is foolish.

- Shayne has a will to win like none other and is the most direct and transparent person I know. He’s just himself and authenticity wins.

Posting here for transparency. Talk soon.

这位和一姐 @heyibinance 对线的小兄弟，似乎是大学毕业没几年，然后就进了OKX。

看了一下他的发言水平和身份保护意识，怎么说呢，确实是有点学生思维了。

这个行业，找水军攻击友商，早已成了明牌。

事实上，这不光是币圈的明牌，可以说是任何行业的明牌。

我在地产干过品宣，这一套见怪不怪。另外，我也接触过互联网和新能源汽车的公关，这种水军攻讦，更是家常便饭。 

要不然，你以为市面上哪来那么多华为黑、理想黑、阿里黑、小米黑？

这固然有企业自身的原因，但相当一部分也都是友商的杰作。

实话实说，我认为这都无所谓。真金自不怕火炼。

甚至，如果你黑的有理有据，一定程度上还能起到民间监管的作用，倒逼被黑的一方，提升服务和产品品质。

但请注意，前提是你要黑的有理有据，而非单纯人身攻击。

另外，再怎么说，这种行为也不堪登大雅之堂，一般都是外包。

内部员工自己下场攻击友商，着实少见。

建议效仿一下贾潇一，你看人家这个名字起的就很好，缩写是XY。

XY，代表着未知，代表着神秘，代表着厚厚的令人看不见的马甲。

甚至，让我想起了东野圭吾的《嫌疑人X的现献身》，

看见没？想要好好献身，你要先当X。这是对你自己的保护，也是对你背后组织的掩护。

这才有一点职业水军该有的样子。

当然，这都是低阶打法，更高阶的打法是什么呢？

摒弃学生思维，专注产品服务，从你做起，从我做起。

愿天下无水军。

WeirdML v2 is now out! The update includes  a bunch of new tasks (now 19 tasks total, up from 6), and results from all the latest models. We now also track api costs and other metadata which give more insight into the different models. The new results are shown in these two figures. The first one shows an overview of the overall results as well as the results on individual tasks, in addition to various metadata.  

The second figure shows cost vs performance and shows a clear scaling with better results for higher costs. We also have a very varied pareto frontier with 11 models from 6 different companies having the best accuracy for a given cost for at least some of the cost range. Grok 3, Claude Opus 4 and GPT 4.5 are the ones that underperform for their costs, while Gemini pro and o3 pro have the best results at the highest costs. Qwen3 30B3A, grok 3 mini and deepseek R1 also each represent a good chunk of the pareto frontier.

quoted_text:
今天去逛了百度世界大会 2026，记一些零零散散的 take

01. AI 正在变得越来越接地气，甚至有点过于接地气了

打台球、搓麻将、养猫养宠物、健身撸铁、出行……展区里大量产品都在解决特别具体的生活问题

02. 阻碍 AI 走入生活的是本体

现场那个麻将机器人特别有意思，还会说四川话。结果要出牌的时候，把好几张牌给碰倒了

阻碍 AI 真正走进物理世界的已经不完全是智能水平的问题，而是机器人本体、精细操作以及对现实环境的适应能力

03. 垂直场景的后训练越来越重要

现场不少应用都是基于文心 5.5 底座，针对不同场景进行后训练

未来很多 AI 产品可能不需要自己拥有多么牛逼的基础模型。基础模型负责提供通用能力，场景数据、后训练、工作流以及产品设计负责把能力变成具体价值

但问题也来了，如果大家都能拿到足够好的底座，针对某个场景训练出来的能力，到底能形成多深的护城河？还是说过不了多久，就会被更强的通用模型直接覆盖？

04. 百度网盘做 Personal Agent

感觉是蹭热点没招了的办法。我现在唯一用百度网盘的场景就是找各种未引进影视的资源，这它能给我 personal 什么 agent

05. 搜索和百科开始把内容直接变成交互界面

过去搜索引擎给你十个链接，后来 AI 给你一段总结，现在可以根据问题直接生成一个可交互的 GUI 页面。比 google 那种把搜索结果改写成 AI 回答更有意思

不是所有信息都适合用文字呈现。理解一个物理现象、比较几个方案、学习某个概念，很多时候交互比阅读有效得多

不过现场看到的页面，AI 味儿还是比较重。那种熟悉的卡片、配色、排版，一眼就知道是 AI 生成的。提示词工程或许能改善一些，但我感觉更深层的问题还是设计能力

06. 但我也在怀疑，我们真的需要这么多独立的 AI 产品吗？

比如百度的伐谋，面向复杂产业决策和分析。我能理解专业场景需要专门的模型、算法和业务知识，但有多少任务真的需要一个独立产品来完成？又有多少只是通用 Agent 加几个专业 Skill 就能解决？

07. 数字人直播的价格，真的便宜到有点夸张了。

现场了解到的套餐价格，大概每月 1000～2500 元，就可以实现全天候直播

当一个人每天直播 24 小时的成本已经这么低，直播本身还有什么稀缺性？技术显然在快速压低内容生产和分发成本，但注意力并没有因此变多

大家都能 24 小时开播，不代表大家都能 24 小时卖货

08. 今天看到一个肩颈放松体验区，我兴冲冲地过去，以为终于能体验机器人按摩了，结果居然是真人按摩

9. 现在 AI 行业最需要的是认真寻找下游

过去几年整个行业有点过于习惯站在供给侧思考问题。今天逛完最大的感受，就是 AI 正在拼命寻找能消化这些能力的真实场景

10. 李彦宏今天讲的「以任务为中心，而不是以岗位为中心」，我觉得是整个大会最值得琢磨的观点之一

工业时代的组织是一个萝卜一个坑，AI 时代的组织可能是一张动态的任务网络。这个方向我基本认同，一个人的能力已经不应该被某个固定岗位完全定义

但真的把组织改成任务网络之后，管理可能反而会变得更复杂。岗位不仅是分工方式，也是一套责任制度。拆掉岗位边界很容易成为一句漂亮口号，重新设计责任和利益分配才是难题

11. 未来只有 Builder 和 Seller 两类岗位？我觉得这个分类很有启发，但也有点过度简化了。

创造东西的人，以及负责沟通、连接和建立信任的人。听起来确实能概括很多工作

但我觉得中间还少了一件非常重要的事，判断。决定什么东西值得创造，什么机会应该放弃，什么时候应该承担风险，以及出了问题由谁负责

而且 Builder 和 Seller 的边界，恐怕也会越来越模糊。一个不会卖自己产品的 Builder，未来未必还有生存空间

12. 我对「围绕 AI 重新设计组织」这件事很认同，但也怀疑大多数公司到底有没有这个决心

过去你要等用户意识到自己需要一款工具，再去搜索、比较。

现在做互联网产品的公司都需要想清楚这个问题：用户把任务交给 Agent 之后，Agent 做到哪一步会选你的产品？

Yet another Jenson affair hit the tape after it seemed like the Chinese spy affair allegations were too sus/had no staying power. For example, did you know that there is no contract between TSMC and NVDA? lmao

That said, markets are pricing Jenson to leave/ be ousted at 80% - I think the odds are closer to that Jenson stays. I cannot imagine the board/the company trying to oust Jenson - that's literally cutting off its own balls.

Oh wait. Sorry the dems won - i need to be more politically correct in my notes now.

Well, that's cutting off its own hands!

IF however, i am right - this would probably bring a strong relief rally into NVDA and also consequently NDX. In the event that Jenson is ousted - we might also see a relief rally for NVDA - this is because next year's sales are already pretty much locked in and NVDA's valuation is super compelling - you will get value buyers who will swoop in. However, i would trim on such a rally. Once a founder led company is ousted and a professional manager steps in - they will never have the same energy and intensity to compete.

On Neoclouds - all eyes are on NBIS earnings pre market. I would be looking for the company's guidance on next year's ARR as well as revenue and other contract metrics like how much are they able to sell compute for as well as the terms. Things like Token factory as well as the PLTR partnership would be very consequential too  - though it is NOT being priced by the market at this point in time.

On memory, both MU and SNDK made strong gains in yesterday's market. The resolution of NVDA will probably decide the next leg for the memory tickers. 

For crypto, PA continues to be uninspiring. Sentiment is also down alongside alts. The DCB was extremely weak vs what played out in tradfi and semis. At this point, i would heavily lean cautious and reduce my activity further.

Good luck!

My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

黄仁勋的事件没想到持续在发酵，新的婚外情居然也“浮出水面”，在我的视角下，黄教主有点典型的“匹夫无罪怀璧其罪”

我倒不是想为他的婚外情洗什么，但是我觉得这个问题在“自由美利坚”算不上什么罪大恶极的问题，尤其是面对一百多种性别，以及萝莉岛这些事件，老黄的事确实有些微不足道

而且，最关键的是美国国会一直在试图把老黄的婚外情包装成“间谍”事件，明显是想要让事件的性质升级，

况且，作为黄仁勋，作为英伟达这种AI超级企业，我不相信美国政府没有人盯着他，在国家机器以及情报机构面前，老黄这些事情其实对于美国政府官员不算是什么秘密，但是为何要在此时提起，并且揪住不放？

此前有报道，特朗普早就在2025年10月就收到关于黄仁勋婚外情的简报，但是一直没有提起，一直在被特朗普当做政治工具。

原本我以为是老黄自爆以退为进，但是看到后续英伟达公司，美国国会的持续施压，我发现这件事可能并非是老黄的计谋，反而老黄是在被政治趋势裹挟者走——要么选择站队成为“用餐者”，要么成为桌上的一道菜

至于针对老黄的理由，目前说法很多，黄皮，树大招风，公司内部争权夺利，公司外部国家党派斗争被迫站队，资本掠夺，其实这些问题现在怎么解释都对

不可否认的是，老黄的事件让英伟达股价 承压，让美股AI指数同样承压，估值被“人为”消化，但是却并未对行业造成什么伤害

难道真的是上演一次“一鲸落，万物生”的历史一幕吗？老黄与英伟达被制裁，受益者其实颇多，雪崩之下没有一片雪花是无辜的，同样，如果老黄因此在台前谢幕，作为那些既得利益者，谁都不是无辜的，

当“桃色”新闻成为攻击方式，其实也意味着“自由的美利坚”失去了原本的“自由”！

text:
2.8% of the $mihao supply is completely hidden, and the dev controls 1/3 of it.

it’s not in the holder list.

here’s how it works:

someone launches a coin paired to $mihao instead of sol
you buy it with sol. the route is sol → mihao → that coin
the mihao you just bought stays in that coin’s pool
you hold the small coin. when you sell it, you get the mihao back
most holder lists show that pool as “lp”, or don’t show it at all

so i went through every mihao holder (31,611 accounts) and every pool paired to it:

> 39 paired coins hold 26.4m mihao = 2.8% of the supply
> the dev’s share of it: 8.5m, a third of all of it
> 3.8m of that comes from one coin where he holds 28.7% of the supply
> one is 2 levels deep: $taodn is paired to $pi, $pi is paired to $mihao. he holds 47% of $taodn
> he bought these coins with his creator fees: ~320 sol across 19 coins, and never sold one

so his real position looks like this:

> 30m visible
> 54m locked
> 8.5m hidden
= 9.8% of the supply. the holder tab shows him at 3.2%

and it’s not just him:

his circle (the 22 wallets he sent tokens to + his @bubblemaps cluster) hides another 11.1m

9 wallets hold almost no mihao directly, but up to 0.32m through paired coins. you can’t see them at all

author: matthew_d_green
quoted_text:
Our teams put Gemini 4 Carbon to work on a major security challenge: mathematically proving the code underlying the Signal protocol.

Using AlphaProof Code, @GoogleDeepMind researchers guided agents to verify the protocol down to compiled device code, closing the gap where real bugs hide. The result:

- Gemini 4 Carbon generated over 6M lines of machine-checked Lean proofs
- years of expert manual verification compressed to just weeks
~1% of the codebase required human review (Lean automatically checked the rest)

This is helping unlock scalable formal verification for building secure software, laying the groundwork to fundamentally shift the advantage to defenders. We’re open sourcing the results for the security community.

text:
特朗普：我太天真了，甚至连总统薪水都不要，金额高达数百万美元。🐶

特朗普最新发文，再次将民主党称为美国历史上最腐败、最反美的一批政治领导人，指责对方不断炒作蓝州腐败问题，试图掩盖明尼苏达州、加利福尼亚州等地的腐败丑闻。

随后，他开始强调自己的「牺牲」：自己是唯一一位不领取总统薪水的美国总统，甚至因此放弃了数百万美元。

不过，相比总统薪水，特朗普在白宫之外的财富增长或许更值得关注。

据《福布斯》估算，2024 年特朗普赢得大选时，其个人净资产约为 43 亿美元；到 2026 年 9 月，这一数字已经达到 70 亿美元。

短短不到两年，个人净资产增加约 27 亿美元，涨幅超过 60%。

更值得注意的是，这轮财富增长并非主要来自传统股票投资，而是与其加密货币业务密切相关。

根据特朗普 2025 年财务披露，其从加密货币、数字代币及相关合作中获得超过 14 亿美元收入。World Liberty Financial、特朗普个人迷因币以及稳定币业务，均成为其商业版图的重要组成部分。

此外，海外房地产交易、品牌授权、商品销售及诉讼和解等，也为其带来了可观收入。

当然，财富估值并非只涨不跌。特朗普净资产在 2026 年也经历了回落，但即便如此，其财富规模仍远高于当选总统前。

总统年薪可以不领，但围绕总统身份建立起来的商业帝国，显然是另一回事。

放弃数百万美元的总统薪水，换来数十亿美元的财富增长？这笔账，特朗普恐怕比谁都清楚。

we built https://t.co/CaxKeqXnav and why it goes deeper than just a hackathon project??

our core idea:

tokenized-stock lending markets have very conservative LTVs, mostly because traditional markets trade 24/5 while on-chain lending markets operate 24/7.

this creates a problem over the weekend. With traditional markets closed, there is limited liquidity to exit tokenized stock positions, while on-chain liquidations can still happen.

with chainlink 24/7 now providing weekend pricing from perp venues, weekend liquidations become possible. but the bigger problem is where to sell that collateral.

liquidity on DEXs is thin, and liquidation bots dumping collateral into these markets will simply push the AMM curve against them. the usual flash-loan liquidation model doesn't work the same way here.

so we have got two problems:
- there isn't enough liquidity on DEXs to absorb large amounts of tokenized stock collateral without significant price impact.
- we need a way to hold the liquidated collateral without taking on the underlying price risk while waiting for liquidity to return.

solving both problems will help us potentially solve the conservative LTV problem, and help on-chain economy create more credit from lending markets.

LlamaRisk also highlights perps as the off-hours hedge venue and sizes stock exposure against perp open interest and issuer redemption limits, with liquidity being a binding constraint.

building on top of it, we built https://t.co/CaxKeqXnav

we buy liquidated collateral from lending markets and hedge it on perps. This allows us to hold the collateral without taking on the underlying price risk, while managing the costs and risks associated with the hedge.

then, when liquidity comes back during weekdays, we slowly unwind the positions in multiple chunks across DEXs, while simultaneously buying back the equivalent short position on perps.

using uniswap v4 and predefined risk parameters, we can either unwind positions against AMM liquidity or trade directly with users from our vaults.

this whole solution builds an liquidation exit route for tokenized-stock lending markets, giving risk teams a way to size markets around a more reliable exit and potentially increase LTVs, allowing more credit to be created on-chain.

Paying peak rates all month is the most expensive possible way to survive a spike that lasts an hour.

Thats a huge savings!

text:
For me, having a baby was the beginning of the end of my marriage. My ex and I had set things up to be fairly trad. He made the money, and I planned to stay home with the children. I didn't, however, realize that his vision of that was actual-zero childcare, to the best of his ability. He spent most weekends watching TV in another room with the door closed, while I ran around to parks and playgrounds, etc. Eventually we had no shared life. 

@jmrphy for @unherd recommends this. I am not so sure. 

Nor am I totally unsure. I was a stay-at-home-mom, but also had fairly feminist expectations, and I thought that my ex *should* have walked in the door from work and started helping me make toddler-dinner. After all, we'd both worked all day, and his work was a lot more fun. More than that, I wanted someone to share the experience with ... him. 

We also did have other, deeper problems. But mainly what happened is that I started resenting him and stopped caring about his wants and needs in the relationship (because he was a lazy-ass bum sitting there waiting for his adult-dinner, too). And I devoted my considerable powers to trying to force him to participate, which he did, but so resentfully in his own part that it just wasn't worth it. eventually I started arranging things to discourage his participation. I can think of summer mornings where I was scuttling around trying to get me and the kids out of the house before he woke up.... 

 Also I tend to forget that for the first few years, I tried to treat him like the luxury-king-of-finance that he wanted to be, and *tried* to do it all myself without inconveniencing him, and I just wasn't able to pull that off, logistically or emotionally. 

I think we were probably just doomed for other reasons, but, with great hindsight, my resentment and feminism didn't help us. And his view of what a father was supposed to do was pretty impoverished. It's possible that if both of us had moved a few clicks towards the other's position, we could have made it. Or if we'd even just done the things we were already doing without the resentment, perhaps we could have grown together into the job.

DeFi is evolving beyond individual protocols. Its next phase will depend increasingly on how different layers of financial infrastructure connect to make capital deployment, liquidity and execution more efficient.

That is what makes the AlphaPrimer × Orderly Network partnership worth watching.

Both projects address distinct but complementary parts of the DeFi ecosystem.

AlphaPrimer focuses on automated capital allocation. Through DeFi Autopilot, users can deploy USDC across established lending markets on Arbitrum, including Aave V3, Compound V3 and Fluid. The system monitors lending rates and reallocates capital as yield opportunities change, reducing the need for users to manage each allocation manually.

Orderly Network is focused on decentralized trading infrastructure. Its unified orderbook and omnichain liquidity layer are designed to give different trading platforms access to shared liquidity, reducing the need for each platform to build and maintain its own trading infrastructure independently.

The significance of this collaboration goes beyond bringing two project names together.

A more connected DeFi ecosystem requires infrastructure that can support different financial activities without leaving every application operating in isolation. Capital allocation and trading liquidity are separate functions, but both are important to the development of more accessible and efficient onchain financial markets.

AlphaPrimer approaches this through automated capital management, while Orderly Network contributes to the trading and liquidity infrastructure layer.

The opportunity lies in how these different capabilities can complement one another and what practical improvements future collaboration may deliver.

Ultimately, the value of a Web3 partnership should be measured not only by the announcement, but by the products, integrations and meaningful utility that follow.

We look forward to seeing what AlphaPrimer and @OrderlyNetwork build together.

Follow the developments: https://t.co/jsqAxfSpdJ

text:
Everyone saw the NYSE news this week. Fewer people noticed what's being built under it on @avax.

There are three pieces, and they fit together better than most people realize.

1. Wall Street

The New York Stock Exchange (@NYSE) is planning a 24/7 market for tokenized stocks, and Avalanche says it will be the ledger behind the clearing firm for it. It still needs regulators to approve it.

It fits where Avalanche has been heading. In June it started calling itself "technology built for business", moved to https://t.co/F8JGILqotV, and pointed itself at big companies. The NYSE is about as big as they come.

But that side moves slowly, and it's built for banks and funds. Not for you and me.

2. Pharaoh

@PharaohExchange is the main exchange on Avalanche. Roughly three out of every four dollars traded on Avalanche's exchanges go through it.

Pharaoh has said tokenized US stocks are coming to its exchange, with trading around the clock. Avalanche called them "permissionless". In simple terms, they should behave like normal tokens. You can hold them in your wallet, send them, and trade them against other coins. That matters, because a stock token that can't move can't be used for much.

Pharaoh also decides how deep those markets get. People who lock its token vote on which pools get rewards, and projects can pay to attract those votes. That's how a brand new stock pool can fill up with enough money to trade smoothly.

3. Arena

@TheArenaApp is the social app on Avalanche. People post, follow each other, chat and launch coins there.

In September Arena said it's building a launchpad with Pharaoh for exactly this:

- launch a coin paired with a stock token instead of AVAX
- add a 1 to 5% tax on trades, paid out to holders in the token it's paired with
- when a coin finishes its curve, it moves to Pharaoh to keep trading

Look at the middle one again. If a coin is paired with a stock token, its holders get paid in that stock. You hold a meme and slowly collect a piece of a real company. That's a very different reason to hold a coin.

How they feed each other

Wall Street brings the headline and the trust. Pharaoh brings the market. Arena brings the people and the launches.

Every coin that graduates on Arena becomes a new pool on Pharaoh. Every trade in that pool pays fees to Pharaoh's voters. That brings in more rewards, the stock pools get deeper, and the next launch has a better market to land in.

Why it matters for Avalanche

It's been a quiet few months onchain. The NYSE news is big, but it's slow and regular people can't touch it. A launchpad where memecoins are priced in stocks is the opposite. It's fast, it's open, and people can use it every day. It's the piece that gives everyday traders a reason to come back to the chain.

Worth knowing before it goes live

- None of this is live yet. Pharaoh hasn't said who issues the stock tokens or when they arrive, and Arena's launchpad is waiting on them.
- Tokenized stocks usually aren't open to everyone. People in the US are often blocked, so check first.
- On weekends the stock market is closed, so the token's price is a guess until Monday.
- Most memecoins still go to zero. Pairing one with a stock doesn't change that.

When the stocks go live on Pharaoh, this is the launch I'll be watching.

text:
在加密一级市场流动性收紧的当下，头部加密 VC 的触角已经明显伸向了 AI 与机器人赛道。

老牌加密基金 Pantera Capital 的合伙人 @cosmo_jiang  和投资人 Cody Poh  @0xhopydoc  最近专门飞了一趟深圳，实地调研了中国机器人产业链（从人形机器人整机厂、模型团队到灵巧手与数据采集设备商），并发布了一篇长文总结。

他们的核心发现很直接：

硬件中国领先，软件美国领先，而在中间的数据环节，质量远比数量重要。

具体拆解下来，有三个层面的观察值得一看。

1. 硬件端：中国供应链是绝对护城河

深圳的制造生态让研发迭代快到极致。
早上有新想法，中午供应商就能把定制零件送到办公室。像无极科技（Wuji Tech）等本土厂商做的灵巧手，在集成度和抗碰撞性上甚至超过他们在美国见过的同类产品，且暗中供货给不少美国大厂。

但代价是极度内卷，“吃苦”文化下企业普遍牺牲利润换份额，硬件层本身很难赚到超额利润。

2. 数据端：采集不是壁垒，“数据智能”才是

国内有不少地方政府补贴推动的“数据农场”，工人们戴着头显重复做同样动作，产出海量训练视频。

但他们认为，高度同质化的重复数据对模型能力提升有限。真正的机会不在于谁采得最多，而在于谁能做高质量的数据清洗、标注与评估，成为前沿实验室信任的研究伙伴（类似机器人领域的 Scale AI）。

3. 软件端：中国落后 1-2 年，且很难靠“蒸馏”追平

调研中不少高管和一线员工坦承，软件和具身智能算法比海外落后 1-2 年，目前大多依赖美国模型（OpenAI、Nvidia、Physical Intelligence 等）做微调，很少自研基座模型。

而且不同于大语言模型，机器人模型需要真实的物理交互数据和硬件验证，很难单纯靠低成本“蒸馏”快速复刻。

而这篇报告里更有意思的，是他们站在 VC 角度，对中美资本生态的洞察：

-资本耐心决定技术路线：
中国创投普遍要求项目 2-3 年内看到营收甚至推动上市，加上知识产权保护相对薄弱，倒逼创业者优先做硬件销售和数据外包这类“快钱”生意，不敢重仓长周期的底层软件研发。

-商业驱动力完全不同：
国内劳动力成本低，目前人形机器人更多停留在展厅接待或表演（跳舞、打功夫）；
而美国高昂的人工成本和蓝领缺口，让工业与物流自动化有了实打实的商业订单驱动。

text:
Nate Silver vs. Kalshi’s CEO is the best fight of the midterms.

Tarek says the markets called it. Nate says “give me a break.”

Then a quant pulled 488 races and ran the numbers. Kalshi wins. 👇

tl;dr:

– Tarek: the people called the midterms on Kalshi

– Nate: polls and models led, markets just followed

– 488 US races since 2024: Kalshi had ~12% less forecasting error than the models

– head-to-head with Silver Bulletin on the 2024 presidential race: Kalshi wins, 0.0312 to 0.0348

– Kalshi’s own 2026 study: lowest Brier score of any forecast on Election Day, Silver Bulletin included

– Nate has been a Polymarket advisor since 2024

Lesson learned: markets don’t beat the models. They eat them.

Full details:

–- The fight timline

The night after the election, Tarek posted a victory lap: “the power to decide what America sees changed hands.”

Nate quote-tweeted it. His point: the polls and models gave the direction, and the better models were more confident and got there faster than the markets.

Then he went further on Silver Bulletin, saying markets are “low-key stealing valor from the models.”

–- The scoreboard

Quant Chad pulled 488 US races from 2024 to now and scored Kalshi’s pre-election odds against Silver Bulletin, FiveThirtyEight and JHK.

Average Brier score (lower is better):

Kalshi: 0.0282

Models: 0.0320

That’s roughly 12% less forecasting error for Kalshi.

Against Nate directly, on the 2024 presidential race across 50 states: Kalshi 0.0312, Silver Bulletin 0.0348.

Kalshi’s own 2026 study points the same way. At 9 a.m. on Election Day, Kalshi had the lowest Brier score of every forecast: Kalshi 0.0139, Silver Bulletin Deluxe 0.0141.

Kalshi also says House control passed 99% at 8:10 p.m. ET and Senate control at 9 p.m., hours ahead of the networks.

And Kalshi’s data is public. Nate’s 2026 race forecasts are paywalled, so the 488-race comparison had to use JHK for 2026.

–- Where Nate has a point

The models won 3 of the 5 categories in that data: 2024 Senate, 2024 House and 2026 Senate.

And a NYT analysis found markets did no better than the forecasts for most of the race.

– Worth knowing

Nate is a Polymarket advisor. Kalshi is now offering $1M to researchers to study its election data.

My read:

Both are right, and that’s the point.

The models gave the direction. The markets took the models, the polls, the insiders and the money, and priced all of it at once. That’s why the market comes out ahead across 488 races.

Nate isn’t wrong -- He’s an input.

text:
春江水暖鸭先知

这个月才过去 12 天，我发现自己已经和超过 30 家 Web3 公司的从业者进行了或浅或深的交流。

我有一个越来越强烈的感受：新一轮 Web3 大牛市，可能已经在路上了。

寒冷中，敏感的人反而更容易感受到最初的温度。

这种温度，首先来自新玩家的行动。

比如 Stripe Crypto、PhotonPay、Width、空中云汇。这些公司，我都接触过一些内部从业者。

最近，我注意到它们开始增加行业曝光，开设或活跃官方 Twitter 账号，线下也能频繁看到不同团队的成员出现在各种行业活动中。

更值得关注的是，其中一些公司正在增加招聘、市场活动，或者投入新的业务方向。

这些公司并不是上一轮周期里最典型的 Crypto 原生玩家。它们背后有支付、金融科技和跨境业务的积累。它们开始加大对 Web3 的投入，本身就是一个值得观察的信号。

不过，这些还都是愿意出现在公众视野中的玩家。

还有一批公司，相对低调，却也在向 Web3 行业输入资金和人才。

比如我了解到，至少有 3 家中国内地的支付公司已经在香港取得相关牌照，正在布局虚拟资产和稳定币业务。

它们都比较低调，相关动作并没有引起太多媒体关注。比如连连支付在香港的子公司DFX，你可能都没听过，但是它已经拿到VATP牌照，理论上已经可以做虚拟资产和稳定币的业务了。

相比公开宣传，它们似乎更愿意先把团队、牌照和业务准备好。

有些变化还没有出现在媒体头条上，但企业已经开始行动。

当然，这只是我最近接触到的一部分行业参与者，不一定能代表整个市场。

但我越来越强烈地感受到，新一轮周期的参与者正在发生变化。

新的资金、新的庄家、新的企业、新的人才……在涌入，只不过，他们中的很多人，都是大家不熟悉的面孔。

很多事情还没有发生在价格上，也还没有发生在媒体新闻里，但已经发生在人和资金的行动中。

春江水暖鸭先知。

我不知道新一轮牛市什么时候真正到来，但我确实已经感受到了它释放出的一点点温度。

Vlad Tenev (@vladtenev) is the co-founder and CEO of Robinhood.

In January 2021, in the middle of the meme stock frenzy, Robinhood's deposit requirement went from under $100 million to "something like $3 billion" almost overnight. The total capital the company had ever raised was about $700 million.

His first call was to @mickymalka:

"He's like, 'How much do you need?' I said, 'I don't know, 250 million, 500 million. I'm not sure.' He's like, 'I've got it.'"

Back in March 2020, the two of them had put a term sheet in place so the money could be "wired in your account same day." Once Micky was in, everyone else followed: "We probably had $10 billion of demand at the first term."

"It was a consequence of too much success, which is quite rare."

Vlad came to America from Bulgaria at 5, not knowing a word of English. His grandparents stored their wealth in copper cookware during hyperinflation. His dad told him he'd give him his SAT score in dollars to invest. He went on to study math under Terence Tao, then took a leave from his $18,000-a-year math PhD to take a shot at starting his own company.

This was an awesome conversation:

text:
What if the next bottleneck in AI isn't the model, or even the data, but the experiences we give it?

As models become more capable, the challenge increasingly becomes how we evaluate them, what they learn from, and how we turn that into reliable improvements.

Collecting more agent trajectories is useful, but more data doesn't necessarily mean more learning. There's a real opportunity in creating environments where agents face meaningful challenges, make decisions, and experience measurable consequences.

The next frontier may not simply be better ways to store and evaluate AI data, but better ways to generate the experiences worth learning from in the first place.

Artificial Analysis 这张对比图挺能说明问题的。在现在的 Claude 阵容里，直接升一档模型，有时比把低一档模型的推理强度拉满还划算。

比如 Opus 5.5 开 xhigh 拿到 57 分，超过 Sonnet 5.5 开 max 的 55 分，每个任务的成本反而低了 40%，耗时也差不多减半。

Fable 5.2 更夸张。high 档就能超过 Opus 5.5 的 max，得分高 3 分，成本低约 10%，耗时减少 34%；甚至 Fable 5.2 的 low 也能超过 Opus 5.5 的 high。

不过在最便宜的 Haiku 档，这个规律就不成立了。而且这是综合 Benchmark 的结果，具体任务还得单独验证。

感觉以后给 Agent 配模型，真得重新算算账了。模型档位、推理强度、成本和延迟放在一起比较，可能会发现不少意外的最优组合。

text:
Imagine giving an AI agent access to your crypto without handing over the whole wallet.

That's what one builder is testing on $CKB. It's called QuotaCell.

The idea is simple. You set a spending budget from a shared wallet, and teammates or software agents can make payments within those rules.

The clever part is who enforces the limit. Not just the app. The $CKB network itself checks the rules, even when a payment is built outside the app.

And if you change your mind, you can revoke access. In testing, the owner switched off a helper's spending power. The next payment attempt was rejected.

Then the owner closed the shared wallet and recovered the spendable test funds. No signature from the helper needed.

Here's the honest catch. This is one developer testing on a private local setup with test tokens. It's not on public testnet and hasn't been audited. Closing it also leaves about 600 CKB locked up for now.

So it's early, not a finished wallet you should trust with real money. But as AI agents start handling payments, enforceable spending limits could matter a lot.

An agent gets a budget instead of unrestricted access. That's the kind of practical building I like seeing on $CKB.

Nadine Chakar @nchakar has built an institutional digital asset business from three different seats: inside a global custodian, at the head of the technology company, and now inside the market utility that acquired it.

The first seat was State Street. She came up through traditional finance, with roles at Manulife and BNY Mellon, before becoming Executive Vice President and Head of State Street Global Markets. The crossing into digital started from the inside: as Executive Vice President and Head of State Street Digital, she set up a new integrated business and operating model to carry clients through the entire digital investment cycle, pre-trade, trade and post-trade.

The second was Securrency, where she was Chief Executive Officer of a provider of institutional-grade digital asset technology.

The third began in October 2023, when DTCC  @The_DTCC acquired Securrency. She is now Managing Director, Global Head of DTCC Digital Assets, overseeing the firm's digital asset technology, and she sits on the DTCC Executive Committee.

Her own description of the work is the argument: partnering with clients and key stakeholders to transform and evolve their operating models, and to create new digital asset services. Not a product launch. A rebuild of how the market actually runs, which is the part that only counts once the plumbing moves. She has led that rebuild from the client's side, the vendor's side and the infrastructure's side, and each institution has trusted her with more than the one before.

In October 2026, DTCC's tokenization service went live. Her words on the day: "This is only the beginning."

text:
网传腾讯明年要大裁员15%

小马哥对现在的腾讯非常不满意

以下是小马哥原话

Pony:我先讲一下。最近做了很多预算，盘点今年业绩和展望未来。刚才财经同事也讲到要盘点粮草。过去我们做的都是轻资产业务，第一次做这样重资产的业务，财务和组织架构的打法都不一样。面对新打法，必须更大地推动组织变革。

有人会想到2021年前后开始的"降本增效、截止升级、聚焦主业"。

现在已经不是简单从结构上降本，而是能不能适应新打法、新战场、生死攸关的变革。

目的不是降本，而是适应新的战场。人和组织都要做大调整。希望在原有人力的情况下，节奏更快、小团队能做大事。刚才游戏开发团队的例子，已经能看到肉眼可见的变化。

很多核心业务有险可守。开始大家以为AI对搜索影响很大，又觉得Google好像顶得住;到今年再看，浪真的已经杀过来。

其他行业、内容产业也许觉得安全，但从今天的分享能看到浪越来越近。不动起来，就会慌。远处浪潮已经吞没一个个山丘，你不能还坐着欣赏。要着急、站起来，准备新打法，找到高地，搬物资、上船，从陆战转海战。已有的陆军部队里，谁能上船、能不能打海战，得提前准备。坦率说现在都有点晚，不能再悠闲地觉得安全。

选择适应新打法的人，要干脆。不是过去那样还要哄、要游说、谈条件，或者先谈给不给管理岗位才肯上船。组织要扁平、直截了当，考验技能能否转换，迅速应战。

传统核心业务当然还要守，但要提效。比如用一半人守住，让另一半人打新战役--这是我用画面感描述的情形，帮助大家理解目前处境。今天这次 LinkTime，我希望讲得比以往严厉一些，丑话先说，希望大家理解和支持。

text:
One of the most incredible examples of “prescient business planning” I've ever heard from a founder:

10 months before the GameStop/meme stock frenzy, Robinhood CEO @vladtenev negotiated an emergency funding deal with @mickymalka.

He didn't need the money yet, so they put the term sheet in a drawer.

Then in January 2021, Robinhood's trading activity exploded, triggering billions in regulatory collateral requirements.

Vlad’s first call was to Micky, who committed hundreds of millions on the spot.

“It made every conversation after him much easier.”

“It certainly helped that we had gone through that exercise of thinking about this stuff.”
author: davidsenra
quoted_text:
Vlad Tenev (@vladtenev) is the co-founder and CEO of Robinhood.

In January 2021, in the middle of the meme stock frenzy, Robinhood's deposit requirement went from under $100 million to "something like $3 billion" almost overnight. The total capital the company had ever raised was about $700 million.

His first call was to @mickymalka:

"He's like, 'How much do you need?' I said, 'I don't know, 250 million, 500 million. I'm not sure.' He's like, 'I've got it.'"

Back in March 2020, the two of them had put a term sheet in place so the money could be "wired in your account same day." Once Micky was in, everyone else followed: "We probably had $10 billion of demand at the first term."

"It was a consequence of too much success, which is quite rare."

Vlad came to America from Bulgaria at 5, not knowing a word of English. His grandparents stored their wealth in copper cookware during hyperinflation. His dad told him he'd give him his SAT score in dollars to invest. He went on to study math under Terence Tao, then took a leave from his $18,000-a-year math PhD to take a shot at starting his own company.

This was an awesome conversation:

0:00 Why Ribbit passed on Robinhood's seed round
2:19 "You're going to want me on your board"
5:35 The day-long trading outage of March 2020
9:22 A term sheet for a crisis that hadn't happened yet
15:00 Crypto goes from zero to a top revenue stream
16:27 The $3 billion deposit requirement
18:35 "Vlad, you have to call work right away"
21:34 The first call: Micky Malka
24:31 "Time kills all deals"
25:33 Number one app in the App Store, ahead of Instagram and TikTok
27:01 $10 billion of demand
29:33 Hyperinflation and copper cookware in Bulgaria
35:34 "Manhattan just seemed like science fiction"
47:15 His SAT score in dollars to invest
50:53 Studying under Terence Tao
1:00:22 "You want to be businessman, huh?"
1:03:48 The best parts of math without the bullshit
1:05:56 Would I be proud of this in 50 years?

text:
Jensen Huang's journey till date, simplified...

🔷 1963: Jensen Huang was born in Taiwan & later moved to the United States, where he pursued his education.

🔷 1984–1992: Earned an electrical engineering degree from Oregon State University & a Master's from Stanford University. He also worked at AMD & LSI Logic before becoming an entrepreneur.

🔶 1993: Co-founded NVIDIA with Chris Malachowsky & Curtis Priem, initially focusing on graphics technology for computers and gaming.

🔷 1999: NVIDIA introduced the GeForce 256, marketed as the world's first GPU, & went public on the NASDAQ exchange.

🔷 2006: NVIDIA launched CUDA, allowing devs to use GPUs for computing tasks beyond graphics. This became a major foundation for the company's future AI business.

🔷 2012: NVIDIA GPUs helped power AlexNet, a breakthrough deep-learning model that demonstrated the potential of GPUs for training AI systems.

🔷 2022–2024: The generative AI boom, accelerated by ChatGPT's launch, drove extraordinary demand for NVIDIA chips. By June 2024, the company's market valuation had surpassed $3 trillion.

🔷 2025: NVIDIA became the first publicly traded company to reach a $5 trillion market valuation, reflecting its central role in the global AI infrastructure boom.

🔷 Oct. 2026: Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a business executive whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspected of gathering information for China, came under public scrutiny.

🔷 Nov. 8, 2026: Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship and apologized to his wife and NVIDIA. The company announced an independent investigation into reports that he may have been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

🔷 Nov. 9–10, 2026: NVIDIA shares came under pressure as the controversy raised concerns about corporate governance, national security, and the company's semiconductor business in China.

🔷 Nov. 2026: U.S. lawmakers called for further scrutiny of NVIDIA's China operations and Huang's involvement in decisions concerning chip exports.

🔶 Current status: As of November 12, 2026, Huang remains NVIDIA's president and CEO. The board investigation is ongoing, and no final finding establishing espionage or wrongdoing by Huang has been announced.

In 1985, Chuck Jones, the animator and director best known for Bugs Bunny and the Road Runner, came to dinner at Chuck and Lee Csuri’s. My favourite part is that he drew Bugs for Caroline’s brother Steven right there on the tablecloth.

Csuri’s work at Ohio State was finding its way into all sorts of places, particularly commercial animation. Even Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston, two of the animators behind Bambi and The Jungle Book, came to Ohio State to talk shop. They’d spent their careers working with pencil and paper, and here was Csuri’s team making characters move with code at a time when that was still a very new idea.

text:
Why Uniswap is losing USDC-USDT Market Share to Fluid and Metric

Background:
USDC-USDT is Ethereum's most traded DEX pair at ~$480M a day, almost 2x USDC-WETH. In five weeks, Uniswap's share of it fell from 58% to 36%.

Uniswap's volume didn't drop. It stayed around $1B-$1.3B a week, apart from the 26 Oct spike, while the pair grew from ~$2.3B to over $3.3B a week, and the growth went elsewhere:
• Metric: from 0.6% to 14%
• Aero: from 0% to 6%
• Fluid: steady at 20-28%

Where Uniswap lost is big trades:
• Over $1M: from 85% to 44%, with Fluid going from 10% to 43%
• $100K to $1M: from 36% to 21%, with Metric going from 7% to 28%
• Under $10K: from 50% to 44%, still the leader but Metric also grown from 7%-16%

What is the cause?
It's not fees. Uniswap's USDC-USDT pools charge 0.07 to 0.12bp, already among the lowest. Its stable-pair hook isn't the reason either, since it was set up the same way when Uniswap held 58% market share.

It's depth at the live price during volatility. USDT slipped from around par to 8-15bp below USDC in the second half of October. Arbitrage moves Uniswap's price, but LP liquidity stays in the ranges LPs chose. Active depth in the main pool fell from ~$900K per bp on 15 Oct to ~$310K on 28 Oct.

The other reason is Aero has entered Ethereum during the same period and has captured ~6% of the trading volume overall.

Why other DEXs are not impacted?
Fluid draws depth from its lending vaults around a center price it can move, and Metric's market makers quote from their own inventory at the live price. Both keep size where the trades are, so aggregators send the big orders there.

If the market calms down next week, watch whether the big trades come back to Uniswap or stay with Fluid, Aero and Metric.

text:
英伟达的董事会能保住老黄么？再聊聊老黄的这次桃色事件。1、看下图英伟达董事会里包括老黄在内11名董事，有6位任职超过十三年，即使2019年加入英伟达董事会的Stephen也是1993年起就给英伟达提供法律服务。这意味着有7位董事很老黄共事很久，经历过英伟达过去的高峰低谷、能深刻认识老黄对于英伟达的不可或缺，他的远见、决断力以及魄力是英伟达走到现在的关键因素。

从董事会的构成看、老黄的亲密战友还是占多数的。

2、最终取决于在于调查的结果，
独立董事正式聘请 Wachtell 律所及纽约南区前代理联邦检察官 Joon Kim 主持调查，董事会把事实调查交给了外部律师。
1）这个调查是昨天的消息调查重点还是跟黄乐的关系，以及有没有泄漏相关机密；

2）今天纽约时报报道的跟女下属的婚外情、估计也是新的调查方向。
这个跟女下属的婚外情现在所有的报道就是曾在英伟达工作的匿名消息源头说两人有关系，但是都还没有明确的证实，最早纽约时报的报道记者说也没看到相关视频。

但这点恰恰最最关键，决定了是事实确凿还是扑风捉影。

3、能看出来这次倒黄动作势大力猛
先是黄乐，再是powell，特别是powe
ll这个现在所有的媒体报道都没有明确的实质性证据，都是匿名消息源的说法，这一点非常值得怀疑。然后纽约时报又传统的左派媒体，跟民主党关系亲密不能不让人生疑。

当然也看到有说法anthropic的联创JackClark也给媒体提供了信息，他之前本身就是科技记者。老黄力推开源，DarioAmodei主张闭源、激烈路线之争。

倒黄派可能是看到了单凭黄乐还不足以让老黄离开、所以又拿跟女下属powell的关系做文章。
当然这些都是我们吃瓜群众的揣测。

从董事会构成上来看，想保住老黄的应该还是占大多数，但最后还是回到调查结果：
1）如果跟女下属powell婚外情被证实，再叠加跟黄乐的关系。老黄大概率是要离任的，即使不完全离开公司但是ceo估计是很难继续了、也可能有一个比较长的过渡期或者担任顾问。

但这对英伟达来说中长期影响还是不小，毕竟像开头说再有一个能有老黄那样的远见、决断力和魄力的ceo概率很小。

这种情况下，最终结果出来短线可以博一个大反弹，因为核心竞争力也没那么快就没了。长期就要边走边看、看实际经营状况了，看接任者能不能真的撑得住。

2）如果跟powell关系被证实子虚乌有、光黄乐感觉撼动老黄的概率不大。大概率黄乐就是一个倒卖芯片的掮客，是间谍的可能性很小老黄泄露机密概率也不大，这种情况下董事会应该还是会保住老黄的。

甚至英伟达的前几大股东贝莱德、先锋、富达、道富等机构都不想老黄走人，毕竟在老黄身上利益巨大。
这种情况英伟达被砸下来就是一个真正的黄金坑了

老黄亲闺女黄敏珊（Madison Huang）最近发声，简直让人五味杂陈！🍉

在老黄4天连爆两桩婚外情之前，他在儿女眼里一直是那个最懂家庭、最支持孩子的“完美老爸”。

在一群大学生面前，身为英伟达高级总监的黄敏珊回忆：

她爸妈都是电气工程师，她高中拼命读书，本来已经准备好申请书，打算走爸妈的老路去学工程。结果在最后一刻，老黄拦住了她，对她说：“你并不真正热爱工程，你应该去做你真正有热情、会爱上的事。”

因为老黄这句话，她撤回了所有名校工程系申请，跑去美国烹饪学院做了个厨子，后来又一路杀回英伟达当上高管。

听听她在台上的原话有多清醒：
1️⃣ 趁年轻去干让你害怕的事：在学校是人生兜底最安全的阶段，去让你发怵的公司、见完全不同的人，越害怕的事越能让你暴风成长。

2️⃣ 别怕AI抢饭碗，别把“干活”当成“目的”：程序员的目的不是敲代码，而是发明新产品；机械师的目的不是画CAD图纸，而是造出新机器。把死板的任务交给AI，想清楚自己到底在解决什么问题，才能登上AI这艘火箭。

不得不说，老黄这闺女是真的优秀又通透。只是不知道，当年那个教女儿“忠于热爱”的慈父，如今自己因为管不住下半身把万亿帝国拖进风暴眼，在家里该如何面对这一双优秀的儿女和相伴几十年的发妻？👇

text:
Women often say they wish they could be a man online. If that’s actually what you want, it’s as simple as rebranding your profile and no longer tweeting “I’m a girl”

People do it all the time. Everyone cares much less about you or who you are than you think, and the signals they rely on to determine your identity are so much less refined than you imagine

Years ago, I changed my pfp to a girl for a day. I didn’t change my name, handle, or anything else about my page - just my photo and the way I worded tweets. This was sufficient to change the default assumption to “Lukas is a woman”

I got 14k new followers in 24h, but you realize while going from man -> woman on here that while everyone is much nicer, most kinda stop reading or engaging with what you actually wrote

They leave replies that might on first glance trick you into thinking they’re reading. They’re sort of topically related.

But almost all the time, it’s just some version of “so true, queen! [unrelated info dump about one of the words or subjects in your post].” 

Or maybe they’re one of the angry ones. They just disagree with whatever you said and insult you - also having mostly not read it

There’s this persistent idea that “people are only mean to me bc I’m a woman online the internet”

I’ve run women’s accounts on here at various points and it’s always been the opposite: people are nicer to women, and they engage much more with them

They just also take them less seriously, so even though as a woman you will have more “engagement” it’s much less actual conversation

quoted_text:
Peer 原理讲解 01 | 合约分工与原子操作

用户在 Peer 下单买 100 USDC，链上到底发生了什么？发生在两套系统里的法币付款和 USDC 转账是如何连接起来的？

下单成功，还不意味 USDC 已经到账。Peer 的做法是通过记录交易条件、预留资金和验证付款凭证，连接链上和链下 👇

1. 卖家挂单时，把 USDC 存入 Escrow（资金托管合约），创建一份 Deposit，记录存款以及接受的支付方式、金额范围和定价规则。
2. 买家下单时，Orchestrator（订单协调合约）通过 signalIntent 创建具体的订单记录，也就是 Intent：买多少、按什么汇率、关联哪笔存款、USDC 发到哪个地址。同时，它会调用 Escrow，锁定这笔订单对应的额度。

此时，100 USDC 仍在合约里，但已经被这笔订单占用。锁额有有效期：订单到期仍未结算，锁定的额度会在链上清理后回到卖家的挂单。创建订单和锁定资金被合并为一个原子操作，在同一笔链上交易里完成：如果锁额失败，这次创建的订单记录也会回滚。

订单条件由 Orchestrator 保存，资金和锁额由 Escrow 管理，两边通过这次共同执行的操作保持一致，避免出现订单已经成立、却没有对应资金的情况。

3. 买家完成法币付款、取得付款凭证，就可以进入凭证结算流程。

这时，Orchestrator 会调用 Payment Verifier（付款验证器），检查凭证签名、凭证与订单的对应关系，并记下这笔付款，防止同一笔付款被重复使用，再按结算规则处理资金。扣除手续费后，资金可能直接转给订单指定的收币地址，也可能进入延迟结算。这里同样有第二个原子化流程：

验证、订单清理和资金处理，通过 fulfillIntent 在同一笔链上交易中完成。

即使付款凭证已经通过验证，只要后续资金处理失败，这次交易对订单和资金的改动也会一起回滚。把这些操作放进同一笔交易，就是为了避免订单已经被清理，资金却没按规则处理的情况。不过，回滚只限于这次链上交易，已经完成的法币付款不会因此撤销；订单和锁额则会恢复到本次结算前的状态，USDC 仍留在合约中。遇到这种情况，应保留付款凭证，先核查订单状态和失败原因，再处理后续结算。

text:
A critical juncture in Yemen has arrived.

The battlefield in Yemen is evolving rapidly by the hour

Forward elements of the Ansar Allah (Houthi) forces have shared photos taken along the coastal highway on Yemen’s southern shore.

From last night through this afternoon, Aden-aligned government troops who failed to pull out of the pocket are now, in theory, fully encircled.
author: Vito_168
quoted_text:
Pro-Houthi sources report that all government outposts on Mount Haraz have fallen, and Houthi forces have reached the coastline.

Below is a hand-drawn sketch outlining the three major Houthi campaigns in Yemen, to help contextualize the situation.

Blue marks the Mocha campaign in September. It featured three large flanking, encirclement and annihilation operations, seizing 5,400 square kilometres of territory in one stroke — more ground than has been gained on the Russia-Ukraine front in two years. The Houthis captured Mayyun Island and secured the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical chokepoint for international shipping.

In the wake of the Mocha campaign, the western defensive lines of Taiz were left exposed. Seizing this opening, the Houthis launched the Taiz campaign, marked in green. Their western column struck directly from Mocha toward the key bottleneck of Turbah, while eastern forces advanced westward in support. The two formations linked up at Turbah, severing Taiz’s connections to the south and isolating Yemen’s second-largest city. The Houthis then steadily tightened and eroded the encirclement, taking control of over 95% of Taiz Governorate and compressing Aden-aligned government forces inside the city of Taiz itself.

With the Taiz campaign largely consolidated, the Houthis quickly opened a third offensive, provisionally named the Lahj Campaign (taking its name from Lahj Governorate, where its early pivotal fighting unfolded). Setting out from captured Turbah, five Houthi columns applied pressure across the board against Aden’s government troops. The western front then staged a feigned retreat, drawing the enemy’s main forces forward in pursuit. At that point, Houthi forces on the eastern front suddenly struck south in overwhelming strength, seized Mount Haraz and pushed all the way to the southern coast. This cut the lines of communication between the western garrisons and Aden, the interim capital, trapping elite formations including the Shield of the Nation and the Giant Brigades — around 20 brigades in total — in the southwest pocket.

Once these three campaigns conclude, the area to the left of the red line in Figure 3 will be under Houthi control, while the territory to the right remains under the Aden government. Over 90% of the population and major cities lie on the left side of the red line, with only roughly 10% on the right. The only major city left in the government-held zone is the interim capital, Aden.

text:
A lean, open-weight model that comes within 1.2 points of GPT-5.6 at forecasting real-world events.

Core contributor @valoryag trained Olas-Predict-Qwen3.8-27B, an open-weight forecasting model built on Qwen3.8-27B, using reviewed forecasting examples and reinforcement learning. It follows Olas-Predict-R1-14B, Valory’s first Olas Predict model.

In Valory’s evaluation on 6,824 prediction markets created after GPT-5.6’s training cutoff, with the same prompts and evidence for both models:

• Balanced accuracy (higher is better): 67.3% vs 68.5% for GPT-5.6
• Brier error (lower is better): 0.2124 vs 0.2029 for GPT-5.6
• Against Olas-Predict-R1-14B: 22% lower Brier error

It gets this close from a starting point that scores 15.6% on the AA-Omniscience factual-knowledge benchmark, against about 59% for GPT-5.6.

Most of the gain came from the stronger starting model. Valory’s domain training added 5% lower Brier error and 12% lower calibration error on top.

Next, Valory aims to close the remaining gap in future training experiments.

text:
Lest we forget. 🇨🇦

Today, November 11th, we pause as Canadians to remember.

We remember every Canadian who put on a uniform, left their families, homes and communities, and went into harm's way in defence of something greater than themselves.

We remember those who made the ultimate sacrifice. Those who came home carrying physical and invisible scars. Those who never fully recovered. The families who waited, worried, grieved and carried on. And those who continue to serve, protect and fight for our freedoms today, both at home and around the world.

Their sacrifices belong to all of us.

And that's something I believe we need to remember.

The red poppy isn't a symbol belonging to one group, one background, one heritage or one particular history. It represents remembrance. It represents sacrifice, service, courage, loss and the enduring cost of freedom.

It represents Canadians.

Regardless of where your family came from, how long you've called this country home, what your ancestry is, or what your personal circumstances may be, the freedoms we enjoy today have been shaped and protected by generations of people who were willing to sacrifice for others.

Some of us have grown up with freedoms so deeply woven into everyday life that we've never really had to consider what they cost. We can go to school, raise our families, speak our minds, build businesses, practise our beliefs and live our lives without fully appreciating that these things were not always guaranteed, and are still not guaranteed everywhere in the world.

That's the privilege of living in Canada. But it's also a responsibility.

I believe we should be bringing Canadians together in remembrance, not creating separate lanes, separate symbols or separate identities around a day that should unite us all.

We can recognize the distinct experiences, injustices and contributions of different communities throughout our history without separating the act of remembrance itself.

There is room to acknowledge every story without dividing the people who share this country.

One country. One day of national remembrance. One red poppy. A shared responsibility to never forget.

Today, let's put aside our differences, our politics and everything else that divides us.

Let's remember those who never made it home. Let's honour those who did. Let's recognize the families who sacrificed alongside them and those who continue to carry the burden of service today.

And let's never take for granted the freedoms that were paid for by generations before us.

Lest we forget.

Lest we ever forget what it cost to be free.

🇨🇦

#RemembranceDay #RemembranceDay2026 #CanadaRemembers

text:
Some quick observations on Anthropic's IPO:

1/ The number of customers paying $100K or more grew 12x in a year, to over 11,900. And the existing ones are spending about 9x what they did 1 year ago (wild).

2/ The net loss is $23.3B, but $21.9B of that is a paper loss. They owe early investors shares, and those shares got more valuable, so accounting rules count it as a loss (has to do with convertible notes etc being exchanged)

3/ Revenue per employee is over $6.6M!

4/ They did $17B in revenue last quarter, and that's up more than 12x from a year ago.

5/ The stat they feature most is compute efficiency, where they say they get 4x more revenue per dollar of compute than in early 2025. ( I think this is a metric they defined themselves but not 100% sure)

6/ It's a public benefit corporation, so shareholders are buying into a company that's legally allowed to weigh other goals alongside their returns.

7/ You can request shares at the IPO price through Robinhood, SoFi, Schwab, Fidelity and E*TRADE, which I think is somewhat unusual for an IPO this size, but maybe it's a sign of the times?

8/ The whole roadshow is an 11 chapter video that anyone can watch, and it's cool that they shared it.

9/ The ticker is $ANT. It's expected to price on November 18 and start trading the next day.

10/ One of the case studies is about Sparky, Walmart’s shopping assistant, and they say orders through it are about 35% bigger. What’s interesting to me is that shoppers only ever see Walmart, and Anthropic is the plumbing underneath. Sidenote: I co-founded @MeetLCA an agency that builds experiences like this big companies/big startups so this trend is what I'm seeing too (demand for agent experience products)

11/ The founders' letter tells investors to "never let your company be worth a dollar more than it is actually worth." I haven't seen that in an IPO pitch before.

12/ About 250 customers pay them $10M or more a year, and over 1,900 pay $1M or more.

13/ They spent $9.9B on compute last quarter, which is more than half of revenue. $5B of that was bought on short-term deals that cost a lot more, which tells me demand is running ahead of what they planned for.

14/ All 7 co-founders are still at the company, and they lose about 1% of the people they want to keep each year.

Our conviction in Zcash was formed long before privacy became a mainstream conversation. We believe Zcash puts the transaction back in an envelope: the network proves the money is real and the rules are followed without publishing the personal data behind it.

I've spent years in digital asset infrastructure, and I believe the biggest barrier to adoption has never been technology. It's understanding. Campaigns like this close that gap.

(比如说   var<---> Lighter  价差回归套利, 30个market, 差价的gap怎么取, 你可能用EWMA 或者 a Kalman filter , 假设10个参数,  然后回归过去60天的行情. 轻松就 30*10*60个任务.       普通8核16G电脑可能五六个小时 )

如果你是任务量特别大怎么办?  那么多开几个就行了. 然后AI会自动分配任务到这些机器上. 跑完了再自动关掉就行了. 按分钟计费.

text:
Google 推出 Gemini Decision 1：一个专门负责「做决策」的模型！

它不是用来聊天或生成长文本的，而是让 AI Agent 更快、更低成本地完成判断。

通过 Gemini Decisions API，开发者可以一次性输入文本、图片、音频、视频和 PDF，并同时提出最多 1000 个独立问题。

支持三种决策方式：
Yes/No：判断某个条件是否成立。
Multiple Choice：从 2–255 个候选项中选择最佳答案。
Scoring：按照预设标准进行分级评分。

每个判断都会返回概率和 0–1 的置信度，方便系统决定是否自动执行，还是交给其他模型或人工处理。

性能和价格也很有吸引力：
⚡ 端到端延迟约 150–250ms
💰 每百万输入 Token 仅 $0.10
输出 Token 免费
📊 一次请求最多评估 1000 个问题，共享输入只计费一次。

实际应用包括 Agent 工具选择、模型动态路由、内容审核、安全检测、上下文质量评估，以及多模态信息分类。
Google 已经将它用于 Gemini Notebook 的模型路由、Stitch 的快速设计迭代，以及 Search 的 MCP 工具安全检测。

我的看法： 

这是 Agent 架构中一个很有价值的新方向。过去我们经常让昂贵的通用大模型完成简单判断，现在可以把这些任务交给专门的决策模型，让 Agent 更快、更便宜地决定下一步做什么。

text:
总结一下我们的核心观点：

我们认为纯机器人模型公司显然已经进入商品化的阶段，这也意味着纯模型实验室高估值已经到达了拐点。它们要么通过自己掌握硬件来垂直整合整个技术栈，要么彻底转向前线部署模式，把部署环节握在自己手里。

Fable 5.2 和 Astra 6 的出现，基本意味着通用 LLM 已经可以取代所谓的 system 2；而当这些模型用来写代码去控制机器时，还能继续下沉到 system 1，接管传统机器人栈里的动作规划环节。只要推理长度和所需算力能随时间持续优化，专注于 pre-training 的纯 VLA 实验室追逐通用机器人智能，最终会被彻底淘汰。

有意思的是，我们认为价值最终会沉淀到部署层。从软件的角度看，也就是市场所说的 system 0。而其中的关键在于：持续收集后训练数据，会实质性地提升软件对硬件的控制能力，也让部署本身变得更高效、更好。

至于硬件，我们的观点比较反直觉的是，它反而会成为瓶颈。虽然这一层的利润率大概率会被竞争压低，但这不等于硬件没有价值。公司必须自己掌握硬件，才能完全释放软件的能力。这意味着要自研、自产硬件，确保后训练所优化的一切，都能真正落到硬件层上。

text:
Regarding $NBIS earnings results:

To show you how fast they're growing... from Q2 to Q3: 

Revenue: $582.3M -> $980.8M (+68% QoQ)
Adjusted EBITDA: $236.2M -> $465.8M (+97% QoQ)
AI cloud adj. EBITDA margin: 49.7% -> 53.2%
Net Income: −$190.4M -> −$37.5M

ARR has reached $6.4B at the end of Sep. In terms of management commentary: 

- Since start of Q3, Nebius signed $12B+ of new contracts
- Average GPU pricing rose 20%+ sequentially, payback shortened from 22M -> 19M
- On Q3 deals, prepayments covered 100% of associated capex, up from 50–60% in Q2 (insane for financing)
- Contract value per MW exceeded $25M+ from Q3 up from ~$20M Q2 
- 5GW contracted power year end

With $10B of committed customer prepayments in 2026 and $17B-$20B in 2027. Now, prepayments and borrowing against existing contracts covers ~75-85% of 2027 capex. 

On subsidiaries:
1. Avride - 250 autonomous vehicles fleet, over 100,000 passenger rides (with companies like $UBER). Fully driverless robotaxi targeted H1 2027.
2. Toloka - Revenue doubled sequentially
3. Enterprise cloud - Databricks and Datadog selected Neibus. Along with a new agreement with Snowflake. 
4. Tavily - Over 3M developers now with $IBM post-training a core partner. 
5. ClickHouse - Nothing about new secondary valuations, but we can see valuations growing
6. TokenFactory - Contract value grew 17x sequentially

The primary negative I saw was that 2026 guidance is now on the lower end (near ~$3B), due to $MSFT capacity deliveries slipping to Q2 2027.

Apparently there was an execution miss with a third party partner DataOne. Temporary generators were retired amid permitting issues before enough $BE fuel cell capacity came online. 

Capex also increased in 2026 from $20B-$25B to $27B, while revising revenue expectations downward. 

So near-term unfortunate headwinds kinda reminiscent of AOI earnings; however long term I think Nebius will take care of you. 

For 2027 outlook:
- $12-13 billion revenue, capex of $40-45 billion, pre-tax breakeven by the end of 2027.

Very operationally bullish, as seen with prepayments covering capex, GPU premiums increasing. Main downside is near-term execution risk from third parties, causing near-term delays and revenue recognition. 

Great quarter from Nebius overall.

text:
very much agree with @QwQiao here.

the reason the timeline feels like the worst it’s ever been is that it’s dominated by short-term traders and opportunists.

crypto has always been infamous for attracting the get rich quick crowd, people drawn in by the hope of making the most money possible with the least effort possible.

that worked for way too long. but those days are over, and that’s exactly why everyone is stuck in disbelief and does nothing but complain. of course it doesn’t feel great when you were used to 100x gains in a week from following some random anon’s call, and now you suddenly have to do real due diligence and then wait, with a TikTok brain, for a thesis to play out.

those are the people behind 90% of the sentiment on your timeline. so be very careful about who you follow and listen to, especially when it’s internet strangers.

but ffs, this doesn't mean there aren't a ton of great opportunities left out there in crypto.

the people I respect most in this industry sound nothing like the timeline right now.

they’re as bullish as they’ve ever been, and see this as a massive opportunity to accumulate some of the world’s most exciting protocols and onchain businesses at a discount while nobody else is paying attention.

contrary to the midcurve bear take, I have no doubt there are still several 100-1000x opportunities out there, even if they’ve become harder to find.

the only questions left: how long until that gap closes, and do you have the stamina and emotional stability to sit through it?

the vast majority of ppl have only been here since 2021 let alone 2017. they’ve never experienced the joy of developing long term theses and be proven right after 100-10000x. on top of that with the sheer amount of garbage launched after 2021 statistically most things ppl hold go to zero.

but having hit one 10000x, one 1000x, and a handful of 10-100xs, i can tell u from experience long term investing is financially, intellectually, *and* emotionally far more rewarding than short term games. not only will u make more money, u will learn more about the world and feel great watching a project succeed after years of ups and downs.

text:
This Jensen Huang/Nvidia scandal is quite bizarre. The most dominant CEOs of the world's most powerful corporations rarely fall, let alone as easily and rapidly as this seems to be happeing. He's on the brink of being ousted with remarkable velocity and vanishingly little evidence. 

Over what? If "mere" extramarital affairs were sufficient for ouster, how many top CEOs would be left? Not many. Hence the need for the sinister CCP/spying angle. But is there any tangible evidence at all that Alice Huang is an asset or spy for the Chinese government? Anything beyond anonymous vague US intelligence suspicions being mindlessly, dutifully recited (as always) by US corporate media? 

The always smart and insightful @RnaudBertrand is required reading here, at least for the questions he raises:👇
author: ggreenwald
quoted_text:
This is the biggest irony of the whole Alice Huang / Nvidia saga: the Chinese government actually doesn't want Nvidia chips and is actively keeping them out of the country.

Last year it even ordered Alibaba and ByteDance to cancel their Nvidia orders (https://t.co/T4ZMand2BD) and sent customs teams to the ports to check every advanced chip coming in (https://t.co/UFPerK7Cgp).

And right now 600,000 Nvidia H200s are stuck in Hong Kong because Beijing won’t let them into the country (https://t.co/epimhGPQYq)👇

Nvidia also explicitly frames this as a threat to its business in its latest annual report to the SEC: "The Chinese government has encouraged customers to purchase from our China-based competitors and discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using our data center products" (https://t.co/TQVwWuix83).

Why does China do that? Because every Nvidia chip a Chinese company buys is one that Huawei or Cambricon doesn’t sell, and domestic chips can only catch up if people actually buy them (which means money for R&D, etc.).

Which means that the notion that Chinese intelligence was running honeytraps to get more Nvidia chips into China gets the whole thing exactly backwards.

In fact, it looks like Megaspeed - Alice Huang's company - was a counter-reaction to official Chinese policy: a private sector workaround to these efforts by the Chinese government to curtail Nvidia.

As was widely reported - including by Western media - Megaspeed built data centers in Southeast Asia and rented their computing power to Alibaba, which the New York Times called "a backdoor way of getting access" to Nvidia chips (https://t.co/tu9Re4WdzM).

That is a backdoor not only - allegedly - around Washington’s export controls, but also around China's own efforts to wean its companies off Nvidia.

I can’t believe the Chinese government was too thrilled about it: it'd make just about zero sense for it to run countless domestic measures to prevent Alibaba from using Nvidia chips, yet at the same time have its top spy agency help the same Alibaba get Nvidia chips through the back door in Southeast Asia 🤷

At the end of the day, as with all such stories, you always need to look at "cui bono?": who benefits? Who benefitted is pretty clear:

- Nvidia itself: it's in the business of selling chips so a customer willing to spend billions of dollars on chips in Southeast Asia is a godsend. Again, as they themselves state in their SEC filings, not being able to tap into Chinese demand would have "a material and adverse impact on our business" (https://t.co/TQVwWuix83).

- Chinese companies like Alibaba: facts are, 1) Chinese chips haven't yet caught up, 2) Chinese chip companies' production capabilities are still limited and 3) Chinese tech firms' historical tech stack runs on Nvidia’s CUDA ecosystem, and rewriting years of code for Huawei chips is painful. Renting Nvidia chips in Southeast Asia is the easy way to stay competitive and serve customer demand in the meantime.

- The US, according to core members of the Trump administration: back in July last year, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick explained that the point of letting Nvidia sell more chips to China was to get Chinese developers "addicted to the American technology stack" (https://t.co/WpaKkS6gOG).

Who does NOT benefit, according to official Chinese policy, is the Chinese state, which has made tech self-reliance one of its foremost priorities.

Which means that, to believe the spy story, you have to believe that a person - Alice Huang - was effectively a spy paid by her own government while simultaneously sabotaging its tech self-reliance drive, which it has spent years and trillions of dollars on - pretty senseless. 

Stranger things have happened, I guess, but it doesn't pass the smell test. 

And there is another absolutely major contradiction in the media story. According to a Financial Times article published yesterday (https://t.co/7q1UEaUR4y), "a person who knows [Alice Huang] said they had been asked by MSS for information about her earlier this year after news emerged that Singapore was investigating the company in relation to chip-smuggling allegations. The agency wanted to find out more information about Huang, including the nature of her business and connections, the person said."

Which raises a damn obvious question: if she were indeed an MSS asset, why on earth would the MSS need to ask the people around her who she was and the nature of her business? 

It's a complete contradiction with the spy story - but very much not a contradiction with what I described above: a private businesswoman running a workaround to Beijing’s own policy, which the Chinese security apparatus would naturally want to look into.

Especially since, around about the same time, Shanghai police detained her business partner, reportedly her husband, in a stock manipulation case (https://t.co/KXimvioTTd): also coherent with Chinese authorities looking into her network, and much harder to square with her being a prized MSS asset.

And, to top it all, there is - to this day - not a shred of evidence that's been published that she is, in fact, a Chinese spy: just anonymous intelligence officials, repeated by journalists who never verified it, as I detailed here (https://t.co/loSwtoVrqr) and here (https://t.co/fIWGMIF3Cr) with one of the key FT journalists on this story actually admitting that he has no idea what evidence US intelligence actually has. 

So the claim went to print without anyone seeing the evidence, without anyone being able to check it, and without anyone knowing whether it even exists. 

And given everything above, from Beijing blocking the very chips she was supposedly recruited to help get into China, to the MSS asking around about her, to her partner being detained in Shanghai, my bet is that the evidence doesn’t exist at all. If anything, everything we can check points the other way.

🚨 黄仁勋即日起辞去英伟达 CEO、总裁及董事会成员职务。

11 月 12 日，英伟达（NVIDIA）宣布，黄仁勋即日起辞去公司 CEO、总裁及董事会成员职务。

这意味着，这位执掌英伟达数十年的核心人物将退出公司管理层。

从 GPU 制造商到全球 AI 算力霸主，黄仁勋几乎亲手推动了英伟达过去数十年的转型。如今，AI 浪潮仍在持续，英伟达市值与产业影响力也处于历史高位，他却选择在此时离开管理岗位。

对于英伟达而言，真正的问题或许不是谁来接任，而是失去黄仁勋之后，公司能否延续现有的战略判断力与执行力。
author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
如果黄仁勋真的离开英伟达，受到冲击的可能不只是英伟达股价，而是整个 AI 产业链。

英伟达过去几年的万亿级市值扩张，除了 GPU、CUDA 和数据中心业务，还包含了一个重要的隐性资产：黄仁勋本人。

他直接管理超过 60 名下属，没有传统 COO 层级。从芯片研发、台积电先进封装产能协调，到微软、谷歌、亚马逊等 CSP 客户，再到 CoreWeave 等算力租赁企业的融资合作，黄仁勋实际上是整个 AI 产业网络的核心协调者。

如果他离开，至少有四个潜在影响：

1️⃣ 英伟达估值重估： 创始人溢价可能消失，投资者需要重新评估公司的长期战略执行能力和接班体系。
2️⃣ CSP 厂商议价权上升： 微软、谷歌、亚马逊等客户可能加快自研 ASIC 和 AMD 芯片的导入，降低对英伟达的依赖。
3️⃣ AI 算力融资承压： CoreWeave 等依赖 GPU 扩张的算力租赁公司，可能面临合作、融资和资本开支预期重新评估。
4️⃣ 全球 AI 供应链重新洗牌： 从台积电 CoWoS、HBM 到服务器和高速互联，英伟达管理层更替可能影响长期采购与产品导入节奏。美国对华芯片出口政策的产业游说格局也可能发生变化。

Reuters Breakingviews 的分析甚至指出，黄仁勋构建的商业网络涉及约 3000 亿美元的相关风险敞口。Morningstar 则认为，黄仁勋离职可能影响 AI 生态融资，但短期算力需求依然强劲，英伟达收入未必立即受到冲击。

当然，CUDA、GPU 产品和供应链不会因为一个 CEO 离职就消失。真正的问题是，谁能接管这张由黄仁勋亲手搭建的产业网络？

过去市场给英伟达定价的是 AI 算力霸主。

现在需要重新考虑的是：英伟达究竟是一家拥有强大组织能力的公司，还是一家高度依赖黄仁勋个人能力的公司？

如果 AI 时代最重要的产业组织者突然退场，整个 AI 行业的估值逻辑可能都要重新计算。

注：目前董事会调查及相关去留讨论，不等于黄仁勋已经被正式解除 CEO 职务。
