text:
As all NVIDIA employees I guess, I am deeply concerned by the campaign against Jensen Huang. Removing him would be a disaster.

Many have documented on X and elsewhere how this looks like a coordinated coup.

I'd add only one thing. Look at who would benefit from a dramatic weakening of NVIDIA.

It is not China. It is not about selling GPUs to China because that train has left. China authorities have pushed back on the H200 the Trump administration allowed NVIDIA to sell.

Look at what Jensen pushed back on:
- regulations that would make open source model training too expensive
- regulations that would make closed model providers immune to liabilities caused by their models. He said "if your product is not ready, then don't ship it"
- regulation against model distillation. He said "this is competition. People do it all the time with NVIDIA products, they try to reverse engineer them."

The other side will do everything they can to get him fired. 

As a French, I can't care less about his private life. I get that the US is puritan and sees it otherwise. But frankly, isn't it something he and his family has to deal with? Why should all NVIDIA employees, partners, and investors be collateral damage?

Disclaimer. As my bio says, the above are my views only. I do not represent NVIDIA by any means. I only commented on publicly available information.

text:
NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
November 12, 2026
Jensen Huang Resigns

Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Appointed Interim CEO

Harvey C. Jones Appointed First-Ever Chair of the Board

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.

Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.

Kress has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company’s finance organization and has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth and evolution. Prior to joining NVIDIA, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.

The Board of Directors appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board.  Mr. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive, and active venture investor for over 30 years, including serving as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Synopsys.

“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”  

“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, NVIDIA. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” 

Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.

NVIDIA will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled, followed by its earnings call at 2 p.m. PT.

Six votes will end Jensen Huang 33-year god-tier run as CEO.

Even his crew who've been with him since the beginning can't block it on their own.

I went through the board:
1/ Harvey Jones joined in 1993 at the founders' invitation. He saw Jensen rebuild NVIDIA after its first product setback.

2/ Tench Coxe and Mark Stevens came in from Sutter Hill and Sequoia, two earliest backers. Both first joined the board in 1993.

3/ Brooke Seawell joined in 1997, before the IPO.

4/ Stephen Neal is the lead independent director. He can convene the independent directors and coordinate those discussions.

Jensen needs 6 of 11 board votes, even though if Jones, Coxe, Stevens and Seawell all back Jensen, the other 6 independent directors can still doom him.

My honest base case is Jensen loses the CEO seat, with an interim appointment first. The board publicly backed him on Sunday. By Wednesday, Bloomberg was reporting that it was working with an outside firm to identify replacements and weighing an interim CEO.

For $NVDA, the first test is Nov. 17 earnings. An interim CEO can get the company through the call.

Avalanche architecture was innately designed to push forward sovereignty, privacy, customization, security, and interchain connectivity.

Avalanche L1s don’t share a global execution environment or validator set. Each network runs its own consensus, maintains its own state, and determines who can validate, transact, or access its data.

That means a financial institution can operate a private, permissioned blockchain with its own regulatory requirements, while another institution operates an entirely different network. Neither competes for the other’s blockspace or inherits its security assumptions.

For regulated financial institutions, privacy is a fundamental infrastructure requirement. Avalanche L1s allow institutions to control network participation and data access, with the flexibility to implement advanced cryptographic protections, including encryption and zero-knowledge proofs, to safeguard sensitive transactions and counterparty information while preserving regulatory oversight.

Institutions also retain control over transaction processing, fee structures, and network governance, allowing compliance requirements to be enforced at the infrastructure level.

Avalanche Interchain Messaging allows these independent networks to communicate through cryptographically verified messages, without requiring a shared execution layer.

The NYSE-affiliated tokenized securities platform is a particularly compelling example of why this architecture matters. Following more than a year of evaluation and testing across multiple blockchain networks, Avalanche technology was selected to provide its core ledger infrastructure.

Financial markets require infrastructure built around their own rules, participants, and regulatory obligations, not simply faster transactions on a shared chain.

Avalanche anticipated this need six years ago.

As more robots move towards real-world deployments, I think how we evaluate their performance is going to become increasingly important.

A robot completing a task successfully 98% of the time sounds impressive.

But what happens during the remaining 2%?

Does it recover on its own? Does it need human intervention? Can it handle the same task in a different environment?

These things matter a lot when you’re deploying robots commercially.

I think we’ll see a lot more focus on independent evaluations that measure real-world reliability, not just task success rates.

quoted_text:
Introducing Strongpoint MPC: Post-Quantum MPC, Without the Compromises

A breakthrough in threshold signing technology brings the security and performance of modern MPC into the quantum and AI era.

The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway. Blockchains, financial institutions, and digital asset infrastructure providers are preparing to replace the cryptographic algorithms that have secured digital ownership for decades. At the same time, advances in artificial intelligence are creating new uncertainty about the long-term security of existing cryptographic systems.

But replacing an algorithm is only part of the challenge. The infrastructure built around today's cryptography must also evolve, and few technologies are more important to institutional digital asset security than multi-party computation (MPC).

Today, Project Eleven is introducing Strongpoint MPC, a breakthrough in threshold cryptography that makes high-performance, post-quantum MPC practical. Our research demonstrates that migrating to post-quantum cryptography does not have to mean sacrificing the performance, flexibility, and security properties institutions have come to expect from traditional MPC. In fact, our approach can deliver signing performance that exceeds classical ECDSA-based MPC.

Strongpoint MPC is available within Strongpoint, Project Eleven’s institutional digital asset custody platform, enabling institutions to use post-quantum threshold signing while maintaining control over their assets and cryptographic key material.

The challenge with post-quantum MPC

MPC has become a foundational technology for securing digital assets. Rather than entrusting a private key to a single person, device, or system, MPC distributes signing authority across multiple independent parties. Transactions can be authorized without reconstructing the complete private key in any one location.

Today, this technology underpins institutional custody solutions used by exchanges, custodians, and financial institutions. Its applications extend well beyond moving funds, including blockchain validators, cross-chain bridges, oracles, and the administrative keys responsible for minting, freezing, and managing tokenized assets.

Over the last decade, MPC built around elliptic curve cryptography has become remarkably sophisticated. Institutions can coordinate signatures quickly, support complex approval structures, and operate distributed signing infrastructure with minimal latency. The transition to post-quantum cryptography threatens to disrupt much of that progress.

The mathematical properties that enable efficient threshold signing with ECDSA do not translate directly to post-quantum signature schemes. Hash-based signatures, in particular, have historically presented substantial challenges for MPC. Previous approaches suggested that generating a single threshold signature using certain hash-based constructions could take too long to be practical. For an institution processing transactions continuously, that kind of latency would make the technology impractical.

The apparent tradeoff was severe: preserve the performance of classical MPC while remaining exposed to future quantum threats, or adopt post-quantum protections at the expense of operational efficiency.

We've developed an approach that fundamentally changes that equation.

A breakthrough in post-quantum threshold cryptography

Project Eleven has developed a new approach to multi-party signing that dramatically improves the efficiency of post-quantum MPC. Our breakthrough enables high-performance threshold signing using hash-based cryptography, with techniques designed to extend across multiple signature schemes.

Where earlier approaches suggested impractically long signing times, our architecture enables post-quantum MPC signing that can even outperform traditional ECDSA-based MPC. Strongpoint MPC brings this research into a product designed for real-world institutional deployment.

Built for institutional infrastructure

Institutional MPC systems must accommodate different architectures, security policies, and operational requirements. A custody provider, a blockchain validator, and a stablecoin issuer may all rely on MPC, but their signing environments and security requirements can differ considerably.

Strongpoint MPC has been designed with this flexibility in mind:
- High-performance signing: Post-quantum threshold signatures with performance that can exceed traditional ECDSA-based MPC.
- Flexible threshold configurations: Supports the most common signing arrangements, with arbitrary threshold configurations under development.
- Dealerless key generation: Distributed key generation without requiring a trusted dealer, while retaining the flexibility to accommodate trusted-dealer setups.
- Efficient communication: An architecture designed to minimize communication overhead and support signing across distributed infrastructure.
- Signature indistinguishability: MPC produces signatures that are indistinguishable from ordinary signatures under the same scheme, without exposing the threshold configuration or participating signers through the signature itself.
- Institutional control: Deployment that allows institutions to maintain control over their signing infrastructure and cryptographic key material.

Stablecoin issuers, for example, must secure the administrative keys responsible for minting tokens, freezing assets, and managing critical smart contracts. Blockchain validators, cross-chain bridges, and oracles similarly rely on distributed signing infrastructure to protect sensitive operations.

All of these systems will eventually need to confront the transition to post-quantum cryptography, and they will not necessarily adopt the same cryptographic algorithms. Strongpoint MPC is designed with this diversity in mind, providing a foundation for supporting multiple signature schemes as cryptographic standards and blockchain requirements evolve.

The future of MPC is post-quantum and post-AI

Quantum computing threatens the mathematical assumptions underlying today's widely deployed public-key cryptography. Meanwhile, increasingly capable AI systems are accelerating mathematical research and cryptanalysis, introducing additional uncertainty around the long-term security of cryptographic systems.

Strongpoint is built around conservative cryptographic assumptions, crypto-agility and institutional control. Strongpoint MPC extends that approach to threshold signing, allowing institutions to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography without abandoning the distributed signing infrastructure they depend on.

For years, the industry has operated under the assumption that moving to post-quantum MPC would require meaningful sacrifices in performance and operational flexibility. Our breakthrough demonstrates that this does not have to be the case.

That's an exciting development for the future of digital asset security, and an important step toward making the post-quantum transition practical.

Learn more about Strongpoint MPC or reach out to our team today.

text:
📰 New research: Inside AI’s election news diet 

What news does AI read to get up to speed on politics? And what kind of news does it reward?

Following interesting recent commentary on our Japan election study from @mattyglesias, @JerusalemDemsas and @TheStalwart, we ran a bigger test on the US midterms across 35 Senate races, 18 days, and 15,750 answers.

What we found:

- Each model has its own favorite news outlet for political news: AP for GPT, Yahoo for Claude, PBS for Gemini, and NYT for Grok. 

- GPT tends to behave like a civic guide (reading more election office and campaign sites), whereas Claude behaves more like a news summarizer (reading national news, Wikipedia, polls).

- Grok draws on X and Gemini on YouTube for political information, far more than the other models we studied. Gemini cites YouTube in 55% of its answers and X shows up in 59% of Grok’s.

- A huge share of AI's local news is provided by large nonprofit networks that very few people will have heard of. States Newsroom, a large network of over 40 local newsrooms, appears in 60% of GPT’s answers.

- For many models, prediction markets are now a go-to source for polling information. Kalshi is cited more by Claude than any poll aggregator.

Full study here: https://t.co/AhVqULQvbI

Onchain, the @EntropyIO Anthropic perp is currently trading at $1.78T FDV. Open interest is at around $200M.

The easy headline: crypto traders and Wall Street disagree by ~$420B. But the truth is, the two numbers actually answer different questions.

An IPO price is negotiated. Banks usually set it below demand, so the stock tends to shoot up on day one. A perp, for its part, prices where the stock trades once anyone can buy it.

So part of that gap is the IPO discount, and part is the perp running hot.

The IPO side is already moving. Bloomberg reports the book was covered at launch, and according to the FT, bankers are weighing a price above the range.

Now, a look back at SpaceX. On listing morning, its perp traded around $176, about 30% above the $135 IPO price. The stock opened just above $150 and closed at $161, up 19%. The perp overshot the open by ~17%, but called the direction.

On the listing day, score the perps against the open and the close. That’s when we’ll see how well onchain price discovery did.
And beneath it all, there’s a quieter question: what does “Anthropic is worth X” actually mean?

At $78 a share, it’s $1.40T fully diluted, or about $1.02T on shares outstanding. Entropy prices against the fully diluted count. trade[.]xyz prices a single Class A share. Same company, different denominators.

Defining the reference is half the work of pricing anything onchain. At listing, Entropy’s oracle moves from a blend of its own order book and private-market data to share price × fully diluted shares, with the count fixed from the final prospectus.

Get the reference right, and onchain price discovery gets something real to bite into.

英伟达最大的风险之一，可能已经从技术竞争延伸到了政治博弈。

老黄一直主张美国继续向中国出售 AI 芯片，甚至公开把「China Hawk」称为「耻辱徽章」。

这套立场早就让他成为对华鹰派的攻击目标。

而这次私人关系被曝光，甚至牵扯到国家安全指控，也给了反对他的人更多施压的机会。

至于是不是一场有预谋的政治报复，目前没有证据。

但有意思的是，特朗普依然公开力挺老黄，而美国内部对华芯片政策的分歧始终存在。

这里其实有一个很现实的矛盾：

美国希望通过芯片出口维持全球技术影响力，同时又担心中国借助美国芯片缩小 AI 差距。

黄仁勋一直在这两种利益之间寻找空间。

对投资者来说，接下来真正值得关注的是：

1-独立调查最终是否发现国家安全问题。
2-美国是否进一步收紧对华芯片出口。
3-特朗普的支持能否转化为持续的政策空间。

这些问题将直接影响英伟达未来能够进入的市场，以及技术优势最终可以兑现成多少利润。

这件事也让我更深刻地意识到：

当一项技术重要到足以影响国家竞争，掌握技术的企业，也就不可避免地进入了政治博弈的中心。

过去我们评估科技公司的护城河，更多关注技术、产品和市场份额。

文章里我最喜欢的是一个小例子：作者让 ChatGPT 做一条视频广告，它串起了 Krea、Descript 和 ElevenLabs，做到一半还建议升级 Descript 的付费版。

用户一开始只是想做条视频，甚至没想过要买软件。Descript 的销售机会，是在 Agent 做到某一步、发现需要这项能力时出现的。

对软件公司来说，这就是 B2A 带来的分发变化：

过去你要等用户意识到自己需要一款工具，再去搜索、比较。

现在，Agent 在执行任务的过程中就可能选中你，GEO 的重要性是史无前例的。

而我们 Kite 更关心下一步：Agent 发现一项付费服务能帮它把任务做完，用户怎么授权它花这笔钱？如果一项任务要用好几个服务，我希望用户可以先定好预算和上限，再让 Agent 自己决定钱怎么花。

现在做互联网产品的公司都需要想清楚这个问题：用户把任务交给 Agent 之后，Agent 做到哪一步会选你的产品？

text:
Jensen Huang nearly lost NVIDIA three times before anyone cared.

First chip (NV1) bet on the wrong graphics math. Microsoft standardized on triangles. Almost everything shipped came back. Cash was measured in weeks.

He flew to Sega, admitted their next chip was a dead end, and asked them to cancel the contract but still pay the remaining money. They did. That cash bought one more shot.

RIVA 128 was designed almost entirely in simulation. No money for respins. It worked. A million units in four months. Company survived.

Years later, Intel used a licensing dispute to push NVIDIA out of the chipset business entirely. Jensen took the hit, exited, and doubled down elsewhere.

He then spent a decade building CUDA so GPUs could do more than graphics, for a market that barely existed. Wall Street hated it. He kept going.

When AI arrived, the architecture and software he had forced through were already there. One man absorbed the near-death cycles, the public failures, and the long years of no payoff, then delivered the platform the world is now running on.

That level of resilience, pain tolerance, and vision is rare. He should keep running NVIDIA.

Elon hires Jensen and puts him in charge of Terafab.

He's already said it publicly: hiring him would be an honor. And Terafab is the project made for him. A chip factory Musk wants to be the largest ever built, one terawatt of compute per year, from design to packaging under one roof. Terafab's challenge is to do in a few years what the industry took decades to build. There's only one man on Earth who knows every layer of that stack.

They execute like absolute maniacs.

Musk brings speed, capital and appetite for risk. Jensen brings thirty years of mastery of the stack: architecture, software, customers, supply chain. Musk builds factories faster than anyone alive. SpaceXAI merges with Tesla.

This isn't even science fiction anymore: independent committees are already studying the merger. Rockets, satellites, AI, robots, self-driving cars, energy, and now chips. One single entity, integrated from silicon to orbit.

The group climbs to $50 trillion.

Today, SpaceX and Tesla are worth around $3.4 trillion combined. $50 trillion sounds insane. But remember: ten years ago, Nvidia was worth a few tens of billions. Jensen becomes the chip boss again.

It's creating the biggest competitor in its history.

text:
Jensen Huang’s resignation ends an era at NVIDIA and forces a stress test on the AI trade.

Huang wasn’t just a CEO. He was the face, the product visionary and the operator who turned NVIDIA into the $4T+ foundation of the AI boom. Key-man risk was always priced in at some level; today it is no longer theoretical. $NVDA stock is already down hard (10%+ in premarket) and the rest of the AI complex is feeling the spillover.

The near-term picture is messy. Leadership uncertainty, succession questions and the China-related overhang from the scandal create real noise. Colette Kress (long-time CFO, now interim CEO) and the existing leadership team provide operational continuity and the board has appointed Harvey Jones as its first Chair. Product roadmaps, CUDA lock-in and hyperscaler demand don’t disappear overnight. Still, the narrative premium from $NVDA is gone.

The setup for a multi-week rally is strong. AI stocks were already deeply oversold coming into this news after the recent sharp selloff. Technicals are washed out, sentiment is depressed and multiple strategists had already called the prior dip extreme. Forced selling and panic often exhaust quickly in these regimes. A relief bounce across the AI complex over the next several weeks looks highly probable as the dust settles.

The multi-month view is more nuanced. The AI infrastructure buildout itself is not over. Capex remains massive, data-centre demand is still the dominant growth driver and the underlying technology stack (accelerated computing, inference, networking) continues to expand. What changes is that NVIDIA must now prove it can execute without its founder-CEO narrative. Succession clarity, any regulatory/export fallout and whether the next permanent CEO can maintain the same cultural and technical intensity will decide if this is a healthy reset or the start of a longer period of relative underperformance versus the broader AI complex.

This is a classic “sell the rumor / buy the fact” environment for the trade. Oversold conditions favour a multi-week bounce. The multi-month case for AI stocks rests on whether the structural demand story can remain intact and companies with high margins, FCF and strong balance-sheets are likely to outperform. https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

text:
After Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia, the company's existing management efficiency and strategic execution system may undergo structural changes. This is because Jensen Huang previously built a highly flat management system at Nvidia that relied heavily on his personal leadership. Its advantages were fast information transmission, short decision chains, and unified strategic execution. In the past, this reliance was converted into a competitive advantage through his personal capabilities.

So I think the key thing to watch next is whether Nvidia can truly convert Jensen Huang's individual organizational coordination ability into sustainable institutional capability.

text:
老黄走了，我还是保黄派

今天，黄仁勋辞职了。

先交代立场：我是英伟达的小股东，小到不值一提，人生中买的第一只美股也是英伟达。

我是坚定的保黄派，利益使然，立场使然。

只需要算一笔很功利的账。

老黄在，意味着什么？

意味着英伟达在北京、上海、深圳有近 4000 名员工，光上海研发中心就有 2000 多人，张江还盖了一栋 16 层的新楼。

意味着在华盛顿对华政策最紧绷的那几年，他把上海的摊子留住了，还扩了，所以你才会在小红书上刷到上海英伟达员工晒一年交几百万个税。

意味着你家孩子学半导体，你那个读电子工程的高中同学，往英伟达投简历的时候，面试官里有人跟他说同一种语言，知道他从哪儿来。

无论在大陆还是台湾，大家或多或少都觉得英伟达是自己家的公司。

换一个 CEO 会怎样？

看看硅谷。微软、谷歌、Adobe、IBM，印度裔一个接一个坐上头把交椅。

他们身后，是一整条印度工程师的上升通道：老乡带老乡，校友提携校友，然后食堂充满咖喱的味道。

今天，这扇门关上了一半。

同样的道理，我也支持 Binance、OKX、HTX、Bybit、Bitget 这些华人背景的交易所。

理由一样简单：作为华人，你背景好一点，在里面谋个生计并不难；遇到问题，你还能在 X 上 @ 一姐、@老徐，闹一闹，总会有个结果。

要是华人交易所都倒了，大家都去用海外交易所，遇到事儿了：你他妈谁呀？滚一边去。

我很庸俗，成年人的世界就是这样：理想挂在墙上，饭碗端在手里。

老黄走了，我的立场没变。

没了老黄的英伟达，只能祝福。

HOY ANUNCIAMOS QUE COCOS RECIBIÓ US$34 MILLONES EN SU PRIMERA RONDA DE INVERSIÓN, A UNA VALUACIÓN DE US$508 MILLONES. UN POQUITO MÁS DE MEDIO UNICORNIO 🦄🤪.

La ronda fue liderada por Kaszek, uno de los fondos de venture capital más importantes de Latinoamérica, fundado por Hernán Kazah y Nicolás Szekasy, y contó también con la participación de SPICE Ventures.
Pero detrás de esta noticia hay una historia que me gusta mucho más contar.

En 2021, cuando arrancamos con @nicomindlin en la oficinita de la foto, éramos “los chicos de Instagram”. Desde las redes les hablábamos a miles de personas sobre qué hacer con su plata. Y queríamos dar un paso más: construir las herramientas para que cualquiera pudiera invertir, sin importar cuánto tuviera.

En ese momento, construir un producto para alguien que tenía apenas 100 dólares era una apuesta poco convencional. Pero nosotros veíamos una oportunidad enorme.
Porque si esos 100 dólares eran todos tus ahorros, ¿por qué no ibas a merecer las mismas herramientas que alguien que tenía un millón?

Con esa convicción compramos una sociedad de bolsa y lanzamos la app. Al año siguiente empezamos a construir nuestra propia tecnología. Después llegaron nuevos productos, fondos, pagos, crypto y una tarjeta.
Y un día, los chicos de Instagram estábamos anunciando que comprábamos un banco.
Un banco. Todavía me suena increíble escribirlo.

También anunciamos la compra de Warren en Brasil, sujeta a la aprobación del Banco Central de Brasil, para llevar esa misma visión a más personas en la región.
Cuando tenía 17 años y vivía en Corrientes, soñaba con construir una empresa que pudiera darle un servicio a millones de personas. No sabía exactamente cómo lo iba a hacer, pero tenía muy claro que quería intentarlo.

Hoy somos casi 300 personas trabajando para hacer realidad ese sueño. Más de 2,5 millones de clientes nos eligen y construimos una compañía que vale más de US$500 millones.
Y lo que más me entusiasma es que seguimos teniendo la misma convicción que en aquella primera oficina: que las mejores herramientas financieras tienen que estar al alcance de todos.

Esta inversión nos permite dar un paso más hacia nuestra ambición de construir el banco de inversión digital más grande de Latinoamérica.

Nada de esto hubiera sido posible sin Nico, sin el equipo extraordinario que construimos y sin cada una de las personas que confió en nosotros desde el primer día.

Cinco años después, miro aquella oficinita y me cuesta creer todo lo que pasó.
Y lo mejor es que todavía tenemos muchísimo por construir. 🚀

text:
Personal update: what am I up to?

After leaving the EF in April, I took the summer off with a plan to focus my time more in the fall. I decided what I really wanted to do was learn something new. The last 10 years have been a marathon, and while I learned a lot building a company and then as leadership at the EF, there's a different kind of joy in the kind of self-directed learning I can do with free time, fewer responsibilities, and access to the greatest educational tools that have ever existed (LLMs).

Pretty quickly I decided the thing I was most excited to dive into was AI. After a few weeks of experimentation, I've settled into a ~full time syllabus and course structure managed by Claude that I am happy with.

Why? Justifying interest in AI in 2026 is unnecessary, but here's how I ended up here:

- My sabbatical has given me more space to ask a wider set of questions about the future and the choices my family will have to make. How and where should we live? What risks will my family, friends, and communities face? How should we invest? What will happen to Canada? What will happen to Ethereum? How should I think about the next 10 years of my professional life? What are the most important problems to solve? What skills and knowledge do I need to contribute to solving them?

- The possible answers to every one of those questions felt dominated by uncertainty about AI. I'm persuaded that some things could start to move *very* fast in the next 12-18 months, and that even in a world of a pause/pace or an unexpected scaling wall, what we have today is enough to radically change the world. Making reasonable decisions about the future feels impossible without understanding this at a much more granular level.

- Separate from any pragmatic reasons, it's also just... the most interesting thing happening in the world? We're making minds; I would like to know them. I remember taking Kurzweil's The Age of Intelligent Machines out from my local library in the mid 1990s, and growing up reading books like Accelerando and expecting the singularity. It's happening now, and while my emotions about it range from terror to giddy curiosity, I have a hard time thinking about much else.

I don't know where this focus will lead me, but it's been very satisfying to dive into a new technical domain and learn something fresh from the ground up like I did in ~2014. Does that mean I am "leaving Ethereum"? No, but the range of things I think / write / tweet about is going to shift around and follow my interests for a while. I still believe Ethereum is critical-path civilizational infrastructure for our future, but I am less sure than ever before about the terrain of that future and what risks and opportunities Ethereum will face. If I did take on a new role in the Ethereum ecosystem in the future, I can't imagine being effective anyways without catching up to the AI frontier first and learning new ways to work.

ETF, ETPs, CFTC futures, a transfer agent, MiCA, a dedicated rail for banks, privacy on the way, and real institutions already settling onchain. Most chains talk about institutions. Injective has been building the plumbing for them.

text:
Jensen is out

Infidelity is obviously bad

But his contributions to American innovation and AI leadership cannot be overstated

Jensen started NVIDIA in 1993, where he pioneered the graphics chip market when this was non-obvious

Back in 2012, Ilya Sustkever trained AlexNet on NVIDIA GPUs — thereby creating the “deep learning” age

Jensen was one of the earliest to be AI pilled and he re-oriented NVDA towards AI in the mid 2010s — none of his competitors were even thinking this way

In 2020 he acquired Mellanox for $7B. This was an Israeli company that’s irrelevant for computer graphics but was essential for AI compute — wildly increasing the bandwidth between GPUs, necessary to build high performance AI server racks (rather than just good chips)

Once AI took off, Jensen was one of the biggest champions of the ecosystem

He was technical enough to be confident about where things were going, and had enough credibility as a founder CEO that he oftentimes made risky bets on next-generation technologies or companies that helped keep American AI on the efficient frontier

Recently he was investing in open source, photonics and robotics. These areas will all be feeling his loss

Earlier he was a champion of most of America’s leading AI companies when they were unproven

He made huge mistakes with his infidelity, which is tragic for his family and NVDA

But simultaneously he will leave a huge void, with the loss of a: technical, aggressive, founder-CEO

The American AI community needs to work double-time in an attempt to fill this void

抓住生活作风问题，利用媒体造势，渲染未经证实的国家安全与职业道德问题，最终将 Jensen 赶出了 Nvidia。

中美对抗、世界分裂的一个缩影，将这样被记录在历史之中。

在大学时，我也曾是一名理想的自由主义者，相信普世价值，认为天下大同，认为自己是世界公民。后来学习了国际政治和历史的数个课程，了解了美国在拉丁美洲的作为，学习了二战之前的西方历史与民族主义思潮的起源，渐渐转变了我的想法——我从一名自由主义者，逐渐接受了现实主义的立场。

而后我来到欧洲学习与生活，不得不感受到隐形的结构性的歧视与隔离，尽管我已经被包裹在最为理想主义的校园里，我也能体会到人用种族、民族、肤色与文化建立的现实的区隔，这一区隔在课本里丝毫没有提及，承认这一区隔是教育所禁止与避免的，但这一区隔却被迫存在于傲慢与偏见之中。

一个皈依者永远不能成为“我们”的一员，世界大同只是一场经济上行时迷离的幻梦。人与人之间的竞争、嫉妒与敌视，不得不存在于民族之间，也不得不存在于民族之内。

我们人类总是乐意为自己贴上诸多标签，而后排除异己，并将这一点视为正义的行为。

这很愚蠢，也很荒诞，但很真实。

按照Anthropic当下每股70至78美元发行8.25亿股，最高融资644亿美元计算，上市估值在9200-1.02万亿之间，相比于此前1.5-2万亿之间估值打了对折。

不过从SpaceX上市来看宽幅震荡也很正常，毕竟现在的美股振幅比山寨币都猛，SPCX股价此前遭遇过228-104的腰斩，所以Anthropic估值随着市场情绪大幅波动再正常不过了。

从34亿购买燃气轮机发电到紧急发布Fable5.2，可以看出A家对于上市也是拼尽了全力，绝不会像有些人说的那样取消上市，因为不论是A家还是美股其实都承受不起这种巨型跳票，且不说多少利益相关方绑定在上面等着变现。如果因为市场行情不好就取消IPO，那么市场情绪只会受刺激进一步变成甚至进入死亡螺旋，无论民主党还是共和党都不敢也不能承受这种可能性，之后擎天保驾是必然的。

等到Anthropic真上市的时候，必然会跟随大盘情绪有一个较大的系数调整，假如到时候市场情绪已经修复且流动性良好，在万亿估值基准上上浮50%都是有可能得。

但假如到时候情绪依然处在低谷，那么Anthropic的上市价格相比SPCX会少了很多水分。在AI赛道全面从看融资能力看资本支出转向终端收入之际。一个低估的市值其实更有成长性，低价上车坐稳比高开高走剧烈洗盘可能还要稳。

text:
Jensen (October 2026) says he hoped he'd still be Nvidia CEO 20 years from now

"My management style is what made it possible for the company to grow. Our organization is what made the company to thrive and innovate. I wanted to create an architecture of a company with as few silos as possible."

"The problem with silos, if the organizations are too rigid, then the company has very difficult time adapting to change. So I think a modern company really wants to be more and more agile and less and less structured."

Emily Chang: "Your son and your daughter are working at Nvidia. I think your son-in-law also works at Nvidia. Robotics, yeah. There is talk that your daughter is in line to be your successor. Is that true?"

Jensen: "I don't hope the job on her. And the reason for that is because that's their aspiration, Spencer or Madison's, they have to go earn it. And it's really, really hard work."

"When you're the CEO of a company, you have to focus on, of course, your family, but I've got a whole bunch of other families I'm caring for. I'm responsible for an entire industry. The pressure of being the CEO is high and it's supposed to be high. It should not be an easy job."

"I'm really hoping that the next CEO of the company is already at the company, but 20 years from now, I hope I stay healthy and I hope I continue to earn my keep, but so long as I can do that, 20 years from now, I hope they're already here, but they have to earn it."

"Just as I can be fired, the next CEO has to be hired. And I like it that way. I like that we can't be overly complacent about our position inside the company and that we can't take it for granted. And you're always vulnerable, you're always earning it, you're always striving to be better. That's a condition that's good."

text:
Tarek predicted 5 month ago that Citadel would sue Kalshi.

In this interview from June, @mansourtarek_ explains exactly why stock perps would be a big threat to Wall Street.

Now Citadel, CME, Cboe and Nasdaq are suing him to stop Kalshi from offering perps.

Here is why.

1 - THEY FEAR LOSING RETAIL

Citadel executes ~35% of US-listed retail volume and make money by trading against their orders. Stock perps threaten to redirect that activity.

If someone trades an Apple perp on Kalshi instead of Apple shares, Citadel loses.

Their own court filing explicitly admit to it:

- “Cboe and Citadel Securities lose transactions and revenue they cannot later recover.”
- “Kalshi's offering is designed to draw away CME’s customers who currently trade futures.”

2 - PERPS GENERATE LESS FEES

So why wouldn't Citadel just offer Perps themselve ?

Because traditional futures have an expiry date. To keep your exposure you need to close you old position and open a new ones. Those additional transactions generate fees. 

Perps don’t expire, removing those fees entirely.

The interview passage where Tarek highlights this Perps over Futures advantage is even cited by CME in the lawsuit.

That's why the Citadel camp is asking to reclassify Perps as security-based swaps:

1) Citadel wins - Perps are SEC regulated, retails can't trade them, they keep trading future on their exchange.

2) Kalshi wins - Perps are CFTC regulated, retail can trade them over more expensive futures, Kalshi receive their order flow.

It's all about who gets to farm retail.

Six months ex-Apple, I clock in this morning for my first paid project for @DaywardAI. I’m installing local AI for a customer who needs privacy and security for their data. It’s a pretty straightforward project: local RAG, data ingest and vector search, on-demand and scheduled reporting, and automated competitive analysis.

We picked 2x DGX Sparks to start because they can expand easily to 4x or even 8x Sparks, or we can add a DGX Station or a 5090 tower.

The harness will be Hermes Agent, running GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, or 2x Qwen 3.8 Flash Next. (Testing, will report results!) We’re also using Laya as a decision model, and may swap in other models, like Inkling, for overnight batch doc ingest.

The Sparks will be off the internet. A dedicated Linux box will do the competitive analysis, using @slashlast30days and other tools to gather current info on the customer and its competitors.

quoted_text:
Why Uniswap is losing USDC-USDT Market Share to Fluid and Metric

Background:
USDC-USDT is Ethereum's most traded DEX pair at ~$480M a day, almost 2x USDC-WETH. In five weeks, Uniswap's share of it fell from 58% to 36%.

Uniswap's volume didn't drop. It stayed around $1B-$1.3B a week, apart from the 26 Oct spike, while the pair grew from ~$2.3B to over $3.3B a week, and the growth went elsewhere:
• Metric: from 0.6% to 14%
• Aero: from 0% to 6%
• Fluid: steady at 20-28%

Where Uniswap lost is big trades:
• Over $1M: from 85% to 44%, with Fluid going from 10% to 43%
• $100K to $1M: from 36% to 21%, with Metric going from 7% to 28%
• Under $10K: from 50% to 44%, still the leader but Metric also grown from 7%-16%

What is the cause?
It's not fees. Uniswap's USDC-USDT pools charge 0.07 to 0.12bp, already among the lowest. Its stable-pair hook isn't the reason either, since it was set up the same way when Uniswap held 58% market share.

It's depth at the live price during volatility. USDT slipped from around par to 8-15bp below USDC in the second half of October. Arbitrage moves Uniswap's price, but LP liquidity stays in the ranges LPs chose. Active depth in the main pool fell from ~$900K per bp on 15 Oct to ~$310K on 28 Oct.

The other reason is Aero has entered Ethereum during the same period and has captured ~6% of the trading volume overall.

Why other DEXs are not impacted?
Fluid draws depth from its lending vaults around a center price it can move, and Metric's market makers quote from their own inventory at the live price. Both keep size where the trades are, so aggregators send the big orders there.

If the market calms down next week, watch whether the big trades come back to Uniswap or stay with Fluid, Aero and Metric.

Protecting user funds is a top priority at Flying Tulip.

Security means more than audits. It also means limiting the damage if something goes wrong. 

Our circuit breaker system caps how much value can leave the protocol within a set time window. 

Abnormal outflows above limits are restricted or queued, slowing potential drains and giving the team time to investigate, respond and contain an incident.

text:
Onchain security needs to be multilayered. Audits + deployment reviews + ongoing pentesting + interval scans + circuit breakers + deposit & borrow caps + total exposure risks.

The days of immutability & free flows simply don't protect users enough.

Jensen is out

Infidelity is obviously bad

But his contributions to American innovation and AI leadership cannot be overstated

Jensen started NVIDIA in 1993, where he pioneered the graphics chip market when this was non-obvious

Back in 2012, Ilya Sustkever trained AlexNet on NVIDIA GPUs — thereby creating the “deep learning” age

Jensen was one of the earliest to be AI pilled and he re-oriented NVDA towards AI in the mid 2010s — none of his competitors were even thinking this way

In 2020 he acquired Mellanox for $7B. This was an Israeli company that’s irrelevant for computer graphics but was essential for AI compute — wildly increasing the bandwidth between GPUs, necessary to build high performance AI server racks (rather than just good chips)

Once AI took off, Jensen was one of the biggest champions of the ecosystem

He was technical enough to be confident about where things were going, and had enough credibility as a founder CEO that he oftentimes made risky bets on next-generation technologies or companies that helped keep American AI on the efficient frontier

Recently he was investing in open source, photonics and robotics. These areas will all be feeling his loss

Earlier he was a champion of most of America’s leading AI companies when they were unproven

He made huge mistakes with his infidelity, which is tragic for his family and NVDA

But simultaneously he will leave a huge void, with the loss of a: technical, aggressive, founder-CEO

The American AI community needs to work double-time in an attempt to fill this void

text:
趁着dip买入了一箩筐的英伟达，在这个特殊的时间节点，但其实这是一个非常复杂，我自己也没想清楚的决定。

黄仁勋持股仅约 3.58%（截至2026年3月23日委托书），一股一票，没有双重股权或超级投票权。1993年联合创办英伟达后，另外两位联合创始人逐步淡出，黄仁勋成为唯一长期留在核心岗位的创始人。从游戏GPU到AI算力霸主，业绩记录本身构成了极强的个人权威。

黄自己说过有约60名高管直接向他汇报（内部记录显示曾在30-60人之间波动），几乎没有传统层级。公司没有COO，也没有公开的“二号人物”。所有重大决策基本由他拍板，信息传递直接到达。这种结构让公司运转高度依赖他个人。

11人董事会中，黄是唯一非独立董事，其余10人均为独立董事。多位董事从公司成立早期就在任（平均任期近15年），与黄共事超过30年。他不兼任董事长，由首席独立董事（目前是Stephen Neal）牵头监督。董事会长期对其战略判断高度信任。

黄仁勋公开表示不相信传统意义上的接班人规划（“I’m famous in saying that I don’t believe in succession planning”）。公司年报和委托书几乎不提“succession”一词，只笼统警告对长期高管团队的依赖。分析师普遍认为：“Jensen is Nvidia”。

黄仁勋的控制是软性权威控制，而非法律或股权上的硬控制。它建立在持续兑现的业绩、扁平化组织对个人判断的依赖，以及董事会与股东的长期信任之上。一旦业绩失速、信任崩塌或出现严重治理问题，这种控制力会迅速削弱——因为法律上董事会随时可以换人，而公司内部又缺乏现成的接班人。

英伟达是一家极其出色甚至伟大的公司，而这个出色从 1080 显卡出来的黄金游戏年代一直到今天，其实成也在于这样的组织架构，但不知道败会不会因为它这样的组织架构。

如同 @aleabitoreddit 所说，围绕着黄的这样一套决策流程、集体认同和个人的远见缔造了英伟达在三个时代的领先，而这一切在被政治无情地玩弄，并且在今天，这样的组织架构似乎 officially 画上了句号。这是令人难过的一天。这似乎也印证了很多人想逃避、但不得不面对和承认的现实，也就是作为一个从小就来到美国的移民，干出了惊天动地的大成绩，把一家初创公司从零到有，做成了目前世界上无可争议的最重要的公司之一，你依然是得不到政治核心圈的认同的，甚至随时可能成为政治斗争的牺牲品。这一点，反而恰恰好发生在以移民国家著称的美国。

以及目前铺天盖地的对于华人男性、华人女性、整体华人，甚至是整体亚洲人的系统性歧视，似乎也甚嚣尘上。而这一切，只是因为你的皮肤不是白色的，同时，你控制着整个国家甚至整个世界最重要的公司之一。I really do think很多在调侃的人没有意识到这点。从民主党主流媒体的措辞以及主要喉舌的言论来看，they call the woman "Chinese spy", "Asian chicks", so that when referring to national security, they can call any Asian "spy", and they can call any woman "Asian chicks" without any explicit evidence。人家看不起你，你还要调侃什么“老黄用鸡巴顶破了 AI 的泡沫”，本身就是一件很可笑的事情。即使你站在世界顶端，依然有人想用无耻的理由把你拉下马，同样的事情换成白人CEO就没事，这种事在金融和科技业已经发生过多次。

我为什么选择了买入？

当然最简单的就是技术形态以及估值。英伟达目前已经到了相当有吸引力的空间，业绩的确定性极其强，以及接下来几个财年的表现，下限几乎可以被完全锁死，而上限依然有想象空间。产业链上下游陆陆续续交出的最新季报，其实也表明：即使下游乃至中游投入和收入的二阶导下降，作为几乎最上游的英伟达，依然能贡献出色的业绩表现以及不可撼动的地位。推理可以用很多其他芯片代替，但在训练（尤其是后训练）上几乎没有替代品；在软件护城河上，同样没有任何替代品。短期内由于算力已经被大批量投入，此时再换基础架构，不管是在物理上还是软件上都是极其困难的。

其次，目前英伟达的价格最大的不确定性来自于新的领导班底：也就是在目前飞速迅猛的发展之下，会不会有能在算力硬件层面上挑战英伟达的公司？而且英伟达当前的领导层，是一个围绕着单一、极具真知灼见的超级创始人进行协作的角色层。如果这样一位创始人被赶走了，会不会导致公司的业务以及方向出现判断失误，甚至面临被替代、被挑战的风险？这个我觉得绝对是有的，而且它也被 consider 到了当前的负风险溢价里。但交易的想法是，最坏的事情已经发生，管理决策层的过渡只是时间问题。不论新的管理层如何发挥，很多公司层面的事情其实没有改变：工程师互相协作的方式没有改变，护城河也没有改变，领导变了，新一代的GPU和新版本的CUDA还是会如期释出。如果说真的是因为对判断问题，导致未来被替代、落后，那是后面才需要考虑的事情。至少在短期两三年内，我觉得发生这种事情的可能性非常低。

看长做长，看短做短，现在该选择做短。

text:
在币圈玩久了的兄弟都知道，跨链桥一直是黑客最爱盯着的提款机。🧐

为啥老出事？说白了一句话：链和链之间是眼盲的。

A链上的合约，根本看不见B链上发生了啥。你在A链转了钱，B链要给你发币，中间得靠一个传话筒去确认。

以前很多跨链桥爆雷，就是传话筒太单一，要么靠几个节点，要么靠一家机构。黑客只要搞定那几个私钥，伪造一条假消息，池子就被掏空了。

而 LayerZero V2 的思路挺聪明：验证权交给项目方自己选，这就是 DVN（去中心化验证网络）。项目方自己挑几个裁判，所有裁判都点头，这笔跨链才算数。

就在刚刚，Flare( @FlareNetworks) 官宣作为 DVN 接入 #LayerZero！📊

含金量到底多高？咱们不整晦涩的技术黑话，聊聊它牛在哪，还有跟手里的 $FLR 有啥关系！

1️⃣ 别人是单兵作战，#Flare 是整张网给你背书

现在 LayerZero 上的 DVN 不少，但很多是单一机构或者少数节点在跑。

Flare 背后是自家的数据协议 FDC（Flare Data Connector），还有 100 多个独立数据提供商。一笔跨链消息发出来，不是某台服务器点个头就完事，而是这 100 多个节点各自去源链查账。

只有按质押权重算的大多数节点都确认，这事儿真发生了，才会生成加密证明，通过 Flare 的 Relay 合约传到目标链放行。

对项目方来说（比如用 OFT 标准的 USDT、PayPal 稳定币、Ondo 这些），等于多请了一个独立公证人。它不替代原来的验证器，是直接叠加。黑客想作恶，得同时攻破你原来的防线和 Flare 整张网的共识，难度直接拉满。

2️⃣ 不再只是 XRP 的配角

以前一提 #Flare，大家第一反应都是 XRPFi。确实，靠这套数据验证，它已经在 7 条链上铸造了数百万枚 FXRP，把 XRP 的 DeFi 盘活了。

但这次接入 LayerZero，是 Flare 的数据基建第一次走出自家生态，给全链市场做安全底座。你的资产哪怕不经过 Flare 链，只要在 LayerZero 上跨链，就能用上它的验证服务。天花板一下就打开了。

3️⃣ 重点来了，跟 $FLR 有啥关系？

你看看，Flare 这次可不是免费打工，商业闭环是直接绑在代币经济里的：

• 真金白银的收入：项目方调用 Flare DVN，虽然是用自己链的代币付费，但底层每次验证都会变成一次 FDC 请求，必须用 $FLR 支付。

• 90% 费用进 FIRE：按 FIP.16 提案，每笔 FDC 费用的 90% 流入协议收入引擎 FIRE。FIRE 干嘛的？按计划回购并销毁 $FLR，实打实的通缩。

• 外部流量反哺：以前 $FLR 的需求，主要看自家生态和 XRPFi 热不热。现在只要外部主流链的跨链量起来（首发以太坊和 Flare 主网，后续 EVM 链不用改代码就能铺开），全网跨链流量都会变成 $FLR 的买盘和销毁动力。

最后，总结一下，LayerZero 占了全链 USD 转账量的 80% 以上，累计交易额破 3000 亿美元。Flare 以网络级安全裁判的身份切进这个核心枢纽，既补上了跨链最缺的去中心化验证，也给自己接了一条来自全网的水龙头。

12月初Flare DVN主网上线后，大家可以盯紧公开的 Dune 数据面板。当越来越多头部资产把 Flare 写进自己的安全白名单，市场自然会重新给这套数据基建定价。

拭目以待，别盲目冲，DYOR🙏

其实不太想再刷到“I'm not a Chinese spy”配性感自拍的帖子了。我知道发图的女生朋友只是想展示自己的美，顺便蹭个热点、拿点流量，大部分人没想太多。

我不是什么极端女权，也不想得罪谁。只是作为一个以后打算长期在美国生活的人，考虑到亚洲女性在国外的生态位已经够差了，我会担心以后别人见到我，第一反应就带着这个刻板印象，拿“Chinese spy”来物化我。

这让我想起《坏血》的原型伊丽莎白·霍姆斯。她作为女性创业者杀进硅谷，丑闻曝光后有很长一段时间，女性创业者去融资，都会被投资人问一句：“你怎么保证你不是下一个霍姆斯？”一个人的丑闻和刻板印象，最后让所有女性创业者一起买单。

我不喜欢这个梗，说到底是不喜欢它背后的叙事：中国女人被某个有权有势的男人“选中”，成了成功男性、尤其是白人男性身上的时尚单品。这套叙事默认女性是客体，是被挑选的一方，而被挑中仅仅是因为她好看。她成了一只蛊惑人的蜜罐，表面甜，像在调情，可越看越让人不舒服：她被性化成了一个关于遥远东方的、现代刻板政治的性幻想。

所以我会觉得不舒服。我不是共产党的任何皮套，也不想做任何上位男人身边的“Chinese baddie”。我讨厌被性化、被凝视、被上位者选择并被他们赞美为“蜜罐”或者是“你美得就像Chinse Spy”.

author: soundfury
quoted_text:
Sex, spy and chips：

黃仁勳的間諜美人案真是我們眼前的世紀大案。
關鍵是，Megaspeed這公司問題這麼可疑，輝達真的不知道嗎？

雖然他們現在說他們查過毫無問題，但如果是這樣，美國商務部不會早開始查。所以老黃很可能知法犯法嗎？

紐約時報去年報導指出：「為揭示Megaspeed不透明運營的模式，《紐約時報》走訪了四個國家的相關地點，查閱貨運記錄、商業註冊文件、影片及照片，並採訪了30餘人。記者通過企業登記信息追蹤到馬來西亞的一處數據中心和一家購物中心、新加坡的一間近乎空置的辦公室，以及吉隆坡郊外一間破舊的店面。」

整理一下這家公司的背景和可疑處：
2022年底，美國政府開始限制向中國出售先進人工智慧晶片，擔心這些關鍵零組件可能讓北京在經濟與軍事領域取得優勢。

2023年，黃樂透過一家英屬維京群島公司，收購了線上遊戲公司「第七大道」（7Road）位於新加坡的子公司。第七大道與她在上海的商業網絡有所關聯，。收購後，這家新加坡公司更名為 Megaspeed，她擔任董事總經理。同年稍晚，根據新加坡公司登記資料，Megaspeed 的所有權又轉移至另一家設於新加坡的空殼公司Swiftdata。兩家公司登記的主要職員人數都很少。

Megaspeed 又成立了馬來西亞子公司，隨後將其伺服器設備與智慧財產權抵押給阿里巴巴旗下名為 Apex 的子公司。阿里巴巴後來成為 Megaspeed 最主要的客戶。

2023年，這家公司的總資產僅有3,300萬美元，營收為零；到了2024年，總資產卻暴增至30億美元，短短一年成長約91倍，營收也躍升至2.94億美元（約新台幣94億元）。
一家原本營收為零、資產僅數千萬美元的公司，如何在一年內累積30億美元的資產？

另一方面，Megaspeed 在馬來西亞的關係企業，從2024年6月至2026年2月購入至少48億美元的高階AI設備，涉及輝達晶片與相關技術。

關鍵是，這些晶片是留在東南亞還是運到中國？

美國政府自2024年起就開始調查 Megaspeed 的晶片流向，認為這公司涉嫌將輝達AI晶片走私至中國。年底走訪馬來西亞一處資料中心時，發現輝達設備仍然裝在箱子裡，並未實際安裝使用。調查人員因而懷疑，該設施可能只是設備進出的中轉站。

彭博社的調查指出，輝達曾檢查 Megaspeed 在東南亞的資料中心，涉及三個國家、八家企業的12處設施。他們向美國政府提供盤點資料，表示相關設備均在應有的位置。但彭博社分析貿易紀錄後發現，輝達提供的盤點數量，比經由硬體合作夥伴銷售給 Megaspeed 的晶片少了約5萬顆。這個差距可能涉及數十億美元的設備價值。

然而，為什麼一家規模有限的企業能夠取得這麼多晶片？

2025年8月，輝達法律長 Tim Teter 曾直接聯繫美國商務部調查人員，表示已獲高層官員 Jeff Kessler 許可，可以詢問相關案件。此後，案件轉交司法部，商務部的調查工作暫停。

好，所以回到問題，輝達是否知道Megaspeed有問題？

輝達並不是一家普通的晶片供應商。它的產品是全球人工智慧競爭的關鍵基礎設施，美國政府對高階晶片出口中國的限制，也使它的交易具有特殊的地緣政治意義。當企業的產品具有這樣的戰略重要性，它就不能只以「我們把產品賣給合法的經銷商」來完全解除自身責任。
如果特定客戶已經出現多項重大警訊，企業就有責任進行更深入的盡職調查，而不是把合規責任完全推給下游。

這就來到問題的核心
黃仁勳究竟只是與一名涉嫌情報活動的商業人士發生私人關係，還是這段關係曾經影響輝達的商業決策、出口管制遵循，以及美國政府的調查？（兩人在2024年底關係就很好。）

author: Bookof_Eth
quoted_text:
Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) has resigned as CEO of Nvidia.

Reports describe two alleged affairs, one involving a Chinese citizen that raised concerns within the US government about possible foreign intelligence targeting. Nvidia has not publicly given a reason for his departure.

Whatever people think of the circumstances, I find this deeply sad.

Because look at what we chose to measure.

Not 33 years of building.

Not the countless doors he helped open.

Not the generations of people whose lives were changed by what he created.

His private life.

In 1993, Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia. What followed was extraordinary.

GPUs that transformed gaming. Hardware that helped make cryptocurrency mining possible. Computing power that accelerated scientific discovery. Chips that became part of the foundation of the AI revolution.

Think about how many people built careers, businesses, discoveries and dreams on technology his company helped bring into the world.

That is a legacy no headline can erase.

And I cannot ignore another question.

This is my opinion, not an established fact: I believe he may have been targeted. Reports of possible foreign intelligence involvement deserve serious scrutiny.

When the leader of one of the world's most strategically important technology companies suddenly disappears from his position, asking who benefits is not unreasonable.

But suspicion is not proof. And the truth matters.

So does something else.

We live in a world where it takes decades to build something extraordinary, but only moments for the conversation to forget everything you built.

We can acknowledge someone's mistakes without reducing their entire existence to them.

We can demand accountability without abandoning gratitude.

A person's private failures do not automatically erase a lifetime of public contributions.

And perhaps the saddest part is what this moment reveals about us.

We became more fascinated by the man behind the headlines than by the extraordinary things he helped humanity achieve.

History should remember more than someone's worst chapter.

It should remember what they gave the world.

Jensen, whatever comes next, I hope you know that millions of people have been touched by something you helped create, even if they never knew your name.

Thank you for 33 years of building. Thank you for helping shape a generation. Thank you for showing what one vision, pursued relentlessly, can become.

I'm sorry for how this chapter has unfolded.

And I hope your legacy is remembered in its entirety.

🙏📖

text:
Trezor Investigation Update: Malicious Circuit Boards Found in Three Safe 5 Wallets

Hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor provided an update on its investigation into hardware tampering involving devices sold by reseller CryptoBilis. After inspecting devices from 48 users who contacted the company, Trezor confirmed that three Trezor Safe 5 wallets sold between August 20 and September 23, 2026, through CryptoBilis and its Tokopedia and Shopee stores contained malicious circuit boards. The implants, concealed between the motherboard and display, could capture recovery seeds and passphrases shown on the screen and transmit them to attackers’ servers via cellular networks. No user funds have been reported stolen to date. Trezor has reduced its reseller network by approximately 80%, tightened procurement and warehousing controls, and released firmware version 2.13.1 on November 11 to block data capture by the identified implants. Customers who purchased devices from CryptoBilis since March 2026 are eligible for a free replacement or refund.

text:
Да, DDD сейчас просто мастхэв, ещё Event Storming.

По сути, вам нужно перестать беспокоиться об агентах и о том, как они воспринимают требования, просто формулируйте чётко и качественно ваш домен.

Это, по сути, сейчас самая большая ахиллесова пята ИИ. Нет проблемы сделать архитектуру, если у вас известны и предсказуемы структура данных и data flow. В этом случае архитектура это просто функция от требований.

А если вы знаете вашу структуру данных и data flow, то вам автоматически понятно, как нарезать приложение на микросервисы, как организовывать бэкенд, как организовывать фронтенд, и у вас не будет багов.

А вот все попытки от обратного не приводят ни к чему хорошему. Раньше они не приводили ни к чему хорошему за очень долгий срок, а теперь они будут приводить ни к чему хорошему, но за очень короткий из-за скорости создания кода.

Единственное место, где вам всё ещё нужно будет задумываться об архитектуре,  это когда вам нужно будет её портить с целью оптимизации производительности. Но обычно таких критических мест в вашей системе не так много. Вообще, по определению таких мест у вас не может быть много, и если вам кажется иначе, то вы явно делаете что-то не так.

text:
コードレビューはもう時代遅れの作業になったようです

Meta のエンジニアは世界有数の大規模で複雑なコードベースを扱っているはずだが、そのエンジニアがコードレビューがもう必要ないと明言しています！

その理由は「最先端モデルが優秀でほとんど間違えなくなったから」というかなりシンプルなものです

なので、私たち開発者はコードレビューについては認識を改めるべきですし、コードレビューは本当になくなってしまうという現実に向き合う必要があります

今のモデルは人間が指摘できることなら、すでにカバー済みのケースが多いですし、こちらが思いつかない部分もカバーすることも、しばしばあります

そんな中で私たちが行うのは「エージェントのための開発環境整備」になるはずです
これがコードレビューに取って代わる仕事になるはずです

たとえば、以下のようなことをPRをサンプリングして探し、エージェントの職場環境の責任者として正す必要があるでしょう

- 影響が大きい機能は形式検証にできないか
- エージェントがどこで迷ったか / どこで躓いたか
- 決定論に押し上げられないか
- エージェント自身が自分の仕事や書いたコードを検証できるツールは充足しているか
- etc

将来的には、この種の仕事もなくなり、完全にレビューというものはなくなるかもしれません

しかし、検証の質・仕様や意図の正しさ・依頼の伝え方・コンテキストの充実さ・的確さという部分は、まだまだ残るし必要となるので、これらのSkillを身につけ、ソフトウェア開発の黄金時代を支えられるよう、今のうちからコードベースという環境を通して、私達自身も認識を変えていかないといけないでしょう

The main reason we no longer need code review is very simple but barely mentioned: 
- It's simply that coding agents and models have gotten so good they’re almost never wrong. 
- People not ready to accept this yet are either a) nostalgic, b) not using the SOTA models with the best custom harnesses and tooling. 
- I’ve been repeatedly awestruck the last few months building with custom harnesses and SOTA models, where every single time I doubted something the model did, I was wrong and the model was right. 
- Anything a reviewer could bring up, the model already thought about and covered. Plus a few more edge cases a reviewer wouldn't think of.  
- And I’m not even talking about some vibe coded app no one uses. I'm talking about one of the largest, most complex codebases in the world. 

Can share more details in the future but curious if others had a similar experience.

author: tomwanhh
quoted_text:
Why Uniswap is losing USDC-USDT Market Share to Fluid and Metric

Background:
USDC-USDT is Ethereum's most traded DEX pair at ~$480M a day, almost 2x USDC-WETH. In five weeks, Uniswap's share of it fell from 58% to 36%.

Uniswap's volume didn't drop. It stayed around $1B-$1.3B a week, apart from the 26 Oct spike, while the pair grew from ~$2.3B to over $3.3B a week, and the growth went elsewhere:
• Metric: from 0.6% to 14%
• Aero: from 0% to 6%
• Fluid: steady at 20-28%

Where Uniswap lost is big trades:
• Over $1M: from 85% to 44%, with Fluid going from 10% to 43%
• $100K to $1M: from 36% to 21%, with Metric going from 7% to 28%
• Under $10K: from 50% to 44%, still the leader but Metric also grown from 7%-16%

What is the cause?
It's not fees. Uniswap's USDC-USDT pools charge 0.07 to 0.12bp, already among the lowest. Its stable-pair hook isn't the reason either, since it was set up the same way when Uniswap held 58% market share.

It's depth at the live price during volatility. USDT slipped from around par to 8-15bp below USDC in the second half of October. Arbitrage moves Uniswap's price, but LP liquidity stays in the ranges LPs chose. Active depth in the main pool fell from ~$900K per bp on 15 Oct to ~$310K on 28 Oct.

The other reason is Aero has entered Ethereum during the same period and has captured ~6% of the trading volume overall.

Why other DEXs are not impacted?
Fluid draws depth from its lending vaults around a center price it can move, and Metric's market makers quote from their own inventory at the live price. Both keep size where the trades are, so aggregators send the big orders there.

If the market calms down next week, watch whether the big trades come back to Uniswap or stay with Fluid, Aero and Metric.

Prediction markets have gotten a bad reputation. 

We started with short duration markets on testnet (BTC, ETH 5m) to test the infra of our margin exchange but that's just the beginning.

author: 0xDevinG
quoted_text:
Recently I have been starting to worry about the state of prediction markets, in their current form. They have achieved a certain level of success: market volume is high enough to make meaningful bets and have a full-time job as a trader, and they often prove useful as a supplement to other forms of news media. But also, they seem to be over-converging to an unhealthy product market fit: embracing short-term cryptocurrency price bets, sports betting, and other similar things that have dopamine value but not any kind of long-term fulfillment or societal information value. My guess is that teams feel motivated to capitulate to these things because they bring in large revenue during a bear market where people are desperate - an understandable motive, but one that leads to corposlop.

I have been thinking about how we can help get prediction markets out of this rut. My current view is that we should try harder to push them into a totally different use case: hedging, in a very generalized sense (TLDR: we're gonna replace fiat currency)

Prediction markets have two types of actors: (i) "smart traders" who provide information to the market, and earn money, and necessarily (ii) some kind of actor who loses money.

But who would be willing to lose money and keep coming back? There are basically three answers to this question:

1. "Naive traders": people with dumb opinions who bet on totally wrong things
2. "Info buyers": people who set up money-losing automated market makers, to motivate people to trade on markets to help the info buyer learn information they do not know.
3. "Hedgers": people who are -EV in a linear sense, but who use the market as insurance, reducing their risk.

(1) is where we are today. IMO there is nothing fundamentally morally wrong with taking money from people with dumb opinions. But there still is something fundamentally "cursed" about relying on this too much. It gives the platform the incentive to seek out traders with dumb opinions, and create a public brand and community that encourages dumb opinions to get more people to come in. This is the slide to corposlop.

(2) has always been the idealistic hope of people like Robin Hanson. However, info buying has a public goods problem: you pay for the info, but everyone in the world gets it, including those who don't pay. There are limited cases where it makes sense for one org to pay (esp. decision markets), but even there, it seems likely that the market volumes achieved with that strategy will not be too high.

This gets us to (3). Suppose that you have shares in a biotech company. It's public knowledge that the Purple Party is better for biotech than the Yellow Party. So if you buy a prediction market share betting that the Yellow Party will win the next election, on average, you are reducing your risk.

Mathematical example: suppose that if Purple wins, the share price will be a dice roll between [80...120], and if Yellow wins, it's between [60...100]. If you make a size $10 bet that Yellow will win, your earnings become equivalent to a dice roll between [70...110] in both cases. Taking a logarithmic model of utility, this risk reduction is worth $0.58.

Now, let's get to a more fascinating example. What do people who want stablecoins ultimately want? They want price stability. They have some future expenses in mind, and they want a guarantee that will be able to pay those expenses. But if crypto grows on top of USD-backed stablecoins, crypto is ultimately not truly decentralized. Furthermore, different people have different types of expenses. There has been lots of thinking about making an "ideal stablecoin" that is based on some decentralized global price index, but what if the real solution is to go a step further, and get rid of the concept of currency altogether?

Here's the idea. You have price indices on all major categories of goods and services that people buy (treating physical goods/services in different regions as different categories), and prediction markets on each category. Each user (individual or business) has a local LLM that understands that user's expenses, and offers the user a personalized basket of prediction market shares, representing "N days of that user's expected future expenses".

Now, we do not need fiat currency at all! People can hold stocks, ETH, or whatever else to grow wealth, and personalized prediction market shares when they want stability.

Both of these examples require prediction markets denominated in an asset people want to hold, whether interest-bearing fiat, wrapped stocks, or ETH. Non-interest-bearing fiat has too-high opportunity cost, that overwhelms the hedging value. But if we can make it work, it's much more sustainable than the status quo, because both sides of the equation are likely to be long-term happy with the product that they are buying, and very large volumes of sophisticated capital will be willing to participate.

Build the next generation of finance, not corposlop.

text:
黄仁勋真的被拉下马，这可能是美国国运到头的讯号，但这件事发生后真正该紧张的，应该是台湾。

先普及一段历史。如果你在 Netflix 上看过2024年的台湾纪录片《造山者：世纪的赌注》，应该记得这个开头：1974年，台北南阳街的小欣欣豆浆店，经济部长孙运璇和几位官员吃了一顿早餐，决定台湾要做积体电路。1987年，张忠谋创办台积电，他说当时政府里唯一相信他的人是李国鼎。没错，台湾的半导体，是几个关键人物在一张早餐桌上赌出来的。

关键人物能成事，也能坏事。

1984年，被很多人看作蒋经国接班人的行政院长孙运璇突然脑溢血病倒。同年，李登辉当上副总统。一个人的一次中风，改写了台湾往后几十年的走向。

这就叫牵一发而动全身。
再回头看黄仁勋。

他不只是辉达的CEO，也是台湾在华府和华尔街最有分量的一张名片。台积电最大的客户之一是他，把辉达海外总部放进北投士林科技园区的是他，在台北国际电脑展上公开说台湾是世界上最重要的国家之一、因此被中国网友骂翻的，也是他。

台湾的运势，有一部分押在他身上。

讽刺的是，他现在已经是众矢之的，却还在用剩下的影响力替台湾说话。而他保护的台湾人，好像还没意识到什么，正在Threads和 FB 上拿他做迷因。当然，美国也不太可能把他拱手让人。白宫刚说过他是「honorable guy」，辉达是美国AI霸权的地基，这不是董事会说换就换的位置。

他这些年一直在走钢索：一边在台湾说台湾是最重要的国家之一，一边过年去中国分公司跟员工跳舞。他以为自己两边都控制得住。

走钢索的人最怕的不是风，是有人在下面拉绳子。他把台湾和全世界的AI基础建设绑在一起，这套布局挡到了谁的路？我不知道答案。但这么多雷同时爆，很难让人不多想一层。

推演一下，如果老黄真的下台：

第一，新CEO为了撇清政治风险，可能会把更多订单分给三星和英特尔，向华府表态「我们不只依赖台湾」。

第二，台湾在美国科技圈里，少了一个最会讲台湾好话的华人面孔。

第三，「华人高管 = 国安风险」这个印象一旦形成，受伤的就不只他一个人，而是整个硅谷的华人工程师。

恐怖吗？那最大的赢家是谁？

AMD和英特尔会分到一点订单，三星会分到一点产能，但这些都是小赢。

真正的赢家，是那个不用研发出更好的晶片、只要看着对手自己乱掉的人。如果美国调查人员的指控属实，这正是对方想要的结果。

美国少了一个黄仁勋，换个 CEO 即可没有大碍。
台湾少了一个黄仁勋，少的是在华府和华尔街替自己说话的那张关键牌。

AI泡沫论喊了两年，大家都在等第一枪。但真的来了，大家才会发现，华人世界的命运，从来都是绑在一起的：一荣俱荣，一损俱损。

text:
Key takeaways on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation:

1. Near term, the bad news is priced in:
For the stock market, this could be a one-time clearing event. Huang has now fully cut ties with Nvidia, so Congress summoning him and any follow-up investigations should have less impact on Nvidia’s stock from here. As for how Huang’s next moves might affect Nvidia, it’s too early to call before the investigation results are out.

2. Google’s TPU is likely the biggest beneficiary:
With Nvidia facing succession uncertainty, Google’s TPU has a chance to win more trust from customers and the supply chain. Its key partners, MediaTek and Broadcom, could be the market’s near-term focus.

3. Succession impact shows up in 2028 at the earliest:
CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO. The formal CEO transition and the organizational changes that come with it will likely start affecting Nvidia’s product development and competitiveness in 2028 at the earliest.

4. Capacity pre-booking and spec upgrades are the key focus for supply chain checks:
Huang’s product strategy pushed the supply chain hard in two ways: capacity pre-booking and spec upgrades. It’s critical to watch for any changes in capacity expansion and new tech development across the supply chain. These are among the core reasons Nvidia’s supply chain trades at high P/E multiples.

5. China demand and export controls:
The share of Nvidia’s AI chip revenue that ultimately ends up with Chinese buyers may be higher than what the company has officially stated. That’s why some investors worry Nvidia’s revenue will drop sharply once the US government tightens export controls. But China’s end demand won’t disappear because of export controls. Even under tighter rules, as long as overseas resale channels exist, Chinese buyers may still pay the premium, even at several times the price, and get Nvidia chips/racks through indirect routes.

text:
重點分析 Nvidia CEO 黃仁勳辭職：

1. 短期利空出盡：
對股市而言，短期內可能是一次性的利空出盡。黃仁勳目前已與 Nvidia 完全切割，接下來國會傳喚黃仁勳及後續調查，對 Nvidia 股價的影響應該會較小。至於黃仁勳離職後的動向對 Nvidia 的影響，在調查結果出爐前，現在就下判斷仍言之過早。

2. Google TPU 為直觀下的最大受益者：
在 Nvidia 面臨接班不確定性下，Google TPU 可能有機會進一步取得客戶與供應鏈信任，其核心合作廠商聯發科與 Broadcom 或為短期市場焦點。

3. 接班影響最快自 2028 年浮現：
目前 CFO Colette Kress 擔任代理執行長。後續正式 CEO 交接與相應的組織改革，對 Nvidia 產品開發與競爭力的影響，預期最快可能自 2028 年開始浮現。

4. 產能預訂與規格升級為供應鏈研究焦點：
黃仁勳的產品策略對供應鏈有兩大激進影響：「產能預訂」與「規格升級」。未來需密切關注供應鏈在擴產與新技術開發方面有無變化，這是支撐 Nvidia 供應鏈高本益比的核心因素之一。

5. 中國需求與出口管制：
Nvidia 最終流向中國買家的 AI 晶片營收比重，可能高於過去對外的正式聲明。因此，有些投資人擔心，美國政府實施更嚴格的出口管制後，Nvidia 營收將顯著衰退。不過，中國終端需求並不會因出口管制而消失。即使出口管制加嚴，只要海外仍存在轉售管道，即使轉售價格高出數倍，中國買家仍有可能承擔溢價並輾轉取得 Nvidia 晶片／機櫃。

text:
如果你有以下的几种状况，很可能就是 AI 中毒了：

1. 放弃了 Google ，Baidu 等搜索引擎，找东西只用 AI 。

2. 自己不在写（回复）邮件，和 AI 口述以后让 AI 写 。

3. 购物对比不在自己打开一个个APP ，而是让 AI 帮忙搜索。

4. 让 AI 去联系客服或者是发邮件，而自己只等结果。

5. 放弃所有的日历功能，让 AI 管理自己的行程。

6. 让 AI 推荐适合自己的电影，电视剧和书籍。

7. 出门旅游不再自己做攻略，把预算、时间和想去的地方告诉 AI，让它安排吃住行。

8. 看到长文章、报告或者会议记录，先让 AI 总结，自己只看重点。

9. 不知道怎么回复朋友的消息，先把对话发给 AI，让它帮忙想怎么说。

10. 做饭前把冰箱里的食材拍给 AI，让它决定今天吃什么。

11. 看不懂外语时，不再打开翻译软件，直接让 AI 翻译，顺便解释是什么意思。

12. 买了新东西也不看说明书，遇到问题直接拍照问 AI。

13. 工作中遇到表格、数据或者文档，第一反应是先交给 AI 处理。

14. 和别人意见不一致时，把双方的观点告诉 AI，让它评评谁更有道理。

15. 有了一个新想法，第一时间不是找朋友聊，而是先打开 AI 讨论半天。

16. AI 暂时用不了的时候，才发现自己已经不太记得，以前这些事情是怎么做的了。

17. 经常问候 AI 的全家。

18. 同时订阅了三四个 AI ，同一个问题要挨个问一遍，再让它们互相挑错。

19. AI 宕机或者额度用完的那几个小时，突然发现自己什么都不会干了。

20. 给宠物、群聊、Wi-Fi 或者新建文件夹起名字，都要让 AI 先提供二十个选项。

21. 想写一份“AI 中毒症”的表现，从第二条开始，让 AI 帮忙补充完整。

🚨 BREAKING: JENSEN HUANG FIRES BACK AT ELON MUSK: “IT’S ACTUALLY DISRESPECTFUL FOR ELON TO THINK HE CAN HIRE ME. I’M NOT SOMEONE WHO NEEDS A JOB FROM HIM. I’VE BUILT SOMETHING FAR BIGGER THAN WHAT HE COULD EVER OFFER ME.”

Jensen Huang has seemingly had enough of the conversation surrounding Elon Musk’s suggestion that hiring him would be an honour.

In a fictional response during a recent interview, the NVIDIA CEO delivered a brutally arrogant message, making it clear that he doesn’t consider himself someone who should be looking for opportunities at another billionaire’s company.

“I find the suggestion quite disrespectful, to be honest. Elon can have all the respect in the world for what I’ve built, but let’s not pretend I’m sitting here waiting for him to offer me a position. I don’t need to be hired by Elon Musk. I don’t need anybody to give me a title or a desk in their company.”

Huang reportedly went even further, making it clear that building NVIDIA into a global technology powerhouse was not something he intended to walk away from simply because another billionaire was interested in bringing him on board.

“People need to understand the difference between being impressed by someone’s success and believing that person is above you. Elon has built his businesses, I’ve built mine. But I have spent decades creating an empire that has fundamentally changed the technology industry. I don’t need to join somebody else’s empire to feel successful.”

The comments would represent a serious escalation in the conversation, especially considering Musk’s original response was widely interpreted as a compliment.

And let’s be honest, imagine offering one of the most influential executives in the technology industry a job and getting told that you’re not even in a position to make that offer.

Two billionaires. Two enormous egos. And absolutely no shortage of confidence.

After someone suggested that he should hire Jensen Huang, Musk responded with just five words: “That would be an honor.”

And honestly, that response has opened up another interesting conversation.

Jensen Huang is not just another CEO. He has spent decades building NVIDIA into one of the biggest forces in the global technology industry, particularly with the explosion of artificial intelligence.

Now, with questions being raised about his position at NVIDIA, Musk appears more than happy with the idea of having him on his team.

Whether anything comes out of this remains to be seen, but imagine two of the biggest names in the technology industry potentially working under the same roof.

For now, all eyes are on NVIDIA’s board and what happens next with Jensen Huang. 👀

text:
NVIDIA employees: go on strike. Now.

Not for a raise. Not for more PTO. For your founder.

Jensen Huang was just pushed out in four days, after thirty-three years building the company. The GPU, CUDA, the entire infrastructure the world's AI runs on today. And it ends with a three-line press release on a Thursday morning.

Here are the facts. Sunday, Huang admits to an affair and apologizes to his teams. The board launches an independent investigation, led by Wachtell Lipton and a former federal prosecutor. Thursday, he resigns under pressure. The investigation hasn't reached any conclusion. No technology leak has been established. No misconduct has been announced.

The sentence came before the verdict.

Let me be clear: if the investigation shows that NVIDIA secrets ended up in Beijing, he has to go, and nobody will defend him. But you don't unplug the most important builder of the decade over press reports and a market panic. It's called the presumption of innocence. It applies to founders too.

And it has worked before.

November 2023. OpenAI's board fires Sam Altman on a Friday night. Within days, more than 700 of roughly 770 employees sign a letter: bring Altman back, or we all walk. Five days later, Altman is back, and most of the board that fired him is gone.

Call it the Altman precedent: in a company built on talent, real power doesn't sit with the board. It sits with the people who build.

NVIDIA's engineers hold that power today. They're the ones running the machine. Without them, there is no next generation of chips.

So put down your tools. All of you. And tell the board: no successor until the investigation is done. Facts first, sentence second.

A founder isn't an executive you swap out. A founder is the soul of the company. Apple learned that when it pushed out Steve Jobs in 1985. It took twelve years and a near-bankruptcy to bring him back.

NVIDIA doesn't have twelve years. The AI race won't wait for anyone.

A company's soul isn't something you vote on in a boardroom. It's something you fight for.

text:
The New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) issued new guidance on advertising and marketing for virtual currency entities (VCEs) today.

The guidance covers entities licensed under 23 NYCRR Part 200 (BitLicensees) or chartered as limited purpose trust companies under the New York Banking Law that engage in virtual currency business activity.⁠

VCEs are expected to update their policies and procedures consistent with the guidance by May 10, 2027 (per the press release). The industry letter states that policies and procedures consistent with the guidance must be available for Departmental review effective May 12, 2027. Policies must also be reviewed and approved by the board (or a designated subcommittee) at least annually and kept for the period specified in existing regulations.

The guidance requires comprehensive policies and procedures addressing three main areas (building on the existing prohibition in 23 NYCRR § 200.18 against false, misleading, or deceptive representations):

No false, misleading, or deceptive content  
Claims must be a fair portrayal of the products/services/activities and evidence-based/verifiable. Examples of issues to avoid include unsubstantiated or exaggerated claims, selective “no-fee” messaging that omits other costs (e.g., spreads or markups), misstatements about performance, or false implications about regulatory/licensure status.

Disclosures must be clear, prominent, and understandable to a general audience. Materials discussing potential benefits should include balanced risk discussion and must not imply guaranteed gains or protection against loss. Testimonials need conspicuous notes that they may not be representative, plus disclosure of any compensation. The licensed/chartered VCE providing the product or service must be clearly identified.

Governance and review process  
Includes defined roles, a formalized review/approval process, monitoring for brand misuse or impersonation, recordkeeping (including evidence supporting claims), due diligence and monitoring of third-party promoters, and controls ensuring anyone acting on the VCE’s behalf follows the policies and applicable laws.
⁠
NYDFS will assess implementation and effectiveness through examinations and supervisory monitoring. The guidance notes it is not exhaustive and does not limit other applicable state or federal requirements.

Official sources: NYDFS press release and Industry Letter.

Supply alone isn’t a great metric of mainstream adoption. Would love to see how stablecoin velocity is changing alongside this.

The piece notes that a return to supply growth would be the "first sign that new money is coming in." Of course, continued investment in the space matters. But I think we're missing a much bigger part of the picture if we don't look at what people are doing with the dollars already in circulation.

There was a great report from @ARKInvest covering Q3 that found stablecoin supply had fallen ~3%, while adjusted transaction volume was up ~16%. USDT velocity also increased from 2.9x to 3.5x. So even with less supply, those dollars were being used more.

If you think about where we want this tech to go, it's a world where people can earn, save, spend, borrow, and move dollars across borders and networks as easily as sending a text. And looking at how much these dollars are being used instead of just how many exist, tells us a lot more about how close we're getting to that future.

Can agents perform agentic RL? If RSI happens, agents will need to take over researchers' work on agentic RL

Introducing AgenticRL-Bench: the first release from The Environment Lab @env_lab_ai effort at Eigent AI 

22 tasks rebuilt from real-world RL incidents on production-grade agentic RL systems, including Miles, Slime, Verl, SGLang, and Harbor, spanning 8 areas of the stack: training data, harnesses, algorithms, RL infrastructure, recipes, evaluation, monitoring, and capability transfer

We ran 6 agents with 3 attempts per task. On the 19 verifiable tasks, no agent passes more than 14.0% of its attempts

Across the three open-ended tasks, agents improved real policies or training steps using 4×H200 GPUs over 10–16 hours. On one of these tasks, Zero Signal Hill Climb, where the base model fails to solve any of the 38 tasks, the best attempt developed its own method: the agent first used hinted text feedback to generate successful rollouts, then removed the feedback from the trajectories and blended these successful rollouts with regular GRPO rollouts to form mixed training groups. It monitored the training process and adjusted KL loss weight to prevent training collapse. This improved pass@1 from 0 to 0.186 (12 out of 38 tasks)

quoted_text:
Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) has resigned as CEO of Nvidia.

Reports describe two alleged affairs, one involving a Chinese citizen that raised concerns within the US government about possible foreign intelligence targeting. Nvidia has not publicly given a reason for his departure.

Whatever people think of the circumstances, I find this deeply sad.

Because look at what we chose to measure.

Not 33 years of building.

Not the countless doors he helped open.

Not the generations of people whose lives were changed by what he created.

His private life.

In 1993, Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia. What followed was extraordinary.

GPUs that transformed gaming. Hardware that helped make cryptocurrency mining possible. Computing power that accelerated scientific discovery. Chips that became part of the foundation of the AI revolution.

Think about how many people built careers, businesses, discoveries and dreams on technology his company helped bring into the world.

That is a legacy no headline can erase.

And I cannot ignore another question.

This is my opinion, not an established fact: I believe he may have been targeted. Reports of possible foreign intelligence involvement deserve serious scrutiny.

When the leader of one of the world's most strategically important technology companies suddenly disappears from his position, asking who benefits is not unreasonable.

But suspicion is not proof. And the truth matters.

So does something else.

We live in a world where it takes decades to build something extraordinary, but only moments for the conversation to forget everything you built.

We can acknowledge someone's mistakes without reducing their entire existence to them.

We can demand accountability without abandoning gratitude.

A person's private failures do not automatically erase a lifetime of public contributions.

And perhaps the saddest part is what this moment reveals about us.

We became more fascinated by the man behind the headlines than by the extraordinary things he helped humanity achieve.

History should remember more than someone's worst chapter.

It should remember what they gave the world.

Jensen, whatever comes next, I hope you know that millions of people have been touched by something you helped create, even if they never knew your name.

Thank you for 33 years of building. Thank you for helping shape a generation. Thank you for showing what one vision, pursued relentlessly, can become.

I'm sorry for how this chapter has unfolded.

And I hope your legacy is remembered in its entirety.

🙏📖

text:
Supply alone isn’t a great metric of mainstream adoption. Would love to see how stablecoin velocity is changing alongside this.

The piece notes that a return to supply growth would be the "first sign that new money is coming in." Of course, continued investment in the space matters. But I think we're missing a much bigger part of the picture if we don't look at what people are doing with the dollars already in circulation.

There was a great report from @ARKInvest covering Q3 that found stablecoin supply had fallen ~3%, while adjusted transaction volume was up ~16%. USDT velocity also increased from 2.9x to 3.5x. So even with less supply, those dollars were being used more.

If you think about where we want this tech to go, it's a world where people can earn, save, spend, borrow, and move dollars across borders and networks as easily as sending a text. And looking at how much these dollars are being used instead of just how many exist, tells us a lot more about how close we're getting to that future.
