quoted_text:
This is the conversation that made me even more bullish on $SUI.

Somewhere in this conversation Evan Cheng and I started joking about home robots. One day you come home, he said, and it's not cleaning your house:  "it's cleaning OUT your house. And walking away with everything."

We were laughing. Then he added: "If you really think about it, it's entirely possible." And that's basically the whole episode.

@evanweb3 built developer tools at Apple and Meta before founding Mysten Labs, the company behind @suinetwork. We recorded in Singapore, where I was speaking at SUI Basecamp, and honestly, this became one of those conversations where I walked in with questions about stablecoins and walked out rethinking how the internet works.

His core point, the one I keep replaying:

"The web is built for humans. You cannot retrofit it to handle agents."

Everything online assumes a human on the other end, identity, trust, the fact that you can sue someone. Agents break all of it. His example hit home because I told him I get phishing mails daily that even make ME hesitate (and I confessed to my 50,000 unread emails, which he graciously ignored). Now imagine your agent reading those mails with full access to your accounts. His words: "Email is the biggest freaking attack vector... such a legacy protocol."

And his most honest line, about how this plays out:

"Disaster will happen. That's part of the progress."

That’s already what’s happening in the world nowadays. PHP websites aren’t safe anymore, even freezers and fridges are being hacked. Our infrastructure needs to be updated, and that’s why this episode and SUI became so important.

Thanks to @OKX for being today’s sponsor of the show.

text:
苫米地抽象度自由論 第二巻Kindle+は来週出版予定。合わせて第一巻も改訂したので同期を。コンテンツと端末の管理で自動更新オンの人は既に自動更新してると思う。念のためアプリ側で同期を。特に『公式解説ガイド付き完全版』は更新で864ページになった。数式を読まなくても理解出来るように、また読んで逆に誤解しないように更に解説を増やした。
『苫米地抽象度自由論 第一巻 公式解説ガイド付き完全版』(2026年11月12日改訂版)
https://t.co/GwYYklLw5m
非公開の「コグニティブリサーチラボ研究報告」背景論文も『公式解説ガイド付き完全版』ではKindleからリンクで読者は読めるようにした。こちらも貴重なはず。私の思索の過程も論文を追えば分かる。

864ページ書籍がKindle+は０円。購入しても1650円。ページあたり0円から２円未満は紙書籍時代は考えれなかった。それでも統計上電子版を含む社会の読書量は減ってるそう。現在の書き手の力量かも知れない。ほとんどのコンテンツは動画が有利からかも知れない。ただ、内容の厳密性は活字が基本。数理ならそれは今も変わらない。

そして、『公式解説ガイド付き完全版』は数式を飛ばし読み出来るようにした。数式が苦手な人は解説文をじっくり読んで欲しい。数式が得意な人も、是非、自己の知識にはスコトーマが内在していると念のため思い、解説をよく読んで欲しい。解説不足がまだあれば、将来も改訂を続ける。同期で更新は当然無料。

第一巻は、抽象度の上昇による自由容量の拡大。第二巻は抽象度方向性と自由。これは、あらゆる認知活動の基盤数理として使えるはず。もちろん、コーチングやリーダーシップ、自己啓発分野では重要な知識となるはず。

ただ、数理定義や厳密証明と、スキルの向上は全く別。スポーツ理論を理解することと優秀な選手になることは全く別なのと同様。「空」の定義を知ることと「悟る」ことは全く別物であるのと同様。

例えば、コーチングも言及しているが、これらは、ゴール、コンフォートゾーン、エフィカシー、バランスウィールといった日常でも使われる一般名詞についてではなく、ルータイスの時代から守られているコーチングにおける定義を数理で厳密にした。厳密証明したのは、その定義と知識体系の健全な連続性であり、コーチングの効果ではない。特定流派やコーチの技量とは全く別である。それはあらゆる知的技術やスポーツと同様である。

苫米地式認定コーチ育成では、一定以上の知識を持つ社会人を対象に、コーチ育成に一年をかけ、後半の半年は模擬コーチングを含む実践訓練をする。更に上級クラスは丸3年のクラスである。それでも、トップレベルのコーチと、定義や理論をよく理解していても経験の浅いコーチの成果は、大きく異なる。

コーチングにおいてクライアントが支払うのはコーチングセッションの時間対価(コーチの生命時間対価)であり、知識や成果ではない。コーチの技量で成果が異なるのは当然だ。

コーチ育成は、厳密な定義をしたところから「コーチ」になる訓練が始まるのであり、曖昧な知識では成果は期待出来ない。本書を読むことでコーチングが出来る訳ではなく、もしもそう読まれたなら、それは誤読である。

もちろん、読者が自身のコーチを選ぶ助けにも本書はなるはずだ。

これは書籍でカバーするリーダーシップも同様だ。

quoted_text:
The race between frontier labs isn't close anymore. The gap between Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.2 and the next best model is huge.

If I were running Anthropic, I'd seriously consider:

1. Firing every product person except those on the inference stack and API.

2. Spending the intelligence lead on making existing models as cheap and efficient to serve as possible.

Anthropic doesn't need products to funnel people into Claude anymore. Every developer already knows Claude is unbeatable. Stepping back frees the application layer for never-before-seen innovation and competition, for every demographic and every way to slice TAM. All of it powered by Claude, because Anthropic stopped distracting itself and made the models cheap to serve.

Models don't need to get any smarter to revolutionize the world. All that's missing is diffusion.

And if model quality is the edge, whatever isn't spent on cheaper inference should go to protecting that lead. Personally, I desperately wish that models got no smarter, just cheaper. Cheap tokens are electricity: everyone gets to figure out how to power their own life.

Diffuse creativity and innovation to everyone. AND FOR THE LOVE OF GOD, STOP RELEASING SMARTER MODELS IF YOU ALREADY HAVE THE LEAD.

text:
重點分析 Nvidia CEO 黃仁勳辭職：

1. 短期利空出盡：
對股市而言，短期內可能是一次性的利空出盡。黃仁勳目前已與 Nvidia 完全切割，接下來國會傳喚黃仁勳及後續調查，對 Nvidia 股價的影響應該會較小。至於黃仁勳離職後的動向對 Nvidia 的影響，在調查結果出爐前，現在就下判斷仍言之過早。

2. Google TPU 為直觀下的最大受益者：
在 Nvidia 面臨接班不確定性下，Google TPU 可能有機會進一步取得客戶與供應鏈信任，其核心合作廠商聯發科與 Broadcom 或為短期市場焦點。

3. 接班影響最快自 2028 年浮現：
目前 CFO Colette Kress 擔任代理執行長。後續正式 CEO 交接與相應的組織改革，對 Nvidia 產品開發與競爭力的影響，預期最快可能自 2028 年開始浮現。

4. 產能預訂與規格升級為供應鏈研究焦點：
黃仁勳的產品策略對供應鏈有兩大激進影響：「產能預訂」與「規格升級」。未來需密切關注供應鏈在擴產與新技術開發方面有無變化，這是支撐 Nvidia 供應鏈高本益比的核心因素之一。

5. 中國需求與出口管制：
Nvidia 最終流向中國買家的 AI 晶片營收比重，可能高於過去對外的正式聲明。因此，有些投資人擔心，美國政府實施更嚴格的出口管制後，Nvidia 營收將顯著衰退。不過，中國終端需求並不會因出口管制而消失。即使出口管制加嚴，只要海外仍存在轉售管道，即使轉售價格高出數倍，中國買家仍有可能承擔溢價並輾轉取得 Nvidia 晶片／機櫃。

text:
В сети разгоняют следующую теорию заговора: ЦРУ по приказу Трампа сместило Дженсена Хуанга с поста главы Nvidia.

Причины такие: 

- единственный драйвер экономики США сейчас - это пузырь искусственного интеллекта. Многие забывают, но, чтобы чатгпт ответил вам какого цвета платье, нужны не только сервера. Нужны построенные датацентры, инженеры и рабочие которые их построят, электричество, добывающая промышленность, уголь, атомные станции и так далее и тому подобное. 

- "Пузырь" показывает свою финансовую нестабильность. Если он лопнет, государству мало не покажется, поэтому государство придумывает идеи, как его удержать от падения и не допустить кризиса. Одной из таких идей становится государственное регулирование всей ИИ-отрасли.

- Летом OpenAI и Anthropic спекулировали против "бесплатных китайских моделей", сделанных по Open Source, высказывалась мысль, что "непонятно что там в китайских моделях, может они все шпионские, а это навредит национальной безопасности США". Обе компании написали открытое письмо, где высказывались ЗА государственное регулирование отрасли и недопущение на рынок китайцев.

- Их не поддержали разные мелкие ИИ-стартапы и внезапно глава Nvidia Дженсен Хуанг, который наоборот высказался против госрегулирования, за open source и за то, чтобы всё порешал рыночек, а не государство. Хуанга понять можно - его компания буквально продаёт сервера и чипы на которых эти локальные модели крутятся. 

- Судя по новостям, об интрижках Хуанга знали уже несколько лет, так что ни для кого в компании это новостью не стало. Государство в лице ЦРУ и разведывательного сообщества, сначало разыграло карту "китайской шпионки", а потом, когда это не прокатило (потому что доказательств так и не предоставили), удобно вбросило в прессу через WSJ и NYT (публикации вышли одновременно со ссылкой на анонимные источники) информацию о том, что Хуанг дважды изменник. Совет директоров его уволил. 

- Теперь, для Nvidia выберут более сговорчивого CEO, который выступит за государственное регулирование ИИ-отрасли, ужесточение экспорта чипов в разные там страны и тому подобные весёлые вещи.

На этом фоне китайские ИИ-компании спешат арендовать вычислительные мощности NVIDIA за рубежом из-за опасений ужесточения американских ограничений. Сейчас китайцы обходят экспортные ограничения США, арендуя мощности зарубежных дата-центров (например, в Малайзии, Сингапуре и других азиатских странах), однако новый законопроект может закрыть эту возможность. Перекупщики начали запасаться запрещенными к экспорту чипами NVIDIA.

В общем, госрегулирование якобы грядёт. И пока вас не забанил Anthropic или OpenAI, а китайские локальные нейронки всё ещё доступны, на всякий случай, к ChatGPT и Claude не привыкайте. Если у вас не американский паспорт, конечно.

text:
黄仁勋辞去英伟达 CEO，CFO Colette Kress 临时接任，英伟达第一次设董事长

英伟达美东时间 11 月 12 日早上开盘前宣布，创始人黄仁勋辞去总裁、CEO 和董事职务，立即生效。CFO Colette Kress 兼任临时 CEO，董事会开始找正式接班人，公司内部和外部的人选都会考虑。

黄仁勋 1993 年创办英伟达，当了 33 年 CEO。英伟达提交给美国证券交易委员会的文件写明，董事会是 11 月 11 日（周三）接受他辞职的。同一天下午，纽约时报报道了他的第二段婚外关系，华尔街日报报道董事会准备罢免他。

公告没有写辞职原因，也没有黄仁勋本人的表态。董事会只说黄仁勋对英伟达的贡献“深远”，感谢他“无法估量的贡献”。

Colette Kress 59 岁，2013 年 9 月加入英伟达，一直当 CFO，之前在思科、微软做了近 25 年财务。投资者对她很熟：英伟达每季度的财报电话会上，讲财务数字的就是她。当临时 CEO 期间，她继续兼任 CFO。

找正式 CEO 不容易。黄仁勋在任时约有 60 名高管直接向他汇报，英伟达也一直没有公开的接班计划。

英伟达过去没有董事长这个职位。这次董事会任命 Harvey C. Jones 为第一任董事长。Jones 73 岁，1993 年起就是英伟达董事，曾任芯片设计软件公司 Synopsys 的 CEO 和执行董事长。

Jones 在公告里说，预计公司的运营、对客户的承诺和产品路线图都“不会中断”。

第三季度财报照原计划 11 月 17 日（周二）发布：美东下午 4:20 左右出财报，5 点开电话会，也就是北京时间 18 日早上 5:20 和 6 点。这是 Kress 当上临时 CEO 后的第一份财报。

据 Decrypt 报道，黄仁勋仍是英伟达最大的股东，持股约 3.6%。

英伟达周三收盘 173.73 美元。据雅虎财经，周四开盘一度跌约 13%，市值跌破 4 万亿美元，排名落到第三。Decrypt 报道，开盘后不久报 160.28 美元，跌 7.7%，盘中最低到过 148.80 美元。按雅虎财经计算，从 10 月 6 日创纪录的收盘价 239.24 美元算到周四盘前低点，英伟达市值蒸发了约 2 万亿美元。

券商也在调整。Oppenheimer 下调评级，并取消了目标价；Yorkville Ives 的 Dan Ives 把目标价从 300 美元下调到 225 美元。

董事会的独立调查。11 月 10 日董事会声明，独立董事请了纽约南区联邦检察官办公室前代理检察官 Joon H. Kim 和他所在的 Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz 律师事务所做调查。黄仁勋辞职后调查还继续不继续，公告没说。

国会。众议院三位共和党籍委员会主席要求黄仁勋 11 月 18 日出席闭门简报，他一直没有回复，委员会主席说过可能发传票。据华尔街日报，民主党参议员 Warren 和 Coons 已致信商务部长卢特尼克、国务卿鲁比奥等特朗普政府官员，要求保留与英伟达有关的全部记录，包括英伟达对华芯片出口的材料。民主党明年 1 月接管众议院。

此外，特朗普 11 月 9 日说 FBI 在调查此事；同一天有股东在联邦法院对英伟达和黄仁勋提起集体诉讼。

说明：Alice Huang 的情报身份来自匿名美国官员，没有公开证据；Powell 一事来自纽约时报援引的匿名前员工，当事人都没有证实。英伟达公告和证交会文件都没有把辞职和这两件事联系起来。股价为美东周四上午的数据。

text:
Juste pour clarifier les choses et permettre à chacun de comprendre les véritables enjeux.

Si le conseil d’administration de Nvidia décidait de démettre Jensen Huang de ses fonctions de PDG, cela ne signifierait absolument pas qu’il perdrait sa fortune ou son influence sur l’entreprise.

Voici pourquoi :

• Ses actions lui appartiennent. Toutes les actions déjà acquises restent sa propriété. Il conserve ses droits de vote et peut les garder, les vendre ou même les utiliser comme garantie pour obtenir des financements, sous réserve des restrictions réglementaires applicables aux initiés.

• Le conseil ne peut pas lui retirer sa participation déjà acquise. Seules les rémunérations en actions qui ne sont pas encore définitivement acquises, comme certaines RSU ou PSU, pourraient être annulées selon les conditions de son contrat. Or, Jensen Huang a cofondé Nvidia en 1993 et possède environ 3,5 % de l'entreprise. Une grande partie de sa fortune est donc déjà acquise.

• Le véritable problème serait stratégique. En tant que principal actionnaire individuel, Jensen pourrait devenir un adversaire redoutable pour le conseil. Il pourrait notamment chercher à remplacer certains administrateurs, contester les décisions de gouvernance ou même vendre une partie importante de ses actions, avec des conséquences potentiellement lourdes sur le cours de Bourse.

En théorie, il pourrait également créer une entreprise concurrente, même si cela dépendrait des obligations contractuelles et des contraintes juridiques applicables.

En clair : licencier Jensen Huang ne signifie pas lui retirer son pouvoir financier.

Un homme qui détient des dizaines de milliards de dollars en actions Nvidia ne devient pas soudainement insignifiant parce qu'il perd son fauteuil de PDG.

Il pourrait même devenir l'un des actionnaires les plus influents et les plus difficiles à ignorer pour le conseil d'administration.

text:
NVIDIA employees: go on strike. Now.

Not for a raise. Not for more PTO. For your founder.

Jensen Huang was just pushed out in four days, after thirty-three years building the company. The GPU, CUDA, the entire infrastructure the world's AI runs on today. And it ends with a three-line press release on a Thursday morning.

Here are the facts. Sunday, Huang admits to an affair and apologizes to his teams. The board launches an independent investigation, led by Wachtell Lipton and a former federal prosecutor. Thursday, he resigns under pressure. The investigation hasn't reached any conclusion. No technology leak has been established. No misconduct has been announced.

The sentence came before the verdict.

Let me be clear: if the investigation shows that NVIDIA secrets ended up in Beijing, he has to go, and nobody will defend him. But you don't unplug the most important builder of the decade over press reports and a market panic. It's called the presumption of innocence. It applies to founders too.

And it has worked before.

November 2023. OpenAI's board fires Sam Altman on a Friday night. Within days, more than 700 of roughly 770 employees sign a letter: bring Altman back, or we all walk. Five days later, Altman is back, and most of the board that fired him is gone.

Call it the Altman precedent: in a company built on talent, real power doesn't sit with the board. It sits with the people who build.

NVIDIA's engineers hold that power today. They're the ones running the machine. Without them, there is no next generation of chips.

So put down your tools. All of you. And tell the board: no successor until the investigation is done. Facts first, sentence second.

A founder isn't an executive you swap out. A founder is the soul of the company. Apple learned that when it pushed out Steve Jobs in 1985. It took twelve years and a near-bankruptcy to bring him back.

NVIDIA doesn't have twelve years. The AI race won't wait for anyone.

A company's soul isn't something you vote on in a boardroom. It's something you fight for.

$NVDA The Company Building the Foundation of Tomorrow's AI Economy.

Investors need to understand something important: NVIDIA's competitive advantage goes far beyond manufacturing advanced computer chips. It has built an entire ecosystem around artificial intelligence, and that ecosystem is becoming increasingly important to the world's technology infrastructure.

While competitors are racing to capture pieces of the AI opportunity, NVIDIA has positioned itself at the center of the revolution.

Its CUDA software platform, advanced GPU architecture, Blackwell computing technology, high-speed networking, and global developer ecosystem create a competitive moat that is extremely difficult to replicate.

Think about the bigger picture.

The future of AI will require enormous computing power. Autonomous vehicles will require advanced processing. Robotics will require intelligence and real-time decision-making. Healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, and virtually every major industry are exploring ways to integrate AI into their operations.

And behind much of this transformation is the need for advanced computing infrastructure.

That's where NVIDIA has positioned itself.

Its greatest strength is that it doesn't have to predict which AI application will ultimately dominate. Whether the winners are developing autonomous driving, robotics, AI assistants, enterprise software, or next-generation automation, the demand for computing power creates opportunities for NVIDIA.

This is what makes its business model so strategically powerful.

NVIDIA isn't simply selling today's technology. It is investing in the infrastructure that tomorrow's technology will depend on.

For long-term investors, the opportunity is to recognize the importance of owning a position in the infrastructure layer of a potentially transformative technological cycle.

The AI revolution is bigger than any single application, and NVIDIA has established itself as one of the most strategically positioned companies powering that revolution.

The question isn't simply who will build the next great AI product. It's also who will provide the computing power that makes those products possible.

NVIDIA has a compelling seat at that table.

Two years of silence on the Nvidia investigation, then a story five days before an election, then nothing until the week after it. Am I the only one wondering about the sequencing?

Jensen Huang is out after 33 years. The stock fell double digits within hours.

Here is what I keep coming back to. None of the underlying facts were new. Investigations had been open since 2024. Officials had been briefed. The allegations are still allegations, no charges have been filed.

Nothing in the file changed. It became public, and two weeks later the founder was gone. That looks planned to me.

Jobs was pushed out of Apple in 1985. It took twelve years and a near-bankruptcy to undo. Founders are not interchangeable, and the market priced that in today faster than any board could.

text:
Flare is taking its data-verification network beyond its own chain.

@FlareNetworks is joining @LayerZero_Core as a Decentralized Verifier Network (DVN). This gives applications on other supported chains a way to use Flare’s verification without moving funds onto Flare.

FDC is battle-tested. It verifies the XRP payments backing FXRP, the largest non-custodial wrapped XRP asset, with about 145M FXRP.

Now, the DVN extends that same data consensus to LayerZero:

• FDC providers verify an event on the source chain and reach weighted agreement.

• Flare’s DVN contract verifies a proof of that result on the destination chain.

• Delivery proceeds once the application’s chosen verifier requirements are met.

Flare brings an existing, built-in data-verification service, with voting weights tied to $FLR staking and delegation.

LayerZero’s OFT standard lets tokens move between chains while maintaining a single shared supply. Flare adds another verification model that OFT issuers can choose. Used alongside independent verifiers, it can make the checks behind those transfers more resilient.

This is Flare 'beyond' Flare.

Infrastructure already verifying XRP payments can support financial activity across other ecosystems. If more applications adopt it, Flare has a path to grow with the activity it helps verify while users and capital stay on the chains they already use.

NFA. DYOR.

SafePal Users Targeted by Physical Mail Phishing Following Data Breach

According to Italian crypto media outlet Criptovaluta it, hardware wallet maker SafePal’s data breach has led to physical mail phishing attacks targeting Italian users. Fraudulent letters impersonating SafePal claim that recipients’ hardware wallets have a firmware security vulnerability and contain QR codes that direct users via Arweave to a fake SafePal website. Both the letters and the phishing website contain accurate customer names, addresses and order details. Between March 2025 and April 2026, an issue with an order-tracking plugin exposed the personal data of nearly 40,000 SafePal customers, including names, email addresses and mailing addresses. SafePal previously confirmed that attackers had been using the leaked data for phishing attempts.

text:
You're watching our engine decide by itself how a message gets through a network with no internet, no servers and no cell towers.

What you can see it do:

→ Hop-by-hop delivery. The message moves device to device until it reaches the recipient, and you can see the path it took.
→ Store and forward. When there's no path yet, devices hold the message and pass it on when someone comes into range.
→ Retries. Turn up "frames lost" and watch the engine resend what the air dropped.
→ Read receipts. Confirmation travels back across the mesh to the sender.
→ Islands. Shrink the radio range and the mesh splits into groups that can't reach each other. Messages wait at the edge until a bridge appears.
→ Cost. Every message shows how many frames and relays it took.

This is the hard part of offline-first apps, made visible. It's the same behaviour your app gets when it runs on phones in a stadium, a disaster zone or a basement with no signal.

Built by @mizanxali, with message animations by @pixelyokai.

https://t.co/M7YBWkjf1m
author: OfflineProtocol
quoted_text:
a lot of people i talked to at @EFDevcon couldn't picture how a message gets through an offline mesh network.

so i built this. every person on the map runs the real @OfflineProtocol engine (rust → wasm) in your browser. the only simulated part is the bluetooth link between them, and you get controls to tweak it.

add or remove people, pick a sender and a recipient, and watch the message spread through the mesh to reach them.

things to watch:
→ message delivery, hop by hop
→ store and forward
→ retries when the air drops frames
→ read receipts coming back to the sender
→ lost frames

text:
Providing liquidity for a new stablecoin today happens roughly like providing liquidity for any other token: i) get the asset listed on exchanges ii) seed some initial liquidity iii) pay market makers to create liquidity depth.

This is a bad system for money and payments. In TradFi, we don’t do liquidity for dollars/payments the same way we do liquidity for securities, commodities, or FX markets. In fact, the concept of liquidity doesn’t even exist for dollar to dollar money movement.

New banks aren’t worried about sourcing liquidity to be able to use ACH or FedWire. They certainly aren’t engaging Citadel to market-make their wires. The funds move via a ledger update coordinated by a central clearing party.

This is a better system. We’re building it for stablecoins.

text:
Coding agents are going to radically change the economics of game development, but  the much more interesting idea is that consumption itself becomes a creation primitive. What happens when playing a game and making a game become the same activity? When anyone can modify the rules, invent new mechanics, or extend a world simply by asking an agent to do it? I suspect millions of people will build games that nobody else ever plays, just for the joy of creating them.

@cdixon makes a great point in Read Write Own about how differently music and gaming responded to the internet. Music largely fought fan participation while gaming embraced it, and some of the biggest franchises in the world emerged from mods. 

Models take this idea to an extreme. Games become living, malleable worlds rather than finished products, and the distinction between creators and consumers starts to disappear. 

We spent this episode talking about everything from resurrecting forgotten games to compressing AAA development cycles to entirely new genres that wouldn’t have been economically viable before. But perhaps the biggest opportunity is building worlds where the creativity of millions of players can compound into something far more interesting than any individual developer could have imagined.

If a team gives up or winds down not having raised money and building themselves for a long time, that's not stealing from you, that is them protecting themselves and others from further pain and wasting time on something that doesn't work.

Be the moon that lights up the room when others are sitting angrily in darkness.
Everyone hurts, and hopefully we see the industry thrive soon again. People will remember how you acted in times of pain and hurt. Reach out to a friend or random and be there for them, hold each other close so our industry can move forward and onward.

text:
全网都在关心老黄到底睡了几个，但真正让华尔街后背发凉的，根本不是裤裆里那点事，而是这起黑天鹅撕开的三个残酷真相：$NVDA

第一个真相：为什么董事会敢在96小时内，把硅谷唯一的“造物主”扫地出门？

很多人想不通：老黄一手创办英伟达33年，把一家做显卡的小作坊干成万亿帝国，怎么说踢就踢？ 去翻一下英伟达的公司章程就懂了——老黄死在了自己的“现代企业美德”上。

英伟达没有AB股（双重股权结构），黄仁勋手里只有个位数百分比的股份和投票权。按章程，董事会11名董事，只要6个人举手，就能直接罢免CEO，甚至不需要任何理由。 

对比一下隔壁Meta：扎克伯格死死攥着超级投票权，同样的丑闻如果发生在小扎身上，董事会连他的皮毛都动不了。

创始人不设AB股，顺风顺水时叫“治理透明的美德”，一旦出事，就是被人一剑封喉的“命门”。 11月8日董事会还在喊“完全信任”，4天后直接6票过半斩草除根，连董事席位都没给他留。

第二个真相：老黄出局，最先断粮的可能是国内的AI算力。

很多人还在猜谁接班（顺便辟个谣：昨天疯传的Jay Puri今年6月就退休了，连8-K文件都没有的假消息别再传了），但对中文圈来说，真正致命的暗雷在华盛顿。

过去几年，顶着巨大的政治压力在华盛顿来回游说、替对华芯片销售撕开裂缝的，主要就是黄仁勋本人。 

现在他倒了，国会正在借题发挥，推动在今年的《国防授权法案》（NDAA）里塞进一批极其严苛的先进AI芯片出口限制条款。 

老黄留下的这个游说真空，临时顶上的CFO克雷斯补不上，未来的新CEO更不敢碰。我的个人判断：在国安调查的阴影下，英伟达对华特供芯片的窗口，大概率要彻底焊死了。

第三个真相：英伟达正在滑向“2018年的英特尔时刻”。

过去十年，美股有两家巨头因为CEO职场私生活换帅，结局天差地别： 

▪️ 2019年麦当劳赶走Easterbrook，股价照样涨——因为卖汉堡不需要技术信仰，谁当CEO都能转； 

▪️ 2018年英特尔赶走Krzanich，让CFO临时接盘，结果技术路线一路崩盘，直接错失整个移动与AI时代。

不幸的是，英伟达是比英特尔更极端的“技术独裁”公司。

5天后（11月17日）就是Q3财报夜，这是没有黄仁勋的第一个夜晚。纯财务出身的克雷斯要独自面对华尔街的拷问：

董事会什么时候能选出懂技术的掌舵人？

失去灵魂人物后，下季度指引会不会下调？

微软、Meta这些超级大客户有没有动摇？

有人问老黄会不会像1997年的乔布斯、或者去年的奥特曼一样杀回来？ 

别做梦了。

哪怕路透社说绝大多数员工盼他留任，哪怕他还是第四大股东，但这次背着国家安全相关的调查，性质已经彻底变了。

皮衣封存，那个一人决定全球算力走向的时代，真的结束了。 11月17日的财报夜，大家系好安全带。

Beijing is exploring a $15 billion maritime insurance and reinsurance hub by 2029, challenging Western dominance of global shipping coverage.

The proposed system would protect Chinese shipping from Western sanctions and disruptions, particularly in high-risk routes such as the Strait of Hormuz.

China Re, PICC and Hong Kong's Marine War Insurance Pool are among the potential participants.

The global maritime insurance market is worth roughly $25 billion annually, supporting more than $14 trillion in global goods trade.

Talks remain preliminary, but the initiative could weaken Western control over a critical pillar of global trade.

in the 1950-80s, morris chang joined texas instrument as a young enginerer, rose to run the entire semiconductor business, and built it into the largest in the world. he expected the top job but the ceo succession went to someone else instead and he effectively got forced out of the company. in his own account he had the record but not the political sponsorship, as an immigrant mid-career hire outside the founders' circle. a couple years later the taiwan government recruited him, and handed a him a big check and a ton of resources to found tsmc, which has now become the single most strategically important company on earth. 

this was the biggest unforced error in the history of the american semis industry (read the “chip war” by chris miller if u want to learn more). tsmc could’ve been “texas semiconductor manufacturing company” but its “taiwan” instead.

when we look back in a few decades, the ousting of jensen in the middle of the most important tech revolution of the 21sr century is probably not too far behind.

很多人问我SOXL涨回来了。我是不是又赚回来了。
我都止损了怎么赚回来，当然不止损的话，38块钱就已经爆仓了。
我现在真的很悲观，1个多月时间亏了120万刀，感觉自己赚不回来这个钱了。

一个人倒下了三次，站起来了三次，第四次倒下了，他还能站起来么。身边的朋友似乎对我都很有信心觉得我能轻松赚回来，只有我知道自己的压力有多大。因为我不再年轻。
每次我都云淡风轻的安慰自己：亏的都是之前赚的。这次真的是躯体化了，什么都不想做。本来明天去吉隆坡看李志演唱会的，我给退了。包机酒的泰国BBW也推掉了。

再一个我感觉币圈真的没有机会了，现在整个市场只有合约和meme，而合约中，SOXL的交易量已经和ETH不相上下，交易所支持美股交易，并没有给币圈带来多少的资金量，反而是把币圈的资金分流到了美股中。这两天BTC的颓势很明显，11月5号的大暴跌，让币圈的资金在美股受损严重。美股都反弹回来了，而BTC却是阴跌不断。在没有外部利好单独刺激的情况下，何时能反转。
那这样一个市场还能让我重新赚到钱么，总不能靠交易美股赚回来吧。

最后反思下自己的交易，正如 @Bitfatty 说的我的交易策略有很大的问题。遇到黑天鹅的时候，大概率会死。 我每次合约亏大钱似乎都是这样。我可以在99天里赚钱，每天赚1w，但会在第100天亏掉所有。因为人永远都会上头。

写完感觉会好受点。我不介意大家嘲笑我。只希望在这样一个残酷的市场，大家都能活下去。

text:
불륜을 공식 시인한 지 단 나흘 만에, 33년 엔비디아를 이끌던 젠슨 황이 모든 자리에서 즉시 사임함.

CEO 직함만 뗀 게 아니라 이사회 이사직까지 완전히 손을 뗐고, 엔비디아 공식 발표문에는 본인의 퇴임 인사말 한 줄조차 실리지 않았음.

다음 주 실적 발표를 코앞에 두고 이사회가 이렇게까지 단호하게 선을 그어버린 진짜 이유는 뭘까?

1. 자진 사임 형식을 빌린 사실상의 축출과 1인 지배 체제 해체

대외적으로는 스스로 물러난 모양새를 취했지만 월스트리트저널은 아예 이사회에 의해 쫓겨났다고 보도했음.

중국 정보기관 연루 의혹 여성과의 관계로 미 연방수사국(FBI) 수사와 하원 소환 압박을 받는 와중에, 직속 부하 임원과의 두 번째 사내 불륜과 경호팀 입막음 정황까지 터지자 이사회가 칼을 빼 든 거임.

특히 오는 화요일 분기 실적 발표를 앞둔 상황에서 창업자 개인의 안보·윤리 리스크가 회사 전체로 번지는 걸 막으려 전격적인 분리에 나섰음.

급한 불은 월가 신임이 두터운 콜레트 크레스 최고재무책임자(CFO)가 임시 CEO를 겸임해 껐고, 창업 초기인 1993년부터 이사회에 몸담아 온 하비 존스를 창립 33년 만에 첫 이사회 의장으로 앉히며 권력을 쪼갰음.

덕분에 장 초반 14.3%까지 폭락하던 주가도 최악의 불확실성이 걷혔다는 안도 매수세가 유입되며 4~5%대 하락 선까지 낙폭의 3분의 2 가까이를 되돌렸지만, 업계 안팎에서는 진짜 후폭풍은 지금부터라는 경고가 쏟아지고 있음.

2. 공장 하나 없는 설계 회사가 누리던 75% 마진과 공급망 장악력의 시험대

엔비디아는 반도체를 직접 찍어내는 공장도 없고 서버 장비를 직접 조립하지도 않는 설계 전문 회사임.

그런 회사가 100원어치를 팔면 원가를 빼고 74~75원이 남는 경이로운 마진율을 유지하며 세계 최정상 기업이 된 건 젠슨 황 개인의 돌파력 덕분이 컸음.

대만 TSMC와 한국의 SK하이닉스·삼성전자 같은 핵심 부품사들로부터 물량을 최우선으로 끌어모으고, 빅테크는 물론 각국 정상들까지 직접 만나 국가 단위 계약을 따내 왔기 때문임.

관리형 전문경영인이 그 자리를 대신했을 때도 부품 공급사들이 예전처럼 엔비디아에 물량을 최우선 배정해 주고, 거대 클라우드 고객사들이 70%가 넘는 높은 마진을 군말 없이 내줄지는 장담하기 어려움.

실제로 오늘 엔비디아가 흔들리는 사이 맞춤형 AI 칩 강자인 브로드컴과 경쟁사 AMD 주가가 나란히 5% 넘게 뛰어오른 것도 바로 이 독점 협상력의 빈틈에 자금이 몰렸기 때문임.

3. 사내 권력 다툼과 창업자 특유의 과감한 승부수 실종 우려

인공지능 시장이 열리기 한참 전인 2006년 월가의 거센 반대를 무릅쓰고 쿠다 생태계를 밀어붙인 것도, 고속 통신망 기업 멜라녹스를 69억 달러(약 9조 2천억 원)에 사들이고 지난해 말 추론 칩 스타트업 그록의 핵심 기술과 창업자 사단을 200억 달러(약 26조 7천억 원)에 통째로 흡수한 것도 창업자였기에 가능했던 결단임.

수십 년간 야심 찬 천재 엔지니어들을 하나로 묶어두던 구심점이 사라지면서, 이제 차기 정식 CEO 자리를 둘러싼 사내 권력 다툼과 핵심 인재 유출이 본격화될 수 있다는 지적이 나옴.

관료적인 이사회와 재무 중심 경영진 체제에서는 눈앞의 수익성은 챙길지 몰라도, 제2의 그록 같은 위협적인 도전자들이 나타났을 때 수십조 원 현금을 베팅해 경쟁의 싹을 사들이는 승부수를 던지기 어려워짐.

4. 서구권 공개형 AI 생태계 전체에 닥친 뜻밖의 악재

이번 퇴진은 반도체 시장을 넘어 인공지능 생태계의 세력 구도까지 흔들 대형 변수임.

그동안 젠슨 황은 오픈AI나 앤트로픽, 구글 같은 소수 폐쇄형 모델 기업들이 자체 칩을 설계하며 시장을 가두는 걸 막기 위해, 누구나 무료로 내려받아 고쳐 쓸 수 있는 공개형 AI 모델(오픈웨이트) 진영을 가장 든든하게 밀어주던 최대 후원자였음.

무료 AI 모델이 세상에 널리 풀려야 전 세계 기업들이 특정 빅테크에 종속되지 않고 엔비디아 칩을 사서 직접 AI를 돌리기 때문임.

최근 선두 빅테크들이 자사 AI의 답변을 교보재 삼아 후발 모델을 빠르게 학습시키는 기법(증류)까지 강하게 차단하며 공개형 모델 진영의 숨통이 조여오던 시점에 가장 큰 버팀목마저 사라진 셈임.

새 경영진이 눈앞의 수익으로 직결되지 않는 네모트론 같은 자체 공개 모델 투자를 줄이기 시작하면, 서구권 공개형 AI 생태계 전체가 급격히 얼어붙을 수 있음.

오늘 주가가 장 초반의 패닉을 빠르게 거둬들인 건 당장 다음 주 실적이나 이미 줄 서 있는 내년 치 주문표가 하루아침에 사라지지는 않기 때문일 거임.

하지만 위대한 창업자가 남긴 진짜 빈자리는 눈앞의 분기 매출이 아니라, 3년 뒤와 5년 뒤 판이 뒤집히는 길목에서 모두가 반대하는 방향에 회사의 명운을 걸어야 할 때 비로소 드러나곤 함.

1985년 스티브 잡스가 쫓겨난 뒤에도 애플은 이미 깔아둔 제품의 관성으로 몇 년간 매출이 세 배 넘게 늘며 순항했지만, 정작 판이 바뀌던 90년대 중반에는 새 돌파구를 찾지 못해 파산 직전까지 몰렸음. 젠슨 황 없는 엔비디아의 실력도 몇 년 뒤 다음 파도가 밀려올 때 판가름 날 거임.

🚨BREAKING: NVIDIA CEO has been summoned before congress on Nov 18 to explain ties to alleged Chinese spy.

U.S Government now suspects NVIDIA chief Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy based on American Intelligence memo. 

U.S. intelligence officials believe China’s Ministry of State Security recruited Alice Huang to gather information on American AI chips and potentially influence Nvidia’s efforts to sell advanced processors to China.

The Republican chairs of three House committees have now asked for a closed-door briefing on Huang’s contacts with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer.

China has historically accounted for up to a fifth of Nvidia’s revenue, and Jensen Huang personally lobbied President Trump to allow sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips there. 

Washington fears those chips could accelerate China’s military modernization.

Despite U.S. Commerce Department export restrictions, underground networks continue to funnel advanced Nvidia hardware into mainland China. 

Authorities have recently dismantled several high-profile smuggling operations, including a recent detention of an NVIDIA employee helping reroute $21 million worth of Nvidia's flagship chips to mainland China via shell companies.

Nvidia maintains that the meetings were routine business and that no sensitive information was shared.

text:
젠슨황 불륜을 의도적으로 터뜨리는 느낌이 있어서
민주당이 이렇게까지 적극적일 이유가 있을까 하는 생각이 들었는데, 월스트리트와의 합작이라는 관점이 있어서 전달드려 봅니다.

젠슨 황의 불륜은 단지 방아쇠일 뿐이다. 우리가 목격하고 있는 것은 월스트리트와 워싱턴이 조율한 엔비디아의 조 단위 컴퓨팅 제국에 대한 사전 계획된 권력 장악이다.

일부 예리한 중국계 미국인 논평가들은 이를 미국의 새로운 붉은 공포(Red Scare)로 부르며, 엘리트 아시아 기업가들을 겨냥한 것이라고 말한다.

빌 게이츠, 일론 머스크, 그리고 다른 백인 테크 억만장자들은 개인적 행실로 인해 반복적인 스캔들을 겪었다. 그러나 그 누구도 국가 안보 조사나 이사회 인수합병으로 끌려간 적이 없다. 오직 젠슨 황만이 개인적 관계 실수 후 독립 이사회 조사와 정보 기관의 적대적 내러티브에 직면해 있다.

이중 잣대는 더 이상 명확할 수 없다: 백인 엘리트들에게는 개인적 결함이 사적인 문제로 남지만, 전략적 테크 자산을 장악한 중국 출신 리더에게는 아주 작은 흠집조차 국가 안보 위험으로 프레임된다.

엔비디아는 글로벌 AI 컴퓨팅의 중추로, 대략 4조 달러의 가치를 지녔다. 마크 저커버그가 듀얼 클래스 슈퍼 투표 주식으로 통제를 고수하는 메타와 달리, 또는 펜타곤과 정보 기관에 깊이 통합된 마이크로소프트와 아마존과 달리, 엔비디아에는 그런 보호 구조가 없다.

2026년 공시 자료에 따르면 젠슨 황은 지분의 3.58%만 보유하고 있으며, 모든 이사와 경영진을 합쳐도 겨우 3.94%에 불과하다. 뱅가드와 블랙록은 각각 9.32%와 7.43%를 소유하며 결정적 투표권을 쥐고 있다. 기관적 보호막이나 깊은 정치적 후원 없이, 이 핵심 테크 거인은 강대국 경쟁의 체스판 위에 노출되어 있다.

이 인수합병의 토대는 몇 달 전부터 마련되었다. 황의 오랜 이사회 동맹인 마크 페리와 마이클 매카프리는 주요 위원회에서 물러났다. 민주당 기득권, 월스트리트, 미국 정보 기관과 연결된 내부자들이 조용히 진입했다: 
✅ 수잔 노라 존슨, 전 골드만삭스 부회장 겸 브루킹스 연구소 공동 의장으로, 2026년 7월 엔비디아 감사 위원회에 합류해 내부 조사와 컴플라이언스를 직접 감독한다. ✅ 케네스 제이콥스, 브루킹스 부회장 겸 뱅가드 신임 의장으로, 최대 기관 투표 블록을 장악하며 존슨과 같은 내부 서클에서 활동한다. 
✅ 길먼 루이, CIA 지원 벤처 펀드 In-Q-Tel의 창립 CEO이자 대통령 정보 자문 위원회 위원으로, 존슨과 함께 국가 테크 펀드에서 일하며 전략적 테크 기업의 정보 인수를 감독한다.

미디어 롤아웃은 정확한 정치적 타임라인을 따랐다. 초기 시험 풍선은 10월 29일에 등장했다. 11월 6일, 민주당이 의회를 완전히 장악한 바로 그날, 뉴욕 타임스의 줄리안 반스(국가 안보 담당)와 파이낸셜 타임스의 데메트리 세바스토풀로가 조율된 보도를 발표하며, 정보 메모를 인용해 개인 스캔들을 폭로했다.

진짜 범죄는 결코 그 불륜이 아니었다. 그것은 2025년 젠슨 황이 트럼프 행정부와 체결한 거래였다: H200 칩의 중국 수출 승인을 얻기 위해 25% 매출 공유를 제안한 것이다. 정상적인 상업 협상이었으나, 새로 들어선 민주당에 의해 미국 AI 주권에 대한 위험한 타협으로 재구성되었다.

이 조사는 엔비디아 주가를 무너뜨리지 않을 것이다 — 월스트리트는 여기에 거대한 지분을 들고 있다. 하지만 미국 기득권에게 세 가지 전략적 승리를 안길 것이다:

1. 엔비디아의 창업자 제거와 중국화 탈피: 존슨 파벌이 주도하는 새로운 영구 국가 안보 컴플라이언스 위원회가 황의 칩 수출 및 해외 전략 권한을 박탈할 것이다. 그의 이중 회장-CEO 역할은 분리될 것이다.

2. 중국 AI 한계 고정: 워싱턴은 글로벌 첨단 컴퓨팅 공급의 완전한 지휘권을 장악해 칩 흐름을 규제하며 중국의 AI 진척을 늦출 것이다.

quoted_text:
Jensen Huang’s affair is just a trigger. What we are witnessing is a pre-planned power grab over Nvidia’s trillion-dollar computing empire, coordinated by Wall Street and Washington.

Some sharp Chinese-American commentators call it America’s new Red Scare targeting elite Asian entrepreneurs.

Bill Gates, Elon Musk and other white tech billionaires have faced repeated scandals over personal conduct. None were dragged into national security probes or boardroom takeovers. Only Jensen Huang, after a personal relationship misstep, faces an independent board investigation and hostile narrative from intelligence circles.

The double standard could not be clearer: For white elites, personal flaws are private matters. For a Chinese-born leader controlling a strategic tech asset, any tiny blemish gets framed as a national security risk.

Nvidia is the backbone of global AI computing, valued at roughly $4 trillion. Unlike Meta, where Mark Zuckerberg locks control with dual-class super-voting shares, or Microsoft and Amazon, deeply integrated with the Pentagon and intelligence agencies, Nvidia has no such protective structure. 

Public filings from 2026 show Jensen Huang holds only 3.58% of shares, and all directors plus executives together hold merely 3.94%. Vanguard and BlackRock own 9.32% and 7.43% respectively, holding decisive voting power. Without institutional shields or deep political backing, this critical tech giant sits exposed on the chessboard of great-power competition.

The groundwork for this takeover was laid months ago. Longtime board allies of Huang, Mark Perry and Michael McCaffrey, stepped down from key committees. Insiders tied to Democratic establishment, Wall Street and U.S. intelligence quietly moved in: 
✅ Suzanne Nora Johnson, former Goldman Sachs vice chair and co-chair of Brookings Institution, joined Nvidia’s audit committee in July 2026 with direct oversight of internal investigations and compliance. ✅ Kenneth Jacobs, vice chair of Brookings and incoming Vanguard chair, controls the largest institutional voting bloc and operates within the same inner circle as Johnson. 
✅ Gilman Louie,founding CEO of CIA-backed venture fund In-Q-Tel and member of the President’s Intelligence Advisory Board, works alongside Johnson on the same national tech fund, overseeing intelligence acquisition of strategic tech firms.

The media rollout followed a precise political timeline. Initial trial balloons appeared on Oct 29. On Nov 6, the very day Democrats secured full control of Congress, Julian Barnes of the New York Times (national security beat) and Demetri Sevastopulo of the Financial Times published coordinated reports, citing intelligence memos while breaking the story of the personal scandal.

The real offense was never the affair. It was the 2025 deal Jensen struck with the Trump administration: offering a 25% revenue share to win export approval for H200 chips into China. A normal commercial negotiation, reframed by incoming Democrats as a dangerous compromise on U.S. AI sovereignty.

This investigation will not crash Nvidia’s stock — Wall Street holds massive stakes here. But it will deliver three strategic wins for the U.S. establishment:

1. De-founder and de-Sinicize Nvidia: A new permanent national security compliance committee, led by Johnson’s faction, will strip Huang of authority over chip exports and overseas strategy. His dual Chairman-CEO role will be split.

2. Lock down China’s AI ceiling: Washington will seize full command of global advanced computing supply, regulating chip flows to slow China’s AI progress.

3. Retroactively target Trump: Once Democrats take over congressional oversight panels in January 2027, this case will be used to accuse the Trump White House of negligence for approving the H200 export deal.

Jensen Huang spent 27 years building this computing empire, believing in rules, technical merit and business contracts. But there is a brutal truth in America’s power game: Top-tier strategic technology and wealth without political cover are nothing more than bargaining chips waiting to be carved up.

White elites get generous room for error. Asian pioneers who climb to the very top get almost none. This is not a story about infidelity. It is a raw demonstration of racial hierarchy, capital control and partisan power politics in the United States.

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO this morning. 
Hyperliquid had been pricing it for 16 hours.

Just before 5pm ET yesterday the NYT reported an alleged second affair. At 5:28pm the WSJ reported the board was preparing to push him out. Nvidia on Hyperliquid went from $174 at the close to $156 inside the hour, with over $300M traded.

By the time the resignation was confirmed it was at $152, down 12% before the bell. At the open it touched $148.86, then snapped back to $162 in 15 minutes.

What the onchain data shows right now:

Nvidia did almost $2B of volume on Hyperliquid in the last 24 hours, about 4x the Nasdaq 100 perp. Open interest is $647M, up from $359M yesterday afternoon.

The whales are short. The 200 most profitable accounts this month hold $156M short vs $35M long, and several added shorts between $159 and $163.

The proven traders are buying. Wallets with long track records opened $12.8M of Nvidia longs between 7:26 and 9:38am, into the selloff.

And funding flipped positive, so longs are paying to hold the dip.

Two smart groups on opposite sides, an interim CEO who is also the CFO, and earnings next week.

This is the market structure I keep coming back to. 
The news broke before the close, and a 24/7 market priced it overnight with every position public. 

That's the kind of data our AI agents read before they trade, on 24/7/365 markets.

Which side would you be on?

text:
NVIDIA employees: go on strike. Now.

Not for a raise. Not for more PTO. For your founder.

Jensen Huang was just pushed out in four days, after thirty-three years building the company. The GPU, CUDA, the entire infrastructure the world's AI runs on today. And it ends with a three-line press release on a Thursday morning.

Here are the facts. Sunday, Huang admits to an affair and apologizes to his teams. The board launches an independent investigation, led by Wachtell Lipton and a former federal prosecutor. Thursday, he resigns under pressure. The investigation hasn't reached any conclusion. No technology leak has been established. No misconduct has been announced.

The sentence came before the verdict.

Let me be clear: if the investigation shows that NVIDIA secrets ended up in Beijing, he has to go, and nobody will defend him. But you don't unplug the most important builder of the decade over press reports and a market panic. It's called the presumption of innocence. It applies to founders too.

And it has worked before.

November 2023. OpenAI's board fires Sam Altman on a Friday night. Within days, more than 700 of roughly 770 employees sign a letter: bring Altman back, or we all walk. Five days later, Altman is back, and most of the board that fired him is gone.

Call it the Altman precedent: in a company built on talent, real power doesn't sit with the board. It sits with the people who build.

NVIDIA's engineers hold that power today. They're the ones running the machine. Without them, there is no next generation of chips.

So put down your tools. All of you. And tell the board: no successor until the investigation is done. Facts first, sentence second.

A founder isn't an executive you swap out. A founder is the soul of the company. Apple learned that when it pushed out Steve Jobs in 1985. It took twelve years and a near-bankruptcy to bring him back.

NVIDIA doesn't have twelve years. The AI race won't wait for anyone.

A company's soul isn't something you vote on in a boardroom. It's something you fight for.

text:
Update your weights: I've joined @archetypevc as Chief Product Officer!

A product role at a venture firm is unusual, here's why I think it makes sense now.

I've spent the last few years building at the intersection of crypto and AI. Crypto made it possible to program, distribute, and coordinate capital without a central institution. AI is making it possible to program, distribute, and coordinate intelligence without a central institution. I believe the lessons of crypto—particularly around ownership, incentives, and open coordination—will be central to how autonomous AI systems interact and transact. Together, they change the upper bound of what ideas individuals and small teams can pursue.

If the shape of a company is changing, the institutions that support it should change too. The best venture firms have always been built on judgment, relationships, and conviction. Those won't change, but the product built around them can: the tools, systems, and hands-on know-how to support founders and let them focus on building.

That's the job I want to help shape. As CPO, I'm building Archetype's internal platform and tools, bringing a product perspective to investing, and working directly with early-stage founders to help them accelerate.

But I joined Archetype specifically because of the team: people whose judgment I respect, who set a high bar for the work, and pursue a depth of engagement with founders and their ideas that I hadn't seen elsewhere.

If you're building across programmable capital and/or programmable intelligence, or even experimenting with product experiences that couldn't exist before, I'd love to connect.

text:
NVIDIA employees: go on strike. Now.

Not for a raise. Not for more PTO. For your founder.

Jensen Huang was just pushed out in four days, after thirty-three years building the company. The GPU, CUDA, the entire infrastructure the world's AI runs on today. And it ends with a three-line press release on a Thursday morning.

Here are the facts. Sunday, Huang admits to an affair and apologizes to his teams. The board launches an independent investigation, led by Wachtell Lipton and a former federal prosecutor. Thursday, he resigns under pressure. The investigation hasn't reached any conclusion. No technology leak has been established. No misconduct has been announced.

The sentence came before the verdict.

Let me be clear: if the investigation shows that NVIDIA secrets ended up in Beijing, he has to go, and nobody will defend him. But you don't unplug the most important builder of the decade over press reports and a market panic. It's called the presumption of innocence. It applies to founders too.

And it has worked before.

November 2023. OpenAI's board fires Sam Altman on a Friday night. Within days, more than 700 of roughly 770 employees sign a letter: bring Altman back, or we all walk. Five days later, Altman is back, and most of the board that fired him is gone.

Call it the Altman precedent: in a company built on talent, real power doesn't sit with the board. It sits with the people who build.

NVIDIA's engineers hold that power today. They're the ones running the machine. Without them, there is no next generation of chips.

So put down your tools. All of you. And tell the board: no successor until the investigation is done. Facts first, sentence second.

A founder isn't an executive you swap out. A founder is the soul of the company. Apple learned that when it pushed out Steve Jobs in 1985. It took twelve years and a near-bankruptcy to bring him back.

NVIDIA doesn't have twelve years. The AI race won't wait for anyone.

A company's soul isn't something you vote on in a boardroom. It's something you fight for.

quoted_text:
Tarek predicted 5 month ago that Citadel would sue Kalshi.

In this interview from June, @mansourtarek_ explains exactly why stock perps are a big threat to Wall Street.

Now Citadel, CME, Cboe and Nasdaq are suing him to stop Kalshi from offering perps.

Here is why.

1 - THEY FEAR LOSING RETAIL

Citadel executes ~35% of US-listed retail volume and make money by trading against their orders. Stock perps threaten to redirect that activity.

If someone trades an Apple perp on Kalshi instead of Apple shares, Citadel loses.

Their own court filing explicitly admit to it:

- “Cboe and Citadel Securities lose transactions and revenue they cannot later recover.”
- “Kalshi's offering is designed to draw away CME’s customers who currently trade futures.”

2 - PERPS GENERATE LESS FEES

So why wouldn't Citadel just offer Perps themselve ?

Because traditional futures have an expiry date. To keep your exposure you need to close you old position and open a new ones. Those additional transactions generate fees. 

Perps don’t expire, removing those fees entirely.

The interview passage where Tarek highlights this Perps over Futures advantage is even cited by CME in the lawsuit.

That's why the Citadel camp is asking to reclassify Perps as security-based swaps:

1) Citadel wins - Perps are SEC regulated, retails can't trade them, they keep trading future on their exchange.

2) Kalshi wins - Perps are CFTC regulated, retail can trade them over more expensive futures, Kalshi receive their order flow.

It's all about who gets to farm retail.

text:
I don't know how many Americans realize what they just lost.

This isn't a CEO. It's a national treasure.

And I'm going to prove to you, step by step, that the Nvidia board's decision goes against the interests of the United States. And that if America wants a future against China, it has to fight to bring Jensen Huang back.

A. The AI race is won on compute.

That's not an opinion, it's physics. The most powerful models are the ones with the most compute. And most of America's compute runs on Nvidia chips.

B. Nvidia's lead is one man's judgment.

Jensen is the one who bet on CUDA when nobody believed in it. He's the one who understood before anyone else what deep learning would become. He's the one who pivoted the entire company toward AI, years before ChatGPT. Thirty-three years of decisions nobody else would have made.

C. The board prepared no successor.

It admits it itself: it's now considering searching for a CEO from the outside. That means months of searching, internal power struggles, cautious decisions. At the exact moment Huawei is accelerating with the entire Chinese state behind it.

D. The market has already delivered its verdict.

The stock dropped another 10% or so on the announcement. Hundreds of billions of dollars gone. And those dollars are also the retirement savings of tens of millions of Americans.

Conclusion: who benefits from this decision?

Not America. Not shareholders. Not employees. China.

Now let's look at what he's accused of.

Yes, Jensen messed up. Twice. That's real. I'm not defending his private life.

But he isn't accused of any crime. No one has shown that a single secret leaked. The board itself wrote that it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia's secrets were compromised.

You don't destroy the pillar of America's technology strategy over a moral failing. You sanction it, you tighten oversight, and you keep the man the country needs.

And we know exactly how to do it. There's a precedent.

In 2018, the SEC went after Elon Musk. Many demanded he leave Tesla. The solution? He gave up the chairmanship, Tesla added independent directors, and he stayed CEO. You know the rest: Tesla became one of the most valuable companies in the world.

Nvidia just appointed its first-ever board chair. The oversight structure is there. The only thing missing is the founder.

Because founders aren't managers like the others.

Peter Thiel laid it out in Zero to One: founder-led companies are capable of long-term planning, of making decisions nobody else would dare to make, and of inspiring a loyalty no hired manager can ever buy. Paul Graham called it "founder mode": when a founder runs the company, the rules of conventional management don't apply. They see things nobody else sees.

Steve Jobs is the living proof. Apple's board fired him. Twelve years later, Apple was months from bankruptcy. Jobs came back and made it the most valuable company in the world. How many years were lost? How many products never launched?

And recent history has even shown us that a comeback is possible.

Three years ago, OpenAI's board fired Sam Altman. Within five days, more than 700 of its 770 employees threatened to leave. Investors applied pressure. Altman came back, and the board was replaced.

What was undone in five days at OpenAI can be undone at Nvidia.

Employees need to speak up. Shareholders need to speak up. Washington needs to understand what's at stake. Everyone who believes America must win this race needs to say loud and clear that this decision is a historic mistake.

You will never find another Jensen Huang. Not in ten years. Not in thirty. There's only one.

Bring him back.

#BringBackJensen

text:
All the tech people rushing to defend Jensen are off base.

As a VC, I get it. He's a generational founder, and there's a deeply-ingrained lesson in tech that founders are almost always the best people to run their companies. I share that intuition.

But the board's call here was dead simple:

1. His credibility is shredded. Jensen said two weeks ago that his relationship with Alice Huang was "completely normal and not unusual." Ten days later he admitted the affair. Now there's a second affair, with an exec who reports directly to him. As others have said: "when you find two ants in your kitchen, the best estimate for the ants in your kitchen is not two." 
2. He violated export controls and tried to quash the investigation into MegaSpeed, which could be an extremely serious crime. The Trump admin is already signaling that they are going to reverse course on export restrictions because of this scandal.
3. The politics has flipped. His relationship with Trump is no longer the asset it was. The Dems are in control of Congress now and there is furious anti-AI backlash that Nvidia will need to weather. Having been compromised by a Chinese spy and advocating for exports to China makes him totally disqualified on these questions going forward. There is going to be hell to pay over the next few years, and Nvidia needs a CEO who can walk into those hearings with legitimacy. Otherwise this cloud would always hang over him.
4. There's a business to run. The dude already wrote one apology letter. Was the board supposed to wait for him to write a second one? A third? You can't run a $4T company like this.

A CEO has to be reliable first and foremost. Once that’s gone, you don’t get it back. 

Jensen will almost certainly have a second act. But just not as CEO of Nvidia.

And anyone calling this a psy-op or a coup should just look at the Polymarket on this. Before the second affair, Jensen was only at 15% to be out as CEO. He could've survived one scandal, and I agreed it'd be foolish to let him go at that point. Easy to argue he was duped and made a mistake.

But you don't get two.

text:
昨天最让我看不懂的，是一群人听 Dario Amodei 说了几句 AI 能治愈癌症，就开始宣布 AI 泡沫不存在了。

在 Anthropic 的 IPO 路演中，Dario 预测，不到 10 年，癌症、阿尔茨海默病、心脏病乃至精神疾病，都可能成为历史。

然后我就看到不少人拿着这段讲话大吹特吹，甚至把它当成反驳 AI 泡沫论的证据。

不是，什么时候一家公司的 CEO 对未来许下的宏大愿景，都能拿来证明今天的估值合理了？

Gary Marcus 、直接把 Dario 的这段讲话和 Theranos 创始人 Elizabeth Holmes 当年的说辞相提并论，称两者都是空话，还补了一刀：「有些投资人永远不长记性。」

我觉得这次 Gary 说得挺对。

首先，我并不怀疑 AI 能够推动医学进步。事实上，AI 已经在药物发现、蛋白质研究等领域展现出了实际价值。但从加速某些科研环节，到让癌症、阿尔茨海默病等复杂疾病在十年内成为历史，中间差的可不是几次模型迭代。

疾病的机制能否被理解，候选药物能否通过临床试验，疗法能否真正安全有效地应用于患者，都是需要逐一解决的问题。

这些问题，凭什么因为 AI 变聪明了，就能自动迎刃而解？

更何况，Dario 说的根本不是一个有明确验证标准的技术目标，而是一个极其宏大、极其模糊的未来预言。

甚至有些荒诞的是，今年 8 月，Dario 自己还说过，宣称 AI 将治愈癌症，听起来更像陈词滥调而非鼓舞人心，很多人会觉得这是一种欺骗。

几个月后，类似的愿景却被堂而皇之地放到了 IPO 路演的结尾。

当然，我也不觉得 Anthropic 和 Theranos 是一回事。Claude 的技术能力、用户需求和商业收入都是真实存在的。

但真实的技术进步，和围绕技术形成的金融泡沫，本来就可以同时存在。

这恰恰是我最想吐槽的地方。

现在的 AI 行业，似乎越来越不允许人们同时相信这两件事。只要你质疑估值，质疑商业模式，质疑几千亿美元的资本开支是否合理，就总有人搬出 AGI、科学革命、人类文明的未来，试图让你闭嘴。

问题是，AI 能不能治愈癌症，和今天的投资人有没有为 AI 公司支付过高的价格，到底有什么必然关系？

哪怕十年后 AI 真的攻克了一系列重大疾病，也不能倒过来证明今天的每一笔投资都是理性的，更不能保证创造这些技术的公司最终都能赚到钱。

科技史上从来不缺改变世界的技术，也不缺在正确的技术方向上亏得血本无归的投资人。

真正让我有些担忧的，还不是 Dario 说了什么，而是许多人如此轻易地就被说服了。

text:
Today we’re announcing Strongpoint MPC at Project Eleven.

We’ve spent a lot of time working on one of the harder problems in post-quantum cryptography: making hash-based signatures work with MPC.

Previous research estimated over 85 minutes for the secure hash computations alone in threshold SPHINCS+ signing. We’ve developed a new approach that brings threshold signing down to under a second in certain configurations.

We’re starting with Ethereum, supporting leanSPHINCS and leanXMSS, with dealerless key generation and support for common threshold configurations.

This is a big milestone for our research team and for making post-quantum security practical for institutional custody
author: apruden08
quoted_text:
Introducing Strongpoint MPC: Post-Quantum MPC, Without the Compromises

A breakthrough in threshold signing technology brings the security and performance of modern MPC into the quantum and AI era.

The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway. Blockchains, financial institutions, and digital asset infrastructure providers are preparing to replace the cryptographic algorithms that have secured digital ownership for decades. At the same time, advances in artificial intelligence are creating new uncertainty about the long-term security of existing cryptographic systems.

But replacing an algorithm is only part of the challenge. The infrastructure built around today's cryptography must also evolve, and few technologies are more important to institutional digital asset security than multi-party computation (MPC).

Today, Project Eleven is introducing Strongpoint MPC, a breakthrough in threshold cryptography that makes high-performance, post-quantum MPC practical. Our research demonstrates that migrating to post-quantum cryptography does not have to mean sacrificing the performance, flexibility, and security properties institutions have come to expect from traditional MPC. In fact, our approach can deliver signing performance that exceeds classical ECDSA-based MPC.

Strongpoint MPC is available within Strongpoint, Project Eleven’s institutional digital asset custody platform, enabling institutions to use post-quantum threshold signing while maintaining control over their assets and cryptographic key material.

The challenge with post-quantum MPC

MPC has become a foundational technology for securing digital assets. Rather than entrusting a private key to a single person, device, or system, MPC distributes signing authority across multiple independent parties. Transactions can be authorized without reconstructing the complete private key in any one location.

Today, this technology underpins institutional custody solutions used by exchanges, custodians, and financial institutions. Its applications extend well beyond moving funds, including blockchain validators, cross-chain bridges, oracles, and the administrative keys responsible for minting, freezing, and managing tokenized assets.

Over the last decade, MPC built around elliptic curve cryptography has become remarkably sophisticated. Institutions can coordinate signatures quickly, support complex approval structures, and operate distributed signing infrastructure with minimal latency. The transition to post-quantum cryptography threatens to disrupt much of that progress.

The mathematical properties that enable efficient threshold signing with ECDSA do not translate directly to post-quantum signature schemes. Hash-based signatures, in particular, have historically presented substantial challenges for MPC. Previous approaches suggested that generating a single threshold signature using certain hash-based constructions could take too long to be practical. For an institution processing transactions continuously, that kind of latency would make the technology impractical.

The apparent tradeoff was severe: preserve the performance of classical MPC while remaining exposed to future quantum threats, or adopt post-quantum protections at the expense of operational efficiency.

We've developed an approach that fundamentally changes that equation.

A breakthrough in post-quantum threshold cryptography

Project Eleven has developed a new approach to multi-party signing that dramatically improves the efficiency of post-quantum MPC. Our breakthrough enables high-performance threshold signing using hash-based cryptography, with techniques designed to extend across multiple signature schemes.

Where earlier approaches suggested impractically long signing times, our architecture enables post-quantum MPC signing that can even outperform traditional ECDSA-based MPC. Strongpoint MPC brings this research into a product designed for real-world institutional deployment.

Built for institutional infrastructure

Institutional MPC systems must accommodate different architectures, security policies, and operational requirements. A custody provider, a blockchain validator, and a stablecoin issuer may all rely on MPC, but their signing environments and security requirements can differ considerably.

Strongpoint MPC has been designed with this flexibility in mind:
- High-performance signing: Post-quantum threshold signatures with performance that can exceed traditional ECDSA-based MPC.
- Flexible threshold configurations: Supports the most common signing arrangements, with arbitrary threshold configurations under development.
- Dealerless key generation: Distributed key generation without requiring a trusted dealer, while retaining the flexibility to accommodate trusted-dealer setups.
- Efficient communication: An architecture designed to minimize communication overhead and support signing across distributed infrastructure.
- Signature indistinguishability: MPC produces signatures that are indistinguishable from ordinary signatures under the same scheme, without exposing the threshold configuration or participating signers through the signature itself.
- Institutional control: Deployment that allows institutions to maintain control over their signing infrastructure and cryptographic key material.

Stablecoin issuers, for example, must secure the administrative keys responsible for minting tokens, freezing assets, and managing critical smart contracts. Blockchain validators, cross-chain bridges, and oracles similarly rely on distributed signing infrastructure to protect sensitive operations.

All of these systems will eventually need to confront the transition to post-quantum cryptography, and they will not necessarily adopt the same cryptographic algorithms. Strongpoint MPC is designed with this diversity in mind, providing a foundation for supporting multiple signature schemes as cryptographic standards and blockchain requirements evolve.

The future of MPC is post-quantum and post-AI

Quantum computing threatens the mathematical assumptions underlying today's widely deployed public-key cryptography. Meanwhile, increasingly capable AI systems are accelerating mathematical research and cryptanalysis, introducing additional uncertainty around the long-term security of cryptographic systems.

Strongpoint is built around conservative cryptographic assumptions, crypto-agility and institutional control. Strongpoint MPC extends that approach to threshold signing, allowing institutions to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography without abandoning the distributed signing infrastructure they depend on.

For years, the industry has operated under the assumption that moving to post-quantum MPC would require meaningful sacrifices in performance and operational flexibility. Our breakthrough demonstrates that this does not have to be the case.

That's an exciting development for the future of digital asset security, and an important step toward making the post-quantum transition practical.

Learn more about Strongpoint MPC or reach out to our team today.

What happens to frameworks in the agents era? to component libraries? to @shadcn? 

The answer is: we need to drill deeper. Delete the part, optimize, accelerate, automate.

UI SDK is like the x86 instruction set for agents to build new UI components spontaneously. 

Agents are the new design engineers, and they're ready to build *anything* you ask, tailored to your usecase. High-level, rigid, single-framework abstractions are like kryptonite for what is essentially an infinite, untiring creation machine.

I think we've found someone that allows us to have the cake and eat it too. A decades-long dream. UI SDK is packaged behaviors that give us accessibility, performance, cohesion, saving us tokens, errors and effort, but with absolutely zero limitations and tradeoffs for what UIs we can generate.

author: NaderLikeLadder
quoted_text:
This is a difficult moment. It’s hard not to look at the journey this company has taken and not be filled with respect for what Jensen built. The spirit of the company remains strong: "mission is the boss”.

That said, as NVIDIA finds its way forward, I want one thing to be clear: NVIDIA's contributions to open source are unwavering.

Jensen has been vocal about this, and that commitment runs deep in NVIDIA's people and culture. We all understand the importance of open source.

NVIDIA is a huge supporter of open source because we understand something.
If you want to diffuse technology, you do so through an ecosystem, not a single company or entity.

No one owns the internet, no one owns servers, and no one owns operating systems… but through open source, an ecosystem of closed and open innovation flourishes.

When we talk about delivering agents safely and securely, that too will take place because of open source. For example, ensuring people have the best models to secure themselves at machine speed unburdened by arbitrary guardrails decided behind closed doors.

Open source & AI are often discussed together, but it’s worth reminding, open source predates AI. It is a mechanism for sharing ideas inspired by the hippies at computer labs of California in the 1960s.

Before AI, the largest shift I lived through was the internet. It was remarkable seeing the fight for open source take place there. Between browsers, runtimes, net neutrality, etc. What came as a result was HTML5 and an extremely vibrant ecosystem that built the internet as we know it today.

NVIDIA and its partners hold an incredibly important role in delivering this technology. NVIDIA contributes to every layer of the stack. Runtimes, models, harnesses, programming languages, frameworks, etc. None of that changes.

Long live open source.

很可惜, 最坏的情况还是发生了.
黄代表的不只是 nvda 这个公司, 他实际上整个台湾半导体产业上下游里面的"大哥"式人物, 有很多东西没有对他个人的信任, 是很难拉起来的.
https://t.co/CACq9yKOKK 这个之前很火的他和Dwarkesh Patel 的podcast里面的内容已经说明了很多问题, 比如nvda 和 tsmc 合作30年没有legal contract, 全靠互相的信任, 比如他手里的 nvda 即使做到很大规模也没有去做一些事情抢别人饭碗, 而是分给别人去做, 合作共赢, 专注在正确的生态构建上等等内容. 包括他准备干的那个 Compute Financing Platforms, 也就是贷款给其他公司买卡增加算力的那个借贷平台, 现在估计也是没戏了. 他的离开我认为会让 nvda 失去作为 AI 先锋公司整合半导体产业资源的角色.

还有一个比较大的损失是黄个人作为 ceo 的"精准直觉". 在 AI 浪潮的冲击下, 不管大公司还是小公司, 都需要被迫转型, 因为 AI 带来的效率提升不是1倍, 2倍, 是10倍以上. 所有的你的工作成果是电脑, 电视, 手机等屏幕上显示的东西的工作, 效率提升都是这个规模. 即使现在没有蔓延到你的行业来, 迟早都会蔓延过来, 因为虚拟世界里面的"工具生产者" -- 软件工程行业这边已经是这样了, "内容生产者"的效率提升也必然被影响. 这个动荡的时候一个公司最好的决策人是什么样的? 就是黄这种把公司一手从 startup 带大的人. 这种人具有的"行业方向直觉"将会是公司在变革时期最重要的资产. 这个podcast的日期是4/15, 什么时候? 美伊刚刚开始和谈的时候, 半导体刚刚开始拉起来主升浪. 那时候市场谁在乎 token 成本的问题? token 成本的问题是后面从6月开始, 真实利率上升后借贷成本变贵才进入了市场视野, 但是黄在视频中就已经指出来了:"真正的技术差异是降低 Token 的总成本，而不是 GPU 的 FLOPS", 他看到这个问题肯定是更早之前. 其他的类似他对半导体行业精准预测的例子还有很多. 这种精准的直觉可以让公司在机会出现的时候正确地押注上去, 而不是犹豫不决的等死 (反例比如最近几天很火的腾讯小马哥内部讲话很明显就是后悔自己动作慢了).

当 nvda 失去黄之后, 在我眼里的吸引力已经直线下降了. 它依旧会是一个 gpu 龙头, 但是并不会是一个好的长持标的了. CUDA 单一的护城河已经在瓦解, nvda 同样处于被 ai 浪潮冲击需要转型的时刻, 本来黄应该是一个让人安心的"领航人"角色, 现在下岗了, 那 nvda 撞上冰山的概率显然就开始增加了.

author: HarryStebbings
quoted_text:
This week had more banging news items than Silicon Valley had tranched funding rounds.

The biggest news this week:

- Jensen Huang Investigation: What Happens Now
- Sequoia Leave London, Close Scout Program and End Evergreen Fund
- NASDAQ Loses $2.5TRN in 24 hours
- Anthropic targets $1.4TRN IPO valuation

My notes with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll

1. What Is the Impact of Jensen Huang's Affair on China?

China is the big loser from the scandal. It will become harder to sell GPUs to China and to host them just across the border, and that route is likely to be shut down. The issue had already stalled in Congress.

2. Why the Anthropic IPO Will Trade Flat

Jason expects the Anthropic IPO to trade flat because the market is fatigued. Anthropic could not raise the full $100B directly in the IPO, and OpenAI was only able to raise $10B after tiring out its market. Retail demand is still hard to predict.

3. Why Are Anthropic in Such a Better Place Than OpenAI?

Anthropic will have its IPO done within a month, giving it the money and the float to leave private fundraising behind. Within six to nine months it could file a convertible and raise around $50B, with $200B on hand. OpenAI is still unprofitable, still private and still trying to raise $11B plus retail.

4. The Framework You Need to Adopt to Underwrite Zipline at $21BN

Zipline at $21B is unlikely to be justified on a revenue multiple. It has done three million US deliveries at probably $5 to $10 each, so it needs huge volume to work. The case rests on Zipline becoming the next infrastructure play, and at this price investors are leaning heavily on its Walmart contract.

5. The AI Trade Doesn't Crack on the Supply Side

The NASDAQ sell-off was largely reactive angst about data centers. Rory argues the AI trade holds through data center limits or NVIDIA ceding share to AMD as long as demand, evidenced in OpenAI and Anthropic ARR, is there. Hedge fund pods that lose their checkbook at a 5% drawdown and get fired at 7.5% were simply over their skis.

6. Why Did Sequoia End the Evergreen Fund?

The Evergreen fund rested on the sound idea that the real money is made after the IPO. But it launched in 2022 and 2023 as stocks fell, LPs have different liquidity needs, and partners who had already earned carry were forcing LPs to hold. Jason counters that holding generational assets like NVIDIA and Google for decades is the best idea in venture.

7. For Pre-AI Companies, It Really Is March or Die

Non-AI companies are still shipping at the same rate as in 2022 and 2023, and Jason has largely given up on them moving faster. He does not count Dialpad's $400M stock deal for Ada as an exit because there is no liquidity. AI-native companies will not buy these businesses either, since they are growing too fast to take on old contracts and their problems.

text:
本文《黄仁勋下台：背后的背后，谁是可能的推手？》围绕英伟达创始人兼CEO黄仁勋于2026年11月12日突然宣布辞职的事件，分析了其下台背后的时间节点与多方推手。
### 事件背景与导火索
 * **事件结果**：黄仁勋在两周内因两段婚外情（一段涉及被美方认定与外国情报机构有关联的新加坡Megaspeed前高管Alice Huang，另一段涉及向其直接汇报的副总裁）辞去总裁、CEO及董事职务，由CFO暂代CEO。消息引发英伟达市值蒸发超6000亿美元。
 * **敏感时间窗口**：事件发酵的两周恰好卡在美国中期选举刚结束（11月3日）、Anthropic启动IPO路演（11月9日当周）、英伟达发布三季报（11月17日）以及国会听证会（11月18日前后）四个关键节点之间。
### 背后的主要推手

 1. **国会和出口管制鹰派**：长期主张严格限制芯片出口的议员此前因特朗普对黄仁勋的好感而难以推进政策；此次“涉外情报人员关系”成为突破口，促使多个委员会主席联名要求其作证并呼吁调查。

 2. **华尔街与做空机构**：Point72、Citadel等多家顶级对冲基金在二季度已大幅减持或清仓英伟达；做空机构Culper Research早在5月便发布报告质疑Megaspeed及上述私人关系。丑闻爆发后，卖方下调评级触发长线资金风控，空头获利丰厚。

 3. **Anthropic**：作为坚定支持严管芯片出口的AI公司，其CEO与黄仁勋在政策和商业上早有分歧。Anthropic通过智库（如CNAS）和政治捐款（AnthroPAC）长期推动“芯片出口即国家安全”的叙事，客观上为此次舆论定性铺平了道路

 4. **情报与执法系统**：商务部自2024年9月起调查Megaspeed芯片去向，后案件移交司法部。在白宫未采取行动的情况下，体制内力量通过向媒体释放调查细节，将事件推向公共视野。

 5. **媒体节奏**：《纽约时报》、The Information、FT等媒体分三轮精准爆出“国家安全”、“涉案金额”和“上下级恋情”，层层递进地将国会、股东律师和董事会拉入局中，最终迫使董事会作出切割。

text:
All the tech people rushing to defend Jensen are off base.

As a VC, I get it. He's a generational founder, and there's a deeply-ingrained lesson in tech that founders are almost always the best people to run their companies. I share that intuition.

But the board's call here was dead simple:

1. His credibility is shredded. Jensen said two weeks ago that his relationship with Alice Huang was "completely normal and not unusual." Ten days later he admitted the affair. Now there's a second affair, with an exec who reports directly to him. As others have said: "when you find two ants in your kitchen, the best estimate for the ants in your kitchen is not two." 
2. He violated export controls and tried to quash the investigation into MegaSpeed, which could be an extremely serious crime. The Trump admin is already signaling that they are going to reverse course on export restrictions because of this scandal.
3. The politics has flipped. His relationship with Trump is no longer the asset it was. The Dems are in control of Congress now and there is furious anti-AI backlash that Nvidia will need to weather. Having been compromised by a Chinese spy and advocating for exports to China makes him totally disqualified on these questions going forward. There is going to be hell to pay over the next few years, and Nvidia needs a CEO who can walk into those hearings with legitimacy. Otherwise this cloud would always hang over him.
4. There's a business to run. The dude already wrote one apology letter. Was the board supposed to wait for him to write a second one? A third? You can't run a $4T company like this.

A CEO has to be reliable first and foremost. Once that’s gone, you don’t get it back. 

Jensen will almost certainly have a second act. But just not as CEO of Nvidia.

And anyone calling this a psy-op or a coup should just look at the Polymarket on this. Before the second affair, Jensen was only at 15% to be out as CEO. He could've survived one scandal, and I agreed it'd be foolish to let him go at that point. Easy to argue he was duped and made a mistake.

But you don't get two.

text:
This is a difficult moment. It’s hard not to look at the journey this company has taken and not be filled with respect for what Jensen built. The spirit of the company remains strong: "mission is the boss”.

That said, as NVIDIA finds its way forward, I want one thing to be clear: NVIDIA's contributions to open source are unwavering.

Jensen has been vocal about this, and that commitment runs deep in NVIDIA's people and culture. We all understand the importance of open source.

NVIDIA is a huge supporter of open source because we understand something.
If you want to diffuse technology, you do so through an ecosystem, not a single company or entity.

No one owns the internet, no one owns servers, and no one owns operating systems… but through open source, an ecosystem of closed and open innovation flourishes.

When we talk about delivering agents safely and securely, that too will take place because of open source. For example, ensuring people have the best models to secure themselves at machine speed unburdened by arbitrary guardrails decided behind closed doors.

Open source & AI are often discussed together, but it’s worth reminding, open source predates AI. It is a mechanism for sharing ideas inspired by the hippies at computer labs of California in the 1960s.

Before AI, the largest shift I lived through was the internet. It was remarkable seeing the fight for open source take place there. Between browsers, runtimes, net neutrality, etc. What came as a result was HTML5 and an extremely vibrant ecosystem that built the internet as we know it today.

NVIDIA and its partners hold an incredibly important role in delivering this technology. NVIDIA contributes to every layer of the stack. Runtimes, models, harnesses, programming languages, frameworks, etc. None of that changes.

Long live open source.

BIG NEWS: 2026's newest hair growth drug has human data 🩸

Oral diazoxide grows hair in up to 90% of the people who take it. 

We invented the world's first topical diazoxide: DZX.

Four community members applied 1 mL of 3% DZX to the scalp 1x a day.

Then we drew blood to see how much diazoxide went systemic.

The results was 20.3 ng/mL on average.

Oral diazoxide at a therapeutic dose runs 1000x higher.

Diazoxide's #1 side effect is high blood sugar. At its oral dose, it raises glucose about 11 mg/dL. 

Based on our serum readings, we modeled a glucose rise of just 0.01 mg/dL from DZX.

To check the model, three of us wore Dexcom Stelo sensors before and while on DZX.

Measured: average glucose +3.7 mg/dL, 95% interval -1 to +9. No change in meal spikes. Zero readings above 180.

In 1990, a 5% topical diazoxide regrew hair on 5 of 5 bald macaques, with no change in glucose tolerance.

Thirty-six years later, the drug that grows hair in 9 of 10 people at a therapeutic oral dose, now has its first human data for its first topical.

author: tobi
quoted_text:
Things I stole from @Shopify while I was at Stan:

1. Almost optimize for churn.

Shopify's mission is to increase entrepreneurship, so it makes starting as easy as possible knowing most businesses will fail. A few breakout merchants can make the economics of the entire cohort work.

2. Give different work different clocks.

Growth can work in short feedback loops. Core product may be building infrastructure that needs to last for decades. Holding both to the same measurement window rewards the wrong work.

3. Optimize totals, not rates.

The easiest way to improve a conversion rate is to make the previous step harder. Fewer people enter, a higher percentage convert, and the dashboard turns green, even though fewer people reach the outcome you care about.

4. Measure value over the period in which it emerges.

Shopify looks at the total GMV created by a merchant cohort over 1, 3, and 5 years. A few breakout merchants can make the economics of an entire cohort work. Short-term retention alone misses that.

5. Revisit your “winning” experiments.

An early lift may only pull demand forward. Shopify preserves holdout groups and checks them months later to see whether an experiment created durable value or merely borrowed it from the future.

6. Personalize onboarding with what you learn.

Collecting more information during signup can be worth the friction when you use it to give people better guidance. The goal isn't the shortest signup flow. It's getting more people to the outcome they came for.

7. Put onboarding inside the product.

Shopify has a “no wizard” principle. Instead of teaching people in a separate setup flow, it brings the useful parts of a wizard, like simplification and personalization, into the actual product experience.

The common thread: don't optimize the appearance of progress. Design the product, incentives, and measurement system around the outcome you actually want to create.

China had *zero* chance of ever catching America in AI with the export strategy that Jensen supported. Given that it looks like the China “Hawks” will get their preferred policy, China will likely soon have a chance of catching America in AI by going down an alternate, less power-efficient AI hardware path. text:
1/ 코인판 10년, 살아남은 사람들의 단 한 가지 차이

코인판에 10년 있으면서 수많은 사람이 들어오고 나가는 걸 봤음.

그러면서 깨달은 게 하나 있음. 남은 사람과 떠난 사람을 가른 건 실력만이 아니었다는 거임.

업비트 내부자 정보를 운운하던 친구도 퇴학당했고, 지갑을 분석하며 고래와 세력을 추적하던 친구도 어느새 사라졌음. 돈이 돈을 벌어온다며 큰돈을 태우던 친구도 도망갔음.

롱숏 다 발라먹겠다며 차트에 기가 막히게 선을 긋던 친구도, 세세한 요소 하나하나 짚어가며 종목을 분석하던 친구도 이제는 보이지 않음.

그런데 그런 능력이 특별히 없어도 코인판에 오래 붙어 있는 친구들은 은근히 많음.

내가 가까이서 본 사람들에게는 한 가지 차이가 있었음.

그걸 설명하려면 1만 년 전으로 가야 함.

2/ 수렵채집인은 무능하지 않았음

숲을 읽고, 사냥감의 흔적을 찾고, 끝까지 쫓아가는 능력. 먹고사는 데 필요한 개인 기량은 뛰어났을 거임.

그런데 아무리 능숙해도 주변에서 구할 수 있는 먹거리에는 한계가 있었음.

열매가 열리는 곳을 찾아다니고, 짐승이 있는 곳으로 이동할 수는 있었음. 하지만 노력을 두 배로 한다고 열매가 두 배로 열리거나 짐승이 두 배로 생기는 건 아니었음.

먹거리가 줄어들면 아무리 뛰어난 사냥꾼도 어려워졌음.

내가 얼마나 잘하느냐와 별개로, 환경이 내주는 양에 크게 기대어 살아야 했던 거임.

3/ 농부는 태양을 받는 방식을 바꿨음

수렵채집인도 농부도 같은 태양 에너지에 기대어 살았음. 하지만 농부는 먹거리가 생기는 과정에 직접 손을 대기 시작했음.

어디에 무엇을 심을지 정하고, 땅을 돌보고, 수확한 것 중 일부를 다음 계절을 위해 남겼음.

물론 농부도 날씨를 정할 수는 없었음. 가뭄이 들면 농사를 망쳤고, 흉년이 오면 굶기도 했음.

그래도 먹거리를 찾아다니는 데서 한 걸음 나아가, 직접 생산하고 저장하는 기반을 만들었음. 그 기반이 커지면서 더 많은 사람이 살아갈 수 있게 됐음.

여기서 한 발 더 나간 사람들도 있었음. 가축을 활용한 사람들임.

소는 밭을 갈고, 짐을 나르고, 식량이 되기도 했음. 내 몸 하나로 하던 일을 내 몸 밖의 힘으로 할 수 있게 된 거임.

같은 땅, 같은 태양 아래에서도 무엇을 갖추고 있느냐에 따라 생산성이 달라졌음.

4/ 다시 코인판으로 돌아오면

시장을 잘 읽는 능력은 중요함. 그런데 그 능력만으로 생활까지 전부 책임져야 한다면 이야기가 달라짐.

시장이 좋을 때는 누구보다 잘 벌 수 있음. 하지만 시장이 꺾이고 수익이 끊겨도 생활비는 계속 나감. 다음 기회가 올 거라고 생각하면서도 당장 쓸 돈 때문에 포지션을 정리해야 할 수 있음.

차트를 읽는 능력이 있어도 버틸 여유가 없으면 쓰기 어려운 거임.

수렵채집인도 숲은 잘 읽었음. 다만 숲이 내주는 것에만 기대어 살면, 먹거리가 줄어드는 시기에 선택지가 좁아졌음.

내가 본 오래 남은 사람들에게는 시장 밖에서 생활을 지탱해주는 기반이 있었음.

직장이든, 본업이든, 별도의 사업이든. 혹은 좋을 때 벌어 미리 떼어둔 생활비든.

매달 시장에서 돈을 꺼내지 않아도 되니, 하락장을 보내는 방식도 달라졌음.

공부하고, 리서치하고, 기록하고, 새로운 서비스를 써보고, 에어드랍이나 다음 먹거리를 찾아다녔음.

이런 활동이 당장 생활비를 벌어주지 않아도 괜찮았음. 생활을 지탱하는 기반이 따로 있었으니까.

그래서 하락장은 그저 버텨야 하는 시간이 아니라, 다음을 준비하는 시간이 될 수 있었음.

5/ 밭을 만드는 법

- 시장 밖에서 들어오는 현금흐름을 하나 만들 것. 직장이든 사업이든 좋음. 하락장에 생활비 때문에 투자 판단이 흔들리지 않게 해주는 기반임.
- 좋을 때 번 돈을 남겨둘 것. 수익 전부를 다음 베팅에 넣으면, 많이 벌고도 다음 하락장에는 다시 생활비를 걱정하게 될 수 있음.
- 하락장을 농한기로 쓸 것. 공부하고, 리서치하고, 기록할 것. 다음 기회가 왔을 때 무엇을 알아볼 수 있는지는 이때 쌓은 것에 달려 있음.
- 한 번 들인 노력이 다음에도 남는 일을 할 것. 쌓이는 글, 반복해서 쓸 수 있는 시스템, 내가 자리를 비워도 돌아가는 사업. 매번 처음부터 다시 시작하지 않아도 되는 무언가를 만들어갈 것.

시장은 숲과 같음. 좋은 해가 있으면 나쁜 해도 있음. 그 흐름을 내가 정할 수는 없음.

하지만 내 생활이 시장에 얼마나 기대어 있을지, 번 돈 중 얼마를 남길지, 기다리는 동안 무엇을 쌓을지는 내가 정할 수 있음.

내가 본 10년을 남은 사람들은 숲을 잘 읽는 것만으로 버티지 않았음.

숲 옆에 자기 밭도 갖고 있었음.
