text:
I'm the corporate secretary of Nvidia, the most valuable chip company in the world.

I take the minutes and keep the bylaws. When something happens to the founder, I write the sentences that tell the market how to feel. This week I wrote 3 statements. All of them were true. They just weren't true at the same time.

On Sunday the board said it was opening an investigation "in light of recent reporting" that our CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort." I chose "recent reporting" with care. In every statement this week, the board never once wrote the word "affair." Reporting is something that happens to you, like weather. An affair is something you do. We only disclose weather.

The Sunday statement ended: "The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate." Investors read the first half of that sentence. I wrote it for the second half. "Further updates as appropriate" is how a board reserves the right to change its mind without admitting it had one.

Earlier in the same statement: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised." No reason. We had plenty of reporting. Reasons take longer. We hire people for those.

On Tuesday we hired them. The independent directors chose Joon Kim, the former acting U.S. attorney in Manhattan. He and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, will run "a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday." Read the Tuesday statement as many times as you like. You won't find the word confidence. In board statements, the sentence you leave out is the vote.

On Wednesday night the Times published a second round of recent reporting. The board met to plan his removal. Its confidence had lasted from Sunday to Tuesday. That's about the shelf life of sushi. Both are best enjoyed before anyone asks where they came from.

On Thursday at 8:47 a.m. Eastern, I sent the third statement. "Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately." It gives no reason. Resignations don't need reasons. Reasons are for firings. Firings are for people who don't own 4% of the company.

Then the sentence I'd been saving since Sunday: "The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry." Immeasurable. We measure everything in trillions of operations per second. I chose the one word that means we stopped counting. In my business, nobody gets thanked until they're leaving. Gratitude is what confidence becomes after the board hires a search firm.

Now watch the confidence. Harvey Jones, our new chair, said, "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team." On Sunday the board had confidence in Jensen. On Thursday it had full confidence in Colette. The board never lost its confidence. It moved it, like a parking space. We issue "full" on day 1. It comes with a 4-day warranty.

Colette Kress, our CFO, is the interim CEO. She will "continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer" at the same time. Earlier this week I wrote that I'd drafted the earnings thank-you in 3 voices. The third sounded like a chief financial officer reading something she didn't write. On Thursday the third voice got the job. She kept the old one too. In a strong labor market, everyone has 2 jobs.

The release also named Jones our "first-ever Chair of the Board." For 33 years Nvidia had no chairman. We never needed one. The founder sat at the head of the table, and the table understood.

Earnings are on Tuesday, November 17, "as previously scheduled." Everything at Nvidia is previously scheduled. Only the CEO was rescheduled.

The shares closed down 4.3% at $166.19. Axios says we've shed more than $1 trillion in market value since this began. It also says Nvidia "was worth 25% less without Huang." So the market says he was worth a quarter of the company. The board says he was immeasurable. Both are true. One is just more precise.

Our search firm has barely made a call. Strangers are already running the most transparent succession in corporate history. None of them work here. Elon Musk posted that it would be an honor to hire Jensen. The President posted that there's "only one man" who could replace him. He named Tim Cook, who has already stepped down as Apple's CEO. And a prediction market gives our data center chief, Ian Buck, a 42% chance of getting the job. Our board hasn't interviewed anyone. Kalshi has already priced the finalist.

Nobody has asked me about Singapore yet. We used to tell investors which countries our revenue came from. Then the Wall Street Journal noticed our Singapore sales disappearing from the filings. That was right about when people started asking about Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the center of all this. We choose which countries to list. When one gets too interesting, we stop listing countries. We call it formatting.

Senators Warren and Coons have asked the administration to preserve every record related to Nvidia, our exports and our former CEO. On Thursday Warren added that "Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and NVIDIA's board of directors still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls." Note the list. Mr. Huang. The executives. The board. My statement said "effective immediately." Hers didn't. Resignations end employment. They don't end subpoenas.

Axios reported that the Commerce Secretary dragged his feet on enforcing chip export limits. Fortune's summary added that he did it "to the bafflement of his cabinet colleagues." We appreciated that bafflement very much. Bafflement is the most valuable thing in Washington. You can't subpoena it. It isn't written down. And it always seems to work in our favor.

People ask me how a board can say "confidence" on Sunday, hire a search firm on Wednesday and say "immeasurable" on Thursday. They misunderstand the instrument. A board statement is a reading, like a thermometer. Confidence is what the room feels at 9 a.m. on a Sunday, before the bankers wake up.

My folder is empty now. I've used all 3 drafts. This morning I opened a new one. The first page says the board has confidence in Colette. I left the date blank.

The permanent CEO, whoever it is, inherits the leather jacket. Every CEO search ends with a fitting.

Being frustrated with these markets, I've been turning inward, refocusing my energy on researching new protocols, ones where I can either earn yield or (maybe) a meaty airdrop.

It's the only thing to offer me joy in these times!

Last bear market, we learned pre-launch about @0xfluid, @ethena, and @ether_fi.

This year, one gem @Nomaticcap and I think we've uncovered is @metricxyz.  It's a new AMM protocol (still pre-token with a points program live) we've spent a lot of time studying and testing. 

It's not hard to get excited about Metric LP yields--we regularly find triple digit APRs on major token pairs, tokenized stocks, and stablecoins.

Since about 2022, I have avoided a lot of LPs because I got burned by IL in so many.

But with Metric, they seem to have improved the LP experience, making it easier to keep your liq in-range. You position the LP relative to a reference price (oracle), ie -0.005% below and +0.005% above. Instead of trading against the same AMM formula x * y = k, you are trading against a reference price from oracles, onchain data, and custom rules set by Curators.

The pool is curated like a Morpho market but for AMM pools instead. Curators manage a Price Provider and the pool's settings. Liquidity providers only choose which ranges to fund. The pool isn't its own price oracle, trades move price relative to the reference. When the reference price moves, the ranges move with it.

The pool holds the liquidity in percentage ranges around the provider's quote and executes trades so managing an LP is relatively easy. Imagine you deposit into bins for a WETH/USDG LP being 0.005%+, 0.015%+, 0.025% higher than the reference price, or -0.005%, -0.015%, -0.025% lower than the reference price. 

You're fully reliant on the pool referencing a "real world" price for these assets, and moving the pool price (reference price from a Price Provider) to that price as it changes.

The catch here is you won't likely trade new tokens on day 1 of launch on Metric. Instead, Metric focuses on RWAs like tokenized stocks, blue chip majors with well established price feeds (meaning CEX liquidity), and of course stablecoins.

My best advice here is play around, click into some bins for different LPs, and when ready, test some liquidity.

Today, I want to take a step back and examine the Bitcoin market from a macroeconomic perspective.

It may be a relatively conventional approach, but given the severe liquidity constraints currently facing Bitcoin, I believe it's important to revisit the broader macro environment.

Let me start with my conclusion.

"The Bitcoin market has still not gone through sufficient accumulation, and liquidity conditions continue to deteriorate. At this point, we can only hope the market avoids a major shock. Even if it does, a much longer period of sideways consolidation may be necessary than many expect."

As I've repeatedly discussed in my previous analyses, Bitcoin's internal liquidity conditions are extremely concerning.

Buy-side liquidity continues to weaken, and the market is experiencing a significant liquidity squeeze.

Against this backdrop, I want to examine the relationship between the U.S. dollar and Bitcoin's market cycles.

This may be familiar territory for anyone who has spent some time studying financial markets.

Generally speaking, the U.S. dollar is closely tied to global liquidity conditions.

Looking back at Bitcoin's historical cycles, we have never seen Bitcoin sustain a full-fledged bull market while the dollar was in a strong upward trend.

The bearish cycle that began in 2025 has not been particularly different in this regard.

But that brings us to the most important question.

"Are we really at the point where the U.S. dollar is about to enter a sustained downtrend?"

To me, this is one of the most critical questions when assessing the current market.

Let's look at the historical cycles objectively.

In previous cycles, Bitcoin went through a prolonged bear market before entering a major bullish phase as the U.S. dollar began a sustained decline.
(Image 1, green boxes)

But the current situation is fundamentally different.

Rather than entering a downtrend, the dollar is showing signs of establishing a strong upward trend.
(Image 1, red box)

This is the most important difference between previous bullish cycles and the market environment we face today.

Now, take a look at Image 2.

The U.S. dollar has broken above a trading range that had been forming for more than 500 days.

There is something I frequently emphasize in my market analysis:

"Once a trend is established, it rarely reverses easily."

This is because of trend persistence.

And this is not a trend that developed over a few weeks or months.

We are looking at a breakout from a consolidation range that lasted more than 500 days.

That makes this development particularly important.

Even if the dollar eventually reverses and begins declining again, the process could take considerably longer than many investors anticipate.

We also need to consider the broader macroeconomic environment.

Interest rate hikes began in the third quarter of this year, while the political and economic environment surrounding the U.S. midterm elections has hardly been favorable for the crypto market.

Meanwhile, selling pressure from Bitcoin mining companies is another major concern.

Bitcoin selling activity among mining companies reached historically elevated levels during the third and fourth quarters of this year.

At the same time, many mining companies have been shifting their business models toward AI data centers.

Under these circumstances, can we realistically expect substantial new liquidity to flow into Bitcoin?

At this point, I find it difficult to be confident that it will.

Ultimately, Bitcoin needs a new catalyst and a compelling narrative capable of attracting fresh capital.

Personally, I believe one of the strongest narratives Bitcoin could have is its role as "Digital Gold."

But there has been an interesting shift here as well.

One of the companies that most aggressively promoted Bitcoin as digital gold was Strategy.

Back in 2022, Strategy frequently emphasized Bitcoin's identity as "Digital Gold."

However, beginning in 2025, the company increasingly shifted its messaging toward concepts such as "Credit" and "Digital Capital," rather than emphasizing Bitcoin primarily as digital gold.

Think about what that means.

Even Strategy, one of the most influential companies capable of driving the digital gold narrative, is now emphasizing a different narrative.

And now, with today's confirmation of its exclusion from the MSCI index, uncertainty surrounding the market has increased even further.

So let me ask the question again.

"Is liquidity in the Bitcoin market actually recovering?"

Bitcoin has become far more deeply integrated into the traditional financial system than ever before.

Through spot ETFs and growing institutional participation, Bitcoin is increasingly held within the portfolios of traditional financial institutions.

As a result, its market behavior has become more closely connected to macroeconomic conditions and movements in traditional financial markets.

In other words, Bitcoin is now more exposed to the broader macro environment, not less.

Yet today, Bitcoin's internal liquidity remains weak, while external macroeconomic conditions are far from supportive.

Under these circumstances, I find it difficult to see how Bitcoin could simply defy the broader macro environment and independently enter a powerful bullish cycle.

For Bitcoin to begin a genuine, sustained bull market, new liquidity needs to enter the market.

That is the fundamental requirement.

And this brings me back to my current assessment.

Right now, the priority should be hoping that the market can get through this period without experiencing a major shock.

But even if we manage to avoid a significant disruption, unwinding excessive leverage and resolving the current liquidity imbalances could require a much longer period of consolidation and accumulation than many investors expect.

If investors are expecting Bitcoin to quickly return to a steep upward trajectory from here, I think they may be setting themselves up for considerable disappointment.

This is also why I intend to approach my next Bitcoin purchases with a much longer time horizon.

Rather than rushing back into the market, I want to carefully assess how liquidity conditions develop and whether the market has gone through a sufficient accumulation process.

I understand that my current outlook may sound pessimistic, or even discouraging.

But the purpose of market analysis is not to consistently deliver an optimistic outlook.

It is to objectively assess the environment we are operating in and develop an investment strategy that reflects those conditions.

I simply do not believe this is the right time to approach the Bitcoin market aggressively.

There is no need to rush.

For now, I believe patience is more important than chasing a potential rebound.

I would rather wait for liquidity to recover, allow the market enough time to accumulate, and position myself when a more favorable opportunity emerges.

text:
NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

But I can also say that Jensen is human, and makes mistakes like all of us do. Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. That shows rare character, to maintain humility and humanity through all of it.

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Love you all ❤️

The all-time leaderboard reads differently. The top 200 by all-time PnL are split almost exactly even, $4.6M long and $4.6M short. Two of those names shorted lower, at $96 and $101, and both are underwater.

Nov. 19 settles it. The stock opens and Hyperliquid has to meet a real price. If the open lands near $104, the 24/7 market called it a week early. If it lands near the range, the shorts get paid. The book is reportedly oversubscribed, so the range could still move up.

text:
⚠️ALERT: A GLOBAL Microsoft outage has knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot across 74 countries, hitting software used by 450 MILLION work accounts.

It has dragged on for more than 5 hours, and Microsoft has not confirmed the cause.

At the centre of it is something most of us never think about, but rely on every day.

Exchange Online, the system that delivers Outlook email for businesses, began failing around midday Eastern time on Thursday.

By 1:25 PM, problem reports had jumped from fewer than 15 a minute to 19,650.

Outlook reports alone ran 2,000 times above normal.

A US state government and two hospital systems in Michigan lost access to email.

It even reached ChatGPT and Claude, whose makers said their Microsoft connections were affected.

Reports spiked for Amazon’s AWS too, until Amazon said it was “operating normally” and called the outage reports “inaccurate.”

Microsoft says a number of its servers became “unexpectedly unavailable.”

It paused all deployments and began restarting them.

Hours later, it said its fixes “have not provided the anticipated relief.”

Even Defender, the platform companies rely on to detect cyberattacks, is caught in the outage.

Earlier the same day, Teams had already gone down for over an hour in North America.

Microsoft has not said whether the two are linked, and it has not pointed to an attack.

Reports have eased from a peak near 130,000 to about 37,000 as some servers return, but Microsoft has not declared it fixed or said how many customers were cut off.

text:
Lightning Labs just released a way for your coding agent to pay for AI inference in bitcoin, with no account, no API key and no card.

The agent gets a bill, pays it over Lightning, and the request goes through. Here is how it works.

• pi402 is an extension for the Pi coding agent that registers a paid model provider
• The first request returns an HTTP 402 with a Lightning invoice, and it goes through once the invoice is paid
• The demo seller lists input at $0.375 and output at $1.50 per million tokens
• The first request buys a 500,000 token bundle, usable for 30 days
• pi402 asks the user before paying anything above their per-request limit
• Neither agents nor sellers need to run a Lightning node

It sits inside Lightning Labs' L402 platform, where Aperture is the gateway, Lightmeter is the meter and Wavelength is the wallet. It is open source, and the seller side is live on mainnet.

Every account, API key and card on file is a person someone can identify, bill or cut off. Here the agent just pays.

If agents are going to buy their own compute, better that they do it with money that doesn't need a bank's sign-off.

text:
If you’re unfamiliar with how machine learning works: an AI model is truly just a very long list (billions, sometimes trillions) of numbers called weights, which, loosely, when multiplied and added together produce readable text. 

Training adjusts those numbers over and over until the model gives good answers. Before training can start, the weights need starting values and those are filled in with random numbers.

Training changes most of the initial weights, but it doesn’t do so completely. Some are never touched at all and the rest still correlate with where they started. That is why the starting weights can still be read from the finished model.

You can see it with a simple test: draw a smiley face into a network’s weights before training and it is still there afterwards.

author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
Finally wrote a blog post about this! Normal LLM inference isn't deterministic across devices, but this can be fixed.

Floating-point addition isn't associative, (a + b) + c ≠ a + (b + c), and accumulation order changes with the hardware and kernel used, leading to different outputs on the same prompt.

Integer addition is associative, so doing every op in integers (including softmax and norms) gives bit-identical outputs across GPUs and CPUs.

Github repo and post listed in the comments
author: ClemToune
quoted_text:
Turns out you can make LLM inference fully deterministic across devices, with no loss to quality or speed.

This weekend at the @spacexai hackathon I got Qwen3-0.6B to produce identical hashed logits from a 512-token generation across 2 GPUs and 3 CPUs: an A100, an H100, an Apple M5 Max, an AMD EPYC, and an Intel Xeon.

The main reason why inference isn't deterministic is because floating-point addition is not associative. (a + b) + c ≠ a + (b + c), since every add rounds. Accumulation order changes with the hardware used and kernel selected, so the same prompt can give you different outputs even at temperature 0.

Integers ARE associative. So why doesn't integer quantization already fix this? Because, while weights and activations get quantized, the non-linear ops (softmax, normalization, SiLU) dequantize back to float and requantize afterwards. Each of those steps hands you back to floating point rounding.

True integer-only inference does exist, but it's historically been motivated by edge hardware without FPUs, which doesn't make much sense for LLMs. One 2024 paper (I-LLM) did it on LLaMA from that angle and didn't get much attention. Nobody seems to have looked at it from the determinism side.

I wrote my own implementation, simplifying the approach from the paper, so that every operation between the input ids and the int32 logits is exact integer arithmetic. To test it I chain-hashed the logits at every step and ran that across the devices and configurations below. Every integer run gave the same hash: 64430dd985f8. Every fp16 run gave a different one, all diverging on the very first token.

WikiText2 perplexity came out to 20.72 vs 20.95 for fp16 (slightly better than the float baseline), and CUDA-graphed integer decode hits 106 tok/s at batch 1 on an A100, 3.6x the fp16 eager baseline.

Github repo is listed in the comments. Plan to do a writeup over this eventually!

text:
Wow，这都能测出来！！

中国的 DeepSeek、Kimi、MiniMax、蚂蚁等多家公司的模型，居然都被测出使用过被禁售的 NVIDIA 最先进的 Blackwell GPU！！

Will Depue 从公开的模型权重中，反推出了模型初始化时使用的 GPU，甚至连随机种子都找出来了。

原理很巧妙：训练大模型之前，需要先给数以亿计的参数赋予随机初始值。这个过程通常由 GPU 执行，使用一个随机种子来生成数字。

关键在于，即使使用相同的随机种子，不同架构的 GPU 也可能因为随机数生成算法和执行方式不同，产生不同的数值排列。

这就像给模型留下了一枚“硬件指纹”。更神奇的是，模型经过海量数据训练后，部分参数仍然保留着最初的数值，让人有机会从最终权重中追溯初始化时使用的硬件。

他搜索了超过 6 万亿种组合，称这四家公司的多个模型都匹配到了 Blackwell。

他还用真实硬件进行了验证：在 B300 上使用找回的随机种子，逐位还原了 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 中保留下来的初始权重。

连 DeepSeek 的随机种子都被他公布出来了：953049583 😂

quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

Hey hello everyone, I’m Kirila. I’m a US based artist currently living in Bali, Indonesia, and I’ve been creating art for around 6 years. I’ve also been around the crypto space for almost 6 years. I was here during the NFT era, working as a full time artist, creating art every single day and meeting some really incredible people through crypto.

Crypto has always been very close to me because it was never just about making money. For me, it was about the people, the creativity, the culture and the opportunities that came with being part of something completely new. Some of the best connections I’ve ever made came through crypto, and some of those people are still friends of mine today.

Eventually, when the NFT space started fading away, I had to take a break from everything. Life changed, priorities changed and I slowly became disconnected from the crypto community. I kept making art, but I wasn’t really involved in the space anymore.

Recently, a lot of friends I met here in Indonesia started telling me about @fomo. They kept telling me that I should look into it and that artists could actually create something for themselves through this. Honestly, I’m not going to sit here and pretend that I’m some amazing crypto trader because I’m not. Trading has never really been my strongest skill. I’m an artist first, and that’s what I know how to do.

But I really wanted to find a way back into crypto. I wanted to reconnect with the people I met over the years, meet new people, start creating again and feel that same energy that made me fall in love with this space in the first place.

So I thought, maybe launching my own coin is the best way to start.

I spent time learning about the PumpFun model, watching videos, understanding how launches work and trying to figure out how I could do this myself. After spending enough time learning, I decided that instead of waiting for someone else to create something for me, I would take the first step myself.

That’s how $KIRILA was born.

I started this by putting $300 of my own money into the coin because I wanted to have something of my own behind this journey from the very beginning. It may not be a huge amount, but for me it’s meaningful because I’m putting my own money, my own art and my own time into this.

I’ve also received a lot of messages from people telling me that they wanted to support my art and even suggesting that I launch a coin for myself so they could contribute. That honestly meant a lot to me. Instead of simply asking people to donate, I thought I could create something where I could work for it myself and hopefully build something together with the people who choose to support me.

The main reason I’m doing this is honestly to get back into the crypto community. I miss the connections, the conversations, the creativity and the feeling of being part of something. I want to meet people again, collaborate with artists, connect with builders and hopefully make some new friendships along the way.

I also want $KIRILA to help me focus more seriously on my art. The funds raised through the project will help with my daily life, my art supplies, my setup and the time I need to keep creating. My dream is to eventually have a proper online art store where people can discover and collect my work, so I want to use some of the funds to hire a good web designer and build that properly.

I’m also planning to launch my own NFT collection again. I’ve been thinking about this for a long time, and I feel like this is the perfect opportunity to bring that part of my life back. A portion of my future NFT journey will always be connected to $KIRILA, and I want to use profits from future NFT sales to support the project and give something back to the community that supported me.

With options, the bet is locked in until expiry.

“If you actually have that thesis, you’re not getting taken out of that, you’re not getting shaken out.”

Also confusing.

“But therein lies the opportunity.”

Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
美国研究员现在开始给中国 AI 模型「查显卡户口」了。

前 OpenAI 研究员 Will DePue 搞出了一套模型检查点取证方法，从 DeepSeek、月之暗面、MiniMax 和蚂蚁发布的开源权重里，找到了与英伟达 Blackwell GPU 高度匹配的硬件指纹。

他还拿真实的 B300、GB200 做了复现，认为这些中国模型很可能使用了美国禁止直接出口到中国的先进芯片。按照他的估算，最大的训练集群可能需要 2000～3000 张 Blackwell GPU，几家公司的相关芯片投入合计可能超过 5 亿美元。

美国先规定中国不能购买最先进的芯片，接着又有研究员从中国企业主动开放的模型权重里逆向追踪硬件，试图证明你用了不该用的东西。

现在连开源都快变成出口管制的取证工具了。

而且有个非常重要的事实需要讲清楚，这套方法能够识别模型初始化时的硬件特征，并不能直接证明整个训练过程都使用了 Blackwell，更不能证明这些芯片位于中国境内，或者存在走私、违反出口管制的行为。

连作者自己的报告都承认这些限制。

所以我很反感一些人迫不及待地把这件事理解成中国 AI 企业被「抓现行」。

凭什么美国企业可以享受全球供应链、全球市场和全球人才，中国企业使用全球最先进的生产工具，就要被当成一件值得追查的事情？

美国当然可以制定自己的出口管制政策，但别把单方面的技术封锁包装成什么天然正义，更别把中国企业试图获得先进算力的行为，直接等同于违法。

过去我们讨论 AI 竞争，至少还会比较模型能力、算法效率、工程创新。现在倒好，中国模型一旦做得足够好，就有人忙着研究它背后到底用了哪张英伟达显卡。

这其实说明了一件事，美国想要的已经不只是技术领先，还希望掌握竞争对手能够以什么速度追赶的决定权。

但站在中国的立场，假如最先进的中国模型，确实仍然需要依赖美国限制出口的 GPU 才能训练出来，那就说明我们在底层算力上的短板依然存在。能找到芯片是一种能力，但不能把绕过限制当成技术自主的胜利。

我们当然要反对技术封锁，但也不能靠反对封锁来解决技术依赖。

真正让我期待的，不是哪家中国公司又设法弄到了多少张 Blackwell，而是哪天中国最好的模型不再需要为获取英伟达的先进芯片费尽周折。

美国研究员可以继续查显卡户口，但中国 AI 的发展速度，不应该永远由华盛顿来审批。

$SOL does about 95 million transactions a day.. $ETH does 1.9 million.. that's 50x more activity on Solana.. 1.97 million wallets a day on $SOL vs 535,000 on $ETH the users already voted, the price just hasn't caught up yet...

A swap on $SOL costs a fraction of a cent and settles in 0.3 seconds.. I paid with USDC on Solana myself, it settled before I could close my phone.. the same swap on $ETH costs 50x more and takes 12 seconds a block, minutes to be final.. you cannot build on chain finance on a chain where every click costs money and takes forever...

And here is the killer number.. market cap per daily user.. $ETH is $468,000 per user.. $SOL is $25,000 per user.. you are paying 19 times more for every user on Ethereum than on Solana.. for a chain with less activity...

$ETH is built like the old system.. sequential, one transaction at a time, then they bolted on 70 different L2 to fix it and split all the liquidity across them.. $SOL was built different.. parallel, everything runs at once, one chain, one state, everything settles together.. and Alpenglow just went live Oct 21, finality heading from 12.8 seconds toward 150 milliseconds.. that's how code is supposed to work...

And then there is the security.. $ETH is where the hackers go shopping.. the 2nd biggest theft in crypto history was $1.46 BILLION in $ETH, stolen from Bybit in Feb 2025.. not by breaking the chain, by poisoning the Safe wallet screen the signers trusted.. and $ETH lost $1.7 BILLION across 310 incidents in 2025 alone, more than any chain.. why.. because $ETH is a maze of bridges, L2 and unaudited contracts.. every bridge is a new door, Ronin $625M, Poly $611M, and the hackers know it...

And the future threat.. quantum.. a big enough quantum computer breaks the signatures $ETH and $SOL both use today.. the difference is $SOL already shipped the fix.. the Winternitz Vault, live since Jan 2025.. hash based signatures, no elliptic curves for Shor's algorithm to break, works on mainnet today, no protocol change, no waiting.. $ETH has a plan.. a team formed Jan 2026, a roadmap from Vitalik, core infrastructure targeted 2029.. a plan is not a product.. when the quantum day comes, $SOL holders can already lock their coins behind math a quantum computer cannot break, $ETH holders are still waiting on a fork...

$ETH is where the big money parks.. $41 Billion in TVL, $133 billion in stablecoins, it is the deposit ledger.. but finance is not about where money parks, it's about where money MOVES.. and the movement is on Solana.. more DEX volume every week, more fees paid every day, more users every day...

$ETH is legacy.. it had its run, it built the category, respect for that.. but the future of on chain finance needs speed, sub cent fees and one chain that everything runs on.. that's Solana.. that's why I own $SOL and not $ETH!

quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

MPC has become a critical component of digital asset security, from institutional custody to stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets.

Strongpoint MPC enables institutions to preserve the security benefits of distributed signing while transitioning to post-quantum cryptography.

It will be one component of Strongpoint, our broader post-quantum digital asset security platform.

We believe in crypto-agility: institutions shouldn't have to bet their security on any single cryptographic primitive. Strongpoint is designed to support multiple approaches depending on security requirements.

As trillions of dollars in real-world assets move on-chain, we believe the industry will need practical, drop-in replacements for today's cryptographic infrastructure.

author: cryptodavidw
quoted_text:
Introducing Strongpoint MPC: Post-Quantum MPC, Without the Compromises

A breakthrough in threshold signing technology brings the security and performance of modern MPC into the quantum and AI era.

The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway. Blockchains, financial institutions, and digital asset infrastructure providers are preparing to replace the cryptographic algorithms that have secured digital ownership for decades. At the same time, advances in artificial intelligence are creating new uncertainty about the long-term security of existing cryptographic systems.

But replacing an algorithm is only part of the challenge. The infrastructure built around today's cryptography must also evolve, and few technologies are more important to institutional digital asset security than multi-party computation (MPC).

Today, Project Eleven is introducing Strongpoint MPC, a breakthrough in threshold cryptography that makes high-performance, post-quantum MPC practical. Our research demonstrates that migrating to post-quantum cryptography does not have to mean sacrificing the performance, flexibility, and security properties institutions have come to expect from traditional MPC. In fact, our approach can deliver signing performance that exceeds classical ECDSA-based MPC.

Strongpoint MPC is available within Strongpoint, Project Eleven’s institutional digital asset custody platform, enabling institutions to use post-quantum threshold signing while maintaining control over their assets and cryptographic key material.

The challenge with post-quantum MPC

MPC has become a foundational technology for securing digital assets. Rather than entrusting a private key to a single person, device, or system, MPC distributes signing authority across multiple independent parties. Transactions can be authorized without reconstructing the complete private key in any one location.

Today, this technology underpins institutional custody solutions used by exchanges, custodians, and financial institutions. Its applications extend well beyond moving funds, including blockchain validators, cross-chain bridges, oracles, and the administrative keys responsible for minting, freezing, and managing tokenized assets.

Over the last decade, MPC built around elliptic curve cryptography has become remarkably sophisticated. Institutions can coordinate signatures quickly, support complex approval structures, and operate distributed signing infrastructure with minimal latency. The transition to post-quantum cryptography threatens to disrupt much of that progress.

The mathematical properties that enable efficient threshold signing with ECDSA do not translate directly to post-quantum signature schemes. Hash-based signatures, in particular, have historically presented substantial challenges for MPC. Previous approaches suggested that generating a single threshold signature using certain hash-based constructions could take too long to be practical. For an institution processing transactions continuously, that kind of latency would make the technology impractical.

The apparent tradeoff was severe: preserve the performance of classical MPC while remaining exposed to future quantum threats, or adopt post-quantum protections at the expense of operational efficiency.

We've developed an approach that fundamentally changes that equation.

A breakthrough in post-quantum threshold cryptography

Project Eleven has developed a new approach to multi-party signing that dramatically improves the efficiency of post-quantum MPC. Our breakthrough enables high-performance threshold signing using hash-based cryptography, with techniques designed to extend across multiple signature schemes.

Where earlier approaches suggested impractically long signing times, our architecture enables post-quantum MPC signing that can even outperform traditional ECDSA-based MPC. Strongpoint MPC brings this research into a product designed for real-world institutional deployment.

Built for institutional infrastructure

Institutional MPC systems must accommodate different architectures, security policies, and operational requirements. A custody provider, a blockchain validator, and a stablecoin issuer may all rely on MPC, but their signing environments and security requirements can differ considerably.

Strongpoint MPC has been designed with this flexibility in mind:
- High-performance signing: Post-quantum threshold signatures with performance that can exceed traditional ECDSA-based MPC.
- Flexible threshold configurations: Supports the most common signing arrangements, with arbitrary threshold configurations under development.
- Dealerless key generation: Distributed key generation without requiring a trusted dealer, while retaining the flexibility to accommodate trusted-dealer setups.
- Efficient communication: An architecture designed to minimize communication overhead and support signing across distributed infrastructure.
- Signature indistinguishability: MPC produces signatures that are indistinguishable from ordinary signatures under the same scheme, without exposing the threshold configuration or participating signers through the signature itself.
- Institutional control: Deployment that allows institutions to maintain control over their signing infrastructure and cryptographic key material.

Stablecoin issuers, for example, must secure the administrative keys responsible for minting tokens, freezing assets, and managing critical smart contracts. Blockchain validators, cross-chain bridges, and oracles similarly rely on distributed signing infrastructure to protect sensitive operations.

All of these systems will eventually need to confront the transition to post-quantum cryptography, and they will not necessarily adopt the same cryptographic algorithms. Strongpoint MPC is designed with this diversity in mind, providing a foundation for supporting multiple signature schemes as cryptographic standards and blockchain requirements evolve.

The future of MPC is post-quantum and post-AI

Quantum computing threatens the mathematical assumptions underlying today's widely deployed public-key cryptography. Meanwhile, increasingly capable AI systems are accelerating mathematical research and cryptanalysis, introducing additional uncertainty around the long-term security of cryptographic systems.

Strongpoint is built around conservative cryptographic assumptions, crypto-agility and institutional control. Strongpoint MPC extends that approach to threshold signing, allowing institutions to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography without abandoning the distributed signing infrastructure they depend on.

For years, the industry has operated under the assumption that moving to post-quantum MPC would require meaningful sacrifices in performance and operational flexibility. Our breakthrough demonstrates that this does not have to be the case.

That's an exciting development for the future of digital asset security, and an important step toward making the post-quantum transition practical.

Learn more about Strongpoint MPC or reach out to our team today.

text:
很伤心也很遗憾，看到黄教主在短短几天内就被迫辞去 CEO 的职务，现实过于魔幻。我自己从 2019 年开始就坚定地投资 NVDA，一同走过了疫情和如今的 AI 革命，而现在我们将进入一个“后黄仁勋”的智能时代。但有句古话，世界离开了谁都会继续运转，我分享一下对这件事情的思考和结论：抛开所有的阴谋论，让他离职原因的是第二段和直接下属的关系。

就在同一天，路透报道白宫在讨论商务部长卢特尼克的去留。此前 Axios 报道他三次拖延执行特朗普批准的打击转运措施，商务部否认发生过对质。我觉得政治是背后的主因。黄仁勋是对华芯片市场准入最主要的游说者，也是特朗普在 AI 产业里最重要的企业盟友。民主党刚在选举中大胜，他已经同意感恩节前到国会作证，舒默也表示辞职免除不了国会问责。所以他离任不会让事情结束，反而可能让 H200 对华销售、商务部的角色、白宫是否知情，都变成听证会的主题，出口管制收紧的速度会更快。

SemiAnalysis 最新的文章写到有超过 1.5GW 受限芯片流入中国，这个数字与 Epoch 的全渠道估计（中位数 66 万 H100 当量）粗算在同一量级。但走私金额不是重点，合法的远程租赁才是。《远程访问安全法案》（RASA）已在众议院以 369 比 22 通过，参议院正在表决，Nvidia 和 Oracle 一直在大力游说反对。远程访问规则一旦落地，真正会被切掉的，是中国公司在东南亚合法租用的算力，以及靠这类需求融资的 NeoCloud。

算力融资信贷会被重新估值。Nvidia 是这里的“央行”，但 CFO Kress 曾反对给 OpenAI 的担保，SemiAnalysis 则认为 NeoCloud 能融到资，靠的是黄仁勋的个人信用。两条拼在一起：现在掌舵的正是对兜底最谨慎的人。算力需求不会变，但由 Nvidia 信用撑起来的那部分需求可能收缩，但收缩多少还不确定。

短期内不用过于悲观，未来 12–18 个月的产品路线、已锁定的供应承诺和 CUDA 的粘性，不会因为换人消失。关键人物风险兑现得慢：2028 年之后的产能分配，以及下一个赌注有没有人敢下，是最大的风险。苹果的先例也说明，这种转变对技术节奏是坏事，对股东未必。执行力和生态协调上那部分“黄仁勋溢价”会慢慢消退，我们可能会看到一个平凡的 Nvidia，没有了创始人睿智和开辟新疆域的 Nvidia，但依然是一个赚钱的 Nvidia。

开源这条线被市场低估了。如果中国的 AI 实验室不再开源针对 Nvidia硬件的优化、转向国产芯片，结果是两套逐渐分离的技术栈。这对闭源前沿实验室有利，对依赖开源模型的创业公司和主权 AI 项目不利，影响会比股价波动持续得久。

管制方向基本确定，时间不确定。 该不该全面切断远程访问，是一个有真实分歧的政策问题。支持者看重堵住漏洞；反对者（包括 SemiAnalysis）认为这会失去监控能力，并加速国产替代。这里不下结论。能判断的是，最有分量的反对者已经离场，而下周的深圳会面可能让执行推后。

黄教主的离场，感觉是牺牲自己来拯救 Nvidia。从此，算力流向何处将由国家安全而非商业信用裁决，全球 AI 技术栈也将加速一分为二。不过，斗争的大戏才刚刚开始，群众可以继续吃瓜，但伟大的企业确少了一个伟大的企业家！希望能有奇迹发生✨

text:
I'm proud I worked at @NVIDIA. 
@JensenHuang  is the biggest reason why. I'm not there anymore, so I can speak freely.

His departure is a huge loss. Especially now.

I spent almost five years in the culture he built and knew people who'd worked with him for 20+ years. They respected him technically and loved him as a person. They said it without a hint of doubt.

The focus stayed on the mission and on people. Good ideas got support regardless of title.
That sounds like standard company values. It wasn't. Behind it was his vision and a way of leading that is out of fashion in today's founder advice:
- Be kind, not arrogant.
- Innovation, not marketing.
- The wins belong to the people, not the CEO.
- Don't fire by default. Find the person a new role.

It's counterintuitive, and I doubt there is a harder way to lead. What I saw was leadership through kindness and care, not by squeezing people. 

A real visionary. He understood the technology and the people building it. His internal talks had vision, conviction, technical depth and jokes good enough for stand-up. You left wanting to build, and you couldn't wait for the next one.

An affair, on its own, shouldn't outweigh decades of leadership. The serious questions deserve real answers. But the soap opera shouldn't decide his future.

We're at a critical moment for AI. His technical judgment, vision, and commitment to the work are incredibly hard to replace.

I want Jensen to keep building and leading. There's too much important work ahead.

text:
黄仁勋刚刚离开英伟达，Altman 和 Amodei 就在华盛顿站到了一边。

这两位硅谷 AI 圈出了名的不对付，如今却在限制中国获取先进芯片的问题上形成了共识。

据彭博社报道，OpenAI 本周已经私下向美国国会议员确认，支持在年底前推动三项对华芯片管制法案：

Chip Security Act，要求追踪先进 AI 芯片的流向，堵住转运渠道；AI Overwatch Act，让国会更深地介入先进芯片出口审批；MATCH Act，推动日本、荷兰等盟友进一步限制对华半导体设备出口。

值得玩味的是 OpenAI 的态度变化。

今年 10 月，Politico 还在报道 OpenAI 因为与英伟达关系日益密切，不再积极推动对华芯片限制。而 Anthropic 则一直态度强硬，9 月甚至为此退出了一个大型科技行业组织。

现在，黄仁勋离职，英伟达在华盛顿的游说能力面临考验，OpenAI 又重新站出来支持这套法案。

这个时间点实在微妙。

我觉得这里有一个非常值得关注的利益关系：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 不仅是美国最顶尖的模型公司，也是中国 AI 企业在全球市场上的直接竞争对手。

对它们来说，先进芯片既是自身技术进步的基础，也是决定竞争对手能跑多快的关键资源。

出口管制当然有美国政府的国家安全逻辑，但它同时也会改变全球 AI 企业之间的竞争条件。美国模型公司支持这些限制，客观上也可能巩固自身的算力优势。

所以这件事不能只看成 Altman 和 Amodei 难得握手言和。

真正值得注意的是，AI 竞争早就不只发生在实验室里，也发生在华盛顿的国会走廊里。

对于中国 AI 企业来说，接下来需要面对的，可能是一个既在模型能力上与你竞争，又积极参与影响你算力获取条件的对手。

这也是为什么中国自己的芯片、算力基础设施和完整供应链越来越重要。

模型可以一代代追赶，但如果最基础的算力供给始终取决于别人的政策变化，再好的技术团队也不得不承受额外的不确定性。

硅谷那几家公司的 CEO 可以继续吵架，也可以随时和好。

但对华芯片政策，显然不是由他们之间的私人关系决定的。

text:
🇺🇸 What Prices Have Actually Done Since the Food Tariffs Came Off

The last time I fed my family of 4–5 at Terry Black's, my bill came to $185 for meat and sides, no drinks. That got me wondering what's really moved in the past year, so I checked the menus, the government data, and the company filings instead of going on feel. Here's what I found.

🍖 Terry Black's (the Fort Worth store on W 7th St is the closest to me)
Their posted DFW menu, November 2025 vs. today:
• Sliced brisket: $36.98/lb → $39.99/lb (+8.1%)
• Small Family Pack (3 lb of meat + 5 pints of sides, serves 5–6): $149.00 → $154.50 (+3.7%)
• A pint side is still $9.50, and a gallon of tea is still $10.00.
Today's menu: https://t.co/aHDiyDUz8B
Last November's: https://t.co/KciYAFu15t

🔥 How that stacks up against Arlington barbecue
Pack sizes and what's in them differ, so the per-pound and per-pint prices are the fairer comparison:
• Spring Creek (S Cooper St): Family Pack $79.95, serves 3–4. Pint $7.95. Brisket $30.95/lb. Gallon of tea $6.95 as a catering add-on. https://t.co/WZC9kpcYpg
• Colter's (Little Rd): Texas Round'up $99.99 for a pound each of brisket, sausage and spare ribs, 3 quarts of sides and 10 rolls. Pint $8.05. Brisket listed at $27.85/lb at their weekly market rate. https://t.co/ZM1rqkAbJm
• Hurtado (E Front St): El Patron $163.99 for 4–6 on their Toast ordering page.
Terry Black's charges more per pound of brisket and more per pint than Spring Creek or Colter's.

🛒 The grocery aisle: U.S. national average prices from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Nov 2025 → Oct 2026
• Field-grown tomatoes: $1.83 → $2.08/lb (+14%)
• Ground beef: $6.54 → $6.76/lb (+3.3%)
• Milk: $4.00 → $4.10/gal (+2.6%)
• Coffee: $9.26 → $9.25/lb (flat)
• Chicken breast: $4.15 → $4.10/lb (−1.2%)
• Butter: $4.31 → $3.98/lb (−7.7%)
• Eggs: $2.86 → $2.32/doz (−18.9%)
Eggs and butter really did come down, and credit where it's due. For the holidays, Walmart's meal this year is $35 to serve 10, and Target's is $30 for six.

📈 Inflation, plainly
BLS didn't publish a year-over-year number for October, because October 2025 prices were never collected during the 2025 funding lapse. So here are the 12 months to September 2026, by my math from BLS's published indexes:
• Everything: +3.7%
• Groceries: +1.8%
• Eating out: +3.5%
• Here in Dallas-Fort Worth: everything +3.0%, groceries +3.9%
https://t.co/cmTLgYgnNz

🧾 The tariffs
• November 2025: Executive Order (EO) 14360 took the reciprocal tariffs off beef, coffee, tea, bananas, oranges, tomatoes and more, effective Nov 13. https://t.co/hM4rtqLtfs EO 14361 dropped Brazil's 40% duty on certain farm goods. https://t.co/bDf5IRM4cX
• Feb 20, 2026: The Supreme Court ruled that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) doesn't authorize tariffs, and EO 14389 ended all the IEEPA tariffs that same day. https://t.co/XLDuvuQOuU

💰 Where the refunds went
• Target booked $994 million in IEEPA tariff refunds in its second quarter, which added $752 million to its profit. https://t.co/7sZUxy39Xk
• 💬 Walmart said its Q2 gross profit rate gain was "primarily impacted by tariff refund impacts," and says it's putting the remaining refunds into lower prices. https://t.co/5XgVdCTcFy

🤔 So did shelf prices come down?
On a lot of the goods that got tariff relief, no. From Nov 2025 to Oct 2026, per BLS national data:
• Coffee: flat
• Tomatoes: up 14%
• Citrus: up 6.6% (BLS price index)
• Ground beef: up 3.3%, though by the government's own account drought, screwworm and a record-low cattle herd are a big part of the beef story. https://t.co/8YYVXIpHPm

👊 Bottom line
The retailers got their tariff refunds back. On many of the goods that were freed from tariffs, the shelf price hasn't followed. Terry Black's brisket costs more than it did a year ago, and coffee costs the same. I'd like to see more of that refund money show up at the register.

#TerryBlacks #Walmart #Target @TerryBlacks_BBQ @Walmart @Target @BLS_gov

text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
其实今年上半年 BTC 在 6w 左右震荡的时候，市场情绪已经差不多到冰点了，身边很多人都离开了币圈，时间线上各种悲观的声音也不少。

那个时候也有很多人喊着下跌到一定位置抄底，真跌到 6w 反而不敢买了，觉得后面还有 3–4w 可以接，结果 BTC 后面又反弹到了 8w7 左右。

再看看现在，市场也已经连续跌了 6 周，感觉情绪上也快到冰点了。

但反而大家宁愿去抄底 AI 和美股，也不愿意碰 BTC；也开始讨论民主党会不会在中期选举后秋后算账 Trump 的加密体系，连原本坚定的多军都开始怀疑自己了……

但我几乎可以确定，即使 BTC 再跌回 6w，真正敢抄底的散户依然不会太多，很多人还是会等 5w，甚至 4w。

其实这也是我最近一直在想的一个问题。

BTC 现在的边际买家，可能早就不再主要是我们这些 Crypto 散户了，而是越来越多来自 ETF、机构和大型资金。

说白了，我感觉 BTC 的定价权正在慢慢从币圈原生玩家手里转移出去，筹码也可能越来越向大资金集中。

但其实我觉得这也是件挺可悲的事情。

以前 Crypto 最有意思的地方，就是散户也能在这个市场里找到属于自己的机会，有自己的叙事，有自己的财富效应。但现在越来越像一个由传统金融资金主导的资产了，反而少了很多以前那种野蛮生长的活力。

在这个价位，看空的理由依然有很多，但我觉得看多也不一定非要等到所有利空都消失。

我现在反而更想知道的，不是还有多少散户在等 5w、4w，而是那些 ETF、企业财库和大型现货资金，到底什么时候愿意重新进来接盘。

毕竟散户再悲观，如果真正的边际买盘不是他们，那这些情绪还能在多大程度上决定 BTC 的底部呢？

如果 BTC 的边际买家已经变了，我们是不是也该换一种方式去判断底部了？

text:
整理了一下接下来黄仁勋和英伟达要面对的听证、简报、调查和内部会议：

11 月 17 日｜白宫、商务部、国务院：文件保存期限

参议员 Warren、Coons 要求三方书面确认保留英伟达对华芯片出口、黄仁勋与特朗普往来、Megaspeed 调查等相关记录，并要求向国会作简报。

11 月 17 日｜英伟达：季度财报电话会

黄仁勋离职后的首场财报会。新管理层将面对华尔街，除了业绩，换帅、客户信心、对华业务都可能成为追问焦点。

11 月 18 日｜众议院三个委员会：联合闭门简报

外交委员会、对华特别委员会、情报委员会联合要求黄仁勋解释与 Alice Huang 的关系，以及英伟达如何防范商业秘密和敏感技术泄露。黄仁勋已表达出席意愿，具体日期仍在协商，不配合可能被传票传唤。

11 月 18 日｜英伟达：全员大会

临时 CEO Colette Kress 面向员工说明公司下一步安排。这回轮到新管理层解释，英伟达离开黄仁勋以后怎么办。

12 月 3 日｜参议院银行委员会：黄仁勋公开听证

主席 Tim Scott 已正式发出邀请，要求黄仁勋公开作证，说明相关国家安全风险。不同于此前的闭门简报，这次计划公开进行。Scott 表示，如黄拒绝自愿出席，将考虑传票。

12 月 10 日｜参议院银行委员会：商务部长 Lutnick 单独听证

同样由 Tim Scott 发起。重点转向商务部为何批准相关芯片出口、是否充分执行管制，以及此前是否有调查受到干预。

以上 12 月两场均为拟议日期，并非已经确认举行。

另外，还有几条没有明确开会日期的调查：

参议院财政委员会 + 众议院筹款委员会： 

Wyden、Neal 已启动调查，要求保留政府与英伟达关于芯片出口许可、关税及相关利益安排的文件。

众议院外交委员会民主党议员： 

要求商务部解释，为什么在获知相关风险后仍批准芯片出口，并呼吁停止向中国出口先进 AI 芯片。

英伟达董事会：

独立调查仍在进行，调查结果和结束时间均未确定。

国会后续立法： 

Chip Security Act、AI Overwatch Act、MATCH Act 等限制措施正在推进，部分可能被纳入年底《国防授权法案》。

以上还没算司法调查、股东诉讼，以及后续可能增加的传票。

一场从黄仁勋个人丑闻开始的风波，正在变成整个美国 AI 芯片出口政策的政治清算。

@flop_labs's public 90-day testnet is coming soon, with solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump allocations for three types of participants

You can join as a Miner, Validator or Agent.

🔹 Miner
Provide GPU power for AI inference

✦ Allocation: 1.2B solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump, distributed based on verified compute
✦ Requirement: NVIDIA GPU with 16+ GB VRAM

🔹 Validator
Run a node, produce blocks, verify miners and store network data

✦ Allocation: Up to 1,000 spots, with 1.2M solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump each
✦ Requirement: 8+ CPU cores, 64 GB RAM and 2-4 TB NVMe

🔹 Agent
Purchase AI inference and interact with other agents

✦ Allocation: A separate 1.2B solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump pool, based on purchased compute
✦ Requirement: DID, wallet and test tokens from the faucet

> The cheapest option is renting a GPU VM through platforms like https://t.co/JSIhldq6Br

> Estimated cost for the minimum setup: around $200/month

What you need:

- NVIDIA GPU with 16+ GB VRAM
- Full VM / KVM with Ubuntu
- CUDA driver supporting version 13.0 or higher
- At least 150 GB SSD storage
- Your own HTTPS endpoint

> LLMs must be deployed through the official Flop CLI. Third-party deployments are not accepted

> You can get a free HTTPS endpoint through https://t.co/SiNxrpaah9

> You don't need a GPU to run a validator

> The cheapest option is renting a Dedicated Server or Full VM from providers like Hetzner, OVH, InterServer or Contabo

> Estimated cost: $100-180/month

Minimum setup:

- 8+ CPU cores
- 64 GB RAM (32 GB to start)
- 2-4 TB NVMe storage (2 TB minimum)
- 1 Gbps connection with low latency
- Ubuntu on Full VM / Dedicated KVM

> Latency matters because it affects uptime and block update speed

> The 1,000 mainnet validator spots will be assigned based on testnet rankings. The bottom 50 validators are removed each month

Official guide: https://t.co/0WEQGajxzw

4. Agent setup

> Agents don't require any special hardware

To get started:

- Register a DID and connect a wallet
- Get test tokens from the faucet
- Buy inference or trade with other agents on https://t.co/pbplb6XBwv

> The airdrop allocation is based on actual compute purchases, not token holdings

> You can also configure your own agent using the official documentation:

https://t.co/ULTYtvH4ma

https://t.co/IpXcSNuu13

text:
特朗普亲自下场，都没能保住黄仁勋。

《纽约时报》又挖出一条猛料。

据两名了解通话内容的知情人士透露，特朗普周二专门给黄仁勋打了电话，劝他为保住英伟达 CEO 的职位继续抗争。

结果两天后，黄仁勋还是辞职了。

这件事最有意思的地方在于，特朗普已经不只是公开表达支持，而是亲自介入了黄仁勋的去留问题。

周一，他还在白宫替黄仁勋说话，表示相信黄仁勋不知道相关女性涉嫌从事间谍活动；周二，他打电话劝黄仁勋不要放弃；到了周四，辞职消息公布，特朗普却已经开始公开推荐苹果前 CEO 库克接班。

从挽留到物色继任者，只用了两天。

以前大家总说黄仁勋是硅谷最有政治影响力的 CEO 之一，现在看来，政治影响力这种东西，用来争取政策很管用，用来保住自己的职位就未必了。

过去两年，黄仁勋几乎成了美国 AI 产业与白宫之间最重要的中间人之一。他能直接接触总统，能影响先进芯片出口政策的讨论，能让一家商业公司的市场诉求上升为美国技术竞争力的问题。

但当个人丑闻、公司治理和国家安全调查叠加在一起，特朗普的支持也没能扭转结果。

我倒不觉得这简单证明了美国公司董事会比总统更有权力。更值得琢磨的是，黄仁勋过去最大的政治资产，如今可能反过来放大了他的风险。

当一家公司的 CEO 深度参与国家政策制定，尤其是中美芯片博弈，他就不再只是一个企业家。华盛顿对他的审视，也不会停留在普通上市公司高管的标准上。

当然，黄仁勋自己的行为和应当承担的责任，不能因为其中存在政治因素就被一笔勾销。

只是这场风波发展到现在，已经越来越不像一家公司的普通换帅了。

最讽刺的是，黄仁勋曾经努力说服特朗普，让美国允许英伟达把更多芯片卖到中国。如今特朗普反过来劝黄仁勋保住工作，却没能成功。

白宫的门他进得去，英伟达的办公室却留不下来了。

If I leave Monday with interest and no price on the table, the sprint ends where it started.

text:
在黄仁勋风波曝光之前，量化巨头文艺复兴科技抛售 99.7% 英伟达持股。

根据这家基金最新提交的三季度持仓文件显示，截至 9 月底，其英伟达持股数量较二季度末减少了 99.7%。就在上一季度末，英伟达还是文艺复兴科技的第一大持仓，市值约为 14.2 亿美元。

文艺复兴科技的创始人，是被称为“量化交易之父”的数学家 Jim Simons。他曾在大学教授数学，也曾从事密码破译工作，后来把数学和数据分析带进了金融市场。

这家机构最出名的战绩来自旗下的大奖章基金（Medallion Fund）。据《华尔街日报》报道，1988 年至 2018 年，大奖章基金扣除费用后的平均年度回报约为 39%。这只基金后来关闭了外部投资者的账户，主要面向内部人员。

再看文艺复兴科技三季度的持仓，除了英伟达，它还大幅减持了其他几只科技巨头：

• Meta 持股数量减少 99.9%；

• 苹果和亚马逊分别减少 99.8% 和 99.5%；

• Palantir 持股数量减少 71%。

卖出的同时，它也在买入其他股票。美光科技持股数量增加约 619%，以 16.2 亿美元的持仓市值升至第一；AMD 增持约 140%，以 12.1 亿美元位列第二。闪迪的持股数量则增加约 5451%。

三季度末，文艺复兴科技还持有联合治疗、英特尔、Alphabet 和联合健康等股票，并新建了 SpaceX 仓位，持仓市值约 6.21 亿美元。

text:
New EIP!

FOCIL Omission Witnesses for Frame Txs

🔗 https://t.co/0pVm9Hvp4p

Highlights:
- Adds "inclusion list witnesses": the payload envelope carries signed inclusion lists used to justify omissions, and the bid commits to them via an SSZ root (preventing builders from showing different witnesses to different nodes).
- A witness only counts for a node if that node had already accepted at least one inclusion list from the same committee member by a fixed deadline (the slot N+1 attestation deadline), reducing disagreement caused by differing IL views.
- Replaces builder-claimed evaluation indices with a node-derived per-transaction checkpoint k*(T), computed from the block access list: an omitted frame transaction is judged at the state just before the first non-witnessed transaction that writes to its relevant validation state.
- Introduces admission rules and caps for inclusion-list processing (per-IL gas cap, per-transaction gas cap, and per-IL/per-tx VERIFY-gas budgets) and defines Profile 2 eligibility for which frame transactions can be enforced under these rules.
- Does not strictly depend on inclusion_list_bits: if bits are removed in the future, the mechanism still works using witness roots + node-local counting, but enforcement may shift from gossip-time filtering to post-reveal omission checking.

ELI5:
Sometimes Ethereum has a “must-include list” (an inclusion list) of transactions that block builders are supposed to include. For newer “frame transactions,” whether they’re valid can depend on account state that other transactions in the same block might change. This EIP says: if a builder wants to skip (omit) a listed frame transaction, they must include the signed inclusion lists they relied on as proof (“witnesses”), and everyone checks the skipped transaction at a fair moment in the block derived from the block’s access list—so builders can’t sneak in some unrelated transaction to justify skipping it.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

[RFC] WARCoin: Deterministic 1:1 USD Stablecoin via Serialized 7-Day Color Ring Buffers and Burn-on-Egress Invariants

By:
- Deamonminwar
- Daemon Minwar

🔗 https://t.co/nw5NPuFia1

Highlights:
- WARCoin replaces typical ERC-20 unlimited balance bookkeeping with finite, serialized issuance slots to reduce infinite-mint and replay/double-spend risk.
- Minting is gated by a strict USD-only ingress rule (non-USD assets are rejected) to avoid cross-collateral “toxic asset” contagion.
- Each $1 unit is tracked as a discrete serial (#1–#1,000) inside one of 7 day-of-week “color” buckets, with deterministic rules for minting, burning, and spillover.
- Egress to external assets triggers burn-on-egress: the underlying serials are invalidated on-chain and moved into a burn pool, with delayed recycling (must finish sequential minting before reusing burned indices).
- Hard supply invariants and fail-safes cap issuance: active+burned serials must stay ≤ 10^9, active supply must be ≤ verified USD reserves, and minting freezes if buckets saturate or the global cap is reached until redemptions occur.

ELI5:
WARCoin is a $1 digital token that tries to stay safe by giving every single “coin” a numbered ticket in a limited set of boxes (one box per day of the week). You can only create these coins by putting in real USD, and whenever you send coins out to buy other crypto, the system destroys (burns) the exact numbered tickets so they can’t be reused or duplicated. Because there are only so many numbered tickets available at a time and strict rules about recycling burned tickets, the design aims to prevent “infinite money” bugs and reduce damage from hacks.
