author: indigox
quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
받) 엔비디아 관련 카더라

1. 자기가 들은 썰에 의하면, 미국 정치권은 이미 6개월 전에 젠슨황의 중국 스파이 이슈를 알고 있었다.

2. 이걸 미국 민주당 주도로 중간 선거 직후 터뜨린 것이다.

3. 터뜨린 이유는 트럼프와 공화당을 견제하기 위함이다. 

  1) 트럼프가 AI 정책을 주도하는 것을 견제하고 

  2) 트럼프와 공화당이 선거 패배 이후 외교, 특히 G2 대중국 외교로 정치 난국을 타개하려고 시도할 것인데, 여기서 트럼프의 핵심 카드가 엔비디아 칩과 젠슨황이다. 

4. 처음에 중국 스파이 뉴스만 나왔을때는 젠슨황의 해임 가능성은 높게 보지 않았다.

5. 근데 사내 불륜 뉴스가 나오는 걸 보니 젠슨황은 해임될 거라고 본다. (젠슨황 해임 발표 이전에 촬영된 영상임) 

  그 이유는 미국 기업들은 규정으로 사내 불륜을 해임 사유로 명시한 곳들이 많은데, 이게 뉴스로 나왔다는 건 해임된다는 의미다.

6. 엔비디아의 순환 투자 구조는 향후 3년은 유지될 거라고 본다. 

  그 이유는 반도체 기업들의 로드맵이 평균 3년 정도를 예상하고 계획되는데, 엔비디아도 칩 개발, AI 통합 등 로드맵을 3년간 유지할 수 밖에 없다. 따라서 이에 맞춘 순환 투자 구조도 유지될 것이다. 이걸 포기하면 사업 근간 자체가 흔들린다.

7. 이번 젠슨황 사태는 중국에게도 큰 타격이다. 어찌됐든 젠슨황과 트럼프를 통해서 AI칩을 우회 확보할 수 있었는데, 이게 차단되어버렸다. 중국 내수 AI칩의 수준은 아직 미흡하고 한계가 있다.

8. 애플의 잡스 사후 후계 사례와 비교하여, 잡스는 미리 팀쿡이라는 체계적 경영의 귀재를 발굴해서 후계를 잘 준비한 반면, 젠슨황은 그렇지 못했다. 따라서 앞으로 어떻게 후계를 준비하는지 관심을 갖고 봐야 한다.

text:
Generative AI isn't the second Industrial Revolution. It's the second Renaissance. 

Software factories are not the way, and it's not because they can't mechanically work. It's because they're the most obvious thing you would do, if the ONLY thing AI improved was speed and scale, but you were making the same things you made before.

AI increases the creative leverage of anyone who really knows how to use it to a degree that makes software factories look like a very quaint idea.

It's not just faster. It's more prototyping, more learning, ability to play with a wider range of ideas across multiple disciplines, the ability to imagine horizons not previously achievable.

text: These seminars and community shaped my thinking centrally.  Days I will always remember.  Thank you Professor Posner.
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
Dick Posner died this week at 87. And an era went with him.

I co-organized the Rational Choice workshop at the University of Chicago with Dick, the late Nobel laureate Gary Becker, and @glenweyl in the late 2000s/early 2010s. We aimed it at everything that seemed important. Chief economists for rival presidential candidates debated under Chatham House rules. The architects of Obamacare sat across from its fiercest critics and reached agreements nobody expected. For example, on Obama-care, that event resolved to an agreement on both sides that, setting the efficiency of government health enterprises aside, the law's only consistent effect was to shift incentives away from direct medical innovation (medicines, devices) and toward logistical innovation (triage, the reorganization of hospitals and health systems)--something that never surfaced in public discussion.

Dick had a hacksaw of a mind. A presenter would be halfway through the first slide and Dick would say, “I think all of this is bunk...” He was curmudgeonly, but not only that. He, Gary, & Glen read everything in advance. Dick's counter-thesis would follow his knee-jerk critique, sometimes sharp and general enough to consume the entire seminar.  

Dick (and Gary, Glen) were engaged and thoughtful to a degree I have rarely seen since. When I presented, their critiques felt like intellectual performance art, destructive and constructive at once. They could be persuaded, but at a cost that almost always changed the character of the original argument.

The workshop (almost always) ended with a dinner continuing the argument that Dick always wanted at the mediocre but white-table cloth Hyde Park eatery, Piccolo Mundo (now closed). When Glen tried to explore other new, spicier options, Dick universally said, "They're all dumps!", and we went back to Piccolo ;-).

For Dick and Gary, the workshop was "Rational Choice!" For me (and maybe Glen), it was "Rational Choice?" We kept finding locally rational choices that added up to collectively irrational phenomena. Defending a question mark against those two exclamation points was an education I will always treasure.

In an era of more fractious civic discourse, academic discourse has gentled. We have entered an era that is more accommodating--that goes along with the speaker. There is a lot to celebrate about this. It certainly feels more inclusive, which I appreciate. But there is a place for conflict...and there was a place for Dick Posner. (Perhaps predictably at the The University of Chicago.) Precisely IF you disagreed with him, Dick fashioned his high-pitched critique to expand your mind. It expanded mine.

In my life, I have met exactly one Dick Posner. I do not expect to meet another.

https://t.co/L0zb7EyPOX

#UniversityofChicago #debate #freedomofspeech #constructiveconflict

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
My Experience With the Leaders of the Jensen Coup

At the start of 2025, numerous Washington, D.C. based NGOs began spreading the false rumor that DeepSeek smuggled 50,000 H100 GPUs. Speaking from firsthand experience, organized think tanks, PR firms, and lobbyists aggressively personally attacked anyone merely asking them to provide evidence. Call them the Export Controls Deep State, or if that’s too right-coded for you, use the Obama-administration term “Foreign Policy Blob”.

The same charlatans are attempting a coup on Jensen Huang, the most indispensable CEO to America’s AI success. If we lost Sam, we have Dario. If we lost Dario, we have Demis. Nvidia is singular. The gap between Nvidia and AMD would be wider than the gap between OpenAI and Mistral, Europe’s top AI company whose models don’t rank in the top 40. This is an attempt to derail the most important company for the American AI industry.

The entire coup against Jensen Huang can be halted by asking a single question. What evidence is there that Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy? The answer, unsurprisingly, is absolutely zero. There is not even the pretense of a factual basis for the claim. “We made it the fuck up, and if you have a problem with that, what are you, pro-China?”

Taking away this obvious falsehood, the coup against Jensen boils down to a celebrity tabloid headline. Moreover, without the entirely fabricated ‘national security relevance’, these tabloid headlines would be at best a weekend story in the New York Post. Another basic question: if there is evidence of ‘national security relevance’, why not charge Jensen? The basic answer: they lack even the evidence to justify a warrant.

During my time in DC, I was advised repeatedly to stay on the good side of the Export Controls Deep State. I was added to many groups for boosting content spreading the 50,000 H100s conspiracy theory. In several groups, I asked whether there was any evidence behind this claim. One group administrator, who was and still is affiliated with Georgetown, explicitly told me to “focus on bolstering the narrative”. I later posted Patel’s pseudo-correction and was subsequently removed from all of these groups.

What you need to understand about the Export Controls Deep State is that they have no incentive to be remotely honest, because they are entirely unaccountable. To this day, they provided zero evidence for their claim. Internet historians later traced the origin of this claim to a tweet by Dylan Patel of Semianalysis. Patel later said they lied about his tweet and that his claim counted legally obtained hardware.

Affiliates of universities and think tanks promote these baseless claims and are taken seriously by the national press. In reality, their theories about Nvidia are as kooky as the guy who shot up Comet Pizza. The reason they succeed is not only because they are unaccountable, but because they constantly use their unaccountability to attack others. There are broader foreign policy implications to these observations about political power, but I will stick to what I witnessed firsthand.

After Trump’s election, his administration began lifting the export control cap. Surprising no one informed about this policy, America widened our lead. Deepseek was closest to catching up to American models in January 2025, literally the moment of peak export controls.

Based on communication with members of the administration, the evidence that a) the export controls were net negative and b) the export controls deep state was acting in bad faith, that as soon as the situation was described accurately, the administration began rolling them back.

Part of this is because many of these NGOs are funded by foundations like Open Philanthropy / Coefficient Giving, who explicitly intend to harm American AI companies because they believe American AI will “cause human extinction”. As a result, the BIS under the Biden administration was used as an informal cudgel against AI companies, both to censor in favor of their worldview, as seen in the Gemini scandal, as well as to backdoor regulation to slow down American AI broadly.

While they love to accuse everyone else of being traitors, the Export Controls Deep State makes Americans poorer and the American military, to the extent they use AI, weaker.

Most of the time, the best you can do is ignore them. They really are unaccountable and the personal retribution isn’t worth the cost. But now, they are leading a coup against the AI industry’s most indispensable man based on lies and tabloid gossip. Everyone should understand that the Export Controls Deep State has never provided any evidence for their claims nor any reason for their word to be trusted.

AI铁王座空出来了，再聊聊老黄的辞职及影响：1、大家没注意的是老黄昨晚不仅辞掉了CEO、总裁连董事会成员的身份也辞掉，可以说退的干干净净跟英伟达彻底切割了，以后老黄只是英伟达最大的个人股东而已。一方面可能婚外情属实，另一方面也说明老黄应该也是面临了巨大的压力，不然董事会成员也不会辞掉。

2、33年以来英伟达董事会首次任命了一位董事会主席，这是跟老黄裸辞一样重要的信息，就是英伟达董事会改组。从“首席独立董事”机制改成正式董事长制，董事会的控制权也在进一步收拢。

英伟达董事会首任主席HarveyC.Jones（哈维·琼斯），1993年加入董事会，前
电子设计自动化巨头新思科技（Synopsys）的CEO和执行董事长，也是投资机构SquareWaveVentures的管理合伙人。

3、对产业的影响可能更深远
如开头所说AI铁王座空下来了，产业教主倒下了，现在看还没人能顶的上去 ：要么产业身位不够、要么资历和影响力也不够。
1）对英伟达来说，短期算是利空落地。如昨晚老黄辞职消息出来前聊到，“如果老黄离任最终消息出来，短线可以博一个大反弹毕竟核心竞争力没那么快就没了，但长期就得边走边看、看实际经营状况，看接任者是不是能真的撑得住”。老黄辞职的消息出来、昨天英伟达也确实低开高走；

2）老黄辞职，英伟达少了一个有远见、有决断力和魄力的掌舵人和领航人，需要特别注意老黄在任时几十名高管都直接向他汇报，那说明英伟达得高管没有谁能有他这样的全局视野、现在看未来是会受限的。

老黄还主导一批用英伟达的信用给数据中心建设兜底的项目，例如之前给OpenAI的合作，同时几家新云厂商特别是CRWV也都是老黄扶持起来的；影响自然也不小。

3）但有受损的就有受益的
老黄离开、英伟达的竞争对手不得笑开怀。AMD、谷歌的TPU、亚马逊的Trainium估计都看到了进一步追赶的可能性。为谷歌和亚马逊自研芯片的核心供应商博通和MRVL又能分到更多的蛋糕了。

4）对整个产业链来说
教主走了，扛大旗没有了，凭老黄一己之力扶持起来的算力产业链可能要放缓，但产业趋势已经形成，最多只是延缓并并不是停滞。

这两天在思考一个点，“slower for longer”的节奏可能更好，不需要动不动就高歌猛进、时不我待的。节奏稍稍降下来、会走的更稳更远。

4、而对整个市场来说
还是维持一周前https://t.co/CGaeac1Pr8聊到的，这是AI中场还远没有到完结，上周四是市场恐慌的一个极值。甚至昨晚老黄的辞职我也没感受到市场如上周四那样的恐慌

会到前面说的“slower for longer” ，过去几年的大干快干让硬件层分走了绝大部分利润，而慢下来，就是在模型层/应用层/平台层/硬件层之间做利润的重分配，资金的投入方喘口气，甚至于硬件层也不是通杀，流动性恐慌后，最终会回到不同环节的供需紧张程度出现定价分化。

quoted_text:
英伟达的董事会能保住老黄么？再聊聊老黄的这次桃色事件。1、看下图英伟达董事会里包括老黄在内11名董事，有6位任职超过十三年，即使2019年加入英伟达董事会的Stephen也是1993年起就给英伟达提供法律服务。这意味着有7位董事很老黄共事很久，经历过英伟达过去的高峰低谷、能深刻认识老黄对于英伟达的不可或缺，他的远见、决断力以及魄力是英伟达走到现在的关键因素。

从董事会的构成看、老黄的亲密战友还是占多数的。

2、最终取决于在于调查的结果，
独立董事正式聘请 Wachtell 律所及纽约南区前代理联邦检察官 Joon Kim 主持调查，董事会把事实调查交给了外部律师。
1）这个调查是昨天的消息调查重点还是跟黄乐的关系，以及有没有泄漏相关机密；

2）今天纽约时报报道的跟女下属的婚外情、估计也是新的调查方向。
这个跟女下属的婚外情现在所有的报道就是曾在英伟达工作的匿名消息源头说两人有关系，但是都还没有明确的证实，最早纽约时报的报道记者说也没看到相关视频。

但这点恰恰最最关键，决定了是事实确凿还是扑风捉影。

3、能看出来这次倒黄动作势大力猛
先是黄乐，再是powell，特别是powe
ll这个现在所有的媒体报道都没有明确的实质性证据，都是匿名消息源的说法，这一点非常值得怀疑。然后纽约时报又传统的左派媒体，跟民主党关系亲密不能不让人生疑。

当然也看到有说法anthropic的联创JackClark也给媒体提供了信息，他之前本身就是科技记者。老黄力推开源，DarioAmodei主张闭源、激烈路线之争。

倒黄派可能是看到了单凭黄乐还不足以让老黄离开、所以又拿跟女下属powell的关系做文章。
当然这些都是我们吃瓜群众的揣测。

从董事会构成上来看，想保住老黄的应该还是占大多数，但最后还是回到调查结果：
1）如果跟女下属powell婚外情被证实，再叠加跟黄乐的关系。老黄大概率是要离任的，即使不完全离开公司但是ceo估计是很难继续了、也可能有一个比较长的过渡期或者担任顾问。

但这对英伟达来说中长期影响还是不小，毕竟像开头说再有一个能有老黄那样的远见、决断力和魄力的ceo概率很小。

这种情况下，最终结果出来短线可以博一个大反弹，因为核心竞争力也没那么快就没了。长期就要边走边看、看实际经营状况了，看接任者能不能真的撑得住。

2）如果跟powell关系被证实子虚乌有、光黄乐感觉撼动老黄的概率不大。大概率黄乐就是一个倒卖芯片的掮客，是间谍的可能性很小老黄泄露机密概率也不大，这种情况下董事会应该还是会保住老黄的。

甚至英伟达的前几大股东贝莱德、先锋、富达、道富等机构都不想老黄走人，毕竟在老黄身上利益巨大。
这种情况英伟达被砸下来就是一个真正的黄金坑了

quoted_text:
This is a difficult moment. It’s hard not to look at the journey this company has taken and not be filled with respect for what Jensen built. The spirit of the company remains strong: "mission is the boss”.

That said, as NVIDIA finds its way forward, I want one thing to be clear: NVIDIA's contributions to open source are unwavering.

Jensen has been vocal about this, and that commitment runs deep in NVIDIA's people and culture. We all understand the importance of open source.

NVIDIA is a huge supporter of open source because we understand something.
If you want to diffuse technology, you do so through an ecosystem, not a single company or entity.

No one owns the internet, no one owns servers, and no one owns operating systems… but through open source, an ecosystem of closed and open innovation flourishes.

When we talk about delivering agents safely and securely, that too will take place because of open source. For example, ensuring people have the best models to secure themselves at machine speed unburdened by arbitrary guardrails decided behind closed doors.

Open source & AI are often discussed together, but it’s worth reminding, open source predates AI. It is a mechanism for sharing ideas inspired by the hippies at computer labs of California in the 1960s.

Before AI, the largest shift I lived through was the internet. It was remarkable seeing the fight for open source take place there. Between browsers, runtimes, net neutrality, etc. What came as a result was HTML5 and an extremely vibrant ecosystem that built the internet as we know it today.

NVIDIA and its partners hold an incredibly important role in delivering this technology. NVIDIA contributes to every layer of the stack. Runtimes, models, harnesses, programming languages, frameworks, etc. None of that changes.

Long live open source.

text:
Recursive self-improvement is one of the most discussed ideas in AI right now.

Banger paper on RSI for frontier pre-training.

They claim to be the first in the world to apply RSI to an entire frontier pre-training run from scratch.

This work uses agent-driven loops on a single frontier pre-training run and produced 801-30B-A3B, an open 30B MoE base that beats Qwen3-30B-A3B and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B.

Pre-training is hard to improve with one big loop. A run costs hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours and happens once, and its real goal is headroom for post-training.

So they split the work into smaller loops that can close. Agents debug infrastructure and data, check post-training headroom with tiny SFT runs, and turn expert judgment into metrics for data pipelines. A shared context store keeps negative results across teams.

With only 6B tokens of SFT and no RL, the model had the highest average on four agentic benchmarks against fully post-trained models, including Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.

text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
Tarek predicted 5 month ago that Citadel would sue Kalshi.

In this interview from June, @mansourtarek_ explains exactly why stock perps are a big threat to Wall Street.

Now Citadel, CME, Cboe and Nasdaq are suing him to stop Kalshi from offering perps.

Here is why.

1 - THEY FEAR LOSING RETAIL

Citadel executes ~35% of US-listed retail volume and make money by trading against their orders. Stock perps threaten to redirect that activity.

If someone trades an Apple perp on Kalshi instead of Apple shares, Citadel loses.

Their own court filing explicitly admit to it:

- “Cboe and Citadel Securities lose transactions and revenue they cannot later recover.”
- “Kalshi's offering is designed to draw away CME’s customers who currently trade futures.”

2 - PERPS GENERATE LESS FEES

So why wouldn't Citadel just offer Perps themselve ?

Because traditional futures have an expiry date. To keep your exposure you need to close you old position and open a new ones. Those additional transactions generate fees. 

Perps don’t expire, removing those fees entirely.

The interview passage where Tarek highlights this Perps over Futures advantage is even cited by CME in the lawsuit.

That's why the Citadel camp is asking to reclassify Perps as security-based swaps:

1) Citadel wins - Perps are SEC regulated, retails can't trade them, they keep trading future on their exchange.

2) Kalshi wins - Perps are CFTC regulated, retail can trade them over more expensive futures, Kalshi receive their order flow.

It's all about who gets to farm retail.

text:
NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

But I can also say that Jensen is human, and makes mistakes like all of us do. Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. That shows rare character, to maintain humility and humanity through all of it.

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Love you all ❤️

text:
黄仁勋走了，英伟达的客户终于敢考虑买别家的芯片了。

《The Information》报道，一家采购英伟达芯片的云厂商高管透露，公司正在认真考虑转向 Google 和 AMD。

最有意思的是后半句：他们早就想分散采购了，但一直不敢，因为怕得罪黄仁勋。

多少有点黑色幽默了。堂堂 AI 算力市场，几百上千亿美元的生意，客户选择供应商，居然还得考虑一位 CEO 的心情。

但这恰恰说明，黄仁勋过去几年建立的权力，早就超出了芯片本身。

英伟达不仅掌握着最紧俏的 GPU，还通过投资、信贷担保、采购承诺，把自己变成了许多 AI 云厂商的重要资金支持者。它既卖铲子，又帮客户融资买铲子，有时候甚至还负责租下客户挖出来的坑。

在这种关系里，采购决策就不只是性价比问题了。你当然可以用 AMD，可以考虑 Google TPU，但万一因此失去了英伟达的支持呢？

技术垄断已经很厉害了，更厉害的是让客户形成一种心理：我最好别惹它。

更讽刺的是，那位高管现在又开始担心，黄仁勋离开之后，英伟达未来几代芯片的研发会不会受到影响。

以前是不敢换，现在是怕不换。

当然，这不意味着英伟达的客户会立刻集体倒戈。CUDA 生态、芯片性能和现有部署规模，依然是真实存在的竞争壁垒。至少短期内，英伟达并不缺买家。

但我觉得，这件事暴露了一个比市场份额更有意思的问题：

过去 33 年，黄仁勋究竟是在为英伟达建立一家不依赖任何人的伟大公司，还是在建立一个所有人都必须围着他转的商业帝国？

两者在他掌权时看起来几乎没有区别。

直到他离开，客户才敢把另一家的产品报价单拿出来。

text:
这是一个时代彻底的终结。

我不知道用怎样的情绪来形容这几天的心情，我也不知道此情此景身在美国的华裔们——尤其是在当前各个领域代表着先进、效率、努力的华裔企业家、工程师们怀揣着怎样的心情和想法看待这场巨大的、突如其来的变化。总之，作为一位33年奋斗在一线、开创了CUDA产业化，甚至带来这场AI产业化繁荣的先驱，黄仁勋的离场，就是一场刀刀见血的政治闹剧。

我相信，持有英伟达这家公司股票的人，即一开始就坚定地信任英伟达未来的人，打心底里一定是信任且拥护那个身穿黑色皮衣的男人的。因为，这家公司的低谷与巅峰，以及与AI应用化命运环环相扣的纽结，几乎就是这个男人一手坚持与缔造的。
黄仁勋没有倒在CUDA无人看好的黎明前夜，他几乎倒在了AI的突围盛放之时。不管原因如何，在这样的时代，他的离开，是比当年苹果失去乔布斯更加令人失望的时刻。

许多人可能会说，黄仁勋失去了CEO的职位，他还有百分之3的股份，足够一生荣华富贵。我想反问，一个64岁的老人，为了自己一生追逐的梦想，他的目的是钱吗？他要的，是AI的一片江山。没有人比他更了解英伟达，从与几十个管理层领导的扁片化管理，就能看出英伟达几乎是牵一发而动全身——他，就是英伟达之魂。

没有了黄仁勋的英伟达，还是英伟达吗？
绝对不可能是了。

33年前，在一家Denny’s的卡座里，三个年轻人决定做一家图形芯片公司。那时没有人知道，GPU这个词三十年后会变成一个国家的战略资源，成了大国博弈桌上最重的筹码。更没有人知道，卡座里那个三十岁的台湾移民，有一天会因为这枚筹码太重，被蓝色的力量从桌边彻底推开。

我们必须承认，事情的起因并不光彩。他给全体员工写信，承认自己对妻子不忠，承认辜负了所有人的信任。
这一点我不想替他辩护，也辩护不了。私德上的账，只能他自己去还。
但我们也都清楚，同样的事如果发生在一家普通公司的CEO身上，它最多是一则花边新闻、一场董事会内部调查、一份措辞体面的声明。能闹的如此满城风雨，乃至全球经济的震荡，与中期选举的结果可以说绝对是休戚相关。

这就是政治的力量，黑暗世界的角力。

黄仁勋所做的一切都在证明，一个移民在这片土地上可以走到多远。可是风暴来临的时候，那股蓝色的力量首先审视的是他的面孔、他的来处、他的族裔，还有他和海峡两岸之间千丝万缕的联系。

如果连黄仁勋都要证明自己的忠诚，那么在硅谷每一间实验室里加班到深夜的华裔工程师，又该如何自处？
这让我深刻地怀疑，痛定思痛。
最近想起CUDA刚推出的那几年。华尔街嘲笑它是烧钱的玩具，股东质问为什么每一块游戏显卡都要背上额外的成本，公司市值一度跌到只剩几十亿美元。
他没有退。
他说英伟达要做的是一个零亿美元的市场，一个现在还不存在、但总有一天会出现的市场。后来，这个市场有了名字，叫人工智能。他熬过了所有技术上的质疑，熬过了无人问津的黎明。最后让他倒下的不是对家AMD和英特尔，也不是其他任何一个竞争对手，而是政治的力量，或者说，是他自己的政治嗅觉和信息位。

我承认，克雷斯是优秀的管理者，英伟达的团队依然是世界上最强的团队之一。下周二的财报会照常发布，新一代芯片会照常交付，股价也许几周后就会有回升之势。

可是那个能在GTC舞台上一口气讲两个小时、凌晨还在给工程师回邮件、同时追问几十个直接下属的人，不在了。

text:
我跟孙哥聊了 5 个小时，播客千万播放量。评论区出现最多的一句话是：孙哥只是会营销、炒作。

聊完我的感觉正好相反。市场高估了孙宇晨的“炒作能力”，低估了他的韧性。

一、他是币圈最有韧性的人

这几年围绕他和 HTX 的消息就没断过。

2023 年，有人 P 图说他被 FBI 击毙了。
2024 年，传他穿仓、要破产。
2025 年，ETH 穿仓、监管调查、资产储备，一轮接一轮。
2026 年，英国那边的监管和制裁，又带出一波资产冻结和平台安全的恐慌。
有些是纯假消息，有些是真麻烦。但结果是：人还在，TRON 还在，HTX 还在运营。
这听起来像废话。但你经历过 2017 的 ICO、2020 的 312、2022 的 FTX 就知道，在这个行业，还坐在牌桌上本身就是成绩。当年比他风光的人，很多现在连名字都没人提了。

二、遇到麻烦，他不跑，他打官司

WLFI 这事是个典型。他前后投了几千万美金，因为代币冻结跟对方闹翻，直接告上法庭。11 月 3 日又有新进展，孙宇晨方面指控 WLFI 没有及时披露涉及阿联酋的所有权关系，向法院提出制裁动议。

官司怎么判我不知道。但对面是一个政治和商业背景都很硬的项目，他没认栽，选择走法律程序一直磕到底。

英国 FCA 那边，去年开始的诉讼，今年 10 月底和解，HTX 退出英国市场并做了相应承诺。这不算赢，其他制裁和冻结的问题也没全解决。但它说明一件事：监管的问题，最后还是得回到法律和合规上一个一个解决，而不是发条推骂回去。

发推谁都会。打一场持续几个月的官司，不是谁都扛得住。

三、他的生意，比他的争议更值得看

最近能明显看到，他把精力放回 HTX 了。

11 月 9 日，HTX 正式上线美股代币现货，第一批 20 个，英伟达、特斯拉、谷歌都在。

资产上链是接下来最大的方向之一，这我之前就说过。但对普通用户来说，光有链上资产没用，你还需要流动性、交易体验，和一个完整的入口。CEX 当然有托管和监管的风险，所以最后拼的还是产品、流动性、安全和信任，不是创始人说了什么。

储备证明、HTX 代币销毁、美股代币，能不能做成，要看数据。但至少他在做事，这比社交媒体上的口水战值钱。

最后

我不是说孙哥没问题。恰恰相反，他身上的争议太多了，多到遮住了另一面。

很多人研究孙宇晨，是为了找下一个争议。你换个角度，把他当成一个创业十几年、穿过好几轮周期、同时经营好几摊加密业务的人来看，结论会不一样。

币圈不缺一夜成名的人。缺的是十几年后还在做事的人。

5 个小时里他说过一句话，我记到现在：跟巴菲特吃饭，是巴菲特占便宜。
所有人都当笑话听。但我觉得，一个被骂了十几年还敢这么说话的人，起码有一样是真的：他没被打倒。

被高估的是争议度，被低估的是韧性。

Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. Probably over a thousand people at this point. This includes hundreds of engineers, CEOs, colleagues, friends, etc.

Also, since there was some spy talk. Jensen is as proud  an American as it gets. I'm in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America.

I stand with Jensen.

Love you all ❤️

author: hamandcheese
quoted_text:
I understand the hesitation to accept US intelligence allegations that Alice Huang was spying for Beijing’s Ministry of State Security (MSS). Years of Deep State overreach, including the discredited Steele dossier, have made such claims harder to take at face value.

That said, the combination of intelligence assessments with corporate records, travel patterns, financial flows, and her personal background makes the MSS-linked explanation the most credible one currently available.

Her trajectory fits known MSS patterns of long-term cultivation rather than an opportunistic affair to expand business. 

Alice Huang grew up in Xiangtan, Hunan, in a residential compound tied to Jiangnan Machinery Factory, a former Soviet-supported state-owned defense enterprise that produces smart munitions and other military products. That places her early life inside the party-state defense system. From there, her path unfolded in stages.

She began with a brief stint in media (Hunan Satellite TV and CCTV). Official databases and longtime staff checks have turned up little, suggesting the work was primarily a stepping stone. By associating herself with the outer circles of these outlets, she built a public persona and gained social credibility through the identity of a journalist while developing sharp interpersonal judgment, speaking skills, and the ability to manage social situations.

She then moved into offshore finance. Entering Hong Kong’s financial sector in 2008, she worked at HSBC private banking and CITIC Securities. There she learned the mechanics of large asset transfers, offshore trust structures, and leveraged financing while building deep connections among wealthy people in Hong Kong and mainland China. This provided practical groundwork for her later role as an offshore intermediary handling chip deals worth billions of dollars.

Next she learned to navigate the gray areas of China’s A-share market. After joining Shanghai Hersing Investment, she and her husband Kang Wei moved into public-facing dealmaking roles. Huang was deeply involved in the FCOM backdoor listing case and the subsequent collapse of LMBB Finance, a major illegal fundraising case involving more than 83 billion yuan (about $11.6 billion USD), whose principal defendant received a life sentence. Yet Huang somehow emerged unscathed, which strongly suggests that special state-security connections protected her.

A mysterious four-year gap then suggests closed-door specialist training. Between 2019 and 2023, Huang’s public résumé was completely blank. Intelligence assessments identified this as the period when she underwent intensive closed-door MSS training. She advanced from an ordinary financial intermediary to a strategic intelligence operative where she became fluent in cutting-edge chip terminology, familiar with methods of evading restrictions, and trained to study the psychological profiles of specific senior targets.

Finally, she was positioned to present herself as a computing industry heavyweight and move in on the target. As the United States tightened export controls in 2023, the MSS arranged for her to quickly take over 7Road’s Singapore business and rename it Megaspeed. She became a major buyer, spending billions of dollars on servers and creating a natural opening into the heart of NVIDIA’s supply chain.

Given the relationship between the Chinese state and its citizens, it is important to note that she did not need to be a full-time intelligence officer to serve as a useful cut-out for chip acquisition and relationship-building. Chinese spycraft is rarely in the James Bond mold.

At the end of the day, NVIDIA controls the overwhelming majority of the global market for AI training chips. Anyone who can shape its allocation decisions or the political environment around export controls obtains a direct lever on the computing power available to Chinese military and industrial AI programs.

Jensen Huang has been among the most effective and consistent public advocates for selling more advanced chips to China. He has direct access to senior US and European decision makers and has argued that restrictions are counterproductive. An intimate relationship that created emotional and commercial interdependence offered a dual channel: potential insight into NVIDIA technology and US policy thinking, plus a trusted voice who could continue lobbying against tighter controls.

His personal and organizational style amplified the risk. NVIDIA has a notably flat management structure with limited layered screening around the CEO. Huang is outgoing, socially gregarious, and comfortable in informal settings, wading through crowds in Taiwanese night markets, enjoying whiskey gatherings, and customer dinners. That approachability is an asset in normal business but it is also the kind of surface area that a professional intelligence service looks for when it deploys a cultivated asset who already speaks the technical language, holds a legitimate customer identity, and can operate in plain sight.

Since Chen Yixin took leadership of the MSS, the service has shown a more aggressive posture toward high tech supply chains, combining offshore financing, shell companies, and targeted personal relationships. Jensen Huang is at the intersection of this technological chokepoint and political access, making him a priority target.

Of course this doesn't PROVE that specific secrets left NVIDIA or that Huang’s lobbying was the direct product of the relationship. But it does show why US intelligence treated the case as a serious counterintelligence matter rather than gossip, why Taiwan monitored the visits, why short sellers and journalists were already examining the commercial links, and why the background and financial architecture are difficult to dismiss as coincidence.

The comparison to the Steele dossier is understandable given past overreach, but the sourcing, timeline, multi-jurisdictional scrutiny, and open source commercial red flags here are materially different.

text:
As all NVIDIA employees I guess, I am deeply concerned by the campaign against Jensen Huang. Removing him would be a disaster.

Many have documented on X and elsewhere how this looks like a coordinated coup.

I'd add only one thing. Look at who would benefit from a dramatic weakening of NVIDIA.

It is not China. It is not about selling GPUs to China because that train has left. China authorities have pushed back on the H200 the Trump administration allowed NVIDIA to sell.

Look at what Jensen pushed back on:
- regulations that would make open source model training too expensive
- regulations that would make closed model providers immune to liabilities caused by their models. He said "if your product is not ready, then don't ship it"
- regulation against model distillation. He said "this is competition. People do it all the time with NVIDIA products, they try to reverse engineer them."

The other side will do everything they can to get him fired. 

As a French, I can't care less about his private life. I get that the US is puritan and sees it otherwise. But frankly, isn't it something he and his family has to deal with? Why should all NVIDIA employees, partners, and investors be collateral damage?

Disclaimer. As my bio says, the above are my views only. I do not represent NVIDIA by any means. I only commented on publicly available information.

text:
1. Bloomberg가 11월 13일 낸 독점 기사, 제목은 황이 스스로를 쓰레기에 빗댄 말에서 따온 것임. 사임이 결정되던 11월 11일 수요일 밤 황의 모습을 다룸.

2. 등장인물이 몇 명 나옴. 

콜레트 크레스는 10년 넘게 CFO를 맡아온 인물로 임시 CEO가 됨. 

하비 존스는 73세이고 반도체 설계 소프트웨어 회사 Synopsys의 전 CEO이며, 엔비디아 최초의 이사회 의장으로 선임됨. 

팀 테터는 한국 보도에 법무총괄로 나오는 엔비디아 내부 인물임.

3. 아래 내용 중 법무총괄과 이사회 대응 부분은 이데일리 내용임.

[사임까지 일주일]

4. 10월 말 NYT가 Alice Huang과의 관계를 보도했을 때 황은 주변에 불륜을 부인했음.

5. 11월 6일 FT가 연인 관계였다고 보도하자 상황이 바뀜. 법무총괄이 황의 자택을 찾아가 사실관계를 추궁했고 황이 인정했다고 함. 이사회는 공개 대응에 소극적이었지만 법무총괄의 강한 요구로 외부 로펌 조사에 착수함.

6. 11월 8일 황이 전 직원에게 이메일을 보내 불륜을 인정하고 가족에게 사과했으며 조사에 협조하겠다고 약속함.

7. 이 무렵 업무에도 차질이 생김. 황은 약 60명의 임원에게 직접 보고받고 직원들의 주요 업무를 이메일로 점검하던 사람인데, 즉각 답하던 회신이 늦어졌다고 함.

8. 11월 11일 NYT가 보고 라인에 있는 임원 Kimberly Powell과의 두 번째 불륜을 보도함. 이것이 결정타였다는 평가임. 이사회가 그날 밤 회의를 열었고 백악관도 회의 사실을 알고 있었다고 함.

[11일 밤과 12일 아침]

9. 기사에 따르면 황은 이사회와의 마지막 논의에서 몇 주 이어온 버티기를 조건 없이 접었음. 평소의 추진력이 사라지고 될 대로 되라는 식으로 말했으며, 스스로를 인간 쓰레기라고 자책했다고 함.

10. 황은 자신의 거취보다 아내를 가장 걱정한다고 했고, 의혹에 휩싸인 여성들의 삶이 망가지지 않기를 바란다고 했다고 함.

11. CNBC에 따르면 이사회는 두 번째 보도 후 분위기가 급변해 밤사이 해임을 사실상 결정했고, 대외 발표 전략을 밤늦게까지 짠 뒤 아침에 공식 결정하고 크레스를 임시 CEO로 발표함.

12. CNN에 따르면 트럼프 대통령은 그 주에 황과 여러 차례 통화하며 안부를 묻고 사퇴 압박에 맞서 싸우라고 격려했음. 사임 후에는 트럼프가 팀 쿡을 후임으로 제안했다고 보도됨.

[사임 이후]

13. 황은 사장, CEO, 이사직에서 즉시 물러났고 앞으로 엔비디아에서 어떤 역할도 맡지 않음. 아직 확정되지 않은 주식 보상 약 1억 800만 달러를 포기하는데, 순자산 약 1,445억 달러의 0.07퍼센트 수준임.

14. 주가는 발표 직후 장중 최대 16퍼센트까지 빠졌다가 낙폭을 줄여 4.3퍼센트 하락으로 마감했다고 NBC가 전함. 시총은 한때 4조 달러 아래로 내려갔음.

15. 샌타클래라 본사 앞에는 꽃다발과 양초가 놓였고 일부 직원은 눈물을 흘렸다고 CNBC가 전함. 많은 직원이 황을 우상처럼 여겼다고 함.

16. 황은 의회 증언에 응하기로 했음. 의원 여러 명이 소환장 발부를 압박한 뒤였음. 11월 18일 비공개 브리핑이 요청된 상태임.

17. 수사도 진행 중임. Bloomberg에 따르면 법무부가 맨해튼 연방검찰 주도로 Alice Huang의 전 직장 Megaspeed가 슈퍼마이크로 제품을 중국으로 빼돌렸는지 조사하고 있음. 슈퍼마이크로는 올해 3월 핵심 임원이 엔비디아 칩 밀반출 혐의로 기소된 서버 업체임. 싱가포르 경찰은 Alice Huang이 재직 중 범죄를 저질렀다고 볼 증거가 충분하지 않다고 밝혔다고 함.

18. Alice Huang은 보안 당국이 아는 상태에서 베이징에 있다고 Bloomberg가 전했고, 중국은 스파이 의혹을 부인함.

[앞으로 볼 것]

19. 후임은 이사회가 사내외 후보를 모두 보고 정함. 예측시장 Polymarket은 데이터센터 사업을 맡은 Ian Buck을 유력 후보로 봤음. 황은 10월 Bloomberg 인터뷰에서 후임이 이미 회사 안에 있기를 바란다고 했고, 자녀 Madison과 Spencer가 후계 자리를 원하면 직접 증명해야 한다고 했음.

20. 애널리스트 Dan Ives는 엔비디아 가치를 황이 있을 때 주당 300달러, 없을 때 225달러로 봤음. 일부 애널리스트는 투자의견을 낮췄음.

21. 엔비디아 실적 발표가 11월 17일로 예정돼 있음.

text:
Nvidia chips are still scarce, even now.

But to maximize that premium, Nvidia has to support the neoclouds.

If the new Nvidia CEO turns even slightly skeptical about supporting the neoclouds, spot prices will take a hit. That will hurt neocloud margins. To avoid this, the neoclouds will have no choice but to reach out elsewhere. AMD, or the TPU camp.

In other words, the neoclouds break free of Nvidia's grip, and Nvidia's dominance and influence both take a hit. That in turn means a hit to the massive order volume that underpins Nvidia's only moat, its control of the supply chain, and it means Nvidia's flywheel breaks.

Jensen worked tirelessly to protect this flywheel. He pushed on many fronts to get a blind eye turned to neoclouds leasing capacity to Chinese hyperscalers, and he encouraged chip exports to China so that China would never forget the taste of the Nvidia sauce, working relentlessly to have China's AI ecosystem built on top of Nvidia. That way, even if the latest GPUs become hard to get inside China, there is still a reason to rent the same chips from overseas neoclouds. Keeping Chinese developers inside the Nvidia ecosystem was also a way of protecting neocloud utilization.

Still, all of this was playing with fire along the edges of the gray zone, something deeply improper and dangerous in the eyes of Washington.

Even so, Jensen did what was best for Nvidia. That cannot be denied.

Jensen meant to wait until the neoclouds could order the next generation of GPUs on their own. He probably saw sharing risk with customers until then as being in Nvidia's interest too. What I want to know now is whether the next CEO can wait that long.

According to the WSJ article... the current CEO does not seem to be that patient.

I worry about an Nvidia without Jensen.

text: This is some of the most remarkable investigative journalism that anyone has published this year
author: hamandcheese
quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
老实说，玩推特这么久，对美国的各种美好滤镜全都碎了，之前觉得美国是自由、民主、科技的象征，现在觉得就那样吧。

认识的很多朋友，大家到了一定年纪/有一定财力后，不约而同开始规划「身份问题」，无疑都是先去 HK/新加坡，如果本就在 HK/新加坡的人，会觉得当地拥挤、生活质量低，又想移民美国。

在美国的华人呢，开始抱怨税收、种族歧视，刻板印象等等。就连黄仁勋这样，从洗盘子到世界第一大公司 CEO，最伟大美国梦的主角，都能因为美国党派之争被干掉，牺牲于政治，有些问题，或许不止一个国家有，也不是移民就能改变的。

特朗普嘴上说着，建算力中心，发展 AI 为了美国，但回头把算力中心建在社区里；说发展 Crypto 行业，结果自己是那个最能掏池子的人。每次看 SEC、CFTC 发各种政策的时候，都要附和一句——我们伟大的特朗普总统领导......真绷不住。

民主党也不遑多让，什么品种的人，上台第一天能喊出限制 AI 发展，并在几天后将亲共和党的企业 CEO 连续清算，就算你掌握全球芯片命脉。在美国加密法案审查中，民主党靠银行业的背后支持，让加密行业存活这么多年，依旧没有法律参考。理由只有——特朗普掏太多钱了！

美国的党派之间内斗，大于行业发展，大于国家未来，大于人类命运。有用之才像黄仁勋，必须 2 选 1，过几年反复横跳清算，当台的就是不好，台下的永远是最好的。但说白了，共和党是少数人的共和，民主党也是几个人的民主。

我不是说，自己所在的国家有多好，中国也有各种各样的问题，有些方面，做的还不如美国，但就个人来说，可以在这里吃到自己喜欢的食物，家人朋友也都在身边，我觉得已经很幸福。

我曾在欧洲住过半年，生活非常难受，交通不方便，食物吃不习惯，晚上不敢出门，朋友仅有工作上的同事，每周末一个人在家里发呆，要多无聊又多无聊，还会偶尔看见商铺“中国人不得入内”的牌子，出去之后，并没有觉得外面的世界有多好。（旅游倒是挺推荐，风景不错）

对于我来说，花很多时间精力折腾移民，最后发现生活质量和心态并没改变多少，属实没必要。

很多人问我SOXL涨回来了。我是不是又赚回来了。
我都止损了怎么赚回来，当然不止损的话，38块钱就已经爆仓了。
我现在真的很悲观，1个多月时间亏了120万刀，感觉自己赚不回来这个钱了。

一个人倒下了三次，站起来了三次，第四次倒下了，他还能站起来么。身边的朋友似乎对我都很有信心觉得我能轻松赚回来，只有我知道自己的压力有多大。因为我不再年轻。
每次我都云淡风轻的安慰自己：亏的都是之前赚的。这次真的是躯体化了，什么都不想做。本来明天去吉隆坡看李志演唱会的，我给退了。包机酒的泰国BBW也推掉了。

再一个我感觉币圈真的没有机会了，现在整个市场只有合约和meme，而合约中，SOXL的交易量已经和ETH不相上下，交易所支持美股交易，并没有给币圈带来多少的资金量，反而是把币圈的资金分流到了美股中。这两天BTC的颓势很明显，11月5号的大暴跌，让币圈的资金在美股受损严重。美股都反弹回来了，而BTC却是阴跌不断。在没有外部利好单独刺激的情况下，何时能反转。
那这样一个市场还能让我重新赚到钱么，总不能靠交易美股赚回来吧。

最后反思下自己的交易，正如 @Bitfatty 说的我的交易策略有很大的问题。遇到黑天鹅的时候，大概率会死。 我每次合约亏大钱似乎都是这样。我可以在99天里赚钱，每天赚1w，但会在第100天亏掉所有。因为人永远都会上头。

写完感觉会好受点。我不介意大家嘲笑我。只希望在这样一个残酷的市场，大家都能活下去。

Bombshell story. The spy narrative is collapsing already.

Is there clear & convincing evidence that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy?

- AG says no. (“no conclusions reached”).
- CIA says no. (“not yet convinced”).
- DNI says no (“not entirely accurate and over-torqued”).
- Ranking Democrat on House Intelligence (incoming Chairman) says no. (“today, at least, I don’t know”). This was immediately after he was briefed.

Who argues otherwise? Anonymous officials tell CNN “it strains credulity to believe that she was not acting as an agent of the Chinese government — simply by virtue of the fact that she is a successful Chinese businesswoman working with one of America’s most powerful companies.”

This is their proof after a year of investigating and surveillance? That she was a “successful Chinese businesswoman”? 

At this point, the only crime that we know for sure happened is the leaking of the classified memo. Who did that and why?

An investigation should be opened.

Everyone believes CUDA is NVIDIA's moat, the reason we've maintained our dominance in the AI era. I've never believed that.

NVIDIA has only one true moat: its people. And the most important of them is Jensen Huang.

I've worked on CUDA compilers, libraries, and DSLs for eight years, from Volta to Rubin. I think I've earned the right to share my perspective on what NVIDIA's moat really is. I hope you'll bear with me.

1. What is CUDA?

Many people think CUDA is just a programming language and its compiler, and that NVIDIA's moat comes from the massive amount of software written in CUDA, making it impossible for developers to leave NVIDIA GPUs.

This is completely wrong. It's an incredibly naive understanding of CUDA.

To me, CUDA is everything NVIDIA does.

CUDA isn't just a language, software, or hardware architecture. It's a product defined by a unique customer experience.

When you find GPU programming too difficult, CUDA gives you an easier way. When your GPU code isn't fast enough, NVIDIA engineers respond and help you solve it. When a handful of GPUs can no longer push your technology forward, NVIDIA has already scaled its computing platform from desktops to massive data centers. When you need more data centers than anyone else can supply, NVIDIA has already secured wafer and HBM capacity years in advance to meet your demand.

That experience is CUDA.

It's made possible by the relentless, day-to-day work of everyone at NVIDIA. And the person who brings all these people together, who gives them a shared vision and purpose, is Jensen Huang.

2. What made CUDA possible?

Patience. Perseverance. An unwavering commitment to a vision.

Around 2006, NVIDIA bet that the future would demand far more computing power, and began transforming GPUs from graphics processors into a platform for general-purpose computing. Initially, it was a commercial disaster. The added costs hurt margins, the market wasn't ready, and the strategy faced enormous skepticism and pressure, including questions from the board.

But Jensen persisted.

For roughly a decade, NVIDIA kept investing in CUDA, building its hardware, software, and developer ecosystem long before the commercial payoff became clear.

Eventually, deep learning arrived. And NVIDIA was ready.

Today, this sounds like an inspiring story. But for those who lived through it, it meant a decade of perseverance, doubt, and being misunderstood.

Looking back at the history of technology, how many people could have done the same?

This is what I've always loved most about NVIDIA.

And now, Jensen has been pushed out.

This won't kill NVIDIA. The company can still create tremendous commercial value. But it has killed NVIDIA's soul. And how far can a body go without its soul?

If this is how Jensen Huang is treated today, how will those of us who built CUDA be treated tomorrow?

I love NVIDIA deeply, but I have to say it: NVIDIA is dead.

I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

My favourite, totally speculative theory, is that the Haung chip rat lines operated with the blessing of the White House. Alice was the fixer, but the affair itself was a cover. The rationale for this was a quiet quid pro quo for access to rare earths and other essentials, while maintaining the optics of being tough on China.

Moreover, the economic circularity of the arrangement suited both sides. Without it, the main narrative for growth collapses both in the West and in China. 

The fact the whole thing was blown open is connected to the Dems coming back into power, and wanting to shut down the AI race. Their agenda is to lock ai down and take it fully in house, citing safety concerns. But everyone knows that is unlikely to happen in practice. A lockdown means asymmetric tech advantage for the US military industrial complex. That is concerning for everyone on the planet as it destabilies the MAD balance that has prevented nuclear annihilation so far.

I think on that basis it probably served the interests of the world for some of these models to be "distilled" by China, and released into the wild. Without deepseek and Kimi the asymmetry would be far worse.

The only thing standing in the way of Chinese, French or even British labs catching up with American labs is access to chips. Blow up Jensen and the rat lines, and the power grab is complete.

Even if it's not the truth, I think it's a good story. And it makes even more sense when you frame it against the attempted ousting of Sam Altman in 2023, and the appointment of Larry Summers to OpenAI, PLUS, the latest revelations about Dario Amodei's wife.

New knowledge goes into her library and memory instead of retraining her, so nothing old gets overwritten:
Nothing new is unlearned:

Ask it something that spans two fields, say neuroscience and machine learning, and it connects them, grounded, from its own reading. Ask it about something that doesn't exist and it tells you it isn't there instead of making something up. It cites what it actually knows. And asks to learn it instead 

Consumer hardware. One home PC. Years of research clicked into place today.

NVIDIA letting Jensen go is a huge mistake, for America and for humanity. It's Apple firing Steve Jobs all over again, but much bigger, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world.

I've been keeping quiet on this out of respect for Jensen's family and team, who I've met and who are amazing humans, and because I personally hate infidelity. So my heart goes out to them in this difficult personal family moment.

Not that I matter at all, but I've known Jensen for a long time and have gotten the chance to spend a lot of time with him, behind the scenes, away from mics and cameras. I have seen him show kindness, humility, care to everyone around him, including strangers, including from the poorest most struggling parts of society, treating all the same with the same thoughtfulness and attention, because they are fellow humans and not because he has something to gain from them. Another data point is what people who know him well have said privately to me about Jensen over the years. I've never had anyone tell me anything but how awesome he is or how much they love him. text:
根本原因还是英伟达没有双重股权结构。

一般来说，会采用ab股方式。
赋予创始人持有的股份更高的每股投票权（通常为10票），而公众股东持有的股份只有1票或0票。

这样创始人即使经济权益占比不高，也能掌握绝对或相对多数表决权。

对比其他公司情况
1. Meta（马克·扎克伯格）
约13.4%经济权益对应约60.6%投票权。
2026年公司进一步设立Class C无投票权股份，用于融资、股权激励和收购，同时通过“绑定协议”限制扎克伯格出售大部分Class C股份，避免稀释其投票控制权。Class B股份通常在转让时自动转换为Class A。

2. Alphabet（拉里·佩奇与谢尔盖·布林） 三层结构，创始人合计约12%经济权益对应约52.7%投票权。2014年通过派发Class C股份，实现后续融资与员工激励而不稀释投票权。

3. SpaceX（埃隆·马斯克） 2026年IPO时明确采用双重股权，部分设计还赋予Class B股东选举董事会多数席位的权利。
结果是约46%经济权益对应约82%–85%投票权。这使马斯克在上市后仍能绝对控制公司。

4. 对比NVIDIA。
自1999年上市以来始终采用一股一票单一类别普通股。黄仁勋约3.58%持股即对应3.58%投票权，无超级投票保护。董事会可根据章程以多数票解除高管职务，无需证明失职。

这种结构的本质是将经济权益与控制权分离。
创始人可通过多轮融资稀释自身持股比例，却仍保留对公司战略方向、董事会组成和重大决策的主导权。

I view these strategies as complementary – in our Atlas release today, both the Chisel web app and Codex/Claude Code integrations are designed for using an agent to build out coarse geometry in 3D and control precise final pixel generation through Atlas model endpoints.

This demo showcases the Chisel variant of Atlas we finetuned for flexible control, capable of taking in any combination of partial RGB and partial depth frames. text:
SemiAnalysis’s Dylan Patel says Google’s TPUs are just as good as Nvidia’s in his nightly benchmarks, and without Jensen’s wheeling and dealing Google could take a ton of share

“It’s sort of a three-pronged strategy. One is you have to have the technical progress, and that keeps you winning. The second is that you have to have supply chain prowess, and Jensen’s the only executive in the semiconductor industry that is going out there and drinking and meeting and convincing all of these supply chain companies to invest like they’ve never done before, give him the allocations.”

“Now if all of a sudden there’s no Jensen, and Google’s like, actually, double my allocation. The TPU, from our benchmarking, we test TPUs. We run benchmarks on them on open source models every night. They’re just as good as Nvidia. But Google doesn’t have that DNA of wheeling and dealing with the supply chain, wheeling and dealing with customers. Now if that DNA is gone, the thing that is Jensen is gone, does that now mean Google can just take a ton of share? It’s a real big possibility.”

“Same with AMD. Technically, they’re awesome, but they’re just not able to wheel and deal like Jensen is able to. And that’s been a lot of the reason why they’ve been behind. Of course, the software as well. One of Nvidia’s biggest moats being CUDA, and software is being rapidly displaced by the fact that AI models are so good at writing software.”

quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

text:
Founder succession is an open problem. 

Successful founders are themselves odd ducks who surround themselves with people who complement their strengths and weaknesses.

By definition, the people who surround a founder are very different from the founder.

But when a founder leaves, we promote the most successful subordinate into an organizational spot which they, almost by definition, don’t fit. 

Replacing a visionary founder CEO with a CFO or COO is comically stupid. Yet it is considered the best practice.

I don’t know the answer to this problem,  and although I have some ideas, I am nowhere close to ready to test them on my own business :)

text:
训练一个大模型可能需要持续数月，几乎没有从头再跑一次的机会。这样的任务，Agent 还能实现递归自我改进（RSI）吗？

SII-GAIR 与 Xinxu AI 最近的论文《No Second Run》，尝试把 RSI 引入大模型预训练，并训练出了 801-30B-A3B。

核心思路是把昂贵的预训练过程拆成多个可验证的小闭环。

Agent 可以定位训练故障、评估数据和训练策略，并通过 Context Infrastructure 共享训练指标、代码变更和失败经验，让整个系统能够持续积累知识、改进流程。

作者报告，团队在三个月内完成了 11.8T Tokens 的预训练。在相同的 1T Token 预算下，22 项 Benchmark 平均分从 47.78 提升到 56.83。不过，这些收益来自多项联合改进，无法单独归因于 Agent。

这个工作对 RSI 和 Harness Engineering 还是很有启发。

当任务昂贵到无法反复重来，局部可验证的实验、长期积累的经验，以及跨任务共享的 Context，可能就是实现持续自我改进的关键。

📎 arXiv: https://t.co/ZYihkjchCy

💻 GitHub: https://t.co/K1ePPEvJpj

quoted_text:
I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

不过今天让我开心的，其实不止是看到朋友账户里的绿色曲线😼

想想刚来 OKX 的时候，每天都有好多东西要学。

那时候遇到问题，第一反应就是找同事求助。

用户遇到问题，我已经能够自己梳理交易过程，判断可能涉及的产品机制，再联系相关同事核实，把事情弄明白，最后解释给用户听。

从被别人帮助，到现在慢慢能够帮助别人，这种感觉真的很棒。

从刚开始小白时，模仿大V拍搞笑视频逐渐有人认识我，到现在快一年时间，真的很感谢陪着我的朋友们。 

看到大家的绿色收益曲线很开心，但更开心的是，回过头来看，自己的成长曲线好像也一直在UP。

继续学习，继续升级，以后我们都向上走。

text:
Arca CIO Jeff Dorman says $ETH's store-of-value thesis assumes every other blockchain will eventually disappear

"I think it's really misguided, right? Again, a store of value, you're saying you're a currency, right?"

"Bitcoin is effectively like an immaculate conception, right? It was a 1-in-a-billion long shot that it actually worked. And then everyone starts to come to it saying, 'Oh, well, Bitcoin can be a store of value. We can be too.' And it makes no sense."

"It's like saying, 'Oh, because the dollar became the superpower of the world over 150 years, then all of a sudden the Zimbabwe dollar is also going to be a store of value,' even though it hyperinflates every year. You can't just point to the one that worked and then say everything is a comp to that."

"There's no rationale for ETH, the token, to be used in any way, shape or form outside of the Ethereum network itself. So if you're going to argue that ETH is a store of value or even a medium of exchange, you have to also argue that every other blockchain is going away."

"The entire world is going to be run on blockchain and it's all going to be run on Ethereum."

text:
He targeted young backpackers traveling across Australia. He offered them rides, gained their trust, and took them deep into the wilderness. For years, people disappeared without a trace. Then investigators discovered something horrifying inside Belanglo State Forest. His name was Ivan Milat, and he became known as Australia’s infamous “Backpacker Killer.”

Ivan Robert Marko Milat was born on December 27, 1944, in Sydney, Australia. He grew up in a family of 14 children and had a history of criminal behavior long before the murders. But between 1989 and 1992, seven young travelers disappeared while exploring Australia.

The first victims were James Gibson and Deborah Everist, both 19, who disappeared in December 1989. In 1991, German backpacker Simone Schmidl vanished. Later that year, another German couple, Anja Habschied, 20, and Gabor Neugebauer, 21, disappeared while traveling through the country. In April 1992, British backpackers Caroline Clarke, 21, and Joanne Walters, 22, also vanished after leaving Sydney.

For years, investigators struggled to connect the disappearances. Then, in September 1992, two people walking through Belanglo State Forest discovered the bodies of Clarke and Walters. Over the following months, five more victims were found in the same forest. Seven young travelers had been murdered and buried in a remote area of New South Wales.

The investigation took a dramatic turn when British backpacker Paul Onions came forward. In January 1990, he had accepted a ride from a man calling himself “Bill.” During the journey, the driver pulled out a shotgun and threatened him. Onions managed to escape and reported the incident to police. Years later, after reading about the backpacker murders, he contacted Australian investigators. He believed the man who had threatened him might be responsible.

In 1994, Onions returned to Australia and identified Ivan Milat. On May 22, police arrested Milat at his home. Investigators discovered weapons, ammunition, camping equipment and personal belongings connected to the murdered travelers. Among the recovered items was a distinctive shirt belonging to Onions.

Milat’s trial began in March 1996. He maintained his innocence throughout the proceedings, but on July 27, the jury found him guilty of all seven murders and the kidnapping of Paul Onions. He received seven consecutive life sentences without the possibility of parole.

But investigators still had one question: were there more victims? Several other disappearances were examined for possible connections to Milat, but no additional murder convictions were secured against him.

On October 27, 2019, Ivan Milat died in prison at the age of 74. He never confessed to the seven murders. Seven young people had left home to explore Australia, but never returned. Paul Onions survived because he managed to escape, and his testimony helped bring one of Australia’s most notorious killers to justice.

Do you believe Ivan Milat was responsible for more murders than the seven he was convicted of?

text:
Tarek predicted 5 month ago that Citadel would sue Kalshi.

In this interview from June, @mansourtarek_ explains exactly why stock perps are a big threat to Wall Street.

Now Citadel, CME, Cboe and Nasdaq are suing him to stop Kalshi from offering perps.

Here is why.

1 - THEY FEAR LOSING RETAIL

Citadel executes ~35% of US-listed retail volume and make money by trading against their orders. Stock perps threaten to redirect that activity.

If someone trades an Apple perp on Kalshi instead of Apple shares, Citadel loses.

Their own court filing explicitly admit to it:

- “Cboe and Citadel Securities lose transactions and revenue they cannot later recover.”
- “Kalshi's offering is designed to draw away CME’s customers who currently trade futures.”

2 - PERPS GENERATE LESS FEES

So why wouldn't Citadel just offer Perps themselve ?

Because traditional futures have an expiry date. To keep your exposure you need to close you old position and open a new ones. Those additional transactions generate fees. 

Perps don’t expire, removing those fees entirely.

The interview passage where Tarek highlights this Perps over Futures advantage is even cited by CME in the lawsuit.

That's why the Citadel camp is asking to reclassify Perps as security-based swaps:

1) Citadel wins - Perps are SEC regulated, retails can't trade them, they keep trading future on their exchange.

2) Kalshi wins - Perps are CFTC regulated, retail can trade them over more expensive futures, Kalshi receive their order flow.

It's all about who gets to farm retail.

I have a major result to share.

I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.

This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it. When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern—a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model.

Again, this evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking. It’s based on a forensic analysis of the model weights released by the companies themselves.

I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models. In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models—including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3—were initialized on NVIDIA Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in NVIDIA’s flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems.

I then verified these results on real hardware. Running unmodified PyTorch with the seeds I’d recovered, a Blackwell B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s untouched starting weights bit for bit, and a rented GB200 reproduced Kimi K3’s to a correlation of 0.999995. A Hopper H100 reproduced none of DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s, and changing the seed by one broke the match. (DeepSeek’s seed is 953049583 by the way.) The method also was verified to match 24 known open-weights models to the hardware that developers said they used.

It is exceedingly unlikely that these results are a coincidence. Across six trillion combinations, the best accidental match should reach only about 8 sigma (i.e., eight standard deviations above what random chance would produce). The real matches range from 49 to 1,385 sigma, and even the weakest single test hits 20.

These were data-center-scale training runs. With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise. It’s quite likely that we see multi-billion dollar expenditure on export-controlled GPUs.

I am highly confident in this result, and it has been independently verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. You can read the full report at https://t.co/YOtzND0Jqk.

There is much more I’ve identified about these models through other forms of checkpoint forensics like this, and will have more to share soon.

"Well then your medical conditions must not have been too serious, Eric, if you didn't qualify for what we put together, which was a pretty broad-based medical marijuana program."

Chris Christie diagnosed a stranger on live television without a chart, a test or a medical degree. The logic is a closed loop: the program was broad, so whoever it shut out was not really sick. The rulebook certifies the illness, and the man who guarded the rulebook certifies the rulebook.

He takes credit for putting it together. Jon Corzine signed the program in 2010. It launched with 11 qualifying conditions. By August 2013 the entire state had one operating dispensary, under rules ranked among the most stringent in the country. By March 2015, three of the six dispensaries the law required were open, for 4,000 patients.

The caller said he would not have qualified in 2016. The record agrees with him. Migraines and chronic musculoskeletal pain joined the list only in 2017, and even then final sign-off sat with Health Commissioner Cathleen Bennett, a Christie appointee who opposed legal cannabis.

So the conditions became serious the day a panel voted. The patients stayed exactly as sick.

Christie called medical programs in other states a front for legalization. He kept his own narrow enough that it could never pass for one, and now remembers it as wide.

New Jersey voters gave the second opinion in 2020: 2,737,746 to 1,343,637.

The patients outvoted the doctor.

Combined with the midterms and Anthropic IPO filing, these things don’t just happen as coincidence. There is something much larger at play that normies like us can never see behind the scenes

The obvious question to ask is who actually benefits from this coup on Jensen. The answers are widespread

1. Hyperscalers: slow down capex timing, remove reliance on neoclouds, give enough time for them to build their own alternatives (Google TPUs, for example). I find it highly unlikely that they had anything to do with it given the track record of these companies. They know it’s not a zero sum market and there are trillions to be made

2. China: neutralize the biggest threat to the country by slowing down AI development and throw the American ecosystem into an uncertainty tantrum

3. US govt: Jensen pushed for more sales and open exports to China. See his Dwarkesh interview as reference. If he was gaining too much ground in making this happen and pressing on the wrong buttons for people, someone might have just found it easier to remove him completely

4. AI skeptics: prove to the world that the entire industry is a hoax by bringing down the face of the industry 

I am sure there will be many more details revealed about this over the coming days and weeks. 

But will say one last thing. When you are this important to such a critical industry with national security concerns and global implications, it is very easy to make enemies out of extremely powerful people

Jensen thought he could live the American dream. Come here an immigrant, build a trillion dollar business, become a centa billionaire and retain the freedom to do what he wants

The system proved him wrong. Above a certain level of wealth, you have actually foregone the ability to ever retain any freedom. It is counter intuitive but very real, and events over the last couple weeks is the perfect example

quoted_text:
链上二级市场俨然一副“熊市”的样子了，处在今年宏观如此不确定的年份，投资、交易、理财真心不容易😭。

反正就一个原则，在局势不明朗的情况下，空仓理财总好过高频操作亏钱。今天要介绍的链上余额宝钱包 @Top_nod  ，就给了一个闲置USDC理财解决方案：

1）先要说明，TopNod是蚂蚁数科旗下的钱包，蚂蚁当年用支付宝把余额宝做成了国民级的现金管理工具。TopNod钱包尝试把类似的逻辑搬到链上，用 @Official_Axil APT Vault来实现数字“余额宝”的功能；

2）具体怎么做呢？APT Vault主要面向闲置的USDC，出事放出规模上限1000万美元，目标8%的APY，并分别配备了T+0或T+7的流动性管理计划，这样设计，主要考虑在收益和可赎回性上做平衡；

3）所以，别一听说“余额宝”和稳定的APY，就想当然以为大户可以无风险套利薅羊毛，T+0的赎回肯定会限制一定额度，超出后会走T+7，这样做其实就是一种日常小额流动性需求和整体资金稳定性之间的取舍，避免极端情况下被集中挤兑。毕竟，挂着余额宝的旗号，最关键就是底层资产的信用风险，和一开始说清楚透明化的规则，用户可以根据需求来选择；

4）从长期看，我觉得TopNod要做的链上余额宝和Neobank类托管钱包要做的交易和资金管理入口都类似，目标让钱包成为管理闲置资金的入口。可能现在还未强烈感觉，等未来稳定币和RWA大规模上链后，这个需求会非常刚性。其实也必须要做成，如果没有稳定、安全的理财渠道，大部分用户只能在这地狱般的交易投机场里被折磨，这样就无从谈起更大规模地增量资金流入了；

以上。

上边已经说的很明白了，有还在场内观望链上机会且不知道何时出手的用户，可以考虑留一部分闲置资金理理财，这样既避免了持U汇率缩水的焦虑，又能保证随时有机会能够出手，最关键是可以管住不受控制的交易亏手😢，何乐而不为？
